Its ballistic protection was self-evident. Its stability was extremely high, providing excellent head protection. In past military campaigns, it could even be used as a pot or a bowl. In the desert, when water was scarce, it could serve as a water collection device—truly multipurpose.
But for Jing Shu, its greatest use wasn’t just bulletproofing; it was also for protection against future natural disasters. During hailstorms, for instance, it could be used for protection—cone-shaped hailstones were deadly when they fell.
Consider the force of an object free-falling from the sky. Who would dare go Bald then? Everyone would wish for more hair or even resort to going out with bedding covering their heads. A plastic basin wouldn’t last more than a few minutes before being smashed.
Not to mention the mudslides and massive thunderstorms following the earthquake predicted in the coming years, or the landslides caused by torrential downpours. For the Banana District, situated at the foot of the mountains, hail was a minor concern.
Lightning-struck stones were the real problem.
It was as if they had offended the Thunder God, Lightning Mother, and Wind Lady, prompting them to vigorously carve up the mountain. This not only produced thunderous roars but also sent various stones flying and burrowing. Of course, scientists analyzed that because the Earth had deviated from its orbit in recent years and was not adapting well, it began its own crustal movements, leading to such violent reactions.
Regardless, having such a highly protective helmet would undoubtedly be a great blessing.
There were many helmets, but Jing Shu didn’t take too many—just about ten, enough for her family. She planned to take them into her space, modify them slightly, and change their color.
There were also some bulletproof vests. Since there weren’t many, Jing Shu took only three sets. These were quite heavy and cumbersome to wear. Huaxia’s troops were rarely issued them, but in the event of war, hundreds of thousands could be produced urgently.
"Professional gas masks too, perfect!" Jing Shu exclaimed, genuinely surprised. These were nothing like the ones sold on certain online platforms for a few hundred yuan that only offered protection against paint fumes.
Although I’m unsure of their exact protection level, they have to be useful against the toxic air and foul stenches of the apocalypse, right?
Believe me, you really wouldn’t want to spend an entire year smelling farts—and not a consistent type of fart, either, but a variety that randomly changed with the weather’s mood...
Rumor had it that the Earth had an upset stomach that year.
This time, Jing Shu took more than fifty gas masks. If she hadn’t, they would likely deteriorate and become unusable in a few years anyway. She stored them carefully in her space, intending to provide them to those in need later—for a fee, of course.

chapters.title: Chapter 198: Uncle, When Will You Live Stream Eating Shit?
chapters.content:
Chapter 198: Uncle, When Will You Live Stream Eating Shit?
Director Zhang walked briskly, humming a tune. When he knocked on the door again, he appeared quite confident. Mr. Jing opened it.
"Is it you?" Mr. Jing said, about to close the door.
"Wait, your daughter has committed a serious crime! She’s already been arrested and sentenced."
Director Zhang briefly explained what had happened, then hinted, "This is a serious matter. She could be sentenced to hard labor for a year or two. Think about it—men and women sleeping in the same quarters, your delicate daughter being eyed by a pack of hungry wolves... However, there is a way out. After all, I’m the one who allocates the housing."
Mr. Jing looked at Director Zhang skeptically.
My daughter’s temperament... could she really have been arrested? Even if she was, honestly, with her terrifying strength, one punch would...
Seeing Mr. Jing’s disbelief, Director Zhang took out three cell phones. "All phones were confiscated. One of these must belong to your daughter, right?"
Mr. Jing finally asked anxiously, "So, you have a solution?"
Director Zhang then revealed an inscrutable smile and, over the next few minutes, continuously hinted to Mr. Jing that as long as he gave him Virtual Coins, he could ensure his daughter’s safe release without the torment of reform.
"You don’t know? Things have really changed in the Second Team. The former Li Yuetian has stepped down, and now Captain Hu is in charge. He’s notoriously grasping, a real shark. So, it’s best to get her out before she even goes in."
Mr. Jing asked anxiously, "Then, Director Zhang, I’d be grateful if you could help."
"Sure thing," Director Zhang said with a satisfied smile, rubbing his hands.
"Thank you very much then," Mr. Jing said gratefully.
What the—??? I haven’t agreed yet! Doesn’t he know the rules!?
"However, I need to pull some strings," Director Zhang said, rubbing his hands and hinting strongly.
"Thank you for helping with that then."
Director Zhang clenched his teeth.
Is this man truly clueless, or is he just pretending?
"Why would I help you for free?"
Was my hinting not clear enough?
"Director Zhang, you just said you would help me. Why are you saying such things now?" Mr. Jing asked, looking surprised.
"Fine, I won’t waste words with you. Bring me 1,000 Virtual Coins, and I guarantee your daughter will come out safe and sound. Otherwise, your daughter will just become a pawn in the struggle between Li Yuetian and Captain Hu."
Director Zhang, unable to tolerate it any longer, blurted this out.
Fortunately, I eavesdropped by the wall earlier today and learned the truth. Now I actually have some leverage.
Suddenly, a long BEEP sounded. Mr. Jing exhaled. "Your timing was perfect. It finally finished recording."
Director Zhang, flustered and trying to sound tough, retorted, "Are you playing me? What can you do even if you recorded it?"
I’ve been careless! After so many years of receiving gifts, everyone always came eagerly to offer them. Even those who were slow on the uptake would understand with just a hint. I’ve never encountered someone like this!
"What can I do?" Mr. Jing proceeded to beat Director Zhang with punches and kicks. After subduing him, he tied him up and then called his daughter. Luckily, one of the three phones was her old one, so her current phone was still with her!
「」
The video recording was uploaded online, immediately causing an uproar. Online comments flew, such as: "Shocking! Does he think the police station is his family’s business?" This gave the onlookers the sensation of watching a serialized blockbuster. These types of videos, exposing dark secrets, are often the most effective at inciting public anger.
The onlookers were all clamoring for updates, but unfortunately, there was no further news. Many cursed the Wu City Government for its slow reaction, as people were nearly being killed while the authorities did nothing to resolve the situation.
「Elsewhere.」
The warehouse was huge. Jing Shu searched many areas. Just as she was delightedly browsing for anything useful, the main door suddenly swung open, and a group of people hurried in.
"They came so quickly," Jing Shu’s lips curved slightly upwards.
Their efficiency is quite high, indeed.
Unsurprisingly, Jing Shu and her companions were immediately uncuffed and invited to the current office. On the table were hot milk and boiled eggs, tokens of solicitude. Leaders personally handed these to them, creating a picture of perfect harmony.
"You’ve been terribly wronged! It’s our negligence that caused you such distress. Rest assured, we will severely punish those involved!"
CLICK, CLICK. The sound of cameras followed.
Jing Shu saw a familiar face.
Isn’t that the female reporter who interviewed me yesterday?
It had to be said, with attention from the higher-ups, things were handled with true efficiency. In just ten minutes, the forcibly occupied house was cleaned up. The squatters were cleared out, additional household supplies were brought in, and the entire house was thoroughly cleaned, making it tidy and beautiful.
Not only that, but the Distribution Management Director involved had also been "kindly apprehended" by the "helpful citizen Mr. Jing" and brought to the office. The police officer who had accepted bribes was dismissed as well.
Half an hour later, Jing Shu once again posted a new video on her social media. It documented a heartwarming scene of police and citizens working together to combat criminals, culminating in a joyous resolution for all.
"Thank you, Wu City Government, and thank you to the leaders for your concern, which allowed this issue to be perfectly resolved! Thanks, everyone, for your attention to Shi Jiujiu!"
From start to finish, Jing Shu did not appear on camera again.
But Shi Jiujiu knew she was the one masterminding this event and stirring up public opinion, not him. His admiration for Jing Shu reached new heights, and a small seed sprouted in his heart.
What if I could work with such a powerhouse in the future and help her guide public opinion?
Meanwhile, Captain Hu, the new broom ready to sweep clean with three bold initiatives in his new role, was suddenly informed, "Your promotion plan has been canceled. You will maintain your current position."
What the—??? What happened? I just finished writing the plan for my three initiatives!
As for Li Yuetian, who had been suspended, he was informed, "For this incident, your annual bonus will be withheld, but your position will be reinstated."
What the—??? What’s going on?
「」
Zhou Bapi had been staring at these two potted plants for two solid hours. He even licked the soil. "Strange, there’s nothing unusual. How is it possible? How can astragalus possibly grow in a pot under these conditions?"
"Uncle, when are you going to livestream yourself eating shit?" Su Malie asked, taking a small bite of a strawberry, not quite satisfied with its taste.
"You child! Such a momentous occasion definitely requires your other uncles to be present," Zhou Bapi coughed.
It’s all my fault for shooting my mouth off earlier. Now I’m being so blatantly humiliated.
"Then I’ll call everyone tomorrow to watch your livestream of eating shit, okay? They’ll definitely have time," Su Malie said excitedly.
"Oh, Jing Shu’s here! Look, Jing Shu has arrived! What took you so long? Where have you been? You kept me waiting!" Zhou Bapi finally managed to change the subject, rushing enthusiastically towards Jing Shu.
"You might not believe this, but I was just arrested. Hold on, who are you?"

chapters.title: Chapter 199: The Medicinal Materials Association of Seven People
chapters.content:
Chapter 199: The Medicinal Materials Association of Seven People
Jing Shu initially thought it was an old acquaintance, since the person had greeted her so warmly. She instinctively responded, but after speaking, realized she didn’t know him at all.
Zhou Bapi enthusiastically welcomed Jing Shu, his face creasing into a chrysanthemum of smiles as he closely examined her as if discovering treasure.
If Su Malie hadn’t been present, Jing Shu would have thrown a punch long ago.
"Oh, oh, look at me forgetting to introduce myself. My surname is Zhou, just call me Pharmacist Zhou..."
Su Malie burst out laughing. "Pharmacist indeed! He’s the same Zhou Bapi who didn’t believe you could grow potted astragalus and said he would livestream himself eating dung if you succeeded."
"Nonsense! My name is Zhou Baqi, Zhou Baqi! You better not call me Zhou Bapi anymore." Zhou Bapi felt he had to make a good first impression, but there went Su Malie, bringing up what should be left unmentioned!
Then it clicked for Jing Shu.
So it’s him,
she thought. She had wondered why she hadn’t seen him at the gathering today.
Zhou Baqi? Or Zhou Bapi?
Zhou Bapi, feeling he couldn’t lose face, then grandly introduced himself, "Young lady, this astragalus you’ve grown is fantastic! I am Zhou Baqi, vice president of both the Huaxia Herbal Medicine Association and the Wu City Herbal Medicine Association."
Zhou Bapi thought this title would surely impress Jing Shu, given that anything association-related sounded very prestigious.
Su Malie, laughing so hard he couldn’t straighten up, said, "If an ’association’ with only seven members and three vice presidents still counts as one, then I really have nothing more to say."
Su Malie instantly transformed into the little prince of party-pooping.
Jing Shu was bewildered.
It feels like I’ve walked into a trap,
she thought.
In my past life, the Medicinal Materials Association seemed like a very prestigious entity. So why are there only seven people now? Wu City has quite a few renowned medicinal herbs. Could it be the legendary ’gather seven people to summon a dragon ball’ situation?
Seeing Jing Shu’s skeptical look, Zhou Bapi coughed. "Ahem, Su Malie is only talking about the official membership of seven people. There are many others who want to join but can’t. Jing Shu, I came here to ask if you really grew that astragalus and honeysuckle after the apocalypse?"
Jing Shu nodded. "Yes."
Zhou Bapi’s hands trembled from excitement as he rubbed them together. "Oh, that’s wonderful, Jing Shu! I wonder if you’re interested in joining our Medicinal Materials Association?"
Jing Shu did have intentions of joining the Medicinal Materials Association. Although she didn’t know much about traditional medicine, she did know about farming. Yet, Su Malie’s words made her feel that this association seemed somewhat underwhelming.
Seeing Jing Shu hesitating, Zhou Bapi became anxious. "Don’t worry! You’ll enter as an official member. We also have hundreds of non-official members. The government is planning to unify the regional medicinal materials soon and will expand the staff to include other cities."
"So how does one typically work? Are there any strict regulations?" Jing Shu was a child of hard knocks; she hadn’t even held a formal job before the apocalypse struck.
"It’s flexible. We’re very relaxed. As long as you can ensure some medicinal herbs survive each month, you can even grow them at home without any issue. As for benefits, they are definitely much better than those of other official civil servants.
"Those at the president level, like myself, handle technical problems—for instance, if medicinal herbs are affected by pests or other issues, we need to step in and solve them. For someone at your level, the main thing is to ensure the plants you’re responsible for don’t die. The government acknowledges we’re in an apocalypse, and cultivating medicinal herbs has become incredibly difficult.
"The old cultivation methods have all been scrapped, replaced by an extremely inefficient individual-based model. But there’s no helping it; the conditions of the apocalypse introduce so many other factors."
Zhou Bapi couldn’t stop sighing. "Thankfully, we in Wu City still have some reserves of medicinal herbs, but those are for saving lives. If we really run out, the survival rate will be even lower than in ancient times."
Indeed, colds and fevers had to be endured with sheer resilience. If you could withstand it, you lived. If not, you died. This didn’t even account for chronic illnesses in the elderly, such as heart disease and hypertension. Without long-term medication, these conditions were simply left to fate.
Zhou Bapi’s wrinkled old face cracked a smile. "How about this: tomorrow, I’ll take you to our Medicinal Materials Association to have a look first. Then you can decide."
Jing Shu emerged from her contemplation and nodded. "Alright."
If there’s nothing particularly disadvantageous, joining the Medicinal Materials Association might actually be a good thing. At least Mom, who cares so much about face, could boast to others, ’My daughter has an official position at the Medicinal Materials Association!’
"Alright then, it’s settled! I’ll stay overnight at Mary’s house tonight," Zhou Baqi declared.
Despite Su Malie’s many pleas for her to stay for dinner, Jing Shu still left for home, leaving only the potted plants behind.
Zhou Bapi said he was going to sleep with these two pots of herbs tonight and bring them to the Medicinal Materials Association in the morning for further study.
As for the exposure of the Spiritual Spring, Jing Shu wasn’t worried at all. Back then, Qian Duoduo, for his foolish son’s sake, had run so many tests on the ice cream and hadn’t detected anything. Therefore, she was even less afraid that Zhou Bapi could discover anything.
Experience had shown that the Spiritual Spring, when affecting these organisms, merely increased certain active molecules and enhanced their functionality. So, as long as the Spiritual Spring itself wasn’t directly tested, she had nothing to fear.
When Jing Shu got back to the villa, it was just in time for dinner. She wolfed down her meal while listening to Grandma Jing’s concerned inquiries about the afternoon’s events. Meanwhile, Wu You’ai, holding his returned phone, was half-heartedly watching comics and nonchalantly appeasing Grandma Jing.
Fortunately, her family didn’t follow the popular video platform and had no idea about the huge battle that had occurred there.
"Enough, Mom, it’s all over now. Look, they’re both fine. A reporter even interviewed me this afternoon," Mr. Jing couldn’t help but advise. He was known as the helpful citizen Mr. Jing, which sounded pretty impressive.
"Quick, look at the news! Africa has flooded! So many people died!"
Everyone’s gaze then shifted to the news.
"How tragic! Africa’s terrain is so high, yet even the great plains could flood! TSK TSK, it’s too sad. Those people didn’t even have time to get out of their underground shelters," Mrs. Jing said sorrowfully.
"Speaking of last year’s extreme heat, living in those dugouts ten or so meters deep was comfortable. My Hua Xia Hainan was supposed to learn from that too, but our Huaxia leaders wisely had us migrate," Mr. Jing said. "Our country really does have foresight."
"How many people must have died? It’s such a tragedy," Grandpa Jing sighed.
The waters that inundated Japan came directly from rising sea levels. Except for Mount Fuji, which wasn’t submerged, the rest of the country was overwhelmed. The waters were so vast that no one could be seen, and entire cities were submerged.
Furthermore, another dozen or so islands were submerged, completely disappearing from the maps.
As for Taiwan Island in Huaxia, with its high terrain, it too was half-submerged, although casualties were not extensive.
But none of these compared to Africa. Because of its high elevation, it wasn’t entirely flooded but was rather inundated, with floodwaters literally drowning many people.

chapters.title: Chapter 200: Move aside, let me dissect and take out the doll (requesting monthly tickets)
chapters.content:
Chapter 200: Move aside, let me dissect and take out the doll (requesting monthly tickets)
They could have evacuated earlier, but their blind confidence convinced them otherwise. After all, that region was the most water-scarce in the world; it seemed impossible that it could flood. Yet, just a few days later, it did.
If other places had disappeared quietly without causing much of a stir, Africa was definitely a disaster zone. Now that everyone had just settled down again, with nothing much to do all day, they constantly refreshed news feeds and social media.
Every day, reports detailed how much various places had flooded. However, casualties in Huaxia were not severe. Except for some people who drowned on the day the floodwaters arrived, other losses were relatively minor.
The government hadn’t tallied how many people had disappeared. However, according to high-level big data analysis, about 2,000,000 people had vanished across Huaxia on that day. This included tens of thousands from Wu City, among them those who had been unwilling to evacuate from high-rise buildings at night.
Considering Huaxia’s baseline of 20,000 deaths daily and a newborn every two seconds on average, its mortality rate in such a massive disaster was relatively low. Japan suffered a 95% mortality rate, Africa around 60%, and other regions approximately 20%.
Of course, the birth rate had also significantly decreased. Among the tens of thousands of residents in the Banana District, there were only a few dozen pregnant women—a hundredfold decrease compared to before the apocalypse. This was linked to malnutrition, reduced sexual activity, and anxieties about successfully giving birth during the apocalypse.
Speaking of which, Zhang Bingbing was also about to give birth. It was uncertain if she could deliver safely under these apocalyptic conditions. Although the apocalyptic government provided maximum support to pregnant women—and they could still go to the hospital a short while ago—the hospital was now flooded. It would take at least a week for it to recover. One could only hope Zhang Bingbing could hold out until then.
The floods had only been raging for a little over a week, yet most people had already transitioned from panic to numb acceptance. One had to marvel at human adaptability.
Half of the news coverage was dedicated to how dire the situation in Africa was and how outdated their policies were. It also mentioned that Huaxia had evacuated over 3,000 volunteers from various parts of the world.
"In the face of national disaster, we must first defend our homeland. Secondly, the country must also safeguard its volunteers. Until the end of the apocalypse, Huaxia will no longer dispatch volunteers. However, for the sake of Friend Countries, Huaxia is willing to donate a limited amount of food."
This profoundly demonstrated that the lives of the Huaxia people were paramount, a sentiment enthusiastically applauded by the citizens.
The latter half of the news reported on organized and orderly post-disaster reconstruction efforts across various regions. To Jing Shu’s surprise, there was a segment featuring various peculiar rescue incidents.
Among them, a Douyin video clip of the Shark Submarine rescuing a thousand people was included. Although it was only a short ten-second segment, it was enough to thrill Jing Shu’s entire family.
"Amazing! My daughter made it onto the news!"
"She really did make it onto the news!"
"Isn’t that our family’s Shark Submarine?"
The news had the entire family excited and laughing. Jing Shu also smiled happily.
This scene of the family gathered for a meal, living together in a warm, cozy villa, is truly wonderful.
Even in her classmate group chat on her phone, everyone was tagging Jing Shu, exclaiming how awesome she was.
But Jing Shu still told everyone, "You all need to keep this as secret as possible, otherwise, I’ll be in big trouble."
Still another day overflowing with troubles!
That evening, Jing Shu took out the hotpot ingredients from her space to make herself an extra meal. Initially, she only planned to eat some of her stockpiled food. But then she craved fresh vegetables, then some fish and shrimp, and finally, she yearned for grilled oysters and scallops with vermicelli.
Alright, I’ll just make everything then,
she decided.
Consider it a reward for my troubled heart today.
Jing Shu didn’t idle. While eating, she tended to the two snakes in her space and discovered they were often engaged in some... amorous activities, almost twenty-four hours a day. COUGH, COUGH.
She also modified the bulletproof vest, helmet, and gas mask she had taken from the warehouse earlier that day. Her current solution was to wipe off the original logos and sew another layer of material over them.
By the time Jing Shu finished tending to the Domestic Poultry, fish, and shrimp in her space, and had inspected the condition of her fields, it was already 2:00 a.m.
Can I finally get a good night’s sleep tonight?
Jing Shu thought blissfully.
...As if!
Ugh, Jing Shu didn’t know what sins she had committed in a past life. She just wanted a good, undisturbed night’s sleep! Was that really so difficult?
At 4:00 a.m., Wu You’ai pushed the door open and came in. Just as Wu You’ai hesitated, wondering whether to wake Jing Shu, Jing Shu’s murderous eyes were already fixed on her.
Wu You’ai acquired: Death Glare x1.
Due to habits from her past life, Jing Shu would awaken at the slightest sound. This was even more true in this life after drinking the Spiritual Spring water; her hearing had become incredibly sharp.
She had heard someone approaching the door. Just as she was inwardly screaming,
Don’t open it! Don’t come looking for me!
Wu You’ai pushed the door open.
"Speak," Jing Shu said, sporting dark circles under her eyes.
Damn it, I only got two hours of sleep!
"Zhang Bingbing’s water broke! It looks like she’s about to give birth! What do we do? There’s no Doctor around. And hey, why does your room smell so strongly of hotpot?" Wu You’ai was at a loss. Unbeknownst to her when it started, Jing Shu had become the pillar of their household; whenever something came up, they sought her out, confident she could handle it.
But childbirth... Jing Shu was truly inexperienced in that area.
It was only a few hours ago that I was thinking about Zhang Bingbing’s delivery, and I didn’t expect her to go into labor so soon!
"That’s just you craving hotpot; we’ll have it tomorrow. We need to boil water, right? Get scissors?"
"Okay! Deep breath, exhale... Deep breath, exhale... That’s how it goes, right? I heard the cervix has to dilate one finger-width at a time, and she can only give birth after it’s ten finger-widths open?"
As Jing Shu carefully dressed, she said, "She probably won’t give birth for another day or two. Let’s go check on the situation first. If things look bad, I’ll find someone. After all, this will be the first baby born in our Banana District since the apocalypse began."
Jing Shu and Wu You’ai, wearing heavy clothes, left the house, taking scissors with them. On the way, they discussed how to handle the delivery and actively researched the topic.
They wouldn’t have known if they hadn’t looked, but one look shocked them.
Giving birth is terrifying!
"If she can’t deliver, we’d have to... make an incision there? HISS! That’s horrifying!"
"Remember in ’The Walking Dead,’ when the main character’s wife gave birth? She’d been bitten by a zombie, so they had to cut the baby out directly. If the mother can’t be saved, should we do that too?" Wu You’ai’s imagination ran wild.
"A C-section, you mean? Zhang Bingbing’s situation isn’t that dire. We’ll give her some anesthesia and then take the baby out."
"Good idea! Everyone, make way, let me handle the dissection and baby extraction! Oh, right, should we gather some experienced mothers? We’re both just young, unmarried women, after all... COUGH, COUGH."
Wu You’ai always found it a bit strange, but the moment dissection was mentioned, especially extracting a baby, her interest piqued. "I heard that for every new baby, the pregnant woman receives 100 Virtual Coins, and the administrator gets 10 Virtual Coins. Those 10 Virtual Coins can be my surgery fee. What do you think?"

chapters.title: Chapter 201: Drip — Employment Successful (Request for Monthly Ticket)
chapters.content:
Chapter 201: Drip — Employment Successful (Request for Monthly Ticket)
"Do you even know whether to cut horizontally or vertically? There are seven layers of fat, and you have to cut through each layer. Plus, there are cosmetic needles. Do you even know how to stitch?" Jing Shu said disdainfully.
"I have to learn sometime. I might end up being the Midwife of this area. If natural birth doesn’t work, I’ll just slice open the belly and take the baby out. Just thinking about it is thrilling. I really regret not studying medicine and hanging out with formaldehyde-soaked cadavers instead of some crappy agriculture. Now I’m stuck with a biology tutor. Ah, such is fate."
"How about this: you handle the cutting, and I’ll handle the stitching? Look at this stitching technique—once you pull this thread, you can’t even see it; it’s all tucked under the skin."
Jing Shu’s eyes lit up. In the coming years, besides the bodies mangled by earthquakes, there would also be those crushed by debris. Her stitching skills would be in great demand. "Dear, I suggest using cosmetic needles. There will be no scars once it’s stitched up."
"Alright, it’s decided then."
The two excitedly discussed how to perform the dissection and stitching all the way. Both were eager to practice on Zhang Bingbing, especially since Jing Shu had the Spiritual Spring and anesthetics, so no one would die.
"If she can’t deliver naturally, we’ll just have to cut her open," Jing Shu said.
It was unclear if it was the lethal impact of Jing Shu’s words, or if the psychologically disturbed Zhang Bingbing had overheard them and felt their power, or perhaps if Zhang Bingbing’s baby sensed the palpable malice from Jing Shu and Wu You’ai.
In any case, by the time Jing Shu and Wu You’ai arrived at Zhang Bingbing’s place, before they could even ask about the situation, or Wu You’ai had the chance to say, "Take a deep breath, inhale and exhale," Jing Shu had already seen a little head poking out from between Zhang Bingbing’s spread legs, as if to say: "No need for you, I’m coming out by myself!"
"Push, push hard!" Wu You’ai rushed forward, shouting to help with the final stages of delivery, at least to prove she had assisted in childbirth before.
Then, with a swift tug, Zhang Bingbing’s husband, holding the baby by its head, pulled out the entire body.
"WAH, WAH!" The loud cries of the baby resounded, not even needing a slap on its sole.
Jing Shu: "???"
Wu You’ai: "???"
"That’s it? It’s born? Just like that?"
"It seems so, yes?"
"It’s a boy!"
"I don’t even know if it’s yours or... mine." The old man looked a bit melancholy. If the baby was his, it would be his son’s younger brother. If it was his son’s, then this would be his grandson.
"Dad, let’s just think of it as our son."
The utterly bizarre dialogue made Wu You’ai decide to send these two for labor reform after the baby’s first-month celebration. Without the child as a point of contention, she figured, such talk would cease.
Jing Shu raised the scissors. She wasn’t here to deliver the baby; she was here to pass the scissors and cut the umbilical cord.
No matter what, Jing Shu could now confidently tell people, "I’ve assisted in a birth and cut an umbilical cord before."
Jing Shu calculated the time. It took less than twenty minutes to deliver the baby. This made her wonder if all those terrifying stories online were just exaggerations meant to scare her.
However, for some people, childbirth is a life-or-death struggle, while others might give birth while riding a motorcycle, or even on the toilet... In short, anything can happen; it’s all up to fate.
"So ugly."
"Babies always look this ugly when they are born."
"Alright then."
As the first child born in the Banana District, naming him was an important matter. Zhang Bingbing’s main husband and secondary husband also recognized Wu You’ai’s authority. "You are the administrator of our district; you come up with a name for the child."
Wu You’ai looked at Jing Shu. "How about you name him, and I’ll enter it into the central database?"
Jing Shu pondered for a moment. "Let’s give him the last name Zhang and call him Zhang Dada. I hope he can grow up safely in this apocalypse."
"Having the last name Zhang is good, taking after his mother. Zhang Dada is easy to remember."
"Let’s settle on Zhang Dada then."
Wu You’ai rolled her eyes.
She’d thought Jing Shu would come up with a more meaningful name.
"Alright, we’ll call him Zhang Dada then."
Wu You’ai put out a call for maternity and infant supplies in the group chat. The user ’I have a baby’ sent over some things her own little one no longer needed, which helped ease Zhang Bingbing’s immediate difficulties. By the time Jing Shu finished dealing with this matter, it was six in the morning.
Jing Shu wanted to go back to catch up on some sleep, but Zhou Bapi was already waiting at the door with his Alpha, flashing his big yellow teeth with a smile. "Let’s head out early; it’s a long drive."
Jing Shu’s teeth clenched.
Alright, I’ll definitely make sure to get a good sleep tonight, then,
she thought.
I thought Zhou Bapi was just being polite when he said it was a long drive,
Jing Shu mused,
but I didn’t expect it to actually be this far!
The mountain range in Wu City ran horizontally. After crossing one mountain after another, they finally arrived. Fortunately, the terrain here was high; otherwise, the car wouldn’t have made it. Based on the route, Jing Shu estimated the journey was about twenty kilometers.
Because the water was knee-deep in places and they had to drive slowly in the dark, it took them over an hour to reach their destination.
"This place used to be for growing snow lotuses," Zhou Bapi explained. "That entire area was our land, where we typically planted common varieties. Two months before the apocalypse, we managed to force-grow one last batch. After that, we switched to greenhouse cultivation. But with this current freak weather, nothing really grows anymore."
"This is Wu City’s old pharmaceutical factory, over twenty years old, and it’s fully equipped inside. That area is for refining medications. Oh, and there’s also a special processing facility for traditional Chinese medicine."
"Look, there’s a warehouse over there. Previously, all medicinal materials transported from Wu City to other provincial cities, or shipped here from elsewhere, had to pass through it. But it’s long been emptied; the government secretly moved everything."
"This area has already transformed into a self-sufficient township."
"Before the apocalypse, tens of thousands of people lived here. After work stopped, more than half were dispersed. Then, last year, after the water shortage, people scattered in all directions, leaving only us. We have to keep planting, even if nothing grows. If there’s no food, we can find other things to eat, but we can’t survive being sick without medicine."
Jing Shu deeply empathized.
Yet, the few medicinal herbs that can be grown are only enough for a small number of people,
she thought.
And among those, only the ones with power or ability will get them. Such is the harsh reality of the apocalypse.
Zhou Bapi parked the car at a newly built, rather tall building. Though it only had three floors, each floor was about five meters high, making it look very imposing.
Zhou Bapi proudly declared, "This was built by the government for the Provincial City’s Medicinal Materials Association before the apocalypse. It’s packed with high-tech equipment; it’s a building that can simulate weather systems. The only downside is its high energy consumption, so there’s only one in each provincial city, just twenty-six in the entire country."
Jing Shu nodded.
Indeed, very impressive,
she thought.
"Alright, you need to press your handprint here to enter," Zhou Bapi said, pointing at the fingerprint scanner by the door.
"BEEP BEEP. Personal data: Jing Shu... Entry successful. Linking to central database... Please provide iris scan."
Something feels a bit off,
Jing Shu thought, but she complied and scanned her iris.
"BEEP—Employment successful."
"There," Zhou Bapi chuckled. "From now on, you are a member of the Wu City Herbal Medicine Association!"
Jing Shu: "???"

chapters.title: Chapter 202: Vice President of the Medicinal Materials Association, I’ve Reserved This (Seeking Monthly Tickets)
chapters.content:
Chapter 202: Vice President of the Medicinal Materials Association, I’ve Reserved This (Seeking Monthly Tickets)
You devious old rascal!
Jing Shu thought.
To think he’d resort to such methods just to get me to join sooner—as if I wouldn’t have joined on my own! Honestly.
Things were going unbelievably smoothly, but the smoother they went, the more uneasy Jing Shu felt.
My original intention in joining the Medicinal Materials Association was to leverage their influence, but why does it feel like I’m wearing a fox skin instead of a tiger’s?
Seeing that Jing Shu didn’t object, which he took as silent agreement, Zhou Bapi grinned, showing his Big Yellow Teeth. He was thrilled, feeling like he had found a treasure.
"Our President is in seclusion," Zhou Bapi began, introducing the people in the Medicinal Materials Association.
Jing Shu was puzzled.
What kind of person is the president, and why is he in seclusion? Is he reliable?
"Everyone else is rushing to the countryside to recruit people," Zhou Bapi continued. "They aim to consolidate all individuals here who can cultivate medicinal materials, and there will be a competition later."
Zhou Bapi led Jing Shu inside and began to explain, "Currently, we’re cultivating mainly the easier-to-grow plants. This area has half moon flower, planted last year for its heat-clearing and detoxifying properties. Since the weather hasn’t been warming up recently, we’re planning to harvest this last batch and then stop planting it. After all, it consumes too many resources."
"This area has some lilyturf, which is good for invigorating the spleen and stomach. It’s mainly planted because someone sponsored the energy required."
"Look at that patch of honeysuckle. Honeysuckle is a widely used medicinal herb. Unfortunately, it only grows leaves and doesn’t bloom, so it fails to meet medicinal standards."
"This is aloe vera. Many we planted last year died. Only the aloe, being drought-resistant, survived."
Jing Shu was speechless.
Damn it! I just spent 200 Virtual Coins on an aloe vera segment. If I’d known they had it here, I wouldn’t have bought it!
Zhou Bapi continued excitedly, "Even though we can simulate sunlight for photosynthesis here and adjust temperature and humidity with the ventilation system, slightly mimicking weather and climate, we still can’t replicate the four seasons. Some herbs need to be planted in spring and harvested in winter. Others should be planted in autumn. But now the seasons are completely chaotic. This leads to herbs that stop growing midway or, due to improper temperature and seasons, only flower without bearing fruit."
Jing Shu wholeheartedly agreed.
You definitely can’t plant something in summer and expect to harvest it in spring, can you? Plants grown out of sync with the seasonal cycle won’t thrive due to temperature and other factors. Planting them would be a waste. Even those hundreds, or thousands, of winter varieties were developed through years of optimization.
"So, how exactly did you manage to grow them?" Zhou Bapi asked. "How did you overcome the issues with weather and seasons?"
This was a puzzle Zhou Bapi couldn’t figure out. He had thought about it all night but couldn’t find a solution. Everyone used constant temperature, even simulating night and day temperatures and humidity, yet nothing worked!
Faced with such a profound philosophical question, Jing Shu, who actually knew nothing about the theory, pondered for a moment and said, "It’s a secret."
I really just planted them casually, and they grew! All I did was water them daily with spiritual spring water diluted a hundredfold. It was just that brutally simple.
Now, I genuinely feel that the Magic Cube Space is an incredibly powerful cheat. In this apocalypse where nobody else can grow anything, my Magic Cube Space combined with the Spiritual Spring can cultivate crops!
When she activated the Second Form and compared her wonderfully plump eggplants to the deformed ones growing in the ground here, an immense sense of happiness washed over her.
Unfortunately, the Spiritual Spring only produces a small amount each day. I can only ensure my own household has enough vegetables and fruits; I can’t save the whole country.
The medicinal herb cultivation base was quite large and featured many varieties. However, some hadn’t survived, and others were wilting.
Whenever people passed by and saw Zhou Bapi inspecting the work, they would respectfully greet him, "President Zhou." None of these workers were officially registered, but their daily wage of 4 Virtual Coins was still quite high.
"Hmm, how is that patch of Angelica dahurica doing?" Zhou Bapi inquired.
"Still the same, sigh."
"Alright, I’ll think of something else. You may go now." Zhou Bapi could only feel his authority in this place.
Zhou Bapi led the way with his hands behind his back. "So, what do you think? You’re now a junior horticulturist at the Medicinal Materials Association. If you can cultivate a new variety, you’ll be promoted one level. If you can successfully grow five varieties and solve three difficult problems, you can be nominated for vice president."
"Does my pot of astragalus count?" Jing Shu asked.
Zhou Bapi shook his head. "It has to be successfully grown here and be usable as medicine. If any plant brought from who-knows-where counted, we’d have far too many vice presidents."
"Work hard," he urged. "The vice president position grants access to advanced big data permissions and comes with considerable rights, including immunity. The police and government can’t touch us; only the Medicinal Materials Association can regulate us. That’s a very powerful privilege indeed! You mentioned yesterday that the young police officer arrested you. If you were a vice president, he wouldn’t be able to arrest you."
Jing Shu’s eyes narrowed.
Zhou Bapi is dangling a huge carrot in front of me, but I really want to bite. So, the Medicinal Materials Association is a rather special entity among all organizations, ranking above food and other societal foundations. In chaotic times, doctors are more valuable than antiques in peaceful times, and medicinal herbs are even more precious.
And those advanced big data permissions—that’s a level even higher than Director Mrs. Jing’s superior’s superior!
Mrs. Jing’s current direct superior is Minister Niu, who is at the ministerial level. Only those above that level have such permissions. From a military perspective, for Colonel Li Yuetian, his superior would need to be at least a Major General to hold such advanced permissions.
So, how could that not be impressive?
This means that although the Medicinal Materials Association has few members and fewer responsibilities, it holds a higher status. So, is the position of vice president equivalent to a Major General?
Most importantly, the path I’ve chosen offers excellent promotion prospects, and it’s in farming, which is my specialty! I especially like that the work is autonomous and performance is judged monthly. That’s what I like best.
However, an equivalent position doesn’t necessarily mean equivalent power. Judging by the powers currently displayed, Colonel Li Yuetian commands the military, which is far greater authority than Minister Niu, who manages agricultural cultivation, and vastly surpasses a figurehead like Vice President Zhou Bapi, who has a high rank but no real power. It’s like in ancient times: some officials with low ranks held substantial power and were formidable, while some with high ranks, like a mere noble title, had no real authority.
"But you need to hurry," Zhou Bapi added. "This year is the last time vice president positions will be open like this. Moreover, cultivators from all over the Provincial City will soon flock here, so the competition will be fierce. Opportunities like this are rare. Make sure you seize it."
Jing Shu finally nodded vigorously, like a chick pecking at rice.
That vice president position in the Medicinal Materials Association—it’s mine.
"Now, let me cultivate the first new variety: astragalus," she declared.
Although the trial field was only ten square meters, it had seven or eight layers of shelving. This scientific planting method indeed saved a lot of resources, which was precisely why the shelves were built so high.
"This is terrible! Terrible!" someone shouted suddenly. "A batch of gastrodia has numerous insect eggs on it! Someone must have irrigated them with unfiltered water, and now the gastrodia stems and leaves are about to be devoured!"

chapters.title: Chapter 203: Are the Newcomers Now So Arrogant? (Request for monthly ticket)
chapters.content:
Chapter 203: Are the Newcomers Now So Arrogant? (Request for monthly ticket)
Fortunately, when this medicinal material planting base was established, an ultrafiltration system was in place—a system not even present in livestock farms or agricultural plantations. Consequently, the agricultural departments that recently relied on rainwater for planting are suffering.
A few days ago, they were excited about growing fresh vegetables for the entire city, and the common people were all looking forward to the future.
All Huaxia people believed that water was no longer scarce and that they could finally grow crops again. However, since yesterday, Mrs. Jing started complaining about the abundance of insect eggs on the vegetables, and she’s been trying to find ways to remove them, though pests in plants are quite common.
She’ll probably come home from work today in tears, lamenting that all the methods she thought of were ineffective against the insect eggs.
Originally, everyone thought ordinary insecticides would solve the problem, but they were useless. The life force of the red earthworms was so tenacious it surpassed that of many other life forms; it’s worth noting they evolved from bacteria.
The medicinal plant base had, like a blind cat stumbling upon a dead mouse, gotten lucky. Because it had its own ultrafiltration system and used filtered water for irrigation, it hadn’t experienced any problems.
It was only in the past few days, after other places used ordinary water for irrigation and numerous red earthworm eggs appeared, that news slowly began to spread among the well-informed. However, the government didn’t pay sufficient attention... not until these insects proved impossible to eliminate did they finally start taking notice.
"What’s all the shouting about? Isn’t it normal to have insects? Let’s go take a look." Zhou Bapi, the Old Taoist, was present and wanted to demonstrate his capabilities to the newcomer, Jing Shu.
Jing Shu followed Zhou Bapi to the third floor, where the gastrodia was planted.
It was still a small experimental field, with only about five levels of shelves. The gastrodia plants in the field were covered from top to bottom with minuscule white insect eggs, so densely packed it was as if they were dressed in a layer of white.
At this rate, lively red earthworms will hatch as soon as today or tomorrow. How wonderful.
Seeing this, Zhou Bapi was both distressed and shocked. "How long have these insects been here? They definitely didn’t appear today! Who is responsible for this batch of gastrodia?"
"It’s... it’s Chairman Tie’s assistant, Xiao Xiao," a big man said, lowering his head.
"Everything was fine before I left on my business trip, and now it’s like this upon my return! You all are responsible," Xiao Xiao retorted, hands on her hips, rolling her eyes at the people before her.
"Wasn’t it because of the torrential rain that day? You said the gastrodia were drying out and couldn’t wait for the filtered water to reach the third floor, so you went out and collected rainwater for irrigation!" another woman with a baby face retorted.
"What does that have to do with rainwater?"
"The crops my Uncle planted only started getting these insect eggs after being watered with rainwater."
Seeing they were about to argue, Zhou Bapi intervened. "First, explain the situation. We’ll assign blame later."
The woman with the baby face said, "These densely packed things started appearing on this batch of gastrodia the day before yesterday. We... we were thinking of dealing with it ourselves..."
Zhou Bapi frowned, bent down, and examined the insect eggs closely.
Another young man said, "This is really strange. We’ve tried worm-killing medicine and all sorts of other methods, but nothing works. These eggs seem to be embedded within the stems and leaves and are difficult to remove. We even scraped some off with a blade, but there were still more inside."
"It’s like blackheads; you have to squeeze hard to get them out. And even if you do, there’s no telling if they’ll grow back. Anyway, my Uncle hasn’t solved this problem either," the girl with the baby face said, puffing her cheeks in agitation.
Zhou Bapi’s eyes lit up as he recalled that Su Malie’s house near the entrance had a salt pool. "Bring me a bowl of highly concentrated salt water!"
Jing Shu, standing to the side, shook her head.
Highly concentrated salt water is only effective against hatched red earthworms. It increases the moisture levels inside their bodies, causing them to curl up. But for the insect eggs... it’s completely ineffective. It might even serve as nutrients for them.
"President Zhou is truly impressive!" Xiao Xiao exclaimed excitedly. Relief washed over her; finally, there was hope. If the gastrodia died, she’d be in serious trouble. At the same time, she rolled her eyes at Jing Shu.
Who does this person think she is, constantly shaking her head, acting all high and mighty as if she knows everything? I can’t stand people like that.
Jing Shu glared back at Xiao Xiao.
This woman is so bizarre!
The highly concentrated salt water was quickly brought over. Zhou Bapi tested it on one plant first. After a few minutes, the insect eggs showed no change, still clinging to the stems and leaves. Zhou Bapi picked at them with his finger, but there was still no reaction.
"Add more salt!"
Zhou Bapi experimented several more times, but it was no use. Frowning, he took a sample of the rainwater; the red earthworms in it immediately curled into a ball. "It seems salt water is useless against these insect eggs."
Zhou Bapi was very disappointed.
The girl with the baby face said, "It’s useless. These are red earthworm eggs from the torrential rain. The ones on the crops at my Uncle’s place have all hatched. This is all Xiao Xiao’s responsibility!"
"If I’m held accountable, you won’t get away scot-free either! You’ve all been taking care of them these past few days!" Xiao Xiao shot back.
"Let’s try a few folk remedies," Zhou Bapi, who was experienced and knowledgeable, suggested, and he immediately began experimenting with them one by one.
Jing Shu watched, shaking her head.
It’s like watching someone try to solve 2x2 by testing 1, 2, 3, 5, and 6, but never 4. So frustrating! I thought someone as experienced as Zhou Bapi might find a solution. Should I remind him that conventional methods are useless for removing insect eggs?
Xiao Xiao had long been annoyed by Jing Shu’s aloof and superior attitude, so she couldn’t help but ask, "President Zhou, who is this person beside you...?"
She acts so high and mighty; could she be from some wealthy family?
"Oh, this is Jing Shu, the new horticulturist I invited. Today is her first day joining the association. She has an exceptional talent for cultivation," Zhou Bapi explained, unable to resist praising her.
The people around couldn’t help but gasp.
This person is so impressive! Leaping three ranks to become a full-fledged member right upon entry! You have to understand, in the entire Medicinal Materials Association of over a hundred people, there were only seven permanent staff members. Oh, now there are eight.
Upon hearing Jing Shu was a newcomer, Xiao Xiao rolled her eyes dramatically again.
"Are all newcomers so arrogant these days? Shaking your head disdainfully while your superior is speaking! When we first arrived, we all knew to keep our heads down and act humbly. As a newcomer, how can you be so brazen? President Zhou is kind and good-tempered, but you can’t just bully him like this."
Seeing that even Zhou Bapi was out of ideas, Xiao Xiao wanted to curry favor with him to lessen her own blame, or at least drag the others down with her.
Jing Shu rolled her eyes dramatically.
What, I can’t even shake my head now? They were clearly doing it wrong!
"So, newcomer," Xiao Xiao continued, "since you’re so disdainful, do you have a better idea? Don’t keep it to yourself. If you don’t have one, then just stay quietly to the side and learn with an open mind."
The girl with the baby face snorted coldly. "Xiao Xiao, that’s enough! Every time a newcomer arrives, you make them do this and that, always finding fault with their work just to show off your seniority, don’t you?"
"But in the end, I’m the one who got the permanent position, not you, Wang Danai!" Xiao Xiao retorted.
Wang Danai’s chubby face turned bright red with anger.
"Who says I don’t have a good solution?" Jing Shu finally spoke. "I’m just wondering if successfully treating this would count as an achievement towards a vice president nomination."

chapters.title: Chapter 204: The Method of Using Poison Against Poison
chapters.content:
Chapter 204: The Method of Using Poison Against Poison
"Nominated for Deputy President? Is that what they meant by choosing another Deputy President from the official staff?"
"Seems like there are others from different cities as well. So many people competing for one position; it’s definitely tough."
Zhou Bapi panted, "I’m out of options now. As long as you can cure them, you’re definitely in the running. And from now on, you’ll be in charge of the gastrodia. It’ll be as if you were the one who cultivated them."
"Why? Why should that be? I’ve worked so hard for over half a year to cultivate these," Xiao Xiao said anxiously.
Zhou Bapi shrugged. "Then you can only watch these gastrodia die, or you can go to your Chairman Tie for a solution. Anyway, it’s certain now that these are red earthworm eggs on them, and it’s directly related to your use of heavy rainwater for irrigation last time. You’ll be held fully responsible."
Xiao Xiao looked incredulously at Zhou Bapi, then stubbornly turned to Jing Shu after a long moment. "Go on then, cure them! Cure them! Since no one else has a solution, and you’re so capable, let’s see how you’re going to resolve this. With so many gastrodia, let’s see if you can save them all!"
Xiao Xiao’s heart was truly in a knot. She hoped Jing Shu would be helpless, yet she also hoped there would be a solution so her own responsibility wouldn’t be pursued. But then again, she was reluctant to give up the gastrodia.
Jing Shu’s lips curved slightly upward. "Only those without ability lecture newcomers like an elder. Watch and learn."
Actually, the method was quite simple, derived from the continuous experimentation of the Huaxia people. Moreover, it was not developed by experts but by an ordinary person.
Now was the time when the red earthworm egg incident was escalating. A few days ago, All China had started mass planting. However, in the following days, they would realize that even with meticulous care—eight hours of simulated light, twenty-four-hour temperature control, an abundant water supply, and so on—the plants were covered with white larval eggs, which looked quite frightening. Most importantly, the worm-killing medicine was completely ineffective.
The entire country was plunged into a frantic search for methods to eliminate the eggs. During this period, ideas bloomed like a hundred flowers, with some people even considering methods like filtering the water source.
Jing Shu did not want to make the method public because the ordinary person who discovered it would receive his deserved reward in the next two days. It was okay to use it in advance, but she didn’t want to take away someone else’s credit.
Therefore, Jing Shu was cautious this time and did not make the method widely known. Moreover, the method was not universally applicable, so it wasn’t widely adopted or promoted; it could only be considered a temporary fix.
There’s an old saying in Huaxia: "Where there is deadly poison, there must be an antidote." Similarly, there had to be a nemesis for the red earthworm eggs. Fighting poison with poison was the best way to deal with them.
When that person was interviewed about how he came up with the method, he said, "I thought at the time, ’Clearly, only about half of what’s in the heavy rainwater are red earthworms. So why does irrigating with that water cause so many of them to hatch?’"
"The experts had tried various methods, seemingly to no avail, but I felt that the red earthworm eggs must have been eaten by the red earthworms themselves."
After careful observation, research, and numerous experiments, that person discovered that adult red earthworms did not eat the eggs. However, the large, long, old red earthworms found in the rainwater, which had lost their reproductive ability, survived by eating these eggs. Especially when these old red earthworms were soaked in salt water, they would frantically feed on the eggs.
So, he spent half a day picking out several thousand of these old red earthworms from tens of thousands of other insects. He soaked them in salt water and then released them into the vegetable fields, where they would devour all the eggs from a large patch of crops. During the process, one must be careful not to pick any of the ordinary, reproductive adult red earthworms; otherwise... it would all be in vain.
So, this method is good for emergencies, but it’s not sustainable for regular use. This is because if you irrigate with the contaminated rainwater each time, dense clusters of eggs will appear. Then, every day, you would have to pick out the old worms, soak them in salt water, and scatter them in the vegetable fields. Most importantly, the vegetables couldn’t withstand such torment. This method was too time-consuming and labor-intensive to be practical for widespread use. Therefore, the government wanted to solve the problem of contaminated irrigation water at its source.
"Get me two large buckets, a net, and fill one of the buckets with pure salt water."
Soon, a bucket of filtered salt water was brought over. Jing Shu then took the other bucket and the net, donned a raincoat, and went out, saying, "Wait for me for a while."
This method might be time-consuming and laborious for others, but for Jing Shu, with the enhancement of the Magic Cube Space, it was simple. She only needed to place all the red earthworms from the collected rainwater into the space and use her consciousness to identify them. She only needed to select those over ten centimeters long that were solitary and not mating—these were the old red earthworms. What would take others at least seven or eight hours to sort, Jing Shu accomplished in exactly ten minutes, picking out almost an entire bucket of these old red earthworms.
While the people inside were extremely curious and grew impatient waiting, they came out to see what mischief Jing Shu was up to. They only saw her under the eaves, scooping up red earthworms from the collected rainwater, netful by netful, occasionally shaking the net as if she were sorting or selecting something specific. The laymen were just watching the commotion, and everyone assumed Jing Shu was merely scooping up red earthworms.
Tsk, just to scoop up some red earthworms and she takes this long. Is it really necessary?
Xiao Xiao grumbled internally with discontent.
"Okay, let’s go," Jing Shu said, carrying the bucket filled with the seemingly less lively red earthworms.
A slight smile touched her lips; she had set a little trap.
Once they reached the third floor, Jing Shu scattered the old worms into the salt water, where they immediately curled up together.
Everyone watched with wide eyes. Someone asked curiously, "What is this for? We already know how salt water affects red earthworms."
"Didn’t President Zhou use salt water to soak them before?"
Next, Jing Shu scooped out the half-bucket of curled-up red earthworms and sprinkled them, little by little, onto the gastrodia, scattering just a dozen or so in each spot. Soon, all five racks were covered with the curled worms.
The moment to witness the miracle had arrived!
These seemingly dead red earthworms voraciously began to feed, as if they had smelled the most exquisite delicacy in the world. The eggs on the gastrodia started disappearing at a rate visible to the naked eye. At this speed, it wouldn’t take even half an hour for them to devour all the eggs. This batch of old worms was destined not to live much longer; their lives would end once they had consumed all the eggs. They couldn’t be kept alive in water any longer.
Surprised gasps sounded from the crowd.
No one expected it to be this simple!
Zhou Bapi was extremely excited. "You’re truly brilliant! I knew I wasn’t wrong about you. How did you come up with this method?"
Jing Shu, occasionally sprinkling more salt water on the gastrodia to accelerate the worms’ consumption of the eggs, replied, "A friend of mine discovered this method through many experiments. It’s not as simple as it looks; there are other steps involved, so don’t try it rashly. He will disclose the detailed method in a few days."
"Of course, of course. Whoever invents something deserves the credit. Saving the gastrodia is a great achievement in itself."

chapters.title: Chapter 205: Surprise! Received an Exoskeleton Mech (Requesting Monthly Tickets)
chapters.content:
Chapter 205: Surprise! Received an Exoskeleton Mech (Requesting Monthly Tickets)
At that moment, Jing Shu saw that Zhou Bapi was even thinking about salt water; she herself was just two steps away from figuring it out, which was extremely frustrating. But now, things had settled down, and in the end, it was she who resolved the issue.
However... the result was also pleasing. Jing Shu clapped her hands and said, "So, does this mean the problem with gastrodia has been solved? Am I in charge of this batch of gastrodia now?"
Zhou Bapi gave a thumbs up. "Yes, I’ll put it in your record right now. Oh, and you can pick five assistants to help you out regularly."
Jing Shu then grandly gestured to invite the girl with baby fat. "King... Danai, right? Then please continue to help."
"Of course." The girl smiled slightly, revealing dimples.
Sneaking a glance at the girl’s substantial bust, Jing Shu fell into thought.
Could it be that one’s name influenced their appearance? People are always envious of what they don’t have.
It was at this moment that Jing Shu decided:
To plant one square meter of papaya and eat one every day. Whether it would enhance her bust was beside the point; the key was that papayas were delicious.
"She really does have some substance, arriving and solving the problems that President Zhou was troubled with."
"Just look at how she’s dressed, and you’ll know she’s no simple character. Haven’t you seen how courteous President Zhou is to her? Although President Zhou is a nice guy, when have you ever seen him treat someone like that?"
Upon hearing this, Xiao Xiao, who had been about to argue, suddenly lost her fire. Covering her face, she turned and ran away.
We can only wait for Chairman Tie to come back to see what this person’s all about.
The storm had finally passed. Jing Shu returned to her test field to start planting astragalus. She wasn’t at all worried about Xiao Xiao having any designs on her fields because, for better management of the medicinal herb cultivation, they were monitored 24 hours a day with no blind spots.
She had just finished planting when she got a call saying Yang Yang had returned and was waiting for her at the villa entrance.
Good heavens, these people said they were only going for one or two months, and look how long it took them to get back! More than two months had passed since the theft incident in the United States.
Jing Shu was hurriedly taken back to the villa by Zhou Bapi.
"I wouldn’t believe for a second that this person doesn’t have connections. Look, President Zhou is even personally seeing her off."
Regarding this new hire who made everyone look at her differently on her first day, everyone held a newfound respect for Jing Shu. Her situation even broke the existing record of someone attending work only once in more than ten days; it was rumored this was special treatment given by President Zhou.
「...」
Five bald men squatted under the large shelter of the villa, each taking small puffs from a single cigarette in turn. Meanwhile, Yang Yang, having securely wrapped her hair, placed her long boots on the edge of a pool and used a syringe to draw up water. "How about you guys make a bet on how long it will take for Jing Shu to arrive? Whoever guesses right gets to try a salt water injection?"
"Are you out of your mind? Who would make such a bet!"
As they were speaking, Jing Shu arrived by car. Zhou Bapi, rubbing his hands, revealed his Big Yellow Teeth. "Jing Shu, if you can spare the time, think of a way to save our Honeysuckle. If you can cure them, that batch of Honeysuckle will be yours."
Zhou Bapi had gone to great lengths to bring Jing Shu in and even promised such a big incentive because he knew she had the ability to grow such high-quality medicinal plants. He had a premonition that the Wu City Pharmaceutical Association might really have to rely on Jing Shu in the future.
"Alright, I’ll think of a way when I go there next time, but it’s not guaranteed to work," Jing Shu said modestly.
This made Zhou Bapi even more pleased. Despite what Jing Shu said, he knew that the Honeysuckle would now be saved. This girl acted as if she didn’t know anything, but she possessed real skill.
Zhou Bapi turned his head and went to look for Su Malie.
Jing Shu saw several big men at the door, all looking at her. Jing Shu also sized up Yang Yang and her group. Except for Yang Yang, who basically hadn’t changed, the others had altered quite a bit; one of them had lost an arm, and another now had a horrific scar on his face.
"Yo, young miss, you’ve been doing pretty well these past six months, huh? We all know about yesterday’s incident with you grabbing the room from Wang Dazhao. It wasn’t in vain that Wang Dazhao risked his life to get that thing for you," said Yang Yang teasingly.
Wang Dazhao lowered his head and said, "Jing Shu, that was like a rebirth for me. These are nothing. Besides, it was everyone’s way of showing gratitude for the special medicine you brought, that they brought this for you."
Jing Shu looked confused. "What exactly is it? Could it be something from the United States?"
Yang Yang waved her hand, and two men went to the back of the pickup truck, pulling out a heavy-looking object.
Yang Yang said, "If it weren’t for your special medicine, the one without a hand and the one with a chunk missing from his face would have long since died from wound infections. We wouldn’t have been able to complete our part of the mission at all. Later, when we saw this thing, I thought that out of all the people I know, you’re the only one strong enough to perfectly control it."
With that, he opened it. It was an awesome piece of Mecha equipment! Just like those fully-armed warriors in movies, it looked incredibly cool, didn’t it?
Jing Shu’s eyes lit up.
"This is an incomplete exoskeleton mech system, the latest product researched by the United States’ Lockheed Company. It cost 800,000, weighs 70 kilograms, and is equipped with a hydraulic booster device, a graphite-selenium casing, and tritium battery power."
"Whether in extreme cold or extreme heat, the sealed exoskeleton system has excellent temperature control capabilities, ensuring it maintains standard performance under any extreme conditions."
"Its bulletproof capability goes without saying, though it definitely can’t withstand missiles or nuclear bombs."
"The left side is equipped with a mechanical claw. It’s enormously powerful, and you can use it like an excavator."
"The right side is fitted with various machine gun mounts and heavy weapon brackets. However, we didn’t manage to retrieve the entire Mecha, so it lacks weapons. Therefore, you can only use it as protective equipment. But there’s one drawback," Yang Yang coughed forcefully.
Jing Shu’s eyes were already sparkling.
Having been killed in her previous life, she had a deep-seated lack of security. Seeing any useful item that could help her survive the apocalypse was irresistible, not to mention that wearing this would mean she no longer had to fear the extreme cold of the apocalypse.
This kind of equipment often appeared in science fiction movies. In Huaxia’s first epic science fiction film, "The Wandering Earth," the characters wore this type of power mech, though there were still some slight differences between the two.
"What’s the drawback?"
"The thing needs to be charged. Once fully charged, it can probably only be used for a few hours... You know, science hasn’t advanced to that level yet."
Jing Shu pondered for a moment.
That seemed acceptable. If the worst came to pass, in a life-threatening situation, she just needed to keep it charged in her space, ensuring it was always ready.
"No problem, I like this thing. It’s fine without weapons; it’s pretty good for defense. Thank you all."
Jing Shu felt she had gained another significant trump card. At the very least, if real danger arose, she could instantly don the suit, which was far more reliable than throwing huge rocks.
"Alright then, I’ll take them back first to make arrangements. My great-grandfather is celebrating his eighty-eighth birthday, and I’d like to invite you all for a meal. Come with Niu later, and we can discuss things properly."

chapters.title: Chapter 206: Suspended Director of Distribution Position (Part 1)
chapters.content:
Chapter 206: Suspended Director of Distribution Position (Part 1)
Yang Yang’s grandfather is celebrating his eighty-eighth birthday with a feast? To think they can still do this during the apocalypse means the Yang family must be quite something.
Wait, I should brew some wine!
Jing Shu suddenly thought.
Whether it’s red wine or white spirits, it would be excellent for gifts or for personal enjoyment. Especially during this extreme cold, a little drink each day would keep one wonderfully warm.
As Jing Shu was pondering whether to replant a batch of red table grapes or use rose-scented grapes next, Yang Yang added, "You don’t need to worry about Wang Dazhao. He’s performed very well. This time, I’m sure to apply for a first-class merit for him, and he’ll be officially instated as a Lieutenant in our Armed Police First Team. As for me, I’m about to be promoted from Lieutenant to Lieutenant Colonel."
Yang Yang was just in his twenties. With connections in his family and his own ability, he was rising through the ranks quite quickly, almost catching up with Li Yuetian!
"Alright, I won’t see you off then." Jing Shu, excited by the prospect, carelessly revealed her strength, effortlessly slinging the mecha onto her shoulder as she returned to the villa.
The rough-looking men behind her swallowed hard. A mecha that took two of them to carry, yet such a petite woman had hoisted it with one hand?
Wang Dazhao gazed at Jing Shu’s receding figure with a complex expression. "Why do you insist on concealing from her that the machine gun and heavy weaponry weren’t seized during the raid? I think it wouldn’t be bad to hand them over to her. Only Jing Shu can bring out the full potential of the mecha."
Yang Yang turned and got into the car. "We’ll give them to her when she can use them. Otherwise, it’s too conspicuous and will only cause her trouble. Ah, our biggest oversight this time was letting Zero escape back to Huaxia and catch the scent of these weapons. What do you think will happen?"
...
After returning home, Jing Shu wiped the mecha until it gleamed and talked about her first day joining the Medicinal Materials Association.
Mr. Jing smacked his lips and shook his head. Although it looked cool, it seemed rather useless.
"In ancient times, armor was hung on racks. I’ll make one for you to hang your mecha!"
"Sure, thank you, Grandpa. I’ll put it up in my bedroom when it’s done."
Having a grandfather who could craft anything felt incredibly good, especially during the apocalypse when there was no mass production and everything had to be handmade.
Although the family didn’t understand the use of something that seemed to belong in the movies, their curiosity wasn’t dampened in the slightest. Once Jing Shu suited up, it indeed felt marvelous.
With her strength augmented, she was like a one-person tank, with explosive combat power and great protective ability, which gave Jing Shu a great sense of security.
The more satisfied Jing Shu was with the mecha, the more she struggled with what gift to give Yang Yang’s grandfather. Something too cheap wouldn’t be fair to Yang Yang, considering his part in her acquiring the mecha, but something too lavish would feel like she was showing off or overstepping.
While Jing Shu was still contemplating the appropriate gift, Mrs. Jing returned home sighing heavily that day. Jing Shu knew without asking that it was because of the red earthworm eggs.
The day after the insect egg incident came to light, everyone finally took the matter seriously. If no method could eradicate the insects, it meant no crops could be grown.
"The higher-ups urgently called to halt all farming projects. They won’t allow us to plant anything until the insect egg matter is resolved.
"Then the other Agricultural Management Departments shifted to cultivating mushrooms, which aren’t affected by red earthworm eggs. Now, it’s estimated that the insects will hatch in three to four days.
"But our Development Zone’s Management Department is in charge of the government’s vegetables, and all the half-grown vegetables are now practically dead." Even her small white apricots lost their appeal as Mrs. Jing spoke. She continued worriedly, "If the leaders’ vegetable supply is cut off, the consequences will be dire!
"The government announced rewards by noon: anyone who can find a solution will be directly promoted to a regular employee, and regular employees will be promoted one level.
"Daughter, you’re full of clever ideas. Please help your mother think of something. If this batch of vegetables can’t be supplied, even Minister Niu will be implicated!"
Jing Shu thought for a moment and said, "Mom, I’ll go with you tomorrow. I have a friend who has a method. It was tested today at the Medicinal Materials Association and seemed somewhat effective."
"Ah, my daughter always has a way."
As expected, the news broadcast also began to cover this incident. Now the whole nation was searching for a solution. It was a critical matter concerning the people’s livelihood, and even the general public was deeply concerned. After all, if they could grow food, they wouldn’t have to eat red earthworms every day—they were thoroughly sick of them after more than a week.
Eventually, the Wu City Government managed to arrange accommodations for all the masses, with every nook and cranny of Banana District filled with people. The once-quiet district was now constantly filled with noise.
Through surveillance, Jing Shu could see people occasionally passing by the villa—some out of curiosity, some sizing it up. There were even those who defecated under the shed. After all, it was more comfortable to do so under shelter from the rain than while getting drenched, and who could tell in the pitch-dark weather?
After Jing Shu mentioned this, Mr. Jing, angry, took a stick and went out to drive the people away. That day, Grandpa Jing raised the fence higher.
Ever since Jing Shu had gotten rid of the distribution director the day before yesterday, the position had remained vacant. People from all three government districts wanted to place their own candidate in the role, leading to dissatisfaction from the other two districts.
In the end, everyone compromised and decided to use elections to determine who would take the position of distribution director for Banana District, with whoever received the most votes winning.
To appear ’fair,’ any citizen could apply, but the condition was that they must have at least three civil servant endorsements. It was ridiculous, just another gimmick.
It was the old trick of underhanded manipulation, all depending on which district government had more clout. The coming days in Banana District would likely be very lively as, for the sake of rallying support, they might tempt people with various types of food.
History changed again at this moment. In her past life, Jing Shu had no power, so nothing like this had happened; the distribution director had remained in place. This time, however, it was Jing Shu who had fought for this benefit for the public.
It didn’t matter who took that position, as long as they didn’t bother Jing Shu; otherwise, they’d be swiftly dealt with just the same.
But unexpectedly, Wang Qiqi had her eyes on the position. She came over at night with a cutter and various professional tools she had somehow gotten her hands on from an abandoned factory.
That left Jing Shu truly at a loss whether to laugh or cry.
"I know your family isn’t lacking for food, but these items won’t be produced anymore. Your grandfather, being a craftsman, could also use them in his work, so I brought them for you," Wang Qiqi said.
"You’ve thought this through, right? Even with my family’s endorsement, you’d just be eligible to apply. People from all three district governments are competing," Jing Shu said.
Wang Qiqi said earnestly, "Now’s the time to fish in troubled waters while they’re at each other’s throats. Seizing this opportunity is like a carp leaping over the dragon gate. Life is too tough right now. I must fight for this; otherwise, I won’t even have vegetables to eat every day.
"Moreover, for you, investing a little in me might turn into a big gain. At least, your influence in Banana District would increase."
"Alright, I can invest," Jing Shu replied.

chapters.title: Chapter 207: Beginning the Salvage (Second Update)
chapters.content:
Chapter 207: Beginning the Salvage (Second Update)
Wang Qiqi took away several recommendations from Jing Shu and began his arduous journey up the social ladder. Although Jing Shu thought it was unlikely for Wang Qiqi to rise to a high position given his lack of resources, Jing Shu could offer him aid when absolutely necessary.
After all, a trustworthy person as a distribution director was much better than others; furthermore, all evacuations and future disaster sheltering would rely heavily on the distribution process.
If Wang Qiqi did indeed become the director, their positions would relatively improve a lot in the future.
Thinking so, investing in Wang Qiqi seems like a good idea indeed.
The items Wang Qiqi brought, except for the steel cutting machine that was currently useful, were of no use, and he handed them all over to Mr. Jing.
Jing Shu planned to use the steel acquired from Su Malie during her downtime in the coming days to cut it into versatile weapons, suitable for both offense and defense.
The idea of launching large steel arrows instead of stones was indeed thrilling.
Meanwhile, in the old group chat, Wu You’ai also announced:
"@everyone, the government will start salvage operations tomorrow. Anyone can sign up, with free transportation, but renting a life jacket costs 1 Virtual Coin. The surface of Wu City is covered with various usable items, all of which can be exchanged for Virtual Coins. Hurry up and register; life jackets are limited in number. This is also a way for you to earn Virtual Coins; you definitely won’t lose out."
"What, we still have to pay? Can those who are good swimmers just go directly into the water?"
Wu You’ai replied, "You can, but we won’t be responsible for your life or death. Oh, and those who have swim rings at home can also bring them."
I have a baby posted, "0.5 Virtual Coins to rent out a swim ring? Who would want that?"
Wu You’ai added, "Also, the big data system has updated the list of all salvageable materials with their corresponding Virtual Coin values and other rewards. You can use this price list to guide your salvage efforts and select useful items. Don’t try to exchange garbage; that would just be embarrassing."
...
