Damn it, he hadn’t ordered anyone to blow up any gas canisters from start to finish!
Just as he was about to speak, his phone rang—it was Jing Shu’s mobile number!
A choked voice came from the other end of the phone, "Dad, it’s me. I’m with Jing Shu, and we’re safe now. Where are you?"
Everyone collectively sighed in relief. It was good that their little one was safe!
Su Xiangnan felt his old heart soften. "It’s good that you’re safe. Where are you? Where are Ah Gou and the other bodyguards? I’ll send someone to pick you up right away. I’m currently at Old Qian’s guest villa."
Ah Gou might very well be a traitor!
"Uncle Gou and the bodyguards are dead," she sobbed. "Jing Shu said the people who kidnapped me probably wanted to provoke you all into destroying each other, so you mustn’t trust the bad guys! You’ve fallen into their trap! Where am I? I don’t know where this is either. After coming up from the tunnel, we arrived at a place that looks like a castle."
"Alright, keep your phone on. I’ll have your location traced. Don’t worry, I won’t get into any conflict with Old Ghost. Stay put; I’m coming to get you right away."
Although Su Xiangnan had many suspicions, nothing was more important to him now than his daughter’s safety. "Quickly, trace Jing Shu’s phone location!"
Qian Duoduo was full of questions. How could Su Xiangnan’s daughter be in the castle? Didn’t they say she escaped through the underground passage? How did she end up in the castle after coming out of the passage? Qian Duoduo felt like he was missing something crucial. Could this be an Immortal Jump?
"Since your daughter is safe now, let’s stop the bombing outside for a bit. Energy is so scarce these days, and both you and I still need to contribute a lot of it to power the Artificial Sun," Qian Duoduo said, his voice tinged with impatience.
Su Xiangnan hurriedly explained, "I really didn’t order the bombing outside, including the first explosion. You heard it too. Someone deliberately kidnapped my daughter to frame you. Now that my daughter has escaped, there’s no need for us to bomb you anymore. I’m afraid someone is intentionally trying to make us destroy each other so they can reap the benefits."
This time it was Qian Duoduo’s turn to sneer. He gestured and said, "Bafu, tell Brother Su what you’ve found out."
"Mr. Su, we’ve just received a report. Over twenty of the men you brought with you emerged from the underground passage, ignited a gas canister in one location, and then fled. They’ve already destroyed a breeding facility, a farm, and three houses. We’ve dispatched security to apprehend these individuals."
"This is a frame-up! It’s definitely a frame-up! Old Ghost, I need to hurry and pick up my daughter. Once I have her, we can discuss anything." Since Su Xiangnan now knew this was a setup, he naturally wouldn’t provoke Qian Duoduo further and significantly softened his tone.
"Alright, let’s go then. We’ll go together and see what tricks you’re up to." Qian Duoduo decided to go along primarily because the incident was happening at the castle. The rest of West Mountain could be blown up without major consequence, but the castle absolutely could not!
He was also wary of Su Xiangnan pulling some stunt; in their circles, Su Xiangnan was notorious for his scheming.
"Look, to be safe, how about I leave these gas canisters here?" Su Xiangnan suggested.
"Absolutely not! You have to take them with you. I’ll only feel at ease if they’re under my watch."
Qian Duoduo didn’t dare let Su Xiangnan leave so many gas canisters behind. What if Su Xiangnan’s men decided to blow this place up...
The large group of people headed towards the location indicated by Jing Shu’s phone. Along the way, they received good news: a government-dispatched unit had finally bypassed the blocked roads and arrived.
Qian Duoduo secretly wiped away a cold sweat. "Quick! Quickly arrange for them to accompany us to the castle to investigate."
Finally, some real support! With these people here, even if Su Xiangnan wanted to bomb his West Mountain, he’d have to think twice. Besides, with this military unit present, who would dare to make a move against him now?
Following the location from Jing Shu’s phone, they indeed arrived at Qian Duoduo’s castle.
"Since when did my own castle have an underground passage? Is it real or fake?" Qian Duoduo’s expression was grimly uncertain. He ordered Wu Fu to take men to protect the young masters and young mistresses, while simultaneously dispatching others to inspect the castle.
...
"You stay here and wait for your dad," Jing Shu said, handing Su Malie a new phone with a changed SIM card. She also gave her a piece of Compressed Biscuits to nibble on slowly.
"Then, where are you going? This really is Qian Duoduo’s home! What on earth do those people want?" Su Malie clutched Jing Shu’s clothes, refusing to let go. The thought of being left alone made her feel terribly insecure.
*Whimper*... It’s so scary!
"I need to go check again. There should be more than one passage here," Jing Shu said, as if recalling something.
"But when we came up, there was clearly only one! Let’s leave these things for the adults to handle. What can we do?"
Perhaps this passage is also part of Lin Yi’s plan,
Jing Shu thought, increasingly feeling that both she and Su Malie were being used as pawns.
Besides, if they really left it to Qian Duoduo and his men to handle, by the time they arrived, it would be too late.
A conjecture began to form in Jing Shu’s mind, rapidly taking hold.
Just as the two of them were nearing the exit, a loud RUMBLING echoed from outside, clearly audible even from within the underground passage. Jing Shu knew something outside was likely being bombed. Su Malie had even speculated at the time that it was probably her father losing his temper and about to blow up West Mountain. Su Malie, who had been struggling to walk, somehow found the strength to run. After all, a journey of over ten kilometers was arduous.
Of course, Jing Shu had added a little Spiritual Spring to the Compressed Biscuits she gave Su Malie; otherwise, Su Malie definitely wouldn’t have been able to run all that way.
"I’ll go check and be right back. If I don’t, we all might die. I suspect Lin Yi plans to blow up West Mountain," Jing Shu said, then turned and headed back down into the underground passage, leaving a tearful Su Malie to wait for her father.
Jing Shu hadn’t wanted to get involved in this mess, but... the recent explosions suddenly reminded her of a notorious declaration made a year ago by Zhetian, one that had caused a huge uproar: "Blow up West Mountain, blow up Qian Duoduo’s old mansion, and rob the tycoon Qian Duoduo!"
At the time, it had seemed like such a ludicrous statement to her. Qian Duoduo was an incredibly powerful figure; he had over 600 people on West Mountain dedicated solely to serving his family of four.

chapters.title: Chapter 267: Explosives
chapters.content:
Chapter 267: Explosives
How many people does Zhetian actually have? They want to blow up West Mountain and rob Qian Duoduo? I’m afraid they wouldn’t even make it through the front door before being shot to death.
Indeed, back then Zhetian didn’t go for West Mountain; instead, they bombed the oil base.
Then they immediately went to make trouble for Jing Shu’s house, even trying to blow up the villa, but Jing Shu stopped them and turned the tables in one fell swoop.
So, Jing Shu had quickly forgotten the joke about Zhetian wanting to blow up West Mountain and rob Qian Duoduo. But now, with Lin Yi’s appearance and the elaborate trap he had meticulously set for so long, Jing Shu was even more puzzled.
What exactly did he want to do?
After all, Lin Yi was none other than Zero, the illustrious leader of over a hundred forces in Huaxia.
So... if Zhetian’s key figure, Zero, was personally leading the charge to blast the wealthy Qian Duoduo’s territory, was Ling Qi, the leader of Wu City’s Zhetian, also there?
Therefore, when the rumbling started outside, Jing Shu became even more certain.
These people were really going to blow up the entire West Mountain!
As for why Jing Shu was so sure, it was because of the underground passageway’s existence.
When Jing Shu and Su Malie escaped to a junction in the underground passageway, Jing Shu saw clusters of marks and residue on the ground.
What were these things? They looked like they had been stored here for a long time and then transported away. So, where were they transported? Where could they possibly go?
When one of the main passageways led directly to Qian Duoduo’s largest, most outrageously luxurious castle, Jing Shu seemed to understand.
It had to be Qian Duoduo’s castle, right? They were going to blow up Qian Duoduo’s mansion!
Thinking back, it all made sense now.
The black residue must be explosives. They must have dug through the underground passage and used the ’elevator’ to transport them. The reason there were so many explosives, Jing Shu recalled, was that Lin Yi had brought back a lot from the United States, but they had never surfaced. So, this batch of explosives must have been stored in the underground passageway.
But this batch should have been brought back last year; the passage also looked like it had been built some time ago.
It’s just... with all conditions met, why didn’t Lin Yi just find the right moment to blow up the castle? Why go through such great lengths to drag Su Malie and the others into this? And what I can’t understand is, if Su Malie was just a pawn, trapping her should have been enough. Why deliberately let them come back? That’s the most puzzling part.
If they wanted to blow it up, just do it directly! Why all this scheming?
Jing Shu thought furiously. The idea that she might be blown sky-high any minute made her legs tremble.
I have to hurry and find those explosives! Otherwise, even if we run... with so many tons, they could level the entire West Mountain! This Lin Yi... he really plays big.
Here, Jing Shu had actually misunderstood Lin Yi. The original plan was to bomb West Mountain last year. However, when Lin Yi learned that Qian Duoduo had constructed a "turtle shell" air defense fortress capable of withstanding ton-level bombing, he abandoned that plan and decided to attack the oil base instead.
Jing Shu wasn’t alone in the underground passageway for long before she indeed found another passage. However, it was disguised with a fake wall covering made from invisible tiles. If Jing Shu hadn’t hammered at it, it would have remained undetected.
Everywhere else was solid and silent, but this one spot echoed with a hollow THUD THUD THUD.
But this passage door won’t open! It’s made of iron!
The thought that explosives might be right on the other side made Jing Shu abandon all caution. She took out a Hand Grenade she had previously acquired from Zhetian.
She knew her actions could very well cause the entire tunnel to collapse, but it didn’t matter; if it collapsed, she could still dig her way through.
Jing Shu was a bit nervous using a Hand Grenade for the first time. In the pitch-dark tunnel, she strictly followed its instructions: unscrewed the cap, poked through the moisture-proof paper, pulled out the pull ring, took a big step back with her right leg, puffed out her chest and held her head high, swiftly stamped her left foot on the ground, suddenly contracted her abdomen, cocked her wrist, and—threw! Then she hit the deck!
One, two, three, BOOM!
She heard a thunderous explosion, and the whole tunnel shook violently.
When the dust settled, Jing Shu shook the grime from her body and coughed a few times. In the pitch-black tunnel, she saw the doorway that had been blown open. To her surprise, it hadn’t collapsed!
Thank goodness for the luck Su Malie brings!
Wait...
Upon closer inspection, Jing Shu realized the workmanship here was completely different from the crudely dug tunnels she had seen before. Air-raid shelter materials had clearly been used!
This place is basically bomb-proof! So, the Hand Grenade I threw only blew the door away and scattered some dust.
Only then did Jing Shu feel she was truly entering Qian Duoduo’s domain.
She continued forward. Indeed, this place was a world apart! Jing Shu crouched, wiped a spot on the ground, and sniffed. It was unmistakably the pungent smell of gunpowder.
Following this tunnel, Jing Shu couldn’t help but feel that poverty truly limited one’s imagination. From that previous section onward, everything, from underground to above, was made from air-raid materials.
If I had to describe it, this is a gigantic air-raid shelter, a turtle shell made of blast walls several meters thick. This place has been fortified to the teeth by Qian Duoduo! I can almost see him building houses with gold.
No wonder Lin Yi’s bombing plan hadn’t been implemented. To actually blast such a professional-grade turtle shell, you’d probably need tens of tons of explosives just to make a dent. I think I understand Lin Yi’s reasoning now. If the external shell can’t be blasted, then why not secretly transport the explosives inside the house and detonate them there? So, although Lin Yi dug the tunnel a long time ago, he never had the opportunity. Only today did he finally manage to bring in the explosives. Does that mean Su Malie and I played a part in this?
Jing Shu quickened her pace. She saw Detonators!
Funnily enough, I’m really familiar with this stuff!
In the fifth year of the apocalypse, the great migration began. The Wu City Government led the Wu City People south. By then, the tectonic plates had shifted into an incredibly complex mess, and they encountered many treacherous terrains that needed to be blasted flat before they could continue—not just for vehicles, but for people too.
Without a second thought, Jing Shu scooped all the Detonators into her storage space.
Are you kidding? Better to get such dangerous things put away quickly!
Below the Detonators lay a thick pipe on the ground. Inside the pipe was a yellow paste, and this pipe led straight to whatever lay ahead!
No doubt about it, this is TNT explosive!
It was the cheapest, most widely used explosive in the world, usable for underwater demolition, and possessed great destructive force. Moreover, it was one of the most stable explosives, least prone to accidental detonation, and unaffected by heavy rain or submersion.
Even gunfire wouldn’t set it off, but it required a Detonator to be ignited.

chapters.title: Chapter 268: Suicide Bombing the Entire Venue
chapters.content:
Chapter 268: Suicide Bombing the Entire Venue
TNT melts at 81 degrees Celsius. Due to its non-flammable nature, it won’t explode if placed in a fire; instead, it will liquefy and can then be molded into various forms of explosives.
The key to an explosion isn’t burning but the rapid production of a large volume of gas. All explosives function by generating a significant amount of gas, much like an overinflated tire will burst.
It can be detonated using shockwave energy; just two Detonators are enough to set it off.
Jing Shu’s heart pounded wildly.
Damn, I’m lucky I found this early!
she thought.
Otherwise, these tons of explosives would have definitely gone off, and the whole mountaintop would’ve been flattened!
Jing Shu had even been responsible for detonations using Detonators back in the day.
Don’t ask how she knew; it was all for a mouthful of food. She had to take on any dangerous job, or she would starve.
Therefore, she was intimately aware of the danger and power of TNT explosives, having felt it profoundly. The sensation of a bomb, triggered by a Detonator she had set herself, exploding right by her ear... a single misstep could have been fatal.
That year, blowing up a small hillock only required a bundle of explosives a few arm-spans wide, set off by Detonators, guaranteed to level the mountain.
To put it more starkly, a five-story commercial building could be obliterated with just 800 kg of TNT, leaving no trace behind.
Jing Shu estimated the TNT explosives piled on the ground amounted to about two tons.
What a sin, such a terrible sin,
Jing Shu muttered as she walked, collecting all of it into her Magic Cube Space. She hadn’t even had a chance to examine her upgraded Magic Cube Space yet, and the first thing she’d acquired was a massive pile of explosives.
Jing Shu finally felt a sense of relief.
It should be safe now, right?
But who could have known? Just then, a RUMBLING sound started outside, and the entire structure began to tremble! This was no longer the gentle patter from before but a genuine ROAR. Based on Jing Shu’s two years of experience identifying sounds, this was a chain explosion!
This method achieved maximum explosive power with minimal explosives, typically used for large-area detonations. It started with the initial Detonators, one triggering the next, with explosives buried systematically throughout the area...
Damn it, there’s more!
Jing Shu clenched her teeth and bolted, not towards the outside, of course, but deeper into the massive air-raid shelter-like structure.
She was like a rat trapped in a cage being bombed now, wasn’t she?
She had known Lin Yi wouldn’t have planted explosives in just one spot! If this was all the explosives there were, it wouldn’t have justified Lin Yi mobilizing manpower to dig a tunnel over ten kilometers long.
So, as the explosions outside continued, one after another, Jing Shu knew with certainty:
There’s definitely more!
Her time was running out! She ran frantically. Sure enough, in an adjacent underground area resembling a sewer system, she found more TNT explosives. Jing Shu swept them all into her Magic Cube Space.
With each successive BOOM, Jing Shu’s heart grew colder.
How many tons of explosives has that bastard Lin Yi planted? He’s probably not just trying to demolish this place but aiming to raze the entire West Mountain to the ground, isn’t he?
And good heavens, just how vast is Qian Duoduo’s estate?!
As the RUMBLING intensified, Jing Shu knew the Detonators’ blasts were rapidly approaching her current location.
I have to be faster, even faster!
It was almost as if she could hear the distinct energy signature of the Detonators activating.
It’s over. Too late. The Detonator has already been activated! Run back!
Jing Shu had always cherished her own life. She sprinted back in a frenzy. These TNT explosives seemed to have been placed with meticulous calculation, each charge designed to obliterate a specific section.
So long as I run fast enough, the explosions can’t catch me!
BOOM!
BUZZING...
Jing Shu was caught by the shockwave and slammed violently against a wall. The tremendous sound instantly deafened her temporarily, a loud BUZZING filling her ears. Fortunately, it was only the tail end of the blast wave. Jing Shu coughed a few times, finding herself buried under rubble.
It seems... not only has my strength increased, but my resilience has improved a bit too?
she thought.
Although it’s very painful, and I’m probably bruised, there are no internal injuries or broken skin. Good. It looks like with the breakthrough in the Magic Cube Space, my body has also leveled up.
Just then, footsteps approached. Jing Shu quickly pressed herself against the pitch-black wall, remaining buried under the rubble, not daring to make a sound. In the darkness, she saw a woman in a tight, black bodysuit with her hair in a ponytail.
The woman shone her flashlight around, saw only debris, then started to walk back, speaking into a communicator, "Plan B has failed. Reason: loss of four segments of explosives. Suspect plan compromised, explosives stolen. Awaiting further instructions."
Jing Shu then heard a faint voice from the woman’s microphone, "Proceed with Plan C. Forcibly detonate the central explosives."
Although the woman’s face was expressionless, tears inexplicably streamed from her eyes. Yet, her voice remained devoid of emotion, like a puppet’s, "Understood, my boss."
Jing Shu frowned.
What’s going on? They’re still going to detonate the central explosives? That sounds incredibly serious.
Jing Shu released two snakes to follow the woman from ahead, while she herself, after shaking off the loose stones and debris, maintained a considerable distance as she trailed her.
After the Magic Cube Space upgrade, this ability had become truly formidable. The snakes acted as her eyes and Scouts, allowing for remote control without the risk of discovery.
Jing Shu followed the ponytailed woman out of the recently bombed underground passage. After tailing her for three minutes, the woman entered a room resembling a conference hall. Behind a large Mirror, there was actually a hidden compartment! Jing Shu felt a chill.
Qian Duoduo’s place is probably so vast, with so many rooms, that he wouldn’t even notice if ten or so square meters went missing, would he? True enough, who would notice if a mirror in a conference hall spanning four or five hundred meters in length was shifted forward enough to create a two-square-meter hidden space?
Inside this hidden compartment were display screens monitoring various key locations. Jing Shu wasn’t worried about being caught on camera; the darkness in the underground passages was so complete that even infrared cameras would likely fail to detect her.
But the crucial point was, there was an entire room filled with explosives! The amount in this single room was equivalent to the total volume Jing Shu had collected so far that day. If these were detonated, no matter how large Qian Duoduo’s house was, everyone inside would be blown sky-high! Besides, RUMBLING sounds from outside indicated the bombardment was clearly not over.
"I’ve reached the central control room. Awaiting instructions."
A cold voice came through her earpiece, "Detonate the primary Detonator."
"Yes, my boss."
The woman immediately began the detonation sequence.
Jing Shu sprinted desperately from behind, cursing herself for not staying closer.
Damn it, this woman is on a suicide mission!
She could never have imagined someone so obedient existing in the world—ordered to kill herself, and she showed no resistance?
Oh, wait, that’s not right, she cried earlier. Bah! Just crying isn’t resisting, is it?!
Jing Shu was cursing a blue streak internally. She no longer cared about exposing her spatial ability; if she were even a second slower, she’d be blown to kingdom come.

chapters.title: Chapter 269: The Hero Who Saved the Game is Injured
chapters.content:
Chapter 269: The Hero Who Saved the Game is Injured
Jing Shu kicked the door open with a CLANG. The detonator was already whirring at high speed; Jing Shu could even see electrical arcs SIZZLING on it!
BOOM!
Just at this critical moment, Jing Shu rushed in. "Store them!"
In an instant, Jing Shu had stored all the explosives in the room into her space. However, the detonator had already activated. In that thousandth of a second, a small amount of explosives hadn’t been collected, so they exploded with a loud BANG!
Jing Shu was blasted away by the shockwave for a second time. This impact was much more severe than the last. Her forehead was smashed open, and blood streamed out, making her look utterly disheveled.
The entire conference room was rocked by a loud BOOM, but thankfully, its force had been reduced a millionfold!
Jing Shu lay there for a while. She didn’t want to move, her whole body aching.
This day has been so damn thrilling! If there were any more explosives, I really wouldn’t know what to do.
Just then, the sound of a large troop’s footsteps came from outside. Jing Shu cursed inwardly.
Of all times, they had to come now! Not earlier, not later!
After thinking it over, Jing Shu reluctantly took out nearly four tons of explosives. She prepared to create the illusion of having cut the detonator wires, knowing full well that everyone outside was exceptionally sharp.
As someone quite familiar with TNT, Jing Shu knew how to stop explosives once the detonator was active. She just needed to ’cut the power’ to the remaining charges. This was easy to say but hard to do. In her previous life, she hadn’t dared to try it. This life, however, she used the more reliable method: her space.
Bright lights suddenly switched on, and Jing Shu shielded her eyes from the glare.
"There’s someone there, a living person!"
"Catch that person!"
"Wait, Captain Wang, this is someone I recognize! She must be the person Mr. Su and Mr. Qian have been looking for."
Lying on the ground, Jing Shu saw a pair of familiar military boots approaching her step by step. Looking up, she saw Yang Yang’s handsome yet serious face.
"Is that Jing Shu?"
Jing Shu’s ears were still ringing, and she could barely hear. "Mm," she managed.
Yang Yang ran over, his footsteps THUDDING rapidly. He helped Jing Shu up. "Are you badly hurt? Mr. Qian brought an old traditional Chinese doctor!"
Jing Shu shook her head. "Not too badly, but I should still get it bandaged."
Captain Wang furrowed his brow. "Yang Yang, what happened here?"
"Captain Wang, this is Jing Shu, a classmate who was with Su Malie during this incident. She protected Su Malie and brought her all the way here. She’s the one Mr. Su was asking about just now. Originally, she was with Su Malie, but she said she suspected Lin Yi planned to blow up the castle, so she went off alone to find clues."
Captain Wang’s expression then eased considerably. "Alright then, get her to a doctor quickly to get bandaged up. The rest of you, check the rubble."
Jing Shu pointed in a direction. "There was a woman inside who used a detonator to set off the TNT explosives. I only managed to disable most of them before she detonated a small portion. Check if she’s still alive."
Captain Wang’s face showed surprise as he pointed to the nearby explosives. "You cut the wires while the detonator was active?"
Jing Shu nodded. "I knew it was possible but had never done it before. I figured if I didn’t act, we’d all die."
"Great! Great! Great job! You really saved all of our lives! We started defusing explosives as soon as we arrived but only managed to clear two decoys. I never expected the main charges to be here. Jing Shu, you’ve made a significant contribution!"
I’ve disarmed several big ones like this. Too bad I can’t take credit for it publicly,
Jing Shu thought.
Her heart ached.
Four tons of TNT! Explosives are so precious in the apocalypse and have so many uses! Oh well, I shouldn’t be too greedy. I still have 14 tons of TNT left, which should be enough for the apocalypse. Am I now truly the queen of munitions?
"Report! The woman’s upper body was obliterated; only her lower half remains."
Captain Wang waved his hand. "Take what’s left back for DNA testing to confirm her identity."
Jing Shu was helped back to the castle’s main hall. Many people were gathered there, yet no one dared to speak loudly. The atmosphere was chillingly tense. Outside, the bombing had gradually ceased. Jing Shu guessed that the entirety of West Mountain had probably been blown to bits by now.
The rumor that West Mountain’s richest man had an entire mountain blown up will probably start spreading like wildfire from today, won’t it?
At this moment, Jing Shu even felt a flicker of curiosity to examine the richest man’s so-called castle. Previously, she had only ever passed by and glanced at it from a distance, thinking it was an impressively grand fortress. Now, her first impression upon entering was its sheer enormity. It was as vast as a palace, with a 10-meter-high ceiling unsupported by pillars. The spacious hall exuded an understated yet luxurious feel.
Though not ostentatiously lavish, every item was priceless.
It’s good to have money. It’s even better to have money in the apocalypse.
Having money is satisfying for a moment; always having money is always satisfying.
"Jing Shu? Jing Shu, how are you? Wuwu, don’t scare me!" Su Malie cried, running over anxiously.
Jing Shu attracted everyone’s attention. When everyone else had just sighed in relief at finding Su Malie, she was the one who had claimed someone was going to blow up West Mountain. Then she went off alone to look for the bomb. Subsequently, West Mountain was indeed bombed. What was worse, even a corner of the castle had been destroyed.
Qian Duoduo’s originally ashen face relaxed slightly. "Quick, get her wounds bandaged," he ordered, then asked, "What’s the situation?" Qian Duoduo had claimed the castle was the safest place, but it wasn’t long before he was proven spectacularly wrong—a large amount of explosives had been planted right inside the castle!
Only when a specialized team came in to inspect did they discover a host of problems.
Qian Duoduo then learned that underground tunnels had been dug beneath the steel fortress he had spent a fortune on. However, due to the material used, the perpetrators couldn’t break through to the entrance.
Therefore, if he hadn’t ordered all the steel fortress’s defenses to be opened today, which allowed someone to exploit a vulnerability and open the tunnel door, they wouldn’t have been able to plant so many explosives!
Yang Yang spoke first: "Mission accomplished! Jing Shu severed the wires to the detonators on four tons of TNT, successfully preventing them from igniting the explosives and saving all of us!"
"Really? That’s incredible!"
"It must be true; look at her injuries."
"God bless us."
Qian Duoduo let out a heavy sigh of relief and gently patted Jing Shu’s shoulder. "Today, I truly thank you. You not only saw through their plot but also successfully thwarted their actions. I, Qian Duoduo, owe you a great debt of gratitude."
Su Xiangnan’s grim expression also softened. He said to Jing Shu, "I’m not as stingy as Qian Duoduo; I owe you two such debts. After all, you saved not only Su Malie but also me."
"Then I owe you four! You saved my entire family of four!" Qian Duoduo snorted.

chapters.title: Chapter 270: Lin Yi Went to See Grandma Jing? (Extra - sponsored by Zihang with a 10,000 reward)
chapters.content:
Chapter 270: Lin Yi Went to See Grandma Jing? (Extra Chapter sponsored by Zihang with a 10,000 reward)
"Alright, alright, let’s save the expressions of gratitude for after we’ve caught the murderer. Time is of the essence. I have a few important questions to ask Jing Shu," Captain Wang said, exasperated. This incident was so perilous, thousands of lives were nearly lost. They had to catch the culprit!
Su Xiangnan glared at Qian Duoduo.
Why did this Old Ghost always have to one-up him?
No wonder they were such long-standing adversaries. Despite being framed this time, he still hated the other with gnashing teeth. Truth be told, Su Xiangnan merely disliked Qian Duoduo as a business competitor. His true, teeth-grinding hatred was reserved for that government official. Su Malie had always believed their relationship was amicable, but that smiling tiger was the one Su Xiangnan found genuinely vexing.
"Yes, we must catch the murderer." Qian Duoduo’s Tang suit was tattered, and his face was caked in dust. Even the walnut he had been playing with for over a decade was gone!
The atmosphere finally eased a bit after Jing Shu successfully prevented the castle’s explosion. Towards their lifesaver, everyone’s attitude was exceptionally kind and admiring. Even the old traditional doctor treating Jing Shu’s wounds was extra careful. Jing Shu was someone who feared pain, and now, out of embarrassment, she couldn’t bring herself to grimace, though she inwardly cursed Lin Yi to kingdom come.
If she had known Lin Yi planned to blow up West Mountain, she would have stolen the explosives ages ago. It would have saved so much trouble.
Jing Shu scanned the people in the castle but didn’t spot that drama-loving, unhinged son of a landlord, nor Qian Duoduo’s daughter, Qian Qianjin, or his wife.
Only later did they learn that Qian Duoduo, upon hearing there was a bomb in the castle, had immediately arranged for his family to leave by helicopter while he himself stayed behind to clean up the mess.
When the only remaining involved parties, Su Malie and Jing Shu, were both present, Captain Wang pointed to Fatty and asked, "Jing Shu, tell us the location of your transaction, the time, and whether it was with this Fatty you made the deal?"
When the Fatty standing behind Qian Duoduo stepped forward, Jing Shu was startled, and Su Malie took a step back.
In an instant, Jing Shu had a rough understanding of the whole situation.
Jing Shu shook her head. "The transaction took place this morning at eight o’clock in the underground casino of an abandoned manor. The person at the time was also called Fatty. They do look quite similar, but the one we dealt with must have been an imposter. Besides, he was already dead in the underground passage by this afternoon."
This particular Fatty was squeezed into a black suit, looking like a disciplined, portly man—not at all like the other Fatty who had been bitten to death by a snake and was found sprawled lazily on a sofa.
Su Malie had a sudden realization. "I knew something was off about that guy this morning!"
Fatty also had a realization. "So, the person we were chatting with on WeChat was the same one! But it must have been the murderer who first completed the transaction with Su Malie and then imprisoned them in the underground casino. Then, the murderer impersonated Su Malie, the trusted Uncle Gou, and two bodyguards with their faces covered to conduct the transaction with me. They created a perfect time discrepancy! That way, the time I mentioned wouldn’t match Su Malie’s disappearance, and you’d all definitely think I was lying."
Jing Shu nodded.
She was likely the unexpected element in this whole drama, causing discrepancies not only in the timeline but also in the identities of the people involved.
Nevertheless, despite such conclusive evidence, a frantic Su Xiangnan would certainly believe that damned Qian Duoduo had kidnapped his daughter to achieve some goal.
The brilliance of the entire scheme was that after the bombing began, Su Malie reappeared unharmed and revealed a conspiracy to frame them. However, with the bombing outside still ongoing, Qian Duoduo would suspect it was a trap set by Su Xiangnan. After all, if the true goal was to make them kill each other, wouldn’t it have been simpler to just kill Su Malie? Why release her now? Only a fool would believe that a supposedly helpless young lady, kidnapped so easily, could not only escape on her own but also uncover a conspiracy—especially by appearing at his castle, his vital stronghold. So, he immediately ordered the castle’s defense system to be activated, unknowingly playing right into Lin Yi’s hands.
All of it, every single thing, was merely a prelude for Lin Yi to bomb West Mountain. His true aim was to get the castle’s defense system activated and then kill everyone who came to West Mountain by blowing them up. This man was utterly insane.
Yang Yang kicked the wall fiercely. "How could we have let him escape back then, only for him to return and seek revenge on us? This incident was definitely intentional! News is already spreading like wildfire outside; its rapid dissemination is undoubtedly his doing. He orchestrated this to lure our entire detachment here and annihilate us!"
Jing Shu nodded.
This man truly has ruthless ambitions.
After the bombardment outside ceased, Captain Wang instructed the remaining people, along with Qian Duoduo’s security guards, to go out and manage the aftermath. Word was that the explosion had struck the side of a mountain, triggering a landslide. Casualties were still being tallied.
"Report! We’ve accessed the database information for the woman whose upper body was blown off. Her name is Ling Qi. By tracing her last call, we’ve located the IP address of the other party from five minutes ago."
Jing Shu’s head was now bandaged. She had briefly cleansed herself with water filtered to remove red earthworms. Qian Duoduo found some of Qian Qianjin’s clothes for her to change into.
The temperature is dropping rapidly. It’ll be frigid soon; I need to put on more clothes.
"We must pursue and apprehend this person this time! What’s the address?"
"Banana District."
"Alright, move out immediately!"
Jing Shu’s hand trembled, and she accidentally tore the leather coat, effectively demonstrating an impressive feat of ripping clothes barehanded.
Those nearby quietly gulped.
How much strength did it take for Jing Shu to tear a leather coat like that?
Jing Shu couldn’t bother with anything else and quickly called Grandma Jing’s home.
The sound of RING... RING... RING... came through the receiver. With each ring, Jing Shu’s heart sank a little further.
"Hello?" Grandma Jing’s voice finally came from the other end.
Jing Shu quietly exhaled. "Grandma? What are you doing?"
She heard Grandma Jing say irritably, "What else would I be doing? Tidying up the first floor with Zijin."
Jing Shu quietly relaxed. "Okay, Grandma. Please don’t go out for the next few days if you don’t have to, alright? By the way, has our next-door neighbor, Lin Yi, come looking for you?"
"Him? We were just talking a moment ago."
Jing Shu’s heart started to THUMP-THUMP again.
"That young man said he’s moving, so he probably won’t be able to chat with me as often anymore. It’s quite a shame. He also said he’d come find me for a chat next time he has a chance, and then he left. He seemed to be in quite a hurry when he went."
Jing Shu said, "...Alright, Grandma. Stay safe at home. If anything happens, press and hold the number 1 key to call me."
After hanging up, Jing Shu called Zijin to confirm the situation. Then, she called her family members one by one. Everyone was fine, which finally allowed Jing Shu to breathe a small sigh of relief.
No, I can’t rest until Lin Yi is caught. It feels like a fishbone stuck in my throat. Lin Yi must be eliminated, or I won’t be able to sleep soundly. Something’s wrong... Something’s not right!

chapters.title: Chapter 271: No Escape for Lin Yi
chapters.content:
Chapter 271: No Escape for Lin Yi
Jing Shu checked the cell phone surveillance but couldn’t find any footage related to Lin Yi. This person had strong anti-surveillance awareness, so it was unlikely they would find anything. Instead, Grandma Jing had left with Zijin an hour ago. That was the time they usually cleaned the old house together, but typically, this was when Grandma Jing cooked! Otherwise, what would the family eat for dinner? Besides, cleaning a house should only take ten minutes!
So, it was very likely that they encountered Lin Yi while cleaning the house! And after that, they couldn’t leave... And the words Grandma Jing had just said—could she have been forced?
Jing Shu took a deep breath and closed her eyes. "Take me with you. I think my grandma might be in Lin Yi’s hands."
The scene at Qian Duoduo’s castle was chaotic. After being one-sidedly bombed, they began urgently dealing with the aftermath. To catch the murderer as quickly as possible, Qian Duoduo even contributed a helicopter.
As for Su Xiangnan, after he finished tallying the casualties on his side, he also called it quits. Su Xiangnan had lost over a hundred gas cylinders, which had exploded accidentally. He had never really meant to bomb West Mountain, but the explosives underground still set off some of the gas cylinders, causing even greater secondary damage.
Energy resources were incredibly precious in the post-apocalypse, and Su Xiangnan now gritted his teeth in hatred for Lin Yi.
Jing Shu, Yang Yang, and his six special forces soldiers boarded the helicopter, heading straight for Banana District. Li Yuetian, who had been on standby, led over a hundred people toward Jing Shu’s villa.
Jing Shu remained restless and anxious.
Hundreds of scenarios had already played out in her mind. She even thought about using the new abilities of the Magic Cube Space to create illusions in Lin Yi’s mind, then rescue Grandma Jing. Such thoughts made her feel a bit better; the Magic Cube Space’s upgrade had come just in time.
Fortunately, the helicopter was fast, reaching Banana District in just five minutes on a direct flight. At that moment, Jing Shu’s villa and Building 25 were already tightly surrounded, ensuring that not even a fly could escape.
The arrival of the helicopter and the large number of officers still caused quite a stir among the residents of Banana District. Spectating was a common pastime for Huaxia people. This continued until Li Yuetian announced over a loudspeaker that a serial killer had fled into the district. He ordered everyone to stay indoors and prepare for inspection. Only then did the shocked onlookers disperse.
Once they disembarked from the helicopter, Yang Yang and his team spread out to search Building 25 house by house, while Li Yuetian led his men to search the surrounding area. Meanwhile, Captain Wang from Yang Yang’s team began a broad search around Banana District.
This was the apocalypse; surveillance wasn’t as widespread as before it began, but major roads still had some. On the way, Jing Shu had asked Yang Yang about Lin Yi.
"How did Lin Yi manage to escape by himself when he was restrained by so many of you?"
Yang Yang was actually quite puzzled by this. "That man is really strange. Maybe everyone let their guard down after the plan succeeded that day. For some reason, I suggested we have a few drinks. When I woke up, he was gone. But before we drank, I specifically made sure he was triple-cuffed and locked in a sealed room, which required our three keys to open. Surely I didn’t unlock it for him while I was drunk, did I?"
Jing Shu fell silent.
That being said, if they let Lin Yi escape, he would likely become as slippery as an eel, never to be found again.
Jing Shu first returned to her villa. Mr. Jing, alarmed by the injuries on her face, thought something terrible had happened. Jing Shu quickly reassured him. Just as she was about to head to Building 25, Grandma Jing and Zijin returned.
Jing Shu: "???"
She then heard Grandma Jing say to Zijin, "I don’t know what’s happening outside. Why are there so many police officers? Something big must be going on."
"I heard they’re arresting a murderer," Zijin replied.
"Grandma? Why are you only getting back now?" Jing Shu looked at Grandma Jing and Zijin with suspicion.
She had heard that making a human skin mask took a long time; surely they couldn’t have been turned into skin suits in just half an hour, right?
Grandma Jing saw the injuries on Jing Shu and said with heartache, "What have you been up to, child? How did you get injured again? Zijin and I were sorting out some damp items today, so it took a bit longer."
"Where is Lin Yi?" Jing Shu thoroughly checked Grandma Jing and Zijin from head to toe, only relaxing once she confirmed they were real.
Zijin shyly lowered her head. Jing Shu was acting so strangely today.
"You child, from now on you must call him Brother Lin. He’s already left, driving out of the province. I heard this time he’s going to a faraway place. He even gave me 500 Virtual Coins, asking me to extend the house’s usage rights for him. He said he’d be back at any time. Honestly, that child..." Grandma Jing sighed.
Jing Shu looked at Zijin, who nodded. "That’s what he said," Zijin confirmed. "We saw him drive away, and he did seem to be in quite a hurry."
Regardless, Lin Yi hadn’t harmed her grandma, and a sense of relief washed over her.
Still, she had a nagging feeling that something wasn’t right.
Jing Shu scratched her head. After making arrangements for Grandma Jing and Zijin, she hurried off to Lin Yi’s house.
Lin Yi lived directly across from Grandma Jing. Currently, the entire building was surrounded, with search teams of two patrolling. Inside Lin Yi’s house, several individuals were looking for traces of his presence, moving all his belongings out.
By the time Jing Shu arrived, the house was nearly empty; the remaining people were moving out the last cabinet.
Yang Yang squatted in the bare living room, lost in thought.
"It’s strange he didn’t make a move on my grandma," Jing Shu said, furrowing her brows.
"He’s gone. We’ll never catch him again. The next time he appears, it will surely be a bloodbath. This time was a fluke; you foiled his plan. But what about next time? Where will he show up?" Yang Yang clenched his fist and smashed it hard against the wall, producing a THUD, as blood immediately began to stream out.
"Yes," Jing Shu murmured, gazing at the wall. An idea flashed through her mind, her eyes suddenly brightening.
"Captain Yang, we’ll take the stuff back first. If there’s anything, just shout; the guys are checking nearby."
Yang Yang waved his hand. "Go ahead. I’ll stay a bit longer."
BANG. The last officer closed the door.
"Damn it, where could he have gone in just ten minutes?!"
"No, he didn’t run. He doesn’t need to run. Why would he? Compared to the dangerous world outside, this is the safest place," Jing Shu said, her eyes shining.
She thought she was beginning to understand Lin Yi’s special ability.
"What do you mean?" Yang Yang frowned.
"Lin Yi, Zero, he’s still in this house!" Jing Shu’s fist pounded on the wall, making THUD THUD THUD sounds.
Yang Yang was even more puzzled. What did Jing Shu mean?

chapters.title: Chapter 272: The Hypnotherapist’s Ability
chapters.content:
Chapter 272: The Hypnotherapist’s Ability
Jing Shu only realized after seeing Yang Yang punch the wall that the fake doors in the underground tunnel and the fake mirrors in the castle—all, without exception, were doors made to look exactly like their surroundings, with new spaces added behind them. This was indicative of a person’s habits. Just like Jing Shu, whose identity as a foodie was an unchangeable part of her very core.
So, even someone as clever as Lin Yi, due to his lack of security, would inevitably hide himself where no one could find him, no matter where he went. It had become a habit for him.
Thus, Jing Shu believed that Lin Yi was here in this house, in a secret chamber he had modified and hidden himself!
It was indiscernible from the outside without a careful look. Of course, even with a careful look, it couldn’t be found. After all, the entire house was empty, with nothing but walls.
Who would think that in such a common residential building, someone would have constructed a small, hidden room?
Jing Shu knocked bit by bit, going around once without finding anything unusual. Yang Yang clearly didn’t understand, but Jing Shu didn’t know how to explain.
Explaining would give herself away—for instance, how did she open the fake door in the underground passage? So, when with clever people, speak less.
Jing Shu knocked around again—up, down, left, and right. This time, she didn’t even spare the built-in wardrobe, and sure enough, one section emitted a crisp sound!
Although not hollow, the sound was different from the surroundings!
This hiding spot was incredibly well-concealed! She estimated that even the police wouldn’t search this place.
Yang Yang and Jing Shu looked at each other. Jing Shu saw a strange expression on Yang Yang’s face, as if he were looking at some kind of freak.
"Now, we just need to open it," Jing Shu said, her fists cracking.
Maybe she should just grab a sledgehammer and smash it open?
Just then, the hidden door opened, revealing Lin Yi’s face with a smile that wasn’t quite a smile. He stepped out and dusted off his hands. "It seems I’ve underestimated you. Next time I make a door, even if it’s a bit more troublesome, I’ll have to use identical materials so it’s not so easily discovered."
Jing Shu’s vision penetrated the door, revealing what was inside: a hidden space of less than four square meters, yet fully equipped. It had all sorts of food, water, and even electricity. There was also a Murphy bed for sleeping. It could be said that it had all the conditions for survival; living in there for a month or so would absolutely be no problem.
"Do you think you can still escape?" Jing Shu sneered.
This person was far too self-assured, wasn’t he?
Outside, hundreds of police officers were searching for him. Now, as long as Yang Yang shouted, everyone would rush in. Even if he had explosives, he couldn’t save himself now.
"Escape? Why would I need to escape? Jing Shu, today is when we truly get to know each other, right? Why such hostility? I haven’t even blamed you for ruining my painstakingly crafted plan," Lin Yi said, hands in his trouser pockets, shrugging casually. He always looked so sunny and optimistic, the corners of his mouth always turned up in a slight smile.
Such a calm and composed demeanor. He must have had an ace up his sleeve to be so indifferent.
"Yang Yang, call for backup."
The hallmark of a major villain is arrogance and verbosity—Jing Shu was determined not to give Lin Yi any time to call for help or anything of the sort.
Lin Yi tilted his head, his fingers rubbing rhythmically against his trousers. He casually tried to negotiate, "Otherwise, Officer Yang, how about you let me go this once? Just pretend you never found me today, and let me comfortably stay in there for a few more days."
Jing Shu scoffed.
This Lin Yi really dared to say such things. It would be a wonder if Yang Yang didn’t beat him to death!
Then, something that made Jing Shu’s jaw drop in astonishment occurred!
Yang Yang pondered for a moment and actually said, "Alright, I’ll let you off this time."
Jing Shu was utterly bewildered.
What in the world is happening?
She then saw Lin Yi walking towards her step by step, the rubbing of his fingers becoming faster and faster. As she watched his long, handsome fingers, Jing Shu felt a wave of drowsiness.
"So, Jing Shu, what do you think? Perhaps you’re tired after a long day. You should go home and enjoy that sumptuous dinner you’ve been wanting. Your grandmother has made a whole table of delicacies for you. Your cousin is waiting for you to come back and tell her about all the novel things that happened today. You are basking in the envious and jealous gazes of your whole family. You really enjoy this atmosphere; you need to express and release your feelings..."
Inexplicably, Jing Shu almost agreed.
I almost fell for your wicked trick.
Jing Shu’s mind suddenly jolted. She activated the Magic Cube Space’s newest ability—Illusion! She instantly snapped back to clarity from the verge of succumbing.
Lin Yi revealed a surprised expression.
"So, this is your unknown trump card? This ability of yours? Whatever you say, people will obediently listen?" The corners of Jing Shu’s mouth curled upward.
If that was the case, everything seemed to make sense now.
But do Superpowers really exist in this world?
"You’re the second person who hasn’t succumbed to my hypnosis," Lin Yi said somewhat regretfully. "It’s not a particularly remarkable ability. It’s just that I’m the world’s only hypnotherapist who can achieve Level 7 hypnosis. In the field of hypnotism, hypnosis is generally divided into six levels."
This was just like Mr. Ma saying it was nothing remarkable and that he wasn’t interested in money.
Jing Shu’s mouth fell open.
Hypnotism? This is actually hypnotism?
It’s when the Hypnotist provides suggestions to the person being hypnotized. Under a hypnotic state, a person might experience "some changes in perception, thought, memory, and behavior."
This includes temporary paralysis, illusions, and amnesia regarding the Hypnotist’s suggestions.
This seemed to be a level higher than the new Illusion ability of Jingshu’s space, though the two weren’t directly comparable. Lin Yi’s hypnotism succeeded through voice, hand gestures, and other cues, subsequently making people do things they wouldn’t even remember.
Lin Yi’s hypnotism was more geared towards the permanence and event-specific nature of a task, ’not resting until the goal is achieved,’ whereas Jing Shu’s had to be within the range of the Magic Cube Space.
But Jing Shu’s Illusion ability was still quite formidable; it was like a cheat code. She could use the Magic Cube Space to directly implant suggestions in a person without needing extra hand gestures, voice cues, or other hints. And if it didn’t succeed once, she could keep suggesting until it did.
"So that’s why Grandma and Zijin said they saw you drive away! You used their mouths to convey the message that you had already left, making all of us think you had escaped?"
"Oh, right! And you made your subordinate Ling Qi commit suicide by detonating the Detonator—that was also your hypnotism?"
"Last year, you also used hypnotism to escape from their hands?"
"And you used hypnotism to extract all of Uncle Gou’s and the others’ secrets, didn’t you?"
Lin Yi began to clap. "However, I didn’t hypnotize Ling Qi. She did it willingly."

chapters.title: Chapter 273: Finally Arrested
chapters.content:
Chapter 273: Finally Arrested
"Jerk."
"My wishes became the edge of her sword. If death could elevate Ling Qi’s status in my heart, she would do it without hesitation," he said. "I understood her, so I fulfilled her wish. From now on, she will live in my heart forever. But what about you, Jing Shu? You are heartless and desireless. What is the purpose of your life?"
Lin Yi certainly lived up to his name as a hypnotherapist, advancing on Jing Shu with an unhurried pace. Jing Shu felt like she was about to fall into his rhythm.
Hypnosis that required interaction with external objects was considered low-level. In contrast, someone like Lin Yi could immerse a person in a mystic state with the sound of his voice alone, causing them to act without even realizing what they had done after listening to him.
As his trump card, he could indeed navigate all dangers without fear. It was only now that Jing Shu understood why, in her previous life, Zero, although just an ordinary person and captured many times, still managed to escape.
Of course, Lin Yi’s hypnosis abilities must have their limits, such as not being effective in crowded or noisy places. This was likely why Yang Yang and his team had been able to capture Lin Yi.
As for whether it would work on a deaf person, that was hard to say; a good hypnotherapist could use various methods to hypnotize someone beforehand.
This was a face-off between a hypnotherapist’s abilities and the Illusion abilities of the Magic Cube Space.
Jing Shu tried several times to implant false perceptions and Illusions in Lin Yi’s mind to influence his decisions, but all attempts undoubtedly failed. Lin Yi’s usually infallible hypnosis ability was greatly diminished when used on Jing Shu; she even resisted it outright.
"Ah, what a hassle." Lin Yi finally gave up on hypnotizing Jing Shu. "Actually, I really like it here. I enjoy chatting with Granny."
"You’ve lost your chance," Jing Shu said. Immediately, she noticed a look of surprise in Lin Yi’s eyes, and then he collapsed to the ground with a thud. Approaching him, Jing Shu found a small mechanism button in the pocket of Lin Yi’s trousers.
After studying it for a while, Jing Shu discovered how it worked: one had to press the small mechanism button first. Then, after stepping on a specific floor tile, it would turn into a suspended trap, ensuring that anyone who stepped on it would disappear instantly. The floor tile would then revert to its original form and could not be opened again.
It was a trap mechanism identical to the one in the Xishan basement! An escape mechanism!
So that was it. The switch was on him—no wonder she couldn’t find it after searching for so long in the basement! He actually wanted to use the same trick as Fatty, and she hadn’t even noticed! Dealing with these people was exhausting; one moment they might be bluffing or begging for mercy, and the next, they could have already made their escape.
If Lin Yi had managed to blend into the crowd in the Banana District, even a thorough search would be like finding a needle in a haystack, especially if people were continuously providing cover for him.
So, seeing he couldn’t hypnotize her, Lin Yi had been planning to run. Befitting his psychology background, he’d persistently tried to hypnotize her to divert her attention, making her think he had some major move up his sleeve...
Luckily, Jing Shu was clever.
She knew not to alert him prematurely.
She had collected the drugging powder used during the robbery at her elder aunt’s son’s wedding and now sprinkled it from her space. Lin Yi’s attention was entirely on Jing Shu, so in the pitch-black room, he couldn’t see the dispersing powder and was overcome in seconds.
"Wake up!" Jing Shu slapped the wooden-like Yang Yang, but there was no reaction. Then, she used the strong suggestive powers of Illusion from her space several times before Yang Yang finally recovered. "What happened? Where’s Zero?"
Jing Shu rolled her eyes and recounted the events. Yang Yang pursed his lips tightly. "So that’s how it is. I knew something was off about the last incident... But how come you weren’t hypnotized?"
Yang Yang looked at Jing Shu with suspicion. Even after knowing her for so long, he still couldn’t see through her. She was a mysterious woman, always managing to surprise and amaze him.
"Well, it’s because my spiritual power is high and my will is strong. Even Zero was surprised that he couldn’t hypnotize me. Look, he even tried to run away."
Yang Yang took out handcuffs, electric shackles, tape, and other restraints from behind his waist and tied Lin Yi up securely, even taping his mouth shut. "Now that he can’t speak, how is he going to hypnotize anyone? This time, we absolutely won’t let him escape again. Now that we know his secret, we have defenses against him, and he has no moves left."
Jing Shu hadn’t expected her intervention to so drastically alter Zero’s fate. In her previous life, he wasn’t captured for several more years. Her actions had also led to the exposure of Zero’s abilities. He had always been extremely cautious when using his hypnotic powers, guarding this secret for many years, and never anticipated they would fail against Jing Shu.
However, Jing Shu was also quite curious. Zero said there was one other person he couldn’t hypnotize. Who was that person? What was so special about them?
Regardless, Zero was finally subdued and brought to justice, which removed a great thorn from Jing Shu’s side. From now on, she could completely sever ties with the Sky Covering Organization. She no longer had to worry that after dealing with the minions, their superiors would come, and after the superiors, their ancestors.
"When will he be sentenced and executed?" Jing Shu asked.
"Don’t know. If it goes by the book, it could be a week or about a month, but..." Yang Yang deliberately lowered his voice. "I reckon he won’t die that easily. He’s stolen not just Huaxia’s data but also core information from the United States. He knows too much. They’ll have to make him tell it all first."
Every second this man remained alive was utterly terrifying.
"Let me know if there’s any news about him."
"Sure. You’ve made a major contribution this time. How about joining a special unit? Wang Dazhao has been promoted again; he said he needs to get promoted quickly to meet your standards."
"I just want to enjoy life in my villa. If there’s anything good, give me a shout."
Yang Yang left with the unconscious Lin Yi. Lin Yi’s belongings were all confiscated.
Jing Shu didn’t dare use them, fearing they might contain surveillance devices.
The troops in the Banana District disbanded. Li Yuetian invited Jing Shu to sit for a while. After getting an update on the situation, he saw that Jing Shu wasn’t in a good mental state and sent her back. "Alright, come back to make your statement when you feel better."
Before dinner, Su Malie sent a message. The fifty to sixty individuals linked to Lin Yi, whom Jing Shu had seen at the underground casino that day, had all been located—dead or alive—and dealt with. Su Malie also mentioned the day’s losses.
Su Malie’s father’s loss of gas canisters went without saying; over thirty men were killed. Apparently, when people went to the underground tunnels to look for Su Malie, they were secretly duped. The culprits switched into their clothes, then went above ground to detonate gas canisters and cause chaos. All of those people were killed.

chapters.title: Chapter 274: After the Sixth Year of the Apocalypse, the Food Is...
chapters.content:
Chapter 274: After the Sixth Year of the Apocalypse, the Food Is...
Qian Duoduo suffered even more severe losses—every place with a house had been rigged with bombs and destroyed. Over a hundred of their six hundred people died from various causes. The staff building at West Mountain, seen on a previous occasion, had been leveled. The bodyguards and servants were without shelter, having no place to stay. Financial losses were also significant. Farms and breeding grounds that cost a fortune to establish were gone. However, it was said that Qian Duoduo’s castle still held plenty of food, so they should be able to hold out.
Overall, today seemed like a scenario where both parties had hurt each other without achieving their goals. Lin Yi had even met with total annihilation.
Wait... if there was anyone who benefited, it seemed to be Jing Shu?
Jing Shu was certain that if she hadn’t made this trip, she would have had no clue when the Magic Cube Space might have upgraded. Thus, the upgrade of the Magic Cube Space definitely increased her life-saving trump cards.
The Magic Cube Space had upgraded, granting her new abilities. Jing Shu also acquired 14 tons of TNT explosives, which would be quite useful in the post-apocalyptic world. She even won valuable goodwill from Su Xiangnan and Qian Duoduo. With these new connections, even if she wasn’t a major player yet, she was moving in the direction of becoming one.
Capturing Lin Yi must have earned her a first-class merit, right? She should be rewarded with some Virtual Coins, marking at least one source of income.
With these thoughts, Jing Shu’s fatigue seemed to lessen considerably. However, eager to see the upgraded Magic Cube, she ate dinner much faster than usual.
Jing Shu’s experiences of the day would naturally be shared as a bit of a joke—not to show off, but to reassure her family. Grandma Jing even specially slaughtered a chicken and stewed fish soup to calm Jing Shu’s nerves. Of course, Jing Shu omitted the part about the explosives, only mentioning that she had uncovered a conspiracy and received a reward; otherwise, Grandma Jing, with her weak heart, might have fainted.
After dinner, each family member had a sip of medicinal wine to dispel dampness and enjoyed some of the available fruit. Jing Shu then asked Mr. Jing to take care of the leeches, and Mr. Jing to walk the chicken.
Due to the large population in the community, the fat chickens were also given plastic raincoats and leashed like dogs. Fortunately, the torrential rain outside made everything so dark that it was hard to tell whether they were dogs or chickens. The fat chickens had grown as big as medium-sized dogs, and no one knew if they would continue to grow.
If they grow too big, would they be taken away for research? Oh, the research institutes might not have time for that now. There are already many new species of mutations and evolutions. Their current focus is on how to produce more food, and I’ve heard they’re researching a type of genetically mutated animal.
Due to her different status in her previous life, Jing Shu hadn’t heard about such things. In this life, however, she happened to hear Su Malie mention it. The idea was to extract genes and combine them with a carrier, introducing the target gene into recipient cells to create new species or plants suited for apocalyptic survival, thereby increasing food production.
Jing Shu listened, somewhat baffled, until Su Malie whispered,
"It’s about making a chicken with legs and wings all over its body, or even having multiple reproductive organs for laying eggs. It could also involve turning cattle into oviparous animals that lay eggs daily, hatching a batch of ’cattle eggs’ each month, or fattening fish by injecting them with hormones and drugs to ensure each generation grows to tens or even hundreds of pounds within months. They might even add Antidark Pigment to each generation or remove the natural photosynthetic ability from creatures, forcefully using other methods to make them grow."
"They’re simply not considering the impact of genetic breakthroughs or modifications, just forcefully increasing their yield. They no longer care about the consequences of eating such things, especially since the higher-ups have said that if the apocalypse continues and the country’s situation remains unchanged, Huaxia might collapse within a decade. So, you might not be aware, but the prices of livestock and various crops have started skyrocketing again recently."
"After all, the country is now storing large quantities of red earthworms, hoping to breed more livestock once enough feed is secured."
After Su Malie’s explanation, Jing Shu finally understood how the infamous ’monster food’ from after the sixth year of the apocalypse came into existence. She realized that significant resources had been heavily invested into its research starting from the second year. Su Malie was right: migration, heavy snowfall, and frigid temperatures beginning in the fifth year of the apocalypse caused Earth’s crop yields to plummet, leading many to starve. Without the development of new food sources, Huaxia would indeed have faced complete annihilation.
If the first five years of the apocalypse were spent consuming local products—including red earthworms, maggots, and rotten corpse insects—then in the later stages, people began to eat these things that had no taste of meat, were oddly shaped, and were difficult to swallow.
Jing Shu shuddered, truly unwilling to recall these memories. In her past life, even these genetically engineered foods were affordable only to people with substantial assets.
She remembered eating genetically altered ’fat fish’ one year. The flesh could hardly be called fish meat; it was like chewing on sawdust, with each cell enlarged a hundredfold, making it hard and tough to swallow. The fishy smell was amplified several hundred times, as if one were smelling a sewer that had been collecting vomit for months.
Yes, eating that fish was like consuming garbage steeped in the fetid water of a gutter.
When the market was flooded with genetically mutated foods, the most precious and valuable items became those that were unchanged, in their original, natural state. Chickens, ducks, and fish from that era became as valuable as pre-apocalypse antiques.
Why were they becoming increasingly valuable? Couldn’t they just be bred extensively?
The reasons were environment and cost.
The phrase ’survival of the fittest’ was no joke. The longer the apocalypse endured, the less likely original, natural plants and animals were to survive if they didn’t grow stronger or adapt to the apocalyptic conditions. These natural organisms were too delicate; factors like darkness, cold, disease, low yields, and high mortality rates made them unsuitable.
Regarding cost, the same amount of food that could sustain only one natural animal could, thanks to genetic breakthroughs, support animals with yields five to ten times higher. With Huaxia’s population at one billion, it was necessary to choose low-cost, high-yield options for breeding. Even then, this was often just enough to prevent the majority from starving.
Natural, original foods were confined to the upper echelons of society.
Shaking her head, she thought these concerns were still too far off.
The issue of genetically engineered creatures was a matter of livelihood for the Huaxia nation. If the ’Father of Hybrid Rice’ hadn’t developed high-yield hybrid rice varieties, perhaps half of Huaxia’s population would have starved.
Indeed, survival was more important than anything.
After Jing Shu locked herself in her bedroom, she took out the Challenge Cube, which had transformed into an 8th Order one. At the same time, she silently invoked, "Magic Cube Space!"
In that instant, the Magic Cube Space entered its Second Form, spreading out with Jing Shu at its center. The current size of the Magic Cube Space was 7x7x7 = 343 cubic meters. If she could meet the upgrade requirements for the 8th Order Cube, she would possess a space of 8x8x8 = 512 cubic meters. Jing Shu was highly motivated!
The 7th Order space had undergone significant changes. The Spiritual Spring in the center still seemed to produce only a pitiful amount each day, but now there were six additional fields, totaling 36 square meters of planting area.

chapters.title: Chapter 275: Cotton and Tobacco Cultivation
chapters.content:
Chapter 275: Cotton and Tobacco Cultivation
Jing Shu did some calculations. While the Spiritual Spring in the Magic Cube Space still produced one gram (20 drops) per day, the six new fields brought an increase. The Magic Cube Space would automatically send one drop of Spiritual Spring to each new field daily. In other words, this added an extra six drops to the daily production, bringing the total number of fields in the upgraded Magic Cube Space to 24.
From the initial six fields, she now had 24. Jing Shu felt an ineffable sense of achievement, much like the pride of a gamer whose virtual farm, starting with just six plots, expanded into the vast holdings of a high-level tycoon.
Especially in this apocalypse where nothing could be grown, having a high-yield farm where she could grow whatever she wanted was so reassuring that it almost brought Jing Shu to tears.
However, there was a drawback with the fields in the Magic Cube Space. Even if nothing was planted, the Spiritual Spring would still automatically dispense one drop into each field every day. This led Jing Shu to suspect that the land needed the daily nourishment of the Spiritual Spring to maintain its current productivity, which doubled crop yields.
Therefore, the fields in the space must not be wasted; something has to be planted every day!
Of course, as the space upgraded and expanded, Jing Shu’s needs also grew. Currently, there were no issues of overproduction or unusable surplus because the number of fields was limited. Although the yield was high, Jing Shu’s demand was also considerable. Moreover, growing a batch of crops generally took about ten days. Not to mention, Jing Shu often fed all vegetable scraps like roots and unwanted leaves to the livestock. Any woody stalks were used as firewood.
Now, Jing Shu’s arrangement for the 24 fields was as follows:
Six fields would still be used for various vegetables. The produce from these, harvested every ten days, would be stored for a month or two before being processed into finished products.
Six fields were dedicated to fruit crops, which Jing Shu would turn into juice. The unwanted pulp was fed to the livestock, and some plants were transplanted to the second-floor greenhouse for her family to enjoy. Any occasional surplus was made into dried fruit.
Six fields were for growing medicinal herbs. It had only been half a year since the Magic Cube Space’s last upgrade. During this time, some of the herbs had matured, and Jing Shu stored them all in the space, planning to dry them next year, as this year was too humid.
However, items like ginseng and Ganoderma needed time to grow, so they couldn’t be rushed.
With the addition of six new fields, Jing Shu now used three to grow cotton and the other three to grow tobacco.
Since the Magic Cube’s fields were few and its production capacity limited, Jing Shu knew that if she wanted to build up her reserves, she still had to rely on the luxury goods of the apocalypse.
After all, those who directly traded in rice and flour during the apocalypse were courting death—weren’t they basically announcing to the world that they were grain merchants? Even the government would likely become envious and find reasons to confiscate their supplies, I figure.
But one could certainly deal in high-end goods, like tobacco and alcohol.
Jing Shu had started two red earthworm factories. Before the apocalypse, their product was as common as corn—astonishing yields but of little value—mostly used to feed livestock and not drawing much attention. However, these two factories were seasonal; she could operate them during the current rainy season, but they wouldn’t be viable in a few months. After that, their output would be purely for sales or personal use.
But tobacco is different, she mused. It’s a sustainable, risk-free business. Only the wealthy, with full bellies and idle time, would seek to continue enjoying life’s pleasures. And naturally, they would have the money to spend on such luxuries.
In the apocalypse, luxury items are the easiest way to make money, she thought. It’s a world of stark contrasts: some die of drought, others of flood, and many starve, while the well-fed rich have money but nothing to spend it on. They have food, yes, but low production capacity means many other goods are simply gone. If they want to buy something, it’s invariably out of stock! Whenever a desirable item does appear, everyone scrambles for it!
Therefore, with her affiliation to the Medicinal Materials Association, Jing Shu could justifiably engage in these activities. To satisfy market demand, she planned to specifically create products for the high-end market: cigars. She would aim to exchange the fewest possible cigars for the greatest amount of capital. How many cigars could be grown in three fields, covering 18 square meters?
Of course, some will be set aside for personal use, like for Mr. Jing and Mr. Jing, who are desperate for a smoke, she thought.
As for planting cotton, it was because she hadn’t expected her family to grow so large, which had led to a shortage not long after the apocalypse began. Later, when the weather turned colder, they would need even more cotton.
Cotton will eventually be as good as currency, she considered. Gifting a cotton garment in the cold winter could be a way to solicit favors and solve almost any problem.
Of course, there was another significant reason: the cow in Jingshu’s space was pregnant, and this time, she might get a few more calves. Jing Shu planned to breed more cows and make shredded beef jerky, beef energy bars, and braised beef. In period dramas, people always entered an inn and called out, "Waiter, a pound of beef, please!" This highlighted its importance.
In the future, when I’m hungry, I can enjoy cumin-flavored, spicy, or scallion shredded beef, slowly chewing the fragrant meat strips perfectly combined with seasonings. Or I could thinly slice braised beef and dip it into chili sauce... SLURP! Just thinking about it makes me drool!
Last year’s beef jerky was already finished, and there had hardly been enough to go around. Now that the space was larger, Jing Shu had the room to breed more livestock and produce more processed meat.
Cottonseed and other cotton by-products were the best fodder for cattle and sheep. Planting cotton would solve the feed problem for her expanding livestock operation. If the cattle and sheep only ate red earthworms, their milk quality and overall condition would drop significantly. So, since she had the means, Jing Shu planned to feed her livestock the best fodder available.
Some might say that with my surplus food, I should be rescuing those who can’t afford to eat, instead of feeding my animals so well, Jing Shu mused. But one-off rescues don’t last a lifetime. In my previous life, I never saw any rich people tossing rice my way.
But for anyone who helped me, I will repay them a hundred, even a thousand times over in this life! As for those who framed me, I no longer demand hundredfold repayment. I’ll simply let them struggle to survive in this apocalypse, watching me eat and drink well, listening to the envious talk about how my family’s life is getting better day by day.
If someone felt life was too hard and wanted to die, Jing Shu would kindly save them. If they still wanted to die, Jing Shu would save them again. Su Meimei was a case in point—but that was a story for another time.
To prevent some deaths, I will also store some red worm cakes, she resolved. The most I can do is provide this food during the hardest times—of course, in exchange for labor. It won’t be charity, and I won’t expect gratitude.
It was just like in my past life when I was on the brink of starvation, she recalled. I often thought that if I had plenty of food, I would do the same. Simply offering to exchange a little food for fair value is the greatest respect one can show others.
「The next day.」
Jing Shu had Mr. Jing set up racks and lights on the third-floor terrace, as she planned to grow tobacco and cotton. After all, these crops needed a plausible, visible origin outside her Magic Cube Space. Hearing about the tobacco cultivation, Mr. Jing and Mr. Jing refrained from their usual arguments and quickly finished building the racks. Only then did Jing Shu plant the tobacco and cotton on the terrace, which was over 20 square meters in size.

chapters.title: Chapter 276: Increasing the Difficulty of Upgrading the Magic Cube Space
chapters.content:
Chapter 276: Increasing the Difficulty of Upgrading the Magic Cube Space
Beyond the transformation of her field, Jing Shu also used eight cubic meters to raise fish. She planned to breed a large batch of fish to make various prepared dishes—such as baked, fried, steamed, and braised—to keep in the Magic Cube Space for snacking at night.
After the Magic Cube Space upgraded, she wasn’t sure if it was her imagination, but her appetite seemed to have increased somewhat.
She got hungry especially easily, which made her irritable.
Last year, she had spent her time drying various vegetables. There wasn’t enough space in the Magic Cube Space to raise more fish then. This year, with both time and ample space,
it was better to prepare these foods now, making them convenient for her to eat anytime. Otherwise, it would be too troublesome and time-consuming to start cooking only when she remembered to eat.
She used another twenty-four cubic meters to breed Domestic Poultry, doubling their quantity.
Jing Shu planned to slaughter another batch of Domestic Poultry in about half a year and turn it all into cooked food. She wanted to prepare early for the fifth-year migration. After all, once the fifth year began and they were constantly on the move, there would be no time to prepare these cooked meals.
The main task for the second half of this year was to turn various types of food into prepared meals and store them in the Magic Cube Space. She had to ensure that she, this ’big-eater’, would have plenty of good food to eat in the future. Then it was about pickling whatever could be pickled, trying to make everything long-lasting so that when she took them out later, people wouldn’t be overly surprised.
For instance, turning fruits into canned goods and vacuum-packing cooked corn. When taken out in front of many people, they at least wouldn’t be too conspicuous, and they could even be passed off as food that had expired before the apocalypse.
After the apocalypse, a vacuum-packed bag of corn was as precious as a 1982 Lafite; indeed, these pre-apocalypse expired foods were diminishing with each consumption.
Therefore, Jing Shu’s Magic Cube Space now consisted of:
1 cubic meter of Spiritual Spring + 24 cubic meters of field + 8 cubic meters of fish school + 24 cubic meters of Domestic Poultry + 286 cubic meters of supplies.
The 286 cubic meters were not fully used up, with more than eighty cubic meters of space remaining.
