What does it have to do with you? Mr. Ma might have a lot of money, but it’s not yours, and it has nothing to do with you."
This was the first time Jing Shu had ever spoken so bluntly in the group chat.
She had always been reserved, preferring to observe silently without voicing her opinions. She wasn’t adept at chatting with people and was even worse at currying favor with influential figures. If she had clung tightly to Su Malie’s coattails in her previous life, she probably would have fared very well. While everyone in the apocalypse was clinging to Su Malie, she remained silent, her inner world a mix of pride and self-importance.
Little did she expect that in this life, she would become the one others relied on.
The group chat fell silent for a moment.
Jing Shu didn’t know what others were thinking, but after speaking her mind, she felt much more relieved. Sometimes, there’s no point in mincing words; one’s own comfort is what matters most.
What Jing Shu didn’t realize was that she had already become a formidable presence among her high school classmates in the group chat. She was no longer the inconspicuous figure from before the apocalypse. After these recent incidents, anyone with discernment could see Jing Shu’s influence, an influence that at times might even surpass Su Malie’s.
Liang Xin seemed to realize that Jing Shu was not Su Malie. He blamed himself for not understanding Jing Shu better. Jing Shu hardly ever spoke and was always seen with Su Malie. This led him to assume she was as easygoing as Su Malie, only for him to be publicly rebuked by her.
Jing Shu, I’m so disappointed in you!
Liang Xin hesitated for a moment, then sent a message: "It really has nothing to do with me, but there are so many other classmates. Surely some of them are close, right? We could all benefit a little."
Jing Shu replied, "Not really."
That was awkward.
If the Jing Shu of her previous life had said such a thing, a crowd might have emerged to ridicule and condemn her. But in this life, no one spoke up.
For the first time, Liang Xin realized that Jing Shu, who rarely spoke, could verbally corner someone with her words once she chose to, metaphorically slapping his face repeatedly. Seeing the lively chat group fall instantly silent, Liang Xin’s face burned with embarrassment. Feeling trapped, he couldn’t help but ask:
"Then, what about Su Malie?"
Su Malie: "Please, we are old classmates, it’s true, and I help when I can. But I’m not your chauffeur, nor am I responsible for feeding you all."
Just when it seemed they had reached a deadlock, Wang Chao emerged, offering a turning point. Jing Shu remembered him. He had followed Zhang Lingling to sell cakes and had eaten Zombie-poisoned cakes for a few days. Surprisingly, he had suffered no ill effects upon returning home. She’d heard he was desperate to earn money because he now had a child.
Wang Chao: "@Jing Shu, I need to ask you a favor. Although the government provided subsidies after my child was born, his mother doesn’t have any milk. It’s okay for us adults to go hungry, but it breaks my heart to see my child starve. He’s almost one year old and, while not yet critically malnourished, he can only crawl. Hearing that you’re the manager at Stone Garden, I truly saw a glimmer of hope. I just want a chance, an opportunity for a trial job. I want to provide for my child and his mother. If the place is at West Mountain, I can definitely walk the two hours to get there; I don’t need any car."
Another person chimed in: "Me neither, I don’t need a car. My elderly parents at home eat red worm cakes every day. They’re malnourished and can’t digest them well. I don’t know how much longer they can hold on. As long as you can give me a job and some other food, I’ll do anything, no matter how hard or tiring."
Jing Shu had lived in the apocalypse for a long time.
What kind of life and death hadn’t she witnessed? At least eight hundred, if not a thousand, people had died before her eyes, and in every imaginable way. In this life, she herself had already killed a considerable number of people. She truly didn’t harbor much sentiment for her high school classmates.
But Jing Shu had a soft spot; she couldn’t bear to hear about children suffering.
In the apocalypse, children represented the only hope. In all those post-apocalyptic movies, if everyone else perished, a child would invariably survive. Oh, usually it would be two children, a boy and a girl. After all, the filmmakers knew that a single child couldn’t ensure the continuation of the human race.
Jing Shu said, "Alright. There are no cars. For those who want to work at Xishan Base, it’s too late today. So, here’s the plan: meet at Xishan Base at 10 a.m. the day after tomorrow. Everyone should think carefully about their skills and what they can contribute. Whether you get to stay or not will depend on yourselves."
"Thank you so much!"
Liang Xin: "Then... are we still having this class reunion?"
Su Malie: "Those who want to work should follow Jing Shu’s advice for the day after tomorrow. Meeting up at Xishan Base can count as our reunion, right? By the way, I need all kinds of live insects. I’ll exchange some food for them. If you’re interested, bring them to me at the gathering the day after tomorrow. However, I only accept live ones, preferably mutated, though ordinary ones are fine too. The more varieties, the better. I’ll only accept each type of insect once, so it’s best if you can find several different kinds."

chapters.title: Chapter 336: Preparing for a Big Move
chapters.content:
Chapter 336: Preparing for a Big Move
Someone asked, "An insect for some food?"
"Yes, provided I haven’t collected it before. To be fair, those who arrive at the base first get to trade with me first."
The chat quickly got flooded with these two topics. Jing Shu didn’t look any further but privately asked Su Malie, "Are you really collecting, or is it just for show? I wouldn’t believe it’s just to give some classmates extra food without beating around the bush."
Su Malie quickly replied with a tearful laughing emoji, indicating her helplessness. "You don’t know; the higher-ups have ordered it. They want to genetically reengineer these insects to make new food. But for now, only silkworm pupae, cicadas, and stick insects have proteins and fats that best meet human consumption needs. At worst, it involves massively breeding cockroaches and then turning them into compressed protein food, but progress is poor. Someone found Dark Pigment in some slowly mutating insects, which contains a lot of protein, so they thought of doing more research on it."
Jing Shu then remembered these experiments had started a few years ago. It was fortunate because these genetically mutated foods were developed during the extremely cold times when nothing else could be cultivated.
Turning cockroaches into compressed protein food... I’d really never heard of that. Wait, wait, holy shit—is that the protein food from my past life fried in corpse oil? Ugh...
Knowing the truth, Jing Shu almost threw up.
Jing Shu had no choice but to gulp down a few marinated eggs to calm her nerves. Still unsatisfied, she mixed all the marinated beef with Chili Sauce and ate a whole basinful, which made her feel a bit better.
Dammit, how many things is the government still hiding from us, the ordinary citizens?
Jing Shu didn’t dare to think about it and didn’t want to anymore. After discussing relevant matters with Su Malie, she began to practice with her Magic Cube.
The news reported another piece of bad news: a global catastrophic earthquake. It was likely not accidental and wouldn’t stop soon. It might even continue for a long stretch, like heavy rain.
"Due to changes in its trajectory and gravitational disturbances, the Earth’s rotation and orbit have become irregular, leading to seasonal disarray. According to the data, this global catastrophic earthquake isn’t due to external influences but is very likely a self-regulation within the Earth. The Earth’s previous rotational period was too fast; now it’s too slow. The two forces tearing at each other have created a swirling energy body. We are calling this seismic event the Tornado Earthquake."
"Simply put, once the Earth completes its self-regulation, the apocalypse will end. So please, everyone, hang in there for a while longer..."
That poor news broadcaster. They always had to find some reason to suggest the apocalypse was ending whenever there was a disaster. It almost made me believe it myself.
RUMBLE!
The ground began to shake violently again. The thunder and lightning outside didn’t weaken over time but seemed to be intensifying.
People hiding in the wetland park were gradually becoming restless. Some tried to leave and return home but were buried alive halfway. This frightened another group, who hurriedly came back. The story spread, growing more exaggerated with each telling—from one person to ten, then ten to a hundred. Eventually, the rumor was that hundreds of people were buried alive by the earthquake just by stepping outside.
I knew how this went. Although the Banana District hadn’t collapsed, if I said I wanted to go back and live there, I’d probably be buried under an avalanche of my family’s protests. Sometimes life is just that painful. I knew the Banana District wouldn’t collapse, but I couldn’t go back. I still had to pretend to be very scared; I wasn’t prophetic, after all.
「On the third morning」
When Jing Shu was about to leave, she met significant resistance. Only after eating over twenty pork and vermicelli buns and guaranteeing countless times that Su Malie’s bodyguards would protect her family did she finally get into Su Malie’s extended-length van and head to West Mountain.
Before leaving, Mr. Jing insisted that Jing Shu carry a black, backpack-like device he had designed over the past two days based on her ideas. In moments of danger, it would deploy, instantly shooting out long, thin claws that would anchor themselves to the surroundings like a spiderweb, and then catapult Jing Shu to safety.
"How is it?" Mr. Jing asked, his face full of anticipation.
Jing Shu wiped the sweat from her forehead. "Grandpa, this is a great device, but I’m afraid I’m the only one who can use it. It weighs dozens of kilograms; who else among you could carry it?"
Mr. Jing replied, "...This is just for you to try first. If it works, I’ll modify it and make it out of aluminum alloy. It will be much lighter."
Su Malie watched with envy as Jing Shu shouldered the large, black, frame-like backpack, remarking that if it were successfully developed, she would buy one too.
By the time Jing Shu and Su Malie arrived, more than twenty people were already waiting at the entrance of Xishan Base. It could be said that, aside from those who had died, most of Jing Shu’s high school classmates were present.
Due to the freezing weather, everyone was huffing, their breath misting in the air, stamping their feet, and some were even jogging in place to stay warm.
Seeing them again on the second day of 2025, they all looked much thinner, just like in my previous life. They were starting to become skin and bones.
Su Malie, as always, wore a bubble dress made from the latest high-tech thermal materials, complete with a matching hat and gloves. Her outfit was both fully functional and adorably luxurious. She exuded vitality, looking like a delicate pink princess, her attire as light and airy as a spring outfit.
In contrast, Jing Shu’s attire was far more ordinary: a white down jacket from before the apocalypse, paired with black leggings. For extra warmth, she had layered thermal underwear and woolen pants underneath. Before the apocalypse, this outfit would have marked her as a neat and tidy girl. But now, in the third year of the apocalypse, after experiencing droughts, floods, and earthquakes, to still be wearing such a pristine white down jacket...
It really screamed ’my family is loaded.’
"You’re finally here!"
"They’re here!"
Classmates in peculiar outfits hurried over, though a few were neatly dressed—a rare sight these days.
However, before they could chat for even a minute, Jing Shu’s phone rang. It was Yang Yang!
What should have been a lively scene of greetings instantly fell eerily silent. Everyone’s gaze shifted to Jing Shu. People instinctively stopped talking, unable to explain why, but there was a palpable fear of disturbing the big shot on her call.
Jing Shu frowned and answered the phone, an unsettling premonition washing over her.
"Hello?"
"Get ready, quickly. We’re about to pull off something big."
On the other end of the line, Yang Yang’s voice was a mix of suppressed yet irrepressible excitement. He sounded like a fierce beast trapped in a cage, roaring with all its might, desperate for freedom. It was the sound of something trying to keep its growls low before breaking out, fearing it might alert an enemy, yet unable to fully contain itself. He was clearly struggling to keep his emotions in check.

chapters.title: Chapter 337: The United States, This Fat Sheep
chapters.content:
Chapter 337: The United States, This Fat Sheep
The more Yang Yang tried to suppress his emotions, the more Jing Shu could detect the feelings behind his words. At this moment, Jing Shu was not so much excited as she felt like ten thousand grass-mud horses were galloping across the prairie!
For a moment, Jing Shu was extremely conflicted.
Originally, according to her plan, she had intended to spend at least a month or two getting ready before heading to the United States with Yang Yang and the others. That way, Jing Shu would be thoroughly prepared and could go to the United States with peace of mind.
The main issue was that the third year’s earthquake had just occurred, and everyone was still unclear about its implications. It was just like when the floods first started; they all assumed it would be over in a few days, or at most, things would calm down in a month or two. But many other dangerous factors were hidden within.
There were just too many accidents this year. For example, in her previous life, her Uncle, Aunt, and their family had died in an earthquake. In this life, Jing Shu was determined not to let them die. Fortunately, that particular incident wouldn’t happen for another six months, by which time everyone would be an "old hand" at dealing with such situations. So, she somewhat trusted her own judgment, but she still had to remember this when the time came.
Because they frequently had to evacuate and change shelters, this year felt more like a guerrilla war against the earthquakes.
Jing Shu also wanted to use the first couple of months to teach her family how to most effectively assess dangers during an earthquake. Although practice made perfect, and everyone would probably grasp the techniques thoroughly in a few months, Jing Shu still wanted to teach her family quickly to provide an extra layer of security for their safety.
I don’t want to go to the United States only to return and find everything lost. That would greatly diminish the meaning of my survival in the apocalypse.
Another factor was the unforeseen change in her parents’ jobs, which filled Jing Shu with all sorts of unknown fears about this third year.
In my previous life, I at least knew where the major dangers lay and could take some preemptive, almost prophetic, measures against disasters. But in this life, I’ve changed the main storyline, so the entire plot is different now. How can I leave Huaxia for the United States with peace of mind under such circumstances?
Moreover, the Magic Cube Space hadn’t upgraded. This meant I could carry far fewer items and couldn’t make adequate preparations. This trip to the United States is a rare opportunity; I have to make the most of it. I’d be worried sick if the Magic Cube Space still couldn’t be upgraded there...
All these concerns made Jing Shu fall into a somber silence, and the atmosphere grew tense. After a long pause, Jing Shu finally asked, "Didn’t you say it would be at the beginning of the year? The New Year hasn’t even passed yet."
The classmates around them pricked up their ears, listening intently to Jing Shu. They all remained quiet; some were shivering from the cold but didn’t dare to stomp their feet and disturb her.
"Because earthquakes are happening globally, and the United States is particularly chaotic due to them. Strike while the iron is hot. Now is the best opportunity. If we miss it, it will be much harder to fish in troubled waters once peace and prosperity return," Yang Yang’s voice was full of temptation.
Jing Shu considered it and realized he was right. These first few days of the earthquakes were indeed the most chaotic times for the entire world, including Huaxia, partly because the sudden earthquakes had disrupted every country’s plans.
Huaxia’s plan had naturally been to recuperate, focusing on agriculture to ensure everyone had enough food. But with the earthquake, planting was out of the question. First, they needed to settle the disaster victims, then lead people to evacuate, and also provide food supplies.
The government must have been at their wit’s end these days.
Russia, known for its fighting spirit, had organized groups to catch polar bears bare-handed. They intended to capture wild animals for food or breeding. However, an earthquake caused nearby snow-capped mountains to collapse, and avalanches buried some border cities. The plan to catch polar bears bare-handed had to be canceled because the earthquakes had buried the polar bears.
A mention must be made of Japan, which was already on the brink of extinction. Currently, less than 1% of its population was hiding in Mount Fuji. The earthquake had also disrupted their plans. To seek refuge, these daring people were flying in rumored perpetual-motion airplanes, supposedly prepared for the apocalypse. They stayed in the sky 24 hours a day, living their entire lives airborne. To avoid lightning, they had to fly at low altitudes.
Amidst the earthquakes, what was the United States doing?
Its citizens were holding banners, demanding a change of president and a share of the grain. The newly appointed president was busy seizing power and purging officials from the previous administration. State governments were clashing with private farm owners. Unlike in Huaxia, where grain reserves were state-owned and compulsory, food in the United States was controlled by private farmers. Major farm owners were forming alliances and fighting against citizens, the government, and anyone else who dared to eye their grain.
The intensification of these conflicts initially harmed the farmers’ interests because the United States government suppressed the rise in grain prices. This eventually led to all grain owners halting their operations.
At this moment, the United States, after two years of apocalyptic civil war, was already riddled with problems. But even a lean camel is bigger than a horse. Besides, the United States hadn’t yet reached the point of food scarcity. The first year had been a struggle for power, the second for profit. After great difficulty, the country had unified, but now the people were dissatisfied with the current welfare system and were still clamoring for grain distribution.
The American public had learned from international news that the whole world faced a dire food shortage. However, a few developed countries with sparse populations and strong industries, like the United States, still lived relatively comfortably. Yet, the day would come when their food ran out. Many large grain producers had already hoarded substantial amounts of grain and even formed gangs.
The United States had not restricted grain purchases. In fact, over these two years, under strong capital control, prices had not increased. But now, a situation had arisen where grain couldn’t be bought because private farm owners were hoarding it and refusing to sell.
For their own interests, citizens also began to clamor. They demanded that regardless of how farm owners handled their grain, the president must distribute enough food to everyone, or face replacement.
The newly appointed president hadn’t even warmed his seat before being overwhelmed by public opinion. What was worse, refugees from neighboring countries like Mexico and Cuba kept pouring in. The United States employed various methods, but there were too many refugees, and they couldn’t be stopped, especially since it was easy to sneak in under the cover of darkness.
So, every day in the United States, countless robberies and murders occurred!
This period in the United States could be described as the most chaotic time in its history. It epitomized the extreme pursuit of personal interests by the capitalist class, a situation where one couldn’t even step outside without several guns.
Compared to this, the six months in Huaxia when humanity seemed lost were mere child’s play. If Huaxia’s turmoil was a third-rate martial arts film, what was happening abroad was a sci-fi gunfight blockbuster—not on the same level at all. However, this also served to better illustrate the fact that public security in Huaxia was indeed good.
At this moment, the United States was like a big, fat sheep, with many neighboring countries eyeing it. If not now, then when?
"Alright, you pick a time. I’ll prepare as soon as possible," Jing Shu said seriously, having come to an understanding.
"The earliest would be the day after tomorrow morning. First, we’ll go to the Imperial Capital and assemble with the main team there, then depart from the Imperial Capital."

chapters.title: Chapter 338: Jing Shu’s Designated Role is a Doctor?
chapters.content:
Chapter 338: Jing Shu’s Designated Role is a Doctor?
"Because we are indeed in a rush, we need to seize this opportunity while it’s most chaotic to increase our chances of success."
This is even faster than I anticipated!
Jing Shu thought.
Ancient wars required three months of preparation for mobilizing troops and gathering provisions. Even modern warfare isn’t initiated so hastily. Preparing in just two days is insane! Last year, Yang Yang prepared for at least half a month before setting out, but this time, they’re ready to leave at a moment’s notice! Such life-threatening tasks naturally can’t afford a spontaneous departure; thorough preparation is crucial. Fortunately, I started preparing a month in advance, getting everything that could be readied in order. Now that we suddenly have to leave, it isn’t so rushed, yet I still feel unprepared! Or rather, not well enough prepared. There are still a myriad of things to handle, and I’ll have to request a long leave from the Medicinal Materials Association again. Two days just aren’t nearly enough.
Yang Yang paused, then whispered, "This time is different from the last. We weren’t sharing everything, and everyone was like brothers, looking after you. This time, the situation is more complex, so you need to bring everything you’ll need, including three days’ worth of food, a first-aid kit, a medical kit, and living supplies. Space is limited, so aside from unrestricted weapons and gear, you’ll need to carry your personal belongings yourself. Oh, and definitely bring the War Armor I gave you last time."
If the last mission was state-sponsored, with the country at least ensuring transportation to the United States, this one seems more self-initiated. Considering Yang Yang’s efforts to gather sponsorship everywhere and his having already signed a contract with Qian Duoduo for the mission to the United States, it appears we’ll be using an aircraft provided by these ’sponsors’ for this trip.
"Hmm." Jing Shu mentally reviewed the items she needed to bring.
There are quite a few, and none can be left behind... Sigh, what a dilemma.
"Bring more of that lifesaving medicine from last time. A big reason you’re able to come this time is because you have that medicine. The team’s positioning for you this time is Doctor and fighter. When it’s time to use the medicine, others will have to pay a price. We’ll discuss the specific rules once everyone assembles. Of course, your role can be adjusted at any moment, but this won’t affect the distribution of spoils, which is calculated based on individual Contribution Value. When the time comes, you’ll wear the latest tech War Armor and dazzle everyone!"
Jing Shu was speechless.
So, it turns out my chance to go to the United States is thanks to the Spiritual Spring. I actually thought my strength, comparable to a human tank, had garnered their attention. But it makes sense; in a world like the United States, riddled with bullets and explosions, no matter how strong an individual is, they can’t outrun a bullet or withstand a cannonball.
Yang Yang didn’t elaborate on how they planned to pull off this big job in the United States, and Jing Shu didn’t ask.
All my classmates are looking at me expectantly right now; it wouldn’t be right to reveal too much. Even if I have ten thousand questions, I need to hold them in.
She hastily ended the call and let out a breath.
Her classmates only saw Jing Shu hang up the phone and let out a breath. Unsure of what had happened, they didn’t dare to ask, only hearing her say she needed to go back and prepare.
Jing Shu said to Su Malie, "I’m sorry, something came up unexpectedly. I’ve made arrangements for these classmates, so I’ll have to trouble you to take me back first."
"I’ll go back with you. I’ll collect insects while you make arrangements for the people. Once that’s done, we can head back together."
That makes sense,
Jing Shu thought.
Otherwise, it would be too much running back and forth.
The insect collection proceeded quickly. Su Malie personally oversaw it, with students lining up one by one to exchange insects for food.
Wang Chao had arrived at eight in the morning. He hadn’t slept all night, spending it catching insects. By now, he had filled a large plastic jar with various kinds, including black beetles, evolved fleas, and new ’cockroaches’ that had emerged in the apocalypse, their dark bodies helping them survive in this harsh environment.
"Give him 20 steamed buns," Su Malie instructed. One bodyguard took the jar of insects, while another handed over the food.
The classmates looked at Wang Chao with envy.
He just caught some insects and got so much food! Su Malie really is foolishly rich and easy to deal with!
"These are repeats. Thirteen steamed buns for this lot."
Still pretty good,
the others thought."You have three evolved insects here. Fifteen steamed buns for these."
Mutated insects are more valuable!
they realized.
"You only get six steamed buns for these."
As the collection progressed, more and more of the insects brought were of repeated species, so the payout naturally decreased. The students who came later couldn’t help but feel regretful. However, Su Malie, being Su Malie, still symbolically gave each student at least one steamed bun.
Some ate their steamed buns on the spot, weeping softly. Others couldn’t bear to eat theirs and carefully wrapped them in tattered cloth to take back to their parents.
"I’ll come to Stone Garden every three days to collect insects. This will be a long-term arrangement. I also collect other living mutated or evolved plants and animals. If any of you have other sources, bring them over, and I’ll give you half a steamed bun as a referral fee."
And so, the matter of insect collection was settled.
Jing Shu led the remaining people from outside Xishan Base into its interior. Compared to her visit last year, much had changed. The base had expanded by about a third, and the magnificent Stone Gate alone was enough to leave everyone as awestruck as Grandma Liu entering the Grand View Garden for the first time.
Compared to the darkness and cold outside, a wave of warmth washed over them the moment they stepped through the Stone Gate. The stones underfoot radiated a gentle heat, and the entire first level of Stone Garden was filled with a soft, faint glow.
"Wow! These are called the Undying Lights! The entire Stone Garden actually has these luminous lamps! That’s incredible!"
"It’s so much warmer in here than at my home. Just being inside is a blessing."
The classmates were dressed in layers of whatever they could find—some in torn plastic bags, others in tattered cloth. To ward off the cold, they bundled up as much as possible. After two years of the apocalypse, a devastating flood, a super drought, periods where essentials were traded for Virtual Coin, and several evacuations, thick clothing was a rarity. As a result, everyone’s attire was a motley collection.
"Ah, Director Jing, you’re finally here! Please, come this way. Let me introduce you. This is Manager Li from the Human Resources Department."
"Manager Li, this is Director Jing. She has recommended a few students to see if there are any suitable positions for them. We don’t practice nepotism here; Director Jing is merely acting as a recommender." Housekeeper Cai, whom Jing Shu hadn’t seen in half a year, had clearly risen in status. He was now dressed in a black suit and white shirt, indicating his considerable position within Stone Garden. However, he still couldn’t help his flamboyant, mincing gestures.
Manager Li was a woman in her thirties, with a serious and meticulous demeanor. She gave a slight bow in greeting and then addressed the group, "The various positions in Stone Garden require corresponding abilities. Those with the necessary skills can become official employees on the second, third, or fourth floors. Those without can only work as temporary staff on the outer expansion projects. Here in Stone Garden, ability is what counts. Benefits and salary are determined by ability. Even if someone is recommended by a director, they will still be dismissed if they fail the daily assessments."
Jing Shu nodded.
It’s precisely because of this management system that Stone Garden is flourishing.

chapters.title: Chapter 339: Arranging for the Classmates
chapters.content:
Chapter 339: Arranging for the Classmates
The originally noisy classmates suddenly quieted down. Some felt pity for those who had tried to sneak in, while those who truly wanted to work hard were exceptionally motivated.
Manager Li continued, "In Stone Garden, we don’t care about background because the people working here are like the boss’s own family. Everyone has a background, so please adjust your attitudes accordingly. However, I still congratulate you for having Director Jing as a stepping stone. If it wasn’t for Director Jing, we wouldn’t have considered you, as Stone Garden already allocates most of its labor to the government and no longer needs high-cost temporary workers."
Jing Shu nodded.
Manager Li, from human resources, might speak arrogantly and strictly, but in the end, she managed to offer a slight compliment. She certainly knows how to handle people.
Many people sighed.
Manager Li extended a finger. "Stone Garden now has three categories of workers. First, permanent staff. They work ten hours a day, receive two meals of white rice and vegetables daily, can bring two family members into a single room, earn an extra Virtual Coin salary, get one day off per month, and undergo a weekly assessment. Those who fail will be demoted to temporary workers.
Second, temporary workers. They work ten hours a day, enjoy one meal of white rice and one meal of rice mixed with insect meal daily, receive a vegetable supply once every seven days, stay in a double room, may bring one family member depending on the situation, and receive no extra Virtual Coin salary or days off. Those who fail twice will be dismissed.
Third, government-recruited laborers. They work eight hours a day, receive two meals of red worm cake provided by the government daily, and are not managed by Stone Garden. However, anyone not performing well can be reported for a reward of 0.1 Virtual Coin."
"That’s the situation," Manager Li said, spreading her arms. "Those with special skills, stand on my right. Those with only strength, on my left. Special skills include excellent breeding, planting, handicrafts, and so on." Everyone quickly started moving; however, few possessed special skills.
Nevertheless, Manager Li was still somewhat satisfied. Pointing toward a large stone nearby, she said, "Every day, we need to transport many large stones like this and move them to places machines can’t reach. The assessment is to transport an irregular large stone to the other side within two minutes. Pass, and you can start work today."
Temporary work was all about physical labor. Many classmates gave up right away, but some, not wanting to miss out, decided to try. After all, the conditions for temporary workers were still good. For the same work, the government only provided two meals of red worm cake, while Stone Garden offered one meal of white rice plus a mixed meal. Crucially, one could live inside Stone Garden—a real sanctuary, free from earthquakes and deafening roars—and even bring a family member to live with.
While some people attempted to move the large stones, Manager Li turned her head, her interest piqued, and asked the few standing to the side, "What special skills do you all have?"
The first to speak was Mu Xiaoxuan. Jing Shu remembered her as the shy girl who had given her Bodhi Tree seeds. Mu Xiaoxuan now looked relatively clean and well-dressed despite her patched clothes, unlike the others with their gaunt, sallow faces.
"My family has traditionally grown various types of peach and fruit trees, as well as a wide range of medicinal trees," Mu Xiaoxuan said, speaking confidently about her planting skills. "I have extensive experience and skills. Even during the apocalypse, my family managed to keep a peach tree alive. I can also cultivate peaches in these times."
Manager Li clapped her hands, pleased. "You are exactly the talent we need! Go directly to the agriculture and planting department to report for work. You’ll become a permanent worker as long as you pass the weekly assessment. If you bring your family’s peach tree, you can even become a manager directly. I’ll have Xiao Wang discuss a partnership with you. Stone Garden has a better environment and can produce superior fruit. When the time comes, your family will still own the rights to the peach tree; we’ll consider it a rental."
Mu Xiaoxuan nodded excitedly.
The weather is too cold, and without electricity to power sun lamps at home, finding a good place for her peach tree is urgent, or they might all die. But she can’t bear to sell them; they’re crucial for her future food supply!
Her classmates looked at Mu Xiaoxuan with envy, never imagining that a poor peach grower from before the apocalypse could become so valued now.
"I ran a tailor shop and can make clothes," someone offered.
Manager Li shook her head. "Your skill isn’t professional enough. Next."
"I was a chef at a five-star hotel. Would that be suitable?" another asked.
"Go to the restaurant department to report and take the assessment," Manager Li instructed. "If you qualify, you’ll work as a temp. If one day your cooking surpasses that of the permanent staff, you’ll be promoted."
Surprisingly, Polygonum multiflorum was also among the crowd. Jing Shu hadn’t noticed him.
Who would have thought he’d be here looking for a job?
It was well known that Polygonum multiflorum’s family grew ginseng. After the apocalypse, the government had consolidated all medicinal material dealers and growers into the Medicinal Materials Association.
Jing Shu hadn’t seen Polygonum multiflorum for a long time. He had been absent from recent class reunions and group discussions. Now, he appeared with a face full of sorrow and melancholy, a stark contrast to the sunny, wealthy young man he once was. His clothes were a clear indication of his hardship: multiple layers wrapped around him like a beggar’s, all completely filthy.
"What about you? Any special skills?" Manager Li asked Polygonum multiflorum.
"I grow ginseng, perhaps?" Polygonum multiflorum said tentatively.
Manager Li looked at him doubtfully, voicing the same question Jing Shu had. "The government consolidated all medicinal resources and talent a year ago. Didn’t you report to the Medicinal Materials Association? They offer quite good conditions over there."
Jing Shu raised her eyebrows, finally speaking. "Yes, I remember seeing in the group chat that during the apocalypse, your family had a lot of ginseng. Even giving one root to the government could earn a lot of Virtual Coin."
Polygonum multiflorum ground his teeth. "Don’t mention those days," he said. "Things were indeed better when we traded some during the apocalypse, but then we were targeted. Last New Year’s, we were robbed—those people had guns and cars. They even threw Molotov cocktails, setting our house on fire, killed my family, and took all the ginseng..."
As he spoke these last words, his lips began to tremble. The memory conjured up his most painful recollections, and he seemed to plunge deep into them. He continued, his voice heavy, "I wanted to avenge my family. I reported it, and they checked massive amounts of data but said those people used dual identities and couldn’t be tracked down. I figured I had to better myself to have the ability to seek revenge, so I went to the Medicinal Materials Association. But unfortunately, ancestral heritage didn’t count, and my immediate relatives—my parents—had no such cultivation records, so I couldn’t get into the Medicinal Materials Association."
Jing Shu frowned.
So that was it. She too had been robbed last year. The perpetrators had died, but their accomplices, who had apparently used dual identities, were never found.
"But I really can cultivate," Polygonum multiflorum insisted. "My family has grown ginseng for generations. I’ve been involved with it since I was three years old..."
Just as Manager Li was about to say that she sympathized but still required a series of assessments, Jing Shu interrupted, "Manager Li, my classmate here really does grow high-quality ginseng. Don’t miss out on such talent."
Manager Li then asked, "Polygonum multiflorum, is it? Go directly to the medicinal cultivation department and report."

chapters.title: Chapter 340: You cannot go to the United States, it’s too dangerous!
chapters.content:
Chapter 340: You cannot go to the United States, it’s too dangerous!
The students’ gazes towards Jing Shu shifted once again. And they said Director Jing was indifferent? With just one sentence, she had arranged for Polygonum multiflorum to be placed in the well-funded, leisurely herbal planting department. It was common knowledge that in the apocalypse, there were no modern medicines left; everyone relied on Huaxia’s traditional herbal cultivation. These herbs were usually boiled multiple times and not discarded until they were turned into medicinal residue for further refinement.
After some thought, Manager Li continued, "In this case, our Stone Garden is indeed in urgent need of various medicinal herbs, as well as talent with rich planting experience and medical understanding. You will start by working under Mr. Zhang as his assistant. Stone Garden has brought over all the traditional Chinese medicine preparation equipment from before the apocalypse. Now, not only do we need to plant herbs, but we also need to manufacture medicines."
"Thank you, thank you!" Polygonum multiflorum exclaimed.
To follow an experienced traditional Chinese medicine doctor as an assistant—wouldn’t that be like having a master? After learning for a year or half a year, I could become a junior doctor too!
With Polygonum multiflorum’s job settled, some were envious and others jealous. Understanding some medical skills and medicinal herb management made one highly sought after, no matter where they were.
Afterward, Manager Li inquired about the specialties of the remaining few people and shook his head in disappointment. Either their professional standards were not up to par, or Stone Garden did not need them. After all, Stone Garden’s own people were more professional in economic and personnel management.
Those who were not hired felt very discouraged and simply went to move stones. Indeed, a few more people qualified. If they couldn’t be full-time workers, being temporary ones wasn’t bad either.
Soon, the temporary stone movers were also decided upon, with six individuals completing the assessment. However, one person remained in the field, still struggling to move stones, eventually slumping to the ground, gasping for breath, unable to continue.
"The stone-carrying assessment is now over. Those who haven’t passed are unqualified," Manager Li announced. "Assignments outside Stone Garden involve physical labor. If you can’t even carry these stones, you’re not suitable. Even if you somehow managed to get in, you’d likely be reported and end up working for nothing." He then declared the end of the temporary worker assessment.
The one person left in the assessment field was none other than Wang Chao. Those who could do it had already finished; those who couldn’t had given up. Only Wang Chao refused to admit defeat.
"I... I haven’t eaten in a couple of days. I have no strength," Wang Chao begged for another chance. "Trust me, I’m really strong. Just give me a steamed bun now, and I’ll have strength right away."
Manager Li shook his head. "At 120 pounds, you’re too frail. Even if you forced yourself to do temporary work, you wouldn’t last three to five days. It’s not that I don’t want you, but you’re likely to die doing this kind of work. I can’t be responsible for that, nor can I disappoint Director Jing."
It turned out that Wang Chao used to be a chubby man weighing 180 pounds. However, in the past two years, after getting married and having children, he had given all his food to his pregnant wife. Working beyond his capacity daily had wrecked his body, and now he couldn’t even do physical labor.
Wang Chao then turned his pleading gaze towards Jing Shu. He had never been like this before, not even when eating the toxic red worm cake. But when it came to providing for his child, he finally succumbed to the harsh reality.
Jing Shu waved him over. "If you can’t do it, don’t force yourself," she said. "If you push yourself to death, what will happen to your wife and children?"
Wang Chao hung his head and finally nodded. "I... I don’t have any other special skills."
Jing Shu frowned. She remembered that back in high school, she had bought game scripts Wang Chao himself had made. Using them had made gaming a breeze, as the scripts ran automatically and completed all tasks. So, she couldn’t help but ask, "Wang Chao, I remember in high school you made game scripts and worked with software and systems."
Wang Chao said cynically, "Yes, but that’s utterly useless now. Stone Garden needs job skills helpful for survival in the apocalypse—food, living, that sort of thing. I don’t have hacker abilities either. Besides, the national network is down. There isn’t enough broadband for new systems, we have no servers, and the government isn’t authorizing any new network infrastructure."
Jing Shu paced back and forth a few steps. "Manager Li, does Stone Garden have an internal LAN and servers?"
Manager Li nodded.
"How about this," Jing Shu proposed, "I’ll privately hire Wang Chao for Stone Garden’s engineering and network department. I’ll commission him to create custom scripts and macros for Stone Garden, developing a unique network management system for us. He can apply big data templates to manage check-ins, roll calls, and the distribution of personnel salaries and benefits. It could even handle intelligent statistics and script execution for the second, third, and fourth tiers, freeing up significant human resources."
Manager Li’s eyes lit up. "I know a little about scripting. Does that mean once it’s running, it can automatically complete pre-set procedures? If so, we really need such talent. Director Jing, I hope to bring this Wang Chao into our headquarters for better management."
"Okay, no problem," Jing Shu agreed.
Another regular position was filled. Wang Chao clenched his fists in excitement, bowing silently to Jing Shu.
The remaining students, seeing that even the ’useless’ Wang Chao had found a good position, crowded forward, eagerly chattering about their own skills. Unfortunately, there was no longer any role that could utilize them.
With time pressing, Jing Shu hurriedly left with Su Malie after settling her classmates’ arrangements.
「...」
"What? You’re going to the United States?!"
Two days flew by. Jing Shu had meticulously organized everything at home. To better ensure her family’s survival, she used every trick up her sleeve. She even tirelessly found various pretexts, while everyone was home, to drag her family out to experience firsthand the booming thunder and the rumbling of earthquakes.
At last, her family was somewhat less ignorant about the earthquakes that had been occurring that year.
To ensure her family’s safety, Jing Shu eventually set up personal locators and emergency alert devices. Her family was unaware that technology had advanced to such a point that simply wearing a bracelet could solve these safety concerns. Little did they know, these were all preparations Jing Shu had made in advance at great cost.
Even Mr. Jing’s inventions had come into play, and Jing Shu’s heart could finally rest a little easier.
Next came the preparations for her trip to the United States. Jing Shu had packed her belongings early on and continued to add new items. During this time, she returned to the villa, cleared some space in her dimensional storage, and secretly stashed more supplies in a rented large warehouse. This was to ensure that even if she couldn’t return, her family would have enough food and clothing to survive the apocalypse.
Time was tight, and just as everything was finally in order, Jing Shu encountered an unexpected communication issue. She was used to being independent, so when she announced her intention to travel far, like a child seeking permission, she faced strong opposition from her entire family.
"No way! It’s the apocalypse now. The country’s trains, planes, and other transportation have all stopped. How could you possibly cross the ocean?"
"It’s too dangerous over there! The television shows wars every day, bullets flying everywhere. It’s too risky."

chapters.title: Chapter 342: Jing Shu’s Companion to the United States
chapters.content:
Chapter 342: Jing Shu’s Companion to the United States
Jing Shu’s figure wasn’t bad; it was just that the bulletproof vest was inherently bulky. Adding an oversized padded jacket on top made her look much more rotund. Her feet sported a herdsman’s style, her legs a rural style. If not for Jing Shu’s pretty face, Yang Yang probably couldn’t have stood looking at this mismatched fashion.
"I’m not changing. Let’s go; I’m warm," Jing Shu said. Afraid of both the cold and death, she hadn’t even put on her modified bulletproof denim hat yet. Besides, making herself look less attractive could also help ensure her safety in the United States. If Jing Shu dressed normally, her beauty might attract all sorts of trouble, and she would probably spend her days dealing with people who had ill intentions toward her. After all, in such an open place, nothing was certain.
Yang Yang shot her a strange look and seemed to want to say something, but ultimately said nothing.
Jing Shu also hesitated.
If Yang Yang dresses so lightly, he’ll freeze to death in the United States. If he tries to borrow my padded jacket then, I definitely won’t lend it to him,
she thought.
Fortunately, Yang Yang drove a military pickup truck that could accommodate Jing Shu’s baggage. It took them another half hour to reach the twenty-year-old airport. Wu City’s new airport was currently being used as a shelter and had no runway available for flights. Much like Xuanwu Lake Park, the new airport, having been submerged for a year, was now full of trash and mud, making it unsuitable for flying.
The old airport was tiny, with only a 400-meter runway and a row of low-rise buildings. Abandoned for many years, it was overgrown with assorted weeds that could survive the apocalypse and teeming with nests of insects; the road leading to it was also full of potholes. When Jing Shu and the others arrived, a road roller was still going back and forth, compacting the surface to ensure the plane wouldn’t have any issues during takeoff.
Jing Shu couldn’t shake the feeling.
Holy shit, is this reliable?
she thought.
This airport is so rudimentary; can I really entrust my life to a plane?
The aircraft parked on the runway wasn’t a pre-apocalypse passenger plane but a very small private jet.
This is... Qian Duoduo’s private jet! So wealthy, so luxurious!
Jing Shu realized.
"Let’s hurry," someone urged.
Jing Shu’s luggage was indeed excessive. Only the baggage containing her weapons and equipment, along with her oversized personal suitcase, could be stuffed into the hold. Another large suitcase simply wouldn’t fit, so she had to carry it on board by hand.
Once on board, Jing Shu realized for the first time how poverty had once again limited her imagination.
The interior of a plane can actually look like a luxurious room, not just be filled with rows of cramped seats!
Yang Yang whispered to Jing Shu, "This is Qian Duoduo’s luxurious private jet. It has a capacity for thirteen people. Excluding the two pilots and one flight attendant, there are our two companions traveling with us to the United States, plus three administrative personnel going to the Imperial Capital on business. So, including us, our companions, the administrators, and the crew, there are ten people on this flight to the Imperial Capital."
As Jing Shu stepped onto the plane, the first thing that caught her eye was a catering bar. A tall, non-Huaxia woman stood there, smiling, nodding, and greeting Jing Shu and Yang Yang. The bar displayed some precious apocalypse-era foods. This spot was analogous to where flight attendants on regular planes would stand to welcome passengers; it served the same greeting purpose on this private jet.
Walking further in, they reached an area comparable to the first-class section of a regular plane. To the right side of the private jet was an adjustable single massage bed. To the left was a dining area with four genuine leather chairs and a dining table, all generously spaced and comfortable—certainly not the cramped quarters of a regular flight, and even more luxurious than first class.
A person was already lying on the single bed, while another person and a dog occupied two of the chairs.
These two must be my companions for the journey to the United States,
Jing Shu surmised.
Further ahead was another cabin door. Beyond it, Jing Shu saw a three-person sofa and a small dining area with a table for two and two sofa chairs. Three people were already seated there.
They must be the ones heading to the Imperial Capital,
she figured.Comfortable warm lighting and soothing background music, combined with the tall attendant’s greeting, almost made Jing Shu feel as if she were back before the apocalypse. This illusion of tranquility shattered when the attendant handed two packages to Jing Shu and Yang Yang.
"Take these two parachutes. Be ready to jump if there’s an emergency," the attendant said in fluent Chinese.
Jing Shu’s smile instantly froze.
EMMP... that’s terrifying,
she thought.
After handing her extremely heavy suitcase to the attendant for storage, Jing Shu led the docile yet curious fat chicken and followed Yang Yang to a four-person table. They were clearly split into two groups: the four of them heading to the United States, and the trio bound for the Imperial Capital.
"Well, well, you’re late," a man, skinny as a monkey and sitting in one of the chairs, said provocatively. "So this is the amazing woman you mentioned, the one who caught Zero? She’s pretty good-looking, but that outfit..." He exuded an arrogant and showy vibe.
He was stroking the dog beside him while sipping a beverage provided by the plane. Jing Shu frowned but didn’t speak. Instead, she noticed his knuckles were very broad; he had a pair of rough, large hands that seemed mismatched with his slight frame.
Yang Yang smiled nonchalantly. "This is Monkey, one of the top Scouts in All China. He has an extra skill in bone shrinking, allowing him to open any door. His main duties in this mission include reconnaissance, counter-reconnaissance, drawing enemy fire, and executing stealth attacks. Role: Scout/assassin, rated B+."
"And don’t let that quiet and obedient-looking little dog beside him fool you. It’s actually a Tosa fighting dog, as ferocious and cruel as a Devil—a breed banned in most countries. It has killed many escaping fugitives. The dog is rated C, but combined with Monkey, their overall rating is A-."
Yang Yang then pointed to the person lying on the single bed. "This is Hao Yunlai, champion of ’Survival Path.’ He has extensive wilderness survival experience and an exceptional ability to mimic various sounds. If necessary, he can also disguise himself. His sixth sense gives him an unusual perception of danger. With him around, we’re bound to turn misfortune into good fortune. His role is Assistant/Logistics, and because of these special abilities, he’s rated A. It’s said that even if no one else from a mission makes it back, Hao Yunlai always will."
Hao Yunlai ruffled his fluffy hair and, with a sleepy expression, gave Jing Shu a nod. He seemed the epitome of a ’laid-back youth.’
This was the first time Jing Shu had witnessed the nation’s "talented people" firsthand.
So such quirky abilities truly exist,
she thought. However, after witnessing Su Malie’s incredible luck, she looked at this ’Hao Yunlai’ and mused,
Bringing Su Malie along might have a similar effect. But... Su Malie is so wealthy now; she probably has no need for missions like this. She truly is a favored child of destiny.
Monkey listened to Yang Yang with a grin, nodding in approval. He then raised an eyebrow, pointed at Jing Shu across from him, and asked, "So, what about her? You haven’t introduced her yet. And what’s the deal with that combat support pet of hers? It only has two legs?"
The fully armed fat chicken was indeed a puzzling sight, and its steel helmet only added to its imposing, if bizarre, presence.

chapters.title: Chapter 343: Arrival at the Imperial Capital
chapters.content:
Chapter 343: Arrival at the Imperial Capital
Jing Shu unbuttoned her thick cotton-padded jacket, feeling a bit hot.
She had sworn that she wouldn’t take it off even in her sleep, yet she wanted to break that oath as soon as she stepped outside.
The fat chicken beside her started dozing off again, so Jing Shu could only take out its nest, spread it on the ground, and under Monkey’s astonished gaze, the fat chicken comfortably settled into it.
Yang Yang found himself at a loss for words, unsure of how to introduce Jing Shu, because he didn’t have complete information about her. To say Jing Shu was impressive was an understatement. As far as he knew, Jing Shu had dealt with Zhetian’s third-in-command, Shangguan Jun, and Zero. She had killed those who ended up dead, while those who survived were still working for the government, selling information. But where her impressiveness lay, he couldn’t quite articulate. It seemed Jing Shu was a jack of all trades, master of none; strong but lacking finesse. To say she wasn’t impressive would be wrong, though, since the incident at West Mountain where she dismantled a bomb bare-handed was truly amazing. Jing Shu was a difficult person to categorize.
"Just call her Mirror; you all know her deeds. She also possesses a rare special medicine that, whether for gunshot or stab wounds, when applied, prevents inflammation and speeds up recovery. This time her role is as a Doctor/Assistant. Her strength is formidable. She will be the one to don the War Armor, and she can also handle the firepower. Based on the fact that at critical moments she has life-saving medicine, her overall strength rating is B."
Those headed to the United States each had a codename, without revealing their real names; Yang Yang’s codename was Goat.
Jing Shu figured it out: Hao Yunlai could sense danger at crucial moments, she herself had life-saving medicine for such times, one was a Scout, and then there was Yang Yang, seemingly weak and unable to carry much. Was this Wu City squad really just a soy sauce supply team?
But then again, what exactly was Yang Yang’s role? Jing Shu had been in contact with him for quite some time but always felt that Yang Yang had an unreal, mysterious aura. Moreover, Yang Yang completely shattered all the beautiful fantasies Jing Shu had about military men—strong, capable fighters, possessing a sunny righteousness—none of which Yang Yang possessed.
Monkey was somewhat disappointed. "All in logistics, contributing less, getting less. This trip seems like it’s going to be a loss."
Yang Yang smiled mysteriously without saying a word.
Monkey perked up again. "But you haven’t explained this thing yet. Are there really mutated animals after the apocalypse? I heard that they want to bring one to the Imperial Capital."
After thinking for a moment, Yang Yang said, "This is the chicken her grandma brought for her to lay eggs on the road, for Mirror to replenish her body."
Monkey stared for a while, scrutinizing the fat chicken’s posture, then burst into laughter. "HAHAHA, I’m dying here! Off to the United States to do big things, and she’s carrying a chicken with her. But this chicken really is huge, eh? If we ever get into a tight spot, letting Hao Yunlai roast a chicken wouldn’t be too bad. That said, it’s just a chicken, isn’t this a bit much? Making a custom steel helmet for it? You made me think it was a battle pet or something."
The fat chicken was unhappy after hearing this. After Jing Shu gently kicked it a few times, it said, "My chicken is a fighting chicken, different from the rest."
Fat Chicken had to be vindicated, she thought. Otherwise, if it achieved a merciless victory in the future, it would make everyone so surprised they’d want to eat their own jaws in amazement.
Monkey not only sprayed his drink back into the cup but all over the table. Unable to hold back his laughter, tears streamed down his face as he said, "Then you better watch out for my Ah Huang. It’s well-known for loving chicken. It’s behaving well with me around, but without me, who knows, it might just steal and eat your chicken. Better keep an eye on your chicken, or if it gets eaten, don’t say I didn’t warn you."
A dangerous glint appeared in Yang Yang’s eyes. With a smile, he took out a long-missed syringe and carefully drew up the drink spilled on the table. He was just about to speak about wanting to try injecting the drink into someone’s body when Jing Shu parroted his warning back at him, "Then you better watch out for my fat chicken. It’s well-known for loving various brain matter and eyeballs. It’s behaving well with me around, but without me, if something provokes it, it might retaliate by pecking a dog’s eyes blind and eating its brains. Better keep an eye on your dog, or if it gets eaten, don’t say I didn’t warn you."
"Well, let’s just wait and see then." Monkey’s smile gradually froze. He had the foreign beauty clear the table, then closed his eyes and said nothing, while Yang Yang pouted, "Stealing my thunder."
「...」
The plane took off quickly. The runway was very short; if it hadn’t managed to take off, it would have crashed into another building. When the plane started racing down the runway, the turbulence had Jing Shu doubting her life choices. Thankfully, it took off without further incident.
The flight from Wu City to the Imperial Capital took five hours. A RUMBLING sound still filled their ears; thankfully, it wasn’t real thunder—otherwise, the plane wouldn’t have dared to take off. They also experienced a few more frightening shudders along the way, but at last, they safely reached the Imperial Capital.
Jing Shu felt as if her delicate heart had taken a strong blow. Even the fat chicken, initially comfortable, was no longer calm, clinging tightly to Jing Shu’s feet. Even Monkey’s Ah Huang was restlessly barking in anxiety.
Hao Yunlai, however, slept like a log. Yang Yang reassured them, "Hao Yunlai not reacting means the flight isn’t dangerous."
"There’s some logic to that..."
But using Hao Yunlai as a human barometer for danger, was that really a good idea? What if he failed?
They had a meal at one point—a luxurious apocalypse stir-fried rice with green vegetables, potatoes, a sprinkle of green onions, soy sauce, and diced ham. Everyone enjoyed it immensely. Even Jing Shu nodded her approval. The taste was indeed quite good. However, there was only one bowl per person, and Jing Shu’s stomach was still growling with hunger after she finished hers.
Unable to bear it after half an hour, Jing Shu took out a basin and bagged instant noodles. She asked for some boiling water and prepared two packs of noodles with five eggs and two sausages. The others looked on enviously, salivating. Under immense pressure, Jing Shu finished off the meal in three minutes, even slurping up all the soup. The rich fragrance of her instant noodles wafted throughout the plane.
It had been a pleasant journey until Jing Shu interrupted it. Even Hao Yunlai woke up, sniffed the air, and said, "Mirror, is that Unified Soup Master Japanese Tonkotsu Ramen you’re eating?"
Jing Shu gave a thumbs-up. "You could tell just by the smell."
"Didn’t we just eat?" Monkey grumbled, constantly swallowing his saliva. "And you can still eat so much, all at once. I wonder what you’ll eat when we get to the United States."
The aroma surrounded him, and Hao Yunlai tried to hypnotize himself:
I can’t smell it, I can’t smell it, I’m sleeping...
Yang Yang pulled out some meatballs his grandfather had fried for him and snacked on them occasionally. Jing Shu offered him some, but Yang Yang shook his head. "You eat too much. Better save some for when we get to the United States, just in case."
Thus, the group had a very uncomfortable arrival in the Imperial Capital. Three administrative staff members hurriedly left, while Jing Shu and her three companions finally reunited with their counterparts from the Imperial Capital.
"Rest for half an hour. After the plane is refueled and checked, we’ll take off again. Once everyone is here, we’ll discuss the detailed plan, division of labor, and the rules for this operation," Yang Yang was saying as another group of people boarded the plane.

chapters.title: Chapter 344: Imperial Capital Captain Zhen Nantian
chapters.content:
Chapter 344: Imperial Capital Captain Zhen Nantian
The air inside the airplane suddenly grew tense, and an instant silence fell.
Jing Shu was actually curious about her companions for this trip to the United States. The stronger their abilities, the higher the chances of success, which meant greater safety. Of course, this also meant she could be less of a burden and avoid constantly needing rescue, unlike Tang Seng, who always cried, "Wukong, save me! Bajie, save me!"
After all, this mission is half-public, half-private, so everyone might have different objectives, but powerful teammates are always a necessity.
Naturally, she would cooperate if possible, but if not, Jing Shu was prepared to go it alone.
The first to approach their group was an incredibly muscular man, over two meters tall. Most striking were the copper wall and iron wall-like wrist and knee guards he wore. Each step he took made the airplane floor go THUD, THUD, THUD, and his powerful muscles looked ready to burst through his clothes. Despite this, he carried two iron balls connected by a chain, walking at the very front.
The muscular man nearly blocked everyone else from view. He glanced toward the back cabin, frowned, and turned his head to say, "There’s not enough room back there."
Just then, the man who had left a deep impression on Jing Shu stood up. He wore a shit-green jumpsuit and an orange hat—an incredibly eye-catching, almost impossible-to-miss combination. But his most striking feature was his tongue!
Jing Shu had lived for quite some time, yet she’d never seen anyone with such a long tongue—it stretched out a good eight or nine centimeters!
The crucial part was that he could flick it out like a snake tongue. He quickly flicked his ’snake tongue’ twice, then patted the equally stunned Monkey on the shoulder with a smile, saying, "You guys go sit in the back. There isn’t enough room for the five of us here."
Strangely, despite his long tongue, his speech was completely normal! What’s more, his voice was magnetic and very pleasant, which couldn’t help but remind Jing Shu of Orochimaru’s tongue from Naruto.
The front cabin of the private plane was spacious, equipped with a four-person sofa, a dining table, and a bed. The back cabin, however, only had two individual seats, a smaller dining table, and a three-person sofa.
The spot where Jing Shu was sitting was indeed comfortable and much more spacious than the back cabin.
"First come, first served, bro," Monkey said. "I’ve already put my luggage away and don’t want to move it. Besides, there are five seats in the back too." Just as he finished speaking, something shocking happened. The long-tongued man swiftly darted out his tongue and licked Monkey’s face a few times. Monkey and Ah Huang, who was beside him, instantly went into a combat stance. Tension flared, and both sides looked ready to draw their swords and crossbows.
Jing Shu saw some unidentifiable liquid on Monkey’s face.
Yang Yang stood up. "Let’s go to the back. It’s true there isn’t enough room for all of them here."
This made it evident that Yang Yang was likely the team leader from Wu City for this mission. Otherwise, Monkey and Hao Yunlai wouldn’t have stood up so readily to move to the back cabin without a word of protest.
It was then that a young man Jing Shu hadn’t noticed before spoke up. He casually patted the tall, muscular man and the long-tongued man on their shoulders and said calmly, "We’ll sit in the back. First come, first served."
Compared to the first two, with their rather distinctive features, this young man was only about 1.7 meters tall. He had short black hair that covered his eyebrows, giving him a cool yet very clean appearance. He looked to be only in his twenties—
too young, Jing Shu thought.
Her first impression was that he was ordinary: ordinary all-black clothing, ordinary height, an Asian male who wouldn’t stand out in a crowd.
But upon closer observation, Jing Shu was surprised. His eyes were pure and clear.
They say the eyes are the windows to the soul. Monkey’s eyes always radiated flamboyance, the muscular man’s eyes were filled with ferocity, and the long-tongued man’s eyes held provocation and frivolity. But in this young man’s eyes, there wasn’t a trace of emotion. His expression was neither sad nor joyful. His way of speaking was declarative, almost a command.
Jing Shu sensed that this ordinary-looking, clean-cut young man with short black hair was actually the leader of the Imperial Capital’s team. His presence was too overpowering! It was like the Demon King, reigning over the world, utterly indifferent to all living beings.
Indeed, with just a few calm words from the black-haired young man, the escalating tension vanished instantly. The muscular man and the long-tongued man turned and walked to the back cabin.
A girl in a short skirt followed quietly behind them without saying a word. The long-tongued man then extended his hand with a bow, "Beautiful Miss Ling, please join me at this two-person table for a delightful rendezvous."
The girl’s cheeks flushed. She quietly declined and quickly sat down in a corner of the sofa, remaining silent. The long-tongued man flicked his tongue twice more and then sat down beside her.
At that moment, the black-haired young man turned to Yang Yang and said, "Once we’ve stowed our luggage, we can discuss the plan for this mission."
Yang Yang nodded. Jing Shu and the others returned to their original seats. Hao Yunlai could now go back to sleep.
Lucky him,
Jing Shu thought.
Jing Shu stroked her chin, her interest in these companions for the trip to the United States growing.
She had a feeling that everyone on this trip was either outstanding in some specific aspect that would clearly benefit the mission, or they possessed formidable firepower and individual strength.
The Imperial Capital team had indeed brought a lot of luggage. The last person to board had to make several trips back and forth. Since the private plane’s cargo hold was too small, they ended up piling all the luggage inside the cabin. This made the originally spacious and comfortable area feel much smaller, cramping everyone together.
The plane finally took off again. Once the Imperial Capital team had settled in with their luggage, all nine people gathered around the large dining table. Yang Yang took out a map and pointed to a location in the United States.
"Our first destination is Sacramento in the United States, a city on the border with Mexico. We’ll start from this border city and gradually move inland. Our second stop will be Austin, the capital of Texas, and so on. Besides our two teams, another team will enter from the Saska side. We will all rendezvous later to complete the mission."
Yang Yang continued, "The direct flight to Sacramento is estimated to take twelve hours. This gives us twelve hours to discuss the mission objectives, detailed plans, division of labor, and procedures. But before all that, we need to understand each other’s abilities and our respective roles within the team. This will help us better leverage our collective strength to complete the tasks assigned by our superiors. What do you all think?"
The black-haired young man nodded. "We are a team. How we compete against each other back home doesn’t matter. Abroad, we must be united. Let’s start with me. I am Zhen Nantian, the leader of the Imperial Capital team for this mission. My role is ’All-Rounder,’ and my current rating is S-level."
It was a brief introduction, yet it left Monkey and the others dumbfounded. Even more surprisingly, the long-tongued man started to say with a smile, "Captain, you’re being too modest. Why not..." But he abruptly fell silent because Zhen Nantian had merely glanced at him.

chapters.title: Chapter 345: Who Uses the Mecha, I Want to Challenge
chapters.content:
Chapter 345: Who Uses the Mecha, I Want to Challenge
Jing Shu squinted at Zhen Nantian, the team leader from the Imperial Capital. She suddenly felt as if the gossipy man’s words had been forcibly stuffed back down his throat. Moreover, she was curious about this Zhen Nantian; he must have something special about him, though unfortunately, it wasn’t explained.
However, everyone surely has their hidden trump cards and wouldn’t reveal everything at a first meeting.
And that name, Zhen Nantian... wasn’t it a bit too imposing and valiant? Despite his average height and small build, the energy he could unleash was extraordinarily powerful.
After Zhen Nantian finished his introduction, Yang Yang, also a team leader, began his. "My codename for this mission is Goat, and I’m the team leader of the Wucheng Team. My role is a special operative and intelligence officer, currently rated A+."
This special operative role was worth pondering. Jing Shu stroked her chin, thinking. After a moment, she realized Yang Yang’s explanation was tantamount to saying nothing at all. So, his ability was A+? What special skill allowed him to reach that level? From the defiant look in Monkey’s eyes, it was clear he wasn’t convinced either. He seemed to be wondering how a weakling like Yang Yang could have such a high rating.
"In the future, please call me Snake Spirit. My mission role is assassin, and my ability involves using my self-developed poisons, currently rated A. I also have my mutated Little Python, rated B+. Therefore, my combined rating is A+." As he spoke, something wriggled on Snake Spirit’s neck. Jing Shu had initially thought it was a tie or a scarf, but then the thing suddenly moved. It turned out to be a snake!
Jing Shu knew about the Tai Ban Snake; it ranked seventh among the world’s top ten most venomous creatures. Each bite released enough venom to kill 150 people, and it was typically a large snake. This Little Snake was a mutation? Regardless, its venom was undoubtedly far more potent than that of the Five-step Snakes she was raising.
The muscular man said disdainfully, "Stop being so dramatic. Your self-made poison is just your saliva."
Monkey turned pale upon hearing this and rushed to the restroom to wash his face several times. This made Snake Spirit roar with laughter, and even Snake Spirit’s own teammates kept their distance from him.
Jing Shu, however, squinted at the snake on Snake Spirit’s neck, her thoughts drifting. Snake meat tasted similar to eel—lean, firm, and chewy, without any unpleasant odor, not fishy like fish or gamey like duck. Snake meat was most delicious when briefly blanched in a clear soup hotpot, and snake skin and bones made a flavorful broth. Having eaten plenty of Five-step Snake, she was curious to try Tai Ban. She wondered if Snake Spirit had cultivated this species extensively. Should she try to get on his good side and ask to sample some other varieties? But seeing how Snake Spirit lovingly caressed his little pet snake like a treasure, Jing Shu wasn’t sure if suggesting stewing or braising it would get her bitten. Sigh, how could she even bring it up? Jing Shu felt a bit wistful.
Then it was the turn of the last member, the one who had acted as a porter. Bald grinned and rubbed his head. "Everyone can just call me Monk. I was expelled from my temple. Fortunately, a discerning benefactor recognized my talents, allowing me to go to the United States for this mission and some personal matters. My role is to provide muscle and infiltrate Zhuangyan Temple in the United States. My rating is A."
Next was a shy-looking girl. Jing Shu noticed her bare legs and ultra-short skirt. She was elegantly eating cookies, sporting an adorable, fluffy bob haircut and a short puffer jacket, exuding a playful, cute, yet shy aura.
Comparing the two women from the teams, it was easy to judge who was more stylish based on attire alone. Jing Shu couldn’t help but feel inadequate. She was afraid of the cold, afraid of dying, and had an enormous appetite—she could eat a whole basin of rice in one meal... Sigh, they were both women, so why was the difference so vast?
"I-I’m Lingling," the girl said. "In the mission, I’ll be the sniper and provide fire support. I’m currently rated A-. This is my companion, a parrot capable of deep reconnaissance, rated C+. So, my combined rating is A." As she spoke, Lingling uncovered a small cage and released the parrot inside. Once freed, the parrot immediately began flying wildly around the airplane, squawking.
"Silly bird, silly bird, come and get me!"
"Spotted a silly mutt, spotted a silly mutt! Silly mutt, come and get me!"
"Spotted a bunch of morons! Report: a bunch of morons spotted!" The parrot landed on Lingling’s shoulder, repeating over and over, "A bunch of morons spotted."
Everyone: ...
The fat chicken opened its narrowed eyes, nudged Jing Shu’s feet, then CLUCKED and laid an egg before falling asleep again. Immediately, Snake Spirit’s strange cry rang out. Pointing at Jing Shu’s chicken, he asked tremulously, "Wh-what is that thing?"
Only then did everyone focus their gazes on Jing Shu. She felt a blush creep across her face. "It’s just a chicken."
"AHH!" Snake Spirit quickly retreated to a corner, utterly terrified. "Wh-why would you bring that thing? Is it your combat pet?"
Snakes are afraid of chickens.
Yang Yang chimed in from the side, "She brought it to lay eggs for her nourishment."
Everyone’s expression turned peculiar. Even Zhen Nantian, who was always expressionless and showed neither joy nor sorrow, sized up Jing Shu with curiosity.
Jing Shu said, "...Actually, this chicken is a fighting chicken. It’s very strong in combat."
She was trying to salvage the situation, but seeing their expressions, she knew no one believed her. Fine, all sorts of pets had their uses, except perhaps the fat chicken... But in this apocalypse, whose fat chicken was more valuable? It laid over twenty eggs a day!
However, this also brought Jing Shu some relief. No one was interested in her fat chicken. There were many oddballs here, which meant the chicken was safer; revealing a bit of its ability wouldn’t lead to it being captured for research.
Finally, it was the big guy’s turn. The chair he dragged over looked like a child’s booster seat with him sitting on it.
"Everyone calls me Tan Ke. My role in this mission is as the front-line tank and human steamroller. My strength lies in powerful bursts, but my weaknesses are slow reflexes and movement speed. I’m currently rated A. I was originally supposed to wear the exoskeleton Mecha this time. Unfortunately, I heard the Mecha was obtained by the Wucheng Team’s captain, so its assignment is up to you. I’d like to ask, which member have you assigned it to? I want to challenge them to see who is more suitable to wear the seventy-kilogram Mecha. Of course, the Mecha is yours, and you have the right to decide who ultimately undertakes this important responsibility."
His words were quite provocative, the implication clear:
Even if I win the challenge, you can still let your chosen person use the Mecha, but everyone is watching.
Jing Shu raised an eyebrow.
So this is what they mean by ’trouble finds you even when you’re not looking for it.’ Is the Mecha really that popular? Although she liked it too, to be honest, if things got dangerous, she’d rather someone else wear the Mecha and take the brunt of the enemy fire.
Yang Yang said with a smile, "To tell you the truth, she’s the strongest person I’ve ever seen. Although she hasn’t received any training or learned techniques for using her strength, wearing the Mecha is genuinely an easy task for her. So, let me introduce our team member: codename Mirror. She possesses Special Healing Medicine and will be the one using the Mecha on this mission. Her roles are Doctor and Assistant, rated B."

chapters.title: Chapter 346: Arm Wrestling
chapters.content:
Chapter 346: Arm Wrestling
At first, Jing Shu thought her B rating wasn’t bad. After all, Monkey, with so many abilities, was only rated B+, and with Ah Huang, their combined rating was just A-. She had no idea that the moment the Imperial Capital team arrived, they would completely overpower the Wucheng Team.
The captain of the Imperial Capital team, Zhen Nantian, was rated S-rank, two levels higher than the A+ rating Jing Shu thought Yang Yang deserved. In contrast, the opposing team was uniformly A-rank. Even more outrageously, Snake Spirit’s Little Python was rated B+, higher than her own rating, even with her Special Healing Medicine!
Of course, this might be because the Little Python could poison an entire group with a single bite, giving it significant killing power, while she could only save a few people, a considerable limitation. Regardless, bringing up her B-rank rating again felt somewhat humiliating.
But Yang Yang seemed quite proud...
Tan Ke’s chair creaked as he settled into it. Frowning, he pointed at Jing Shu and said, "Just a B-rank woman? A woman without fast-twitch muscle fibers, whose muscle ratio isn’t even 30%, and you’re telling me she’s strong? Are you questioning my professionalism? In that case, let’s have a contest."
