Jing Shu fed him a drop of Spiritual Spring. While doing so, she sent a message to Yang Yang to rendezvous, briefly explaining, "I think I’ve found the data for the formula here. Meet up with me!"
She continued to drag Hao Yunlai forward.
After a good while, Hao Yunlai’s bleary eyes fluttered open, and he immediately cried out, "Painful, painful, PAINFUL!"
"Where does it hurt?" Jing Shu stopped and turned to look at Hao Yunlai, whose eyes were still hazy with confusion.
"Help me up," Hao Yunlai said painfully.
Jing Shu hauled Hao Yunlai up. He painfully straightened his body, revealing his scraped buttocks and thighs. The pain made him limp.
"Look, I’m injured. I might not be able to walk."
Jing Shu was speechless.
"AHEM." Jing Shu said, embarrassed, "Things were too urgent just now, so I just dragged you. How about you switch positions so I can drag you from the other side? Something urgent came up."
"Okay." Hao Yunlai obediently took off his clothes and spread them under the sack. "You can go now."
Something felt odd, but she couldn’t quite put her finger on it.
Jing Shu dragged Hao Yunlai at a frantic pace. With only his head sticking out, Hao Yunlai was frequently struck by a dozen or so swinging bundles, accompanied by THUDDING sounds. He quickly retracted his head back into the sack and tore a small hole to observe their surroundings.
Jing Shu felt a pang of regret. It seemed she wouldn’t be able to stuff anything more into her storage space for the time being. Wasn’t there supposed to be another secret room full of supplies? Still, having a conscious Hao Yunlai with her was, ultimately, for safety.
The robot moved incredibly fast, always staying just slightly ahead of Jing Shu. It guided her with a clear target in mind: the very tall tower.

chapters.title: Chapter 438: The Fraud
chapters.content:
Chapter 438: The Fraud
By the time Jing Shu arrived, Yang Yang was already there; he had found a white convertible from somewhere. It resembled a tourist sightseeing car and was loaded with all kinds of supplies; it was clear he’d had a bountiful harvest. In contrast, Jing Shu appeared somewhat disheveled, carrying over a dozen parcels from which something odd would occasionally fall out.
For instance, an artist’s painting had just fallen out. Jing Shu, in a rush, punched and ruined it. Instead, she treasured the emptied crystal picture frame as if it were precious, placing it on Hao Yunlai’s head before they continued on their way.
Yang Yang parked the car outside the tower, and Jing Shu placed her parcels in it before looking up at their ultimate target—the tower.
This tower was the main reason Jing Shu and her group dared not approach. It was a military defense tower with a two-kilometer perimeter. This meant the interior of Rhein Manor was effectively a vacuum zone, so the tower only targeted external invaders.
Although Jing Shu didn’t quite understand it, tests conducted by Snake Spirit and her group indicated that the tower housed many advanced intelligent weapon systems. These systems would formulate attack plans based on an intruder’s size and shoot down any moving, non-living entities that approached.
They had previously considered using armored vehicles or tanks, but those couldn’t get near the area. Not to mention, next to it was North America’s largest Zhuangyan Temple, which also possessed considerable armed forces. However, even if they managed to sneak in, they would have no way to take down the tower from two kilometers away.
"Where is Hao Yunlai?" Yang Yang looked around but couldn’t find him.
"I’m here..." Hao Yunlai poked his head out, looking disheveled. His neck was adorned with various pieces of jewelry and the crystal picture frame. His left hand held what looked like a very expensive candlestick, and his right, an antique diamond plate. He stood up with a CLATTER, and many small trinkets—items that had fallen out on the way and been forcefully stuffed back onto him by Jing Shu—also tumbled to the ground. Hao Yunlai dared not ask about them, nor did he dare discard them.
"You’ve worked hard." Jing Shu pulled Hao Yunlai out and removed all the miscellaneous items. In the process, she retrieved the high-tech "Eternally Burning" candlestick and "Indestructible" diamond plate, as well as the crystal picture frame, and placed them all into the white convertible.
...
"That’s the situation. We can tweak our Plan B now," Jing Shu said as she and Yang Yang entered the high tower. Hao Yunlai, who was practically crippled, still hobbled into the tower after Jing Shu; after all, who knew what dangers might lie within.
"We can’t take that tycoon’s word at face value. Things are probably not that simple," Yang Yang suggested. "Let’s try to shut down this tower’s operations first. That should allow the others to get in easily and save us a lot of trouble."
The tower had over a dozen levels. Each was just over ten square meters in size—very small—and designed to house weapons. Each level had an intelligent mainframe, and the weapons on each level were different, with different operational areas and ranges.
With the chip, Jing Shu could indeed move about freely, but these mainframes were not under her control. She had no authority to shut them down, nor were there conventional options like ’unplugging the power’ or ’cutting the wires.’
Jing Shu considered smashing the machines, but a warning appeared: forcefully destroying them would trigger a self-destruct sequence or something similar. So, she came up with another method.
"A 120mm Chasing Gun? I’ll dismantle your entire turret and base. Let’s see you chase anything then!"
"A 12-barrel, largest-caliber rocket launcher? Turning this over to the state would earn at least 500 Contribution Value."
"A Single-wing reconnaissance early warning aircraft? This is a real treasure. With this, we can conduct surveillance from home anytime we want."
"A terminal high-altitude area defense system? This one’s a bit troublesome, but if I remove its booster, it’ll be useless, right? Wait, it looks like the surrounding materials can also be taken back for research. That way, each of us could get at least 200 Contribution Value."
"Look, these Tracking Guns embedded in the fortress walls are equipped with the latest technology. They’re perfect as new weapons for us."
At first, Hao Yunlai didn’t understand what Jing Shu was up to. But as he watched her skillful dismantling—twisting off some parts, forcibly yanking out others—his jaw gradually dropped in astonishment.
They couldn’t disrupt the mainframe’s operation, but the rules didn’t say they couldn’t remove the weapons! No, wait... these weapons were ’naturally detaching’ themselves!
Initially, Jing Shu just wanted to stop the tower from operating. But later, she actually started estimating the value of the components, even having Old Yang and the disabled Hao Yunlai act as laborers, moving the items down piece by piece...
When Plan B was modified on the fly, with Zhen Nantian taking control of the overall situation, Lingling providing sniper cover from outside, and Snake Spirit leading Monkey inside, they found Jing Shu had nearly dismantled all the tower’s components. Only the mainframe was left, humming:
"Searching for Chasing Gun..."
"Searching for rocket launcher..."
Snake Spirit drove the white tourist vehicle, carting load after load of materials to the outskirts of Rhein Manor. Tan Ke was outside to receive them and was responsible for then transporting these supplies to freighter number 808 on the Canal.
Finally, Jing Shu and the others reached the tower’s secret chamber. Prompted by the robot’s incessant urging, they used a chip to unlock it. Cautiously pushing open the door, they were all wary of deception.
An icy chill washed over them. On the ground lay a pool of blood that had not yet congealed and a corpse, gruesomely battered by a blunt object. Upon closer inspection, it was the middle-aged man, dressed exactly as he had appeared on the screen.
Of course, besides the corpse, the room was full of confidential documents, important materials, and the target of Jing Shu’s team’s current mission: the newly developed life-extending formula!
Yang Yang darted forward and immediately gathered all the documents into his arms. Jing Shu, meanwhile, stuffed the jumbled test tubes and all sorts of potentially useful experimental materials into a sack, while Monkey swept up the supplies along another wall.
CLICK!
The sound of another click echoed, accompanied by the flash of a camera.
Jing Shu and Yang Yang spun around. A robot in the corner had raised its manipulators in a V-sign. Its screen displayed images of their recent actions, starkly contrasted with the corpse on the ground.
"Confirmation of Master Job Sibus’s death. Executing death protocol. Sounding alarm. Initiating Rhein Manor final self-destruct sequence..."
"Death confirmation transmitted. Identifying murderers. Initiating global manhunt. Reward: 1,000,000 pounds of food..."
"Requesting assistance..."
At that moment, an insidious alarm blared throughout the entire Rhein Manor, followed by the THUMP-THUMP of signal guns.
"BEEP BEEP BEEP..." An urgent, life-threatening countdown began.
This sound... I’m all too familiar with it,
Jing Shu realized.
Isn’t this the same sound as when the entire house exploded before?
Even Hao Yunlai clutched his head, muttering, "Danger, danger, very dangerous..."
"So, he lured us here to make others believe he was really dead!" one of them exclaimed.
The man’s motive was simple: to make Jing Shu and the others his scapegoats! A tycoon who faked his own death—how could he possibly collaborate with people robbing his villa’s supplies? Moreover, he would never share this secret with anyone. Dead men tell no tales.

chapters.title: Chapter 439: Mom, It’s You This Time
chapters.content:
Chapter 439: Mom, It’s You This Time
So, from the very beginning, the tycoon had stated that the entire Rhein Manor was a gift to them. However, it was a gift meant to accompany them on Huangquan Road. He intended to kill everyone from the start, including his own "corpse."
Not destroying the body and eliminating all traces would mean waiting for specialized personnel to inspect and discover the discrepancies. The best method is to destroy all evidence,
he must have thought.
A tycoon who would go to such lengths to fake his own death, and who was so desperate for others to believe it, must have encountered immense trouble himself.
But the immediate problem for Jing Shu and the others was the robot’s announcement: Rhein Manor had initiated its self-destruct sequence.
Just how powerful will this explosion be?
Jing Shu wondered.
Monkey said anxiously, "Run! Hurry and get Snake Spirit to drive over and pick us up!"
"Locking all floors. Closing all passageways. Sealing all exits," the robot intoned.
"What do we do? We can’t get down?"
In the blink of an eye, Jing Shu had swept everything, large and small, from the secret room into her Magic Cube. There was no time for a closer look. Hearing that all exits were sealed, she punched the robot, sending it flying.
Just as she suspected, they were trapped on the eighth floor of the high tower. Unable to go up or down, they were stuck on this level with all exits sealed! There were no windows up here at all. With all exits closed, even jumping was impossible.
They might as well prepare to die,
she thought grimly.
"What do we do? What do we do?"
Yang Yang quickly posted their current situation in the group chat, telling the others to evacuate first. He asked Snake Spirit to be ready for a pickup and told Lingling to request immediate support.
The formula is in hand, but now we have no way to get out alive!
Although Yang Yang had sent out a distress call, they still had to find their own way to escape. As the BEEP BEEP BEEP grew more urgent, everyone felt as if their lives were being roasted over a fire.
Jing Shu furrowed her brow. She could use a weapon port to place explosives outside in mid-air. This would blast a huge hole in the tower’s special material, enclosed structure. That way, they could jump down.
Although the eighth floor is a bit high... I still have a parachute or something similar,
she considered.
The only question is, how long until this countdown bomb explodes?
"The longer the delay before detonation, the more powerful the bomb," Yang Yang explained to everyone. "It’s like a controlled demolition; he must have planted explosives in many locations. If he truly intends to blow up the entire Rhein Manor, we still have some time to escape. Dozens of seconds have passed without an explosion. This means he’s not just trying to eliminate us ’murderers.’ After all, Rhein Manor has many secrets it wants to keep hidden.
If it were me, I’d also plant more explosives to ensure the whole manor is reduced to rubble. As for whether we can escape... heh.
"
"But if we don’t get out of this tower soon, we’re done for!"
Monkey, agitated, went up and shook the robot violently. "Mirror, don’t you have a weapon chip? Can’t you control it? Can you tamper with the program?"
Jing Shu shook her head. Just as she stepped forward, ready to blast a hole through one of the walls from the outside, Hao Yunlai suddenly knelt, clutching his head in extreme pain.
"Danger... very dangerous..."
Suddenly, Hao Yunlai screamed.
"What’s going on?" Jing Shu was somewhat stunned.
It... couldn’t be, could it?
But that seems unlikely, doesn’t it?
Jing Shu mused. She knew some people were born with incredible luck. She had witnessed Hao Yunlai’s luck before in the Underwater World.
How to describe it... He seems to influence the luck in his vicinity, or perhaps makes the luck of all nearby creatures extremely poor, thereby allowing himself to escape disaster.
But what is this situation? There’s no external interference. Instead, we’re trapped on the eighth floor, about to face an explosion—not just a small one, but potentially the entire Rhein Manor. Hypothetically, could Hao Yunlai actually prevent the entire Rhein Manor from exploding? Given its sheer size, surely his luck isn’t *that* heaven-defying, is it?
At a time like this, I can’t rely on anyone else,
Jing Shu resolved.
It’s safest to keep control in my own hands.
"I have a way!" Jing Shu couldn’t afford to hold back; they needed to leave immediately. But no sooner had she spoken than the entire earth suddenly quaked. The tower shook violently, and Jing Shu was slammed against a wall. Fortunately, she was wearing her thickest clothing and a helmet, so although she was hit, she was actually quite all right.
"It’s an earthquake!"
"Quick, grab onto something! The tower is going to collapse!"
Panicked, Jing Shu quickly added more thick layers of clothing. She was still trying to find something to secure herself when the entire tower collapsed!
Amidst the chaos, Jing Shu heard Hao Yunlai’s faint voice, "Mom, it’s you this time. It seems I really have to go down and meet you."
Huh? Is Hao Yunlai sleep-talking?
Jing Shu wondered.
BOOM! A deafening crash. Jing Shu’s entire body ached, and her head throbbed as if it would split.
How tall is an eight-story tower? Jumping down without protection would surely be fatal.
But Jing Shu’s situation was even more dire. The entire tower had come crashing down, causing the room they were in to crack apart, with steel bars and rubble flying everywhere. It was almost as bad as jumping from an eight-story building.
Jing Shu had luckily taken cover in a corner and, miraculously, was not seriously injured. Also miraculously unharmed were Yang Yang and Hao Yunlai. Monkey, however, wasn’t so fortunate. Half his body was crushed under the rubble, his legs nearly useless. Jing Shu hauled him up. Monkey’s agonized screams made her ears ring.
Jing Shu looked up at the broken tower.
So that’s why we weren’t too badly injured,
she realized.
Who would believe it? A tower of such height had snapped in the middle. Miraculously, the lower and upper sections acted as buffers, sandwiching the eighth floor right in the center. This spared them from the worst of the impact, preventing Jing Shu and her group from being crushed to death.
If this was due to Hao Yunlai’s bizarre luck, then that’s truly terrifying!
Hao Yunlai had fainted completely again. Yang Yang, coughing, got to his feet and looked up at the sky. A rumbling sound approached—it was a helicopter. The national rescue team had arrived!
A ladder was lowered. They just needed to climb up to escape. They had to hurry! Rhein Manor could explode at any moment!
"BEEP BEEP BEEP BEEP..." From a corner, the robot, pinned under debris, still managed to emit a faint sound.
While the others were distracted, Jing Shu swiftly stored the robot in her Magic Cube Space.
If it’s going to explode, let it explode in there,
she thought. However, once inside the Magic Cube Space, it stopped moving completely, as if it had jammed.
Perhaps this robot is the only way to contact that tycoon,
Jing Shu mused.
In that case, it absolutely must stay in the Magic Cube Space.
Regardless, since the tycoon gave me such a huge ’gift,’ I’ll definitely have to return the favor someday—with something even bigger,
she vowed.

chapters.title: Chapter 440: The Self-Destructing Rhein Manor
chapters.content:
Chapter 440: The Self-Destructing Rhein Manor
So even if space was at a premium, Jing Shu cleared some room for the robot, believing that with a clue, they wouldn’t have to worry about not finding Job Sibus.
At the same time, Jing Shu was also filled with anticipation. The luxurious and precious materials at Rhein Manor this time, things she couldn’t have imagined in her previous life, were merely trinkets to the wealthy—items they couldn’t take with them.
When she finally found him, Jing Shu was eager to see what other, even more precious, assets he possessed.
None of the team members on the perimeter knew what Jing Shu was up to. Once they learned of the helicopter evacuation, they quickly retreated. The priest, having just arrived, led the nuns in a final sweep, and Jing Shu saw everything clearly.
From a distance, the priest proclaimed compassionately, "I will pass over you and strike down the humble beings of Egypt, and calamity shall not touch you and destroy you. The divine spirit said, do not be afraid; go forth, my brave children, and redeem them!"
...
The ladder dropped down, and Yang Yang jumped onto it. Below, Jing Shu tied the nearly incapacitated Monkey and the unconscious Hao Yunlai together, allowing Yang Yang to secure them to the ladder with a rope. Monkey and Hao Yunlai were then suspended above like hanged ghosts.
"Hurry up and get on!"
Yang Yang hooked his foot on the ladder, hanging upside down mid-air, as the helicopter hovered at varying altitudes.
"BOOM! BOOM!" Just then, explosions began from the center of Rhein Manor! Mushroom clouds rose into the sky, waves of heat rushed at them, and at the same time, colossal waves blasted the Underwater World upside down. The toughened glass instantly shattered into deadly shrapnel, flying everywhere and slicing through anything in its path!
The central explosives acted like a fuse, igniting the surrounding explosives in a domino effect visible to the naked eye. The ground began to shake ferociously, and mushroom clouds exploded throughout the vast Rhein Manor. The enormous noise made everyone’s ears ring, rendering them unable to hear anything being said.
Jing Shu had already packed the goods from the eighth secret chamber cleanly. Taking advantage of their distraction, she stuffed some more items into her storage space—items of undetermined nature but seemingly high-end. She would sort all these materials out later.
Jing Shu had wrapped the packed goods into seven or eight sacks, roped them together, and slung the entire chain over her shoulders. After returning the identity chip to the corpse, she took a sudden leap and grabbed onto the dangling Yang Yang.
"CRACK!" With a crisp snap, Yang Yang’s arms were broken from the impact of Jing Shu’s jump. Jing Shu, with all her parcels, weighed several hundred kilograms. Yang Yang’s perseverance kept him from being pulled down, his grip steadfast on the ladder.
Yang Yang’s face turned pale with pain, sweat pouring down, but he didn’t let out a scream.
Meanwhile, Jing Shu seized the last section of the ladder. "That was too close. Wait a moment. When it’s safer, I’ll set your arms for you."
Yang Yang: ...
"RUMBLE! RUMBLE!" The explosions grew closer. In just a matter of seconds, they spread from the center. Once the last person was on board, the helicopter surged upward tens of meters with all its might. Then, it throttled up fully but couldn’t ascend any more! It was overweight!
DRONE... The helicopter’s engines roared with the strain; the packages hanging below, like a string of kites, were suddenly yanked dozens of meters into the air.
"BOOM!" With a tremendous explosion, the self-destruct point at the base of the high tower finally detonated. An immense wave of heat surged towards them.
Jing Shu felt as if her feet and face were about to catch fire.
A mushroom cloud churned up beneath her as the helicopter rapidly left the scene, but it couldn’t avoid the lowest packages being affected by the blast.
A package broke away and fell.
Jing Shu’s heart ached for a long time, wondering what precious item had been lost.
Jing Shu clung tightly to the ladder, not daring to let go. The helicopter also started to wobble; it was severely overloaded. They had said they were coming to rescue a few people. And while there were indeed only a few individuals, they also brought along a string of packages. The person at the very bottom was truly fierce, managing to carry such a large collective bundle without being strangled by it. In any case, the helicopter was quite unstable with the extra seven or eight hundred kilograms of weight.
The rumbling continued unabated.
Just how much explosives had Job Sibus planted?
The billion-dollar Underwater World was completely demolished, with even the outskirts affected.
The vast Lailin Manor was reduced to ruins in this explosion, all its buildings shattered. From aboard the helicopter, Jing Shu saw the once magnificent manor now a vast sprawl of wreckage, spreading rapidly to the side beneath the dense smoke.
"COUGH, COUGH."
The helicopter flew toward the Canal. After a few minutes, it finally escaped the blast area, meeting up with Tan Ke and his group. At the same time, several more helicopters appeared in the sky, and many armored vehicles emerged from Zhuangyan Temple, indicating the severity of the incident.
Just as Jing Shu had anticipated, the robot successfully relayed a message. Reinforcements were arriving en masse, though it was unclear if they were from the Government or some other faction.
After dropping off Jing Shu and her group, the helicopter hastily fled. Jing Shu and her associates successfully boarded cargo ship No. 808 awaiting them and took advantage of the chaos to escape.
It was expected that news of billionaire Job Sibus’s death would soon make headlines in the United States. Meanwhile, the priest, with the few remaining nuns, went to tie up loose ends. In New York, the priest still wielded considerable power, although he remained a mystery to this day.
Tan Ke, looking at the horrific scene, said angrily, "Shouldn’t we report that Job Sibus isn’t actually dead and that this incident was his premeditated fake death?"
Zhen Nantian, frowning, took out a social media app and handed it to Jing Shu. There was no choice; both of Yang Yang’s hands were broken, and both Monkey and Hao Yunlai were unconscious, leaving Jing Shu as the only able-bodied person.
Zhen Nantian said, "You are wanted by the United States. Now the whole country knows, and your photos are all over the major social networks. Many forces in the US definitely want to find you, as some formulas are in your possession. Of course..."
"If you were presumed dead in this explosion, things might be a little better."
"So, we can’t report or disclose anything. Anyone with the slightest connection to this matter will be implicated."
Snake Spirit frowned. "Those other helicopters saw ours just now, but they didn’t have time to intervene. Besides, if they inspect the site and don’t find any bodies, they’ll still be suspicious."
Lingling wiped her gun. "There will still be a grace period. As long as we escape back to Huaxia, they won’t be able to find us."
Jing Shu stood up, clenched her fists, and rubbed her hands together, then added, "Of course, we can’t let others know the billionaire is still alive in this world. I’ve saved the robot’s chip. If we can find this man in the future, his wealth will be all ours!"

chapters.title: Chapter 441: The Fat Chicken That Uses Others’ Heads as Its Nest (First Update)
chapters.content:
Chapter 441: The Fat Chicken That Uses Others’ Heads as Its Nest (First Update)
The Fat Chicken clucked at her feet, and Gou Tuizi fully agreed with Jing Shu’s statement.
Speaking of this, when Jing Shu first boarded the 808 cargo ship, she saw a peculiar sight: Tan Ke’s dense hair had been methodically pecked, strand by strand, into a chicken’s nest. The Fat Chicken was comfortably nestled there, two black chicks perched on her back.
It was hard to imagine that a 2-meter-tall, muscular man, who had exuded such a powerful aura when Jing Shu first met him, now had chickens nesting on his head.
The Fat Chicken was large, and Tan Ke was strong. This combination made it look as if Tan Ke were wearing a brownish-yellow, feathery chicken hat. And what a hat it was—an old hen that actually moved, weighed over forty kilograms, and was so plump it fanned out like a giant parasol, completely obscuring Tan Ke’s vision.
Jing Shu: "..."
"Get down from there, quickly..." When Jing Shu had gone to the Underwater World with Yang Yang and Hao Yunlai, she had only left the Fat Chicken with Tan Ke for a moment. How had it come to this?
Tan Ke smiled sheepishly. "I was about to move some supplies and was afraid of losing your chicken, so I put her on my shoulder. Unexpectedly, she made a nest on my head and refused to come down. But she did lay quite a few eggs for me, as if it were a trade."
A chicken bartering eggs for comfort!
With that, Tan Ke carefully took out eight eggs from his pocket and handed them to Jing Shu. After all, at 50 Contribution Value each, these eggs were treasured by the entire team. A chicken that laid only one egg a day wasn’t particularly precious, but one that could lay more than twenty, or even thirty eggs a day—providing essential nutrition for the whole team—was invaluable. Although Jing Shu herself consumed most of the eggs.
Not to mention, the eggs laid by the Fat Chicken were exceptionally delicious. Anyone who tasted them once craved them again, even at the exorbitant price of 50 Contribution Value.
"Since the Fat Chicken gave them to you, you should keep them," Jing Shu said. She knew that whenever team members used Contribution Value to exchange for eggs, the others would immediately ask Jing Shu to make them fried eggs, egg custard, or scrambled eggs. Only Tan Ke carefully hoarded his, saying they were for his little sister. (Jing Shu, to her credit, didn’t charge an extra processing fee for these dishes; she was quite merciful.)
Jing Shu shot the Fat Chicken a look, letting it know it should behave.
So, the Fat Chicken neatly arranged Tan Ke’s hair with its beak, even using its saliva to give him a new "hairstyle." Then, with its chicks in tow, it flew down and, like a loyal lackey, followed at Jing Shu’s feet, behaving with exceptional docility.
Tan Ke grumbled, "Oh, I *really* have you to thank for the new hairstyle."
The Fat Chicken clucked smugly, "You’re welcome, you’re welcome."
The teammates looked on with envy at the Fat Chicken. When they first encountered it on the plane, many had laughed at Jing Shu for bringing a chicken along. Yet, how many times over the past few months had they relied on its eggs to survive? This was true even though everyone also paid a handsome sum in Contribution Value for them.
Even dogs reputed to be among the world’s ten fiercest breeds, whose owners had boasted they loved eating chicken, were now mere underlings to the Fat Chicken. Furthermore, in the Underground Black Market fights, the Fat Chicken showcased its combat prowess. It won ten bouts for Jing Shu, earning hundreds of thousands of Black Market Coins. These victories also enabled everyone else to win money and exchange for supplies.
The Fat Chicken’s contributions were plain for all to see. Consequently, people were inevitably more indulgent towards it, even pampering it, which had made the chicken quite arrogant.
...But back to the previous topic.
Lingling’s hand, which had been cleaning her gun, paused. She lowered her head and said softly, "I’m afraid we might never be able to return to the United States again."
"Why?" Jing Shu asked in surprise. If there were many wealthy Qian Duoduos in the country with a demand for foreign goods, it would still be possible for them to venture out once a year, provided there was ’sponsorship.’ The United States was like a fatted sheep, ripe for harvesting at intervals. Although conditions grew increasingly dire over time, the truly ’fat sheep,’ in the end, were like salted duck eggs—rich and practically oozing oil!
Truth be told, Jing Shu was quite envious of those tycoons with private planes. Although the fuel cost for a single flight was exorbitant, in the apocalypse, if one could make such a trip to plunder resources, fuel costs would be negligible compared to the sure profit, rich as oil.
If the Magic Cube Space reached Tier 13 or higher, it could definitely hold a small airplane,
Jing Shu mused.
Then, even if I came out alone to other countries, I could gather more supplies. After all, resources will only become scarcer.
She couldn’t help thinking that acquiring airplanes or attack helicopters wouldn’t actually be too difficult; she could even steal them if necessary. However, the lack of a place for storage and maintenance posed a significant problem, making them inconvenient. Otherwise, during the Underground Black Market supply runs, she might have risked smuggling an attack helicopter into her Magic Cube Space, taking it out when needed and stowing it away when not.
Ultimately, the space was just too small. It was hard to imagine how she had managed to raise chickens, farm, and store apocalypse supplies when the Magic Cube Space was initially only 4x4x4 meters—a mere 64 cubic meters.
"The Magic Cube Space is only at Tier 8. There’s still a long way to go," Jing Shu sighed. Although she had been practicing with the Magic Cube lately, advancing to Tier 9 would still take some time. Firstly, with her teammates around, constantly pulling such a large cube out from her pants wasn’t exactly proper. Secondly, she was simply too busy and couldn’t find enough time.
After returning home this time, Jing Shu planned to dedicate herself to practicing with the Magic Cube Space. She aimed to upgrade it to a sufficient size before the fifth-year migration, which was crucial for her upcoming plans.
Lingling explained reservedly, after pulling out her smartphone and opening the official website to translate for Jing Shu and the others—who, being unable to read English, never paid attention to United States Government news and were thus unaware of recent major events.
"We’ve been put on the United States’ blacklist," Lingling began. "Now, not only have our appearances been exposed, but the fingerprints, facial scans, and iris scans we registered back in Austin have all been disseminated through a Government-issued wanted notice. We’re globally wanted, with substantial rewards posted. Any information leading to us is worth 50,000 pounds of food. If someone manages to capture one of us—for instance, Bo—and turns them over to the United States Government, the reward is 300,000 pounds of food!"
Tan Ke’s eyes widened. "We’ve been exposed? Impossible! Didn’t we just make off with millions of pounds worth of stuff? The thing is, we only took a third of the rare minerals. The bulk of it was taken by that despicable fraudster, Dr. B."
Snake Spirit raised an eyebrow. "Surely we wouldn’t be on the Government’s blacklist for just that small amount of material?"
"You probably don’t know that recently, in Austin, hundreds of thousands of people in the entire castle have contracted a fatal disease! The amount of blood they cough up each day could circle the Earth three times. Concurrently, a large number of high-ranking officials and farm owners have died.
Every day, bodies are stacked as high as mountains. This has incited greed in many, who have subsequently looted resources, leading to numerous bloody incidents. Simultaneously, on the outskirts, many people have suffered from mild radiation exposure and fallen ill. Austin is now in total chaos and has become a veritable ghost town, which is having a profoundly negative impact on the United States."

chapters.title: Chapter 442: Jing Shu Wanted by the United States Government
chapters.content:
Chapter 442: Jing Shu Wanted by the United States Government
"Although people had sensed something was off with the city walls for some time, the issue couldn’t be detected due to the new materials used by Doctor B. Moreover, on the very first day Doctor B disappeared, the city’s upper echelon was quite anxious. This was because Doctor B’s leadership was crucial for matters concerning both the Concentrating Stone and the Life Water.
It wasn’t until two days later that the Austin City high-ups finally conducted a thorough investigation, and the truth came to light. It turned out that all of it was a scheme by Doctor B and Tis. We were also involved in digging tunnels and secretly transporting materials away. How else could millions of pounds of supplies vanish in the blink of an eye?
So, it was only natural that they included all of us in the bounty, and it was normal to be considered accomplices. Of course, the bounty amount was also boosted by contributions from the Big Boss of the Underground Black Market Slave Masters. That boss looked furious. First, all his food was stolen, followed by his most precious minerals. He swore to find us, chop us up, and feed us to his pets.
The Austin incident had such a significant impact that, understandably, Doctor B and Tis were the priorities. However, we had a ’prior record,’ so it has become very difficult to enter the United States again since our fingerprints and faces had already been recorded."
With the course of events clear, everyone fell into silence. Only Jing Shu was looking at the news, where her photo from the video footage and other details could be seen.
The photo showed her wearing a bulky cotton coat and a green helmet. Though she looked like an older woman, her features were still pure and beautiful, and the bare-faced Jing Shu inadvertently turned the wanted picture into what seemed like a portrait.
Forget that Jing Shu in her previous life loved beauty. After wasting ten years in the apocalypse—suffering rheumatism in the second year, scars from frostbite in the fifth year, and being gaunt from years of malnutrition—she had long ceased to care about her appearance. Little did she expect that the beauty she coveted so much in her past life would be unintentionally restored to her after rebirth.
Life, indeed, was full of the unexpected, which is why Jing Shu sometimes dreamt that her Magic Cube Space filled with supplies had disappeared. Jing Shu would wake up in fright and would often ponder this problem. Though it was very unlikely that the Magic Cube Space would vanish, she, to be safe, would not put all her eggs in one basket. She was determined to stash an additional portion of the Magic Cube Space’s supplies in the villa, another in her secret storage, and even bury some in the soil on the hillside behind. She intended to actively upgrade the Magic Cube Space to ensure better survival in the apocalypse while also not becoming overly dependent on it. Gaining it is my fortune, losing it is my fate; she resolved to maintain a healthy mindset to face the unknowns of life ahead.
Jing Shu returned to her senses, looking at the document. It bore the English line: "Issued By Intelligence Agency of United States of America."
The translated version of the bounty notice roughly read:
"Issued by the Intelligence Agency of the United States of America.
[Code Name Doctor B, ringleader of a fraud syndicate, inventor of a new type of Concentrating Stone with radiation values exceeding 300, causing the death of hundreds of thousands in Austin City. He then concocted the ’Water of Life’ scam, swindling the good and honest citizens of Austin out of millions of pounds of food and millions of pounds of rare minerals, and also stealing Austin City’s latest dehydrated vegetable technology.]
[Code Name C Lady...]
[Code Name D Tis...]
Soon, Jing Shu finally found the description pertaining to herself:
[Code Name J: Used her innocent appearance to blend in with the good and honest citizens, enticing them to invest. She also made multiple false testimonies during the verification of the ’Water of Life,’ providing cover for Doctor B. Many of the good citizens claimed that they would have never been deceived if not for Code Name J, who, in partnership with Doctor B, used a cave on the outskirts to secretly transport away all the supplies and the rare minerals, playing a decisive role in the entire scam.
Note: Without J, that damn Doctor B would definitely not have been able to transport so much material away, and he also despicably and brutally slaughtered the brave warriors present. Therefore, J is categorized as an A-class bounty, with the reward amount doubled!]
Innocent appearance? Huh?
Jing Shu propped her chin, genuinely surprised by the high regard the United States Government placed on her, not to mention the increased bounty—it was truly a gesture of elevation for which she was grateful.
"It seems that the United States is indeed not a good place to go to anymore."
Unless one changes their face and swaps their fingerprints and iris, but who can be sure whether the rich resources of the United States will still be available in a year or two? The United States is just barely clinging to life as it is.
As for returning to the United States, no one else offered an opinion. There were other regions rich in resources they could go to instead. For instance, with the increasing scarcity of oil, it wouldn’t be a bad idea to head to an oil-rich country and bring back some petroleum. This was especially true since after the fifth year of the ice age, anyone who couldn’t burn fuel for warmth would freeze to death!
Besides, they had acquired all the special products they could find in Miguo; it was time to procure some from other places.
And in the dead of winter, no one can survive at negative 70 degrees Celsius!
The cargo ship, numbered 808, moved slowly towards its destination. After reaching it, Jing Shu and the others would take Qian Duoduo’s luxurious private plane back to Huaxia Imperial City, while the cargo ships would continue to transport goods by sea, returning to Huaxia only after more than ten days.
Jing Shu set Yang Yang’s broken bones and even generously donated some black Wanzi rolled with Spiritual Spring, considering she had accidentally injured Yang Yang.
As for Monkey’s injuries, they were more severe, with both legs being crushed. Jing Shu could only flatten some of the rolled Wanzi and apply them to his legs, along with some orally administered Wanzi rolled with Spiritual Spring. Whether he could fully recover was uncertain.
As for Hao Yunlai, he was truly knocked out cold. Given that Hao Yunlai had paid a heavy price to save Jing Shu and the others, she gave him a drop of the highly effective Spiritual Spring and some black Wanzi for free. Not only did he not show signs of waking, but he even started to snore.
Knowing that Jing Shu had woken up after being fed a drop of Spiritual Spring before, it could only indicate that his current condition was quite serious. This kind of sleep was extremely abnormal, potentially leading to him sleeping to death.
Jing Shu’s Spiritual Spring had a great restorative effect on life force, particularly on cuts and similar wounds. However, in Hao Yunlai’s case, he had no other injuries apart from some external damage to his thigh. With all his vital signs normal, the Spiritual Spring didn’t seem to have much of an effect.
"Let’s wait until we return to the country to assess Hao Yunlai’s condition. Have someone from the Imperial Capital take a look at him. If there’s really no solution, I’ll take the risk and try something else," Jing Shu said.
Her mind inexplicably recalled the time she entered the mountains and touched the entrance to the fourth dimension, almost bursting apart due to lack of a fulcrum. That scar hurt so fiercely that the pain was gut-wrenching, a memory vivid and fresh. Even though the red liquid from the fourth dimension used ’time’ to rewind the injury, the physical memory remained. For over ten days, she lived in agony.

chapters.title: Chapter 443: Sitting in Rows to Distribute Supplies (Additional Update for WY_1007’s Number One Fan)
chapters.content:
Chapter 443: Sitting in Rows to Distribute Supplies (Additional Update for WY_1007’s Number One Fan)
Right, I’ve absorbed some of that blood-red crystal and liquid. I wonder if it can save people? If so, how?
Jing Shu’s consciousness returned to the Magic Cube Space. The one cubic meter of blood-red liquid stored there had decreased slightly.
One thing was certain: the red liquid was diminishing.
Perhaps it’s due to its unique nature; after all, it’s a ’temporal’ substance from the fourth dimension. Just as time flows, so too could it diminish. Or perhaps the Magic Cube Space is covertly using it, or my own body is absorbing it. I’ll have to research this when I get back. Right now, returning to Huaxia is the most critical thing!
They had to hurry and escape the United States. As they were all wanted, being discovered could mean they’d never make it back.
I still wanted to check out the largest place in the United States, but the space is already full, and we have enough loot to transport back,
Jing Shu thought, considering their substantial haul, and decided it was enough.
After more than half a day’s journey, Cargo Ship 808 reached the new dock. Their arrival at the transfer point was uneventful. After ’settling accounts’ onboard, everyone bid farewell to the 808 and boarded a luxurious private jet.
Qian Duoduo’s private luxury jet couldn’t carry much cargo, so the group redistributed the spoils from Rhein Manor.
Jing Shu’s items stored in her space weren’t included in this tally. However, the Z10 generation synthetic meat she found when obtaining the chip key would need to be publicly declared later. Although Jing Shu would bring them out, these spoils still belonged to her.
The distribution of the team’s loot was straightforward: whoever collected the goods had the right to distribute them, choosing what they needed first. The remainder could be auctioned for Contribution Value or donated to the country for Contribution Value rewards, which would then be evenly divided among the group.
Some convenient and high-value items Jing Shu kept for herself, such as the Z10 generation synthetic meat formula and this mission’s target, the ZS880 liquid.
The equally precious Mars Meteorite, a source of rare elements for ZS880, was unanimously designated for handover to the state. This would yield a large amount of Contribution Value, to be split evenly among them.
Jing Shu claimed most of the dozen or so packages she had collected from the villa. The rest were offered to whoever bid the lowest Contribution Value. If multiple people were interested, an auction was held, with the resulting Contribution Value still being divided among everyone.
As for the seven or eight packages from the high tower, Jing Shu took only a few items, giving almost ninety percent to her teammates. These contained many precious foods and supplies.
Although these were valuable, Jing Shu already possessed most of these supplies and food. Furthermore, she had acquired enough high-grade materials from the villa and Job Sibus to fill her space, so she didn’t need more.
"Mirror, you collected the most goods. Don’t you want the high tower’s stuff anymore?" Snake Spirit asked somewhat sheepishly.
After all, to others, the items from the villa—jewelry, crystal picture frames, everlasting candlesticks—might have seemed like junk. However, the supplies from the high tower’s secret room were substantial and genuinely vital for survival in the apocalypse.
Most importantly, Jing Shu had risked her life to save these supplies, snatching them at the last second before an explosion. It wasn’t that she was taking more than her share; she had taken greater risks, so it was only fair.
"No, I’ve taken quite a bit already," Jing Shu coughed.
I’ve used my space to store so many things,
she thought.
It’s not that I’m embarrassed—COUGH COUGH—after all, I relied on my own abilities to pack these materials into my unique space. Without it, these items would have just been left to rot. No one else would have had time to take much anyway.
Their access to the villa’s goods, and subsequently the high tower’s more abundant supplies, had only been possible after navigating the laser room and obtaining the key.
Though, perhaps the priest might send a nun to try and snatch them... But he probably can’t get past those dangerous lasers to obtain the chip key.
Speaking of the priest, he hadn’t left with them. "The priest still has unfinished tasks. We’ll go ahead. Little Black will continue to assist him," Yang Yang had said at the time.
Little Black couldn’t return to Huaxia with them,
Jing Shu mused.
His best option was to continue completing tasks with the priest in the United States. Maybe he would even take over the priest’s work someday. I just hope that if we meet again, he won’t be constantly uttering ’God’ and ’Amen’.
Once Jing Shu’s items were sorted, the weapons dismantled from the high tower were next. These were all loaded onto Cargo Ship 808. Jing Shu reserved an early warning aircraft for herself. Most of the other weapons were turned over for Contribution Value, which was then distributed fairly. The other squad members took some miscellaneous usable weapons.
Next came Monkey’s loot. After he made his selections, the remainder was divided among the group. Jing Shu didn’t see anything she particularly wanted.
Yang Yang had also found a lot of materials—an entire truckload. He was clearly quite capable, having emptied the entire Technology Building. It held a real trove, much of it valuable scientific research material that could be exchanged for a significant amount of Contribution Value.
Aside from the ZS880 formula—a mission item that had to be handed over—Yang Yang kept some items he needed. The remaining scientific materials were collectively traded for Contribution Value, which was then split equally.
Jing Shu, however, spotted an interesting item among Yang Yang’s haul: a desiccated tree trunk in a glass container filled with a special fluid. The label read: "Unknown. Item under research. Appears dead. All attempts to revive it have failed, yet it does not completely perish."
It doesn’t seem very useful, and probably wouldn’t fetch much Contribution Value either. It resembles the withered tree at the entrance to the fourth dimension, yet it’s not quite the same,
Jing Shu mused. She acquired it for 50 Contribution Values, planning to try nurturing it in her space to see if it could be revived. Jing Shu had an unusually strong affinity for all plants and Domestic Poultry, provided they were valuable—that is, productive.
If Fat Chicken didn’t lay eggs, it probably wouldn’t have ’Number 1’ status. So, the treatment Fat Chicken receives depends on its will to survive... COUGH COUGH.
Sensing an inexplicable gaze, Fat Chicken hurriedly laid an egg.
Contribution Value truly is the universal currency in this circle,
Jing Shu reflected with growing certainty.
And it’s hard to earn, since only materials from abroad can be exchanged for it. I wonder how much these people have managed to gain from their ventures abroad.
In the distribution of the manor’s goods, Jing Shu received the most, but the others also earned a substantial amount of Contribution Value. The ZS880 life-extension formula alone would yield a considerable amount for everyone. Add to this the cauldron they all obtained, and that was another source of Contribution Value. After all, the first mission was a collective effort, but this last one, being partly official and partly private, definitely came with Contribution Value rewards.

chapters.title: Chapter 444: Jing Shu Sorts Out the Spoils of War (An additional - for the first top voter bookworm v1v1v1)
chapters.content:
Chapter 444: Jing Shu Sorts Out the Spoils of War (An additional Chapter for the first top voter bookworm v1v1v1)
Furthermore, by turning in unneeded resources they would acquire next, everyone could be allocated a considerable amount of Contribution Value. With this, not only did Jing Shu have to transport these miscellaneous goods back, but she could also rake in a significant amount of Contribution Value. Jing Shu felt an indescribable joy blooming in her heart. Her teammates, too, had all reaped substantial rewards.
"Welcome aboard."
It was the same beautiful flight attendant, smiling as she assisted everyone with boarding. However, after several months of trials and tribulations, the once-strangers had become well-acquainted. Naturally, returning came at a price. Three teammates were carried onto the plane; one was unconscious, their life uncertain. From another team, everyone perished except for a priest who survived. Who would have thought this mission would be so ghastly?
There was no Monk to carry luggage this time; his hands were gone. Severe burns had left him unconscious to this day. If not for Jing Shu’s medicine keeping him alive, he would have long since passed away.
Everyone carried the various materials they had salvaged from the United States onto the plane. During their first meeting, Jing Shu and a few others were in the front cabin, while Zhen Nantian and his people were in the back. This time, the three injured were settled in the back to rest, and the others gathered in the front cabin.
Of course, as a Doctor, Jing Shu had to administer medicine to the three injured. Their conditions weren’t great, and specific treatments would need to be evaluated back at the Imperial Capital.
The luxury plane finally took off, and Jing Shu and company quickly embarked on their journey back to Huaxia. It wasn’t that they didn’t want to stay in the United States. It was that they didn’t dare to stay any longer.
Yang Yang took out his notebook to calculate the grand total and summarize. "The materials from the first mission, including dozens of shiploads of goods, have already reached Huaxia and have been successfully delivered. These materials can allow tens of millions of Huaxia’s citizens to have enough to eat and survive. The authorities decided to award an additional 3,000 Contribution Value to each person."
Jing Shu rested her chin in her hand and opened the Magic Cube Space’s Second Form, organizing the materials gained from the first mission.
For the mercenary mission to advance in the Underground Black Market, I stealthily acquired many Diamond Mines. The output from these Diamond Mines can be commissioned for secondary processing when I return home or saved for a better price when New Energy is introduced.
Using the Fat Chicken Arena’s victory market, I made several hundred thousand Black Market Coins. These were all exchanged for apocalypse necessities, which have already been shipped back to Huaxia. I confirmed with Mom and Dad a few days earlier that the materials are at Li Yuetian’s place with the Second Team; they’ll be mine to claim once I’m back. Although I spent a lot of Contribution Value, these materials were all obtained through official channels, convenient to use without having to skulk around.
Then, during the smuggling mission, I killed Pei Qi. From this, I acquired her two massive snakes, her private treasure trove, wines, various food delicacies, a large pile of firearms, and more. I’ve already sorted the firearms and plan to distribute some to my family upon my return.
Pei Qi’s firearms later played no small role; at least the RPGs took down an armed helicopter, and the rest proved to be very useful.
Oh, and during the time on the luxury boat, I couldn’t resist nabbing many of the United States’ specialties. In the ship’s cold storage, I snatched various American olive oils, goose liver paste, ghee, cheeses, and expensive caviar. I took tons of tuna, world-class Iberian ham, boxes of longan, premium Kobe beef, and turkeys. Boxes of ice cream, thousand-layer cakes, puddings, desserts, and more also filled my space, taking up more than 30 cubic meters. These all expanded my inventory, and there are so many items I haven’t even tasted before!
I can’t resist such untried delicacies! Each country truly has its own unique specialties. Now, I want to go to Turkey for some roast meat!
COUGH. COUGH.
Later, when passing through the breeding area, I encountered super large Boston lobsters, precious sea urchins, king crabs, and so on. I feel that the biggest gain was these living creatures. Because they can be bred indefinitely in my space, and in the apocalypse, these creatures are slowly going extinct. I’m collecting as many different species as possible; after all, eating just one type would become tiresome.
One regret is that when the Slave Master later flew over in a gunship, I didn’t have the space to secretly keep the downed multi-million-dollar armed helicopter. In the future, I definitely want to get an armed helicopter as my vehicle!
Jing Shu swiftly added the plan to her to-do list.
Later, in the mountains, the dead tree that almost caused everyone’s death produced a red liquid, of which I collected a lot. This time, I found a small dead tree in Job Sibus’s manor and don’t know if it’s the same dead tree from the fourth dimension. I plan to try cultivating it to see; I’m very curious about things from the fourth dimension.
Also, I acquired a Sulfur Ant Queen in the mountains and named it Number 3, officially promoting it as my new pet. Along with it, I gained the allegiance of hundreds of thousands of Sulfuric Acid Ants, which greatly increased my armed forces. Its value is enormous as well, as it will bring me a steady stream of benefits in the upcoming apocalypse. The sulfuric acid it produces could become an industrial chain and even a money-printing machine. Sadly, some were killed in the explosion at Rhein Manor.
"The second mission was also very successful. Qian Duoduo successfully obtained the equipment, and we received some extra oil coupons," Yang Yang said, holding a notebook and tallying the Contribution Value spent on transactions by everyone during that period.
Jing Shu also started sorting out the gains from the second mission.
This mission was Qian Duoduo’s private mission to obtain vegetable dehydration technology and was completed in Austin City. I partnered with Dr. B to swindle a huge amount of supplies. Considering radiation issues, everyone only took away the rare ores, and I received just 100 tons. However, it’s still quite impressive. Firstly, these were obtained through legitimate channels, and secondly, rare ores will become increasingly scarce and valuable without mining technology in the apocalypse. With this batch of ore, I can do a lot of things.
At the same time, I obtained coffee Seeds from the Austin Castle and planted them in the Magic Cube Space. After some time, they are about to mature. This is the most expensive Gesha coffee tree in the world. Its beans produce a brew with notes of lemon, tangerine, and strawberry, tasting more like fruit juice than coffee. These flavors intermingle, leaving a floral aftertaste.
Of course, I didn’t plant six cubic meters of coffee trees just because I was craving it. Definitely not! It was certainly because it could resist the spread of a new zombie virus expected in two years, help suppress the growth of rotting flesh, and prove very effective against certain organisms. That was why I planted it. HUMPH.
The biggest gain from the second mission was 400,000 Seeds. This is my private property. I’ve divided them into three parts: one part to exchange for Contribution Value with the nation, one part for Wu City (though the price isn’t yet negotiated), and one part to keep for myself. Similarly, these were obtained through legitimate channels and are very precious.
At the same time, I also realized that Zhen Nantian’s ability might be related to dimensions.
Jing Shu promptly jotted this down.

chapters.title: Chapter 445: Jing Shu, How Can I Explain This to You? (Bonus - for WY_1007 reaching 10,000 rewards)
chapters.content:
Chapter 445: Jing Shu, How Can I Explain This to You? (Bonus Chapter for WY_1007 reaching 10,000 rewards)
She was constantly exploring the concept of Dimension Space, always believing that everything in the world could be explained by science. If it couldn’t be explained, it simply meant that current technology had not yet reached the level required to do so.
The first phase of the third mission involved the Monk burning his arms to obtain the cauldron; he received ninety percent of the Contribution Value, while the rest was evenly divided among everyone else. The second phase took place at Rhein Manor, where the Contribution Value for obtaining the recipe was divided evenly among everyone, including the priest, Little Black, and the Monk.
As for resources, even without the priest and Little Black, the Contribution Value from auctions, submissions, and other sources would also be evenly distributed among everyone.
"For the final mission, everyone’s Contribution Value can be divided according to this ratio after we return to the country and it’s evaluated by our superiors. The previous resources have also been distributed, so now we just need to settle our individual debts."
As he spoke, Yang Yang’s gaze turned towards Jing Shu, a headache brewing.
How would the leadership view this bill once it was submitted? What had happened to all the Contribution Value? Spent on meals? On cigarettes? On enjoying life?
Having embarked on so many missions, Jing Shu was the only one among them who had turned the routine accumulation of Contribution Value into a mobile general store, providing comprehensive and capable logistical support. Everyone had to spend tens, hundreds, or even thousands of Contribution Value at her "store" every day.
Jing Shu had medicine, food, and various daily necessities. She was essentially a walking store, able to meet anyone’s needs during any crisis.
She always brought Fat Chicken along, as well as scallions, lettuce, and cilantro grown in a huge bundle on her back. If needed, she could whip up egg fried rice, seafood egg custard, or even a pack of large-bone broth instant noodles for 50 Contribution Value, with an added egg for another 50 Contribution Value.
Later, Jing Shu also introduced discounted meals, like a Malatang for 88 Contribution Value that wasn’t too numbing, spicy, or hot, but was incredibly delicious and unforgettable. She also offered side dishes like roasted ham and air-dried shredded beef—she had everything imaginable.
Of course, you could also choose not to order specific dishes and instead pay 128 for a daily meal plan or 648 for a weekly one. You’d eat whatever Jing Shu ate, and she guaranteed you’d be full. Picky eaters like Zhen Nantian and Lingling opted for the 648 meal plan, enjoying savory and spicy dishes with Jing Shu. They had three different meals a day, with meat, vegetables, and soup; she was skilled in frying, deep-frying, boiling, and stewing! The meals were nutritious and well-balanced, even making Lingling look more radiant.
Jing Shu didn’t just cover meals; she catered to almost every aspect of life. If you ran out of clothes, blankets, or toilet paper, felt cold, hot, or uncomfortable, or craved a cigarette, alcohol, or coffee—as long as you had a need and Contribution Value, you could enjoy her "lifestyle package." It wasn’t 998, not 338, but just 199 Contribution Value. Plus, there was a special offer: pay 1,000 and get an extra 100.
Yang Yang tapped the tabletop, another headache forming as he looked at the list of figures next to Zhen Nantian’s name: -648, -199, -1,000+100.
If the leadership asked about these peculiar numbers, how was he supposed to respond? That the squad was running a special promotion: spend 1,000, get 100 free? Hm?
Finally, Yang Yang managed to get past his headache and said, "Mirror, excluding the Contribution Value from the third mission, your current Contribution Value is 28,000. If you reach over 30,000, you can apply for the Elite title, which means direct promotion to A-rank."
"After we return this time, the country will give you a new evaluation. But I want to ask you: do you want a higher score, or just an average one?"
Jing Shu glanced at Zhen Nantian, who nodded slightly. It seemed Zhen Nantian had told Yang Yang about the possibility of her possessing Dimension Space items.
The others showed no unusual expressions, likely meaning they were unaware, not even knowing about Dimension Space.
So, Yang Yang knows about Dimension Space, and it’s possible he has Dimension Space items too? Otherwise, how could he have been rated A+?
Jing Shu couldn’t think of any other ability Yang Yang possessed that would warrant such a high rating.
Yang Yang’s meaning was simple: did she want to continue keeping her abilities a secret, or reveal her strength to everyone and receive a high rating?
After thinking it over, Jing Shu realized she didn’t understand this "dimension" concept well. However, if the price was exposing her space, she’d rather not understand anything at all.
In my view, whether it’s Zhen Nantian, Yang Yang, or even the opening to the fourth dimension, none of them seem particularly heaven-defying, at least not compared to my Magic Cube Space. Therefore, it’s better for my Magic Cube, being so unique, to remain quiet and maintain an air of mystery.
"Let’s just go with that. Base it on what the country already knows about me." This meant Jing Shu wouldn’t excessively display her abilities.
Yang Yang nodded. "Alright. Then, once the Contribution Value from this mission is tallied and your evaluation is added, I think your rating will be around A- or A. You’ve reached the standard for a national-level elite."
Afterward, Yang Yang began to settle accounts and summarize for each person. Even the stoic Zhen Nantian, who spent Contribution Value like water, had a surplus of tens of thousands. This didn’t even include the unsettled Contribution Value from the third mission; everyone had truly profited handsomely this time.
Jing Shu closed her eyes and continued organizing the items obtained from the third mission. She had acquired so many things from Rhein Manor that her space was now full. Jing Shu had to meticulously arrange everything to maximize storage, and after she finished, a few cubic meters were freed up.
Jing Shu was quite happy. She looked at the over 500 cubic meters of space, neatly packed to the brim with various energy sources, gourmet food, grain, and live Domestic Poultry—creatures from the sea and land. Although the variety was still limited, for Jing Shu, who had survived on rotten food in her previous life in this resource-scarce world, this was already very satisfying.
Next, she planned to expand the variety of species as much as possible, collecting all the delicious creatures that flew in the sky. She would also prepare the necessary resources for the harsh environment that was fast approaching.
「...」
At last, they arrived at the Imperial Capital! The moment the plane landed, Jing Shu patted her chest.
Safe at last, finally safe. Motherland, we’re back! We no longer have to endure coercion from the United States!
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM! The familiar pattern, the familiar sound; the Imperial Capital still experienced its daily "triple tremor," accompanied by roaring thunder and flashing lightning.
The complex terrain meant Huaxia endured more disasters than other countries, but the ingenious Huaxia people had already begun to find patterns in the earthquakes.
"First, let’s send Hao Yunlai, Monkey, and the Monk to the Government Hospital. We’ll rest for two days. During that time, we’ll report to the Imperial Capital’s special intelligence department for re-evaluation, and then we’ll return to Wu City."
That was the plan, but its implementation differed. Jing Shu first called her family, telling them she would be home in a few days. Then, she finally succumbed to exhaustion and fell into a deep sleep. She slept for two whole days. The prolonged tension had taken its toll, and once back in the Imperial Capital, Jing Shu could no longer hold on and finally got some proper rest.
When she woke up, she found a group of people in white coats playing "Fight the Landlord" in front of her, while Fat Chicken protectively stood behind her like a mother hen.
Jing Shu looked at her surroundings.
Yes, I’m on Qian Duoduo’s plane.

chapters.title: Chapter 446: Uncle, You’ve Successfully Caught My Attention!
chapters.content:
Chapter 446: Uncle, You’ve Successfully Caught My Attention!
She checked her most precious luggage again to make sure the fat chicken was guarding it well, confirming that the surroundings were still secure.
Jing Shu felt a bit bewildered, her mind still sluggish from the long sleep. Just like that, she watched an old man in a white lab coat and three others play several rounds of Fight the Landlord. Meanwhile, she managed to brush her teeth and wash her face. It wasn’t until she took out a frying pan that the men in lab coats realized she was the person they had been eagerly waiting for!
"You’re awake?"
The old men chuckled.
Several kindly-looking old men put down their cards, pushed up their glasses, and moved closer, causing Jing Shu to step back two paces.
...
"So, you’re from the Special Intelligence Bureau, here to reassess me?" Jing Shu began, piecing things together. "You’re from Skyline Hospital in Imperial Capital, here because of Monk and Monkey’s injuries, to discuss academics and, incidentally, buy those Wanzi I made myself, right? Yes, I know you aren’t short of money, but please wait a moment. You’re from an Imperial Capital research institute asking for sponsorship and wanting to borrow some ZS880 potion samples from me? And you, sir, are from the Starvation Food Supervision Bureau, wanting to trade for the Z10 bacteria synthetic meat formula? Okay, just put the sack on the ground and wait a bit. And you all played Fight the Landlord to determine who could approach me first, but then played so many rounds just to decide which three of you even qualified to play for that right?"
Jing Shu asked, her jaw practically on the floor, as the four old men in lab coats nodded in unison.
"So, you still haven’t decided who goes first?"
The four old men nodded again.
Why would these important-sounding and imaginative institutions choose a few unreliable-looking old men to handle their affairs? It makes everything seem so much less impressive,
Jing Shu mused. Still, the tasks needed doing. One couldn’t underestimate even the street sweepers in Imperial Capital; who knew, they might casually pull out a potato or cucumber that countless people would scramble for.
"Alright then, let’s start with the gentleman from the Special Intelligence Bureau," Jing Shu said. "What rating are you thinking of giving me? No worries, I don’t have any special abilities or hobbies. My strength is just as my teammate explained. Are you going to give me an A+? No, no, I prefer to keep a low profile; an A would be better. What? My chicken got a B rating? So, my overall strength remains A+? Okay, I understand. Do I sign here? Thank you so much. The Special Intelligence Bureau is really professional these days, even offering door-to-door service."
After bidding a warm farewell to the first old man, Jing Shu turned her attention to the old man from the prodigiously expensive Skyline Hospital.
"Come, sir," she said, "these are the secret Wanzi I’ve prepared over time. They’re made from various precious herbs, which I’ve, well, rubbed off myself. Please apply them directly to Monkey and Monk’s affected areas. There’s no need to discuss academics; you can see I’m quite busy..."
The old man dabbed a bit of the Wanzi with his ring finger, tasted it with his pinkie, and kept nodding. "Truly a good medicine!" He happily took a box of black Wanzi, signing a debt acknowledgment for Monkey for two thousand Contribution Value before leaving. Naturally, the medicine for Monk was a gift from Jing Shu.
"So, my good sir," Jing Shu said to the next, "are you here to borrow a sample of ZS880? Oh, you mean to borrow one and return ten later? No problem, just get Yang Yang or Zhen Nantian to vouch for you. What? Lingling is from your research institute? Alright then, let’s draw up a contract..."
Finally having seen off the first three gentlemen, Jing Shu turned her attention to the last customer. "Sir, you’re from the Starvation Food Supervision Bureau, and you’re here to trade for that formula, but I’m curious what you plan to barter with?"
The last old man had an unkempt beard and wore muddy rain boots. Though clad in a white lab coat like the others, he looked more like a rice paddy farmer underneath.
The man produced a burlap sack and opened it, revealing two black-beaked creatures with fleshy growths on their necks. They were still formidable fighters despite being bound and seemed quite aggressive.
Jing Shu frowned, peering intently before asking uncertainly, "Are these two geese?"
The old man laughed, revealing gapped, yellowed teeth. "These are Lionhead Geese, the king of geese! They lay eggs very rarely, but their value is high, especially after special processing. The taste is incredibly delicious, absolutely delectable! In the Imperial Capital right now, people are queued up all the way to the Mediterranean for a taste."
Jing Shu swallowed the drool that was about to spill. She rummaged through her Magic Cube Space—she had no geese!
I can’t believe I haven’t bred geese!
she thought. Before the apocalypse, due to lack of funds and because her Magic Cube Space was too small, she had only bred the most common Domestic Poultry—chickens, ducks, sheep, cows, quails, and rabbits. Besides, duck eggs could be made into salted duck eggs, and Peking duck was also delicious.
Geese had low yields, their eggs were too gamey, and they consumed a lot of food, so she hadn’t bothered breeding them.
But braised goose, red-braised giant goose, plum goose, goose meat stewed with vegetables, braised goose, and sauce-braised free-range chicken... those dishes must taste amazing, right? I haven’t eaten goose meat in fifteen or sixteen years!
Times were different now.
In the apocalypse, what’s most important? Fill my stomach! Hoard resources! Arm myself! Every creature in the apocalypse needs to fully manifest its value. A goose can be trained as a guard goose, a patrolling goose. Though they lay fewer eggs, if they reproduce more, there will be more eggs.
After some mental calculation, Jing Shu affirmed the value of the geese. "Alright," she declared, "your kind meets my standards. Approved."
Now that Jing Shu’s Magic Cube Space had expanded and she had enough funds, she was considering how to revive nearly extinct Domestic Poultry when someone brought her two paired Lionhead Geese! Jing Shu quickly checked in the Magic Cube Space app; indeed, the value of Lionhead Geese was the highest among all geese. ’The king of geese’ was no exaggeration—regular geese had red beaks, but Lionhead Geese had black beaks and were very distinct.
"You want to trade the formula for these two geese?" Jing Shu gestured back and forth with her fingers, asking uncertainly.
The old man looked at Jing Shu as if she were a fool. "Nowadays, Domestic Poultry is precious indeed. These Lionhead Geese are the last of their kind. Swap them for your uncertain formula? Do you take us for fools?"
Jing Shu’s face stiffened.
Hmm... had I smiled too much, making them think they could take such liberties? Did he bring the geese just to mock me, to make me envious? Was he intentionally trying to tempt me into committing some unforgivable crime?
Sir, you’ve successfully caught my attention!
she thought.
Before Jing Shu’s expression could change further, the old man, grinning with his gap-toothed smile, said, "Tan Ke from your team is from our Starvation Food Supervision Bureau. He said you’ve raised chickens that can lay dozens of eggs a day. We’ve observed them, and indeed it is so. That’s why, well, I brought these geese to you."

chapters.title: Chapter 447: Da Hua and Gou Dan
chapters.content:
Chapter 447: Da Hua and Gou Dan
"Hmm??" Jing Shu frowned.
What did this mean?
She sized up the old man; his bones seemed quite robust.
Could it be that he had set his sights on the fat chicken?
That seemed unlikely, though. Tan Ke was someone she knew well enough to be certain that anyone who would reveal information about the fat chicken wouldn’t be looking to take advantage. Besides, from a species valuation perspective, an old mother hen was worth less than a lion-headed goose. And in terms of battle pets, Tan Ke was also well aware that the fat chicken wasn’t just for laying eggs; it definitely couldn’t be traded away.
The old man coughed sheepishly and said, "What we mean is, we’d lease the lion-headed geese to you for a year. As for the rent, a part of it could be the Z10 synthetic meat recipe. We know you’ve got a knack for raising domestic poultry, and we won’t pry into your secrets. You would just need to breed 10 healthy lion-headed geese for us every three months, for a total of 40 geese as the final part of the rent. Any extras you hatch can be kept for yourself. Of course, if you need it, we can also provide professional nutritional feed, and every three months when we come to collect the geese, we can airlift it to you."
So, the rent would be the Z10 synthetic meat recipe and the breeding of 40 lion-headed geese, including their feed.
Jing Shu squinted and looked thoughtful. She knew that living animals, especially breeding pairs of domestic poultry, were very valuable. Last year, the price for a pair of live chickens had reached thousands of Virtual Coins, hundreds of times more expensive than grains, not to mention lion-headed geese that were on the brink of extinction.
There were many factors involved in the breeding of domestic poultry. Food and nutrition could be managed, and temperature could be regulated with air conditioning, but climate, external factors, and the sun in the apocalypse posed challenges that made the already scarce population of domestic poultry extremely difficult to breed!
The most significant factor was the disrupted seasons that led to disarray in the breeding period of domestic poultry, causing the majority to stop reproducing altogether. Besides, with constant droughts or downpours, not to mention earthquakes and lightning—living in such daily turmoil—animals had no mind for breeding, and neither did humans.
However, Jing Shu’s Magic Cube Space was the most comfortable place to be. It could simulate the perfect living temperature and climate for these animals, so naturally, their reproduction rate was high.
The old man talked about renting, but Jing Shu didn’t really care about that. If she could just borrow a few geese for a few eggs, she could endlessly breed them herself.
What she lacked was the breeding stock.
For others, this might pose some risk, but for her, it was non-existent.
Seeing Jing Shu’s hesitation, the old man knew he might have asked for too much. "We know this is a tough ask. After all, a lion-headed goose only lays about 40 eggs a year, and it’s not certain that they will all hatch. Hatching requires even higher temperature precision, and in this apocalypse, the success rate is even lower. But you, girl, have raised chickens so well. If you raise geese, you surely can achieve pre-apocalypse production levels, right?"
Jing Shu’s fingers rhythmically tapped on the table as she stared at the fierce lion-headed geese for a while.
So the lion-headed goose only laid so few eggs a year, huh.
"Old man," she asked, "if you don’t lack for anything, why don’t you raise them yourselves? You seem to have more expertise."
The old man gave a bitter smile. "Not to hide it from you, but in the year before the apocalypse, Da Hua and Gou Dan hatched about 30 goslings. But now, three years into the apocalypse, they’ve only laid 30 eggs in total, with only 10 hatched, and 6 of those died. Those that managed to survive either have disabilities or are underdeveloped; it seems they’ve mutated."
So the species has started evolving to adapt to the apocalyptic environment. The unsuccessful mutations die, and the successful ones aren’t yet perfect. It looks like I need to hurry up and collect the original species.
Jing Shu swiftly recorded this in the Magic Cube Space, noting it down as one of her tasks.
But the problems mentioned by the old man weren’t issues for her at all. Just a few days in her space and a bit of Spiritual Spring water would ensure an egg a day.
"Old man, I can rent your geese, but the risk is too high. It might turn out that I don’t get many in the end. I can only promise eight every three months."
"Ten."
"Eight."
"Nine."
"Eight."
"Okay, deal."
"By the way, old man, do you guys buy lion-headed geese?"
"We do, for a high price. There’s a line of people in the Imperial Capital waiting to place orders that stretches to the Mediterranean."
That’s great; it must be a very good market.
Under the old man’s reluctant gaze, with one hand exchanging the formula and the other the geese, both parties signed the contract. Finally, with Tan Ke as the guarantor, they completed the transaction.
[Party A: Starvation Food Supervision Bureau]
[Party B: Mirror]
[Third Party Guarantor: Tan Ke]
[Contract Content: After friendly consultation between both parties and in the spirit of equality, mutual benefit, and joint development, this contract pertains to Party B renting Party A’s property (specifically, the Lion-Head Geese Da Hua and Gou Dan) and Party B providing goose rearing and breeding services as follows:
1. Party B provides the Z10 synthetic meat formula and, every three months, supplies Party A with 8 healthy goslings. After a total of 32 goslings have been provided within the year, Party B shall return the Lion-Head Geese, Da Hua and Gou Dan. Should the provided number of goslings fall short, Tan Ke will make up for the loss. Any additional goslings and goose eggs produced shall belong entirely to Party B.
2. Every three months, Party A provides Party B with sufficient, nutritious feed and is responsible for transporting and receiving the goslings. If Party A breaches the contract, Tan Ke will be responsible for the loss.
3. Force Majeure: If Da Hua or Gou Dan die due to force majeure, or if the goslings die en route due to uncontrollable circumstances or other such accidental factors, Tan Ke will be responsible for the loss.
4. Party A has the right of first refusal to purchase goose eggs and goslings owned by Party B, but the price must satisfy Party B.
