He hadn’t expected this young woman to be so perceptive as to praise him right away, unlike those who had recently been complaining about him, which had worsened his father’s illness. Things had only quieted down after his mother wrote a letter and had one of those individuals transferred.
"Of course it’s true! Oh, Mom, just stop asking," Gold Dominator said, slightly impatient and a little guilty.
"AHEM. AHEM." Jin Tianci coughed weakly and was helped to sit up. He adjusted his gold-rimmed glasses and turned to the middle-aged man. "Jun Jia, is this true?"
The portly middle-aged man was sweating profusely. As he looked at Jing Shu’s smiling face, it seemed like a devilish grin. He then glanced at his excited sister doting on her son, and finally, his gaze fell upon his brother-in-law—filled with disappointment and suspicion, yet clinging to a sliver of hope, wanting to ensure his wife and child were settled before he died.
If he shattered this beautiful illusion, would he die a terrible death? His nephew would turn on him, his sister would turn on him, even his brother-in-law would turn on him! After all, he was the one who’d failed to manage Gold Dominator. This damned girl! Couldn’t she even flatter properly? Her attempt was a complete disaster! He had to make a mental note of this.
Jun Jia was in a real dilemma. He was supposed to be helping collect supplies, yet his nephew was clearly funneling them into his own private stash! Of course, Jun Jia himself had also profited handsomely—much better than when he was under his upright Brother-in-law Qingshui.
Besides, if he lied, his brother-in-law wouldn’t bother to investigate such a minor matter. It was just some supplies, and with his assurance, even if an investigation were initiated, he could manipulate things.
Jun Jia steeled himself and nodded. "It’s true, Brother-in-law. These past few days, Gold Dominator has been very sensible. He helped me collect a lot of supplies. We in Wu City can hold out for a while longer."
Jin Tianci exhaled slowly in relief, nodding contentedly. "Gold Dominator, you’ve finally grown up. I hope you can find your own path in the future and not be like you were before." Mrs. Jin’s eyes welled with tears, and she nodded, deeply moved.
Gold Dominator lowered his head, a peculiar light shimmering in his eyes. The feeling of being acknowledged by his father for the first time was very different. His father had always treated him like a subordinate, with nothing but commands and disapproval.
Despite his father always speaking in a soft and apparently easygoing manner, Jin Tianci’s gentleness was like central air conditioning, evenly distributed to everyone. At home, his father’s word was law, unquestionable. Gold Dominator never had a voice in any matter. His father was busy with work and scrupulously honest, while his mother, indulgent in pleasures and lavish spending, always doted on his father. Although they spoiled him, he still felt he had no real status in the family.
And now, in the apocalypse, shouldn’t he be thinking for himself? His mother had expended so many connections and Virtual Coins just to barely keep his father breathing. Yet, she never thought to leverage his father’s status to secure more resources while he was still around. Once his father was gone and his power faded, they would have absolutely nothing left.
Luckily, I’ve managed to secure quite a lot for myself during this period,
Gold Dominator thought.
What was expected to be a heartwarming family reunion took a turn after Jin Tianci nodded and then said:
"Then, Jun Jia, show me the accounts for this contingent and all the sponsored supplies, as well as the records of weapons exchanged from the storerooms. I want to see which contingent has over-fulfilled its quota. They won’t need to meet any more quotas for the next few months. Furthermore, such behavior must be rewarded; record it as a merit."
Jin Tianci paused, then continued, "Also, circulate this to all contingents as an example. If all the major merchants were this proactive, Wu City would surely overcome this disaster."
Gold Dominator’s smile vanished. Jun Jia froze like a jammed tape. The silence was so profound you could hear a pin drop. A slow smile spread across Jing Shu’s lips. She was curious to see how they would handle this.
The situation had exploded. Sweat poured down the plump, middle-aged man’s face. The accounts and records? They didn’t exist. Not even the fivefold quantity of supplies was there—it was all in his and his nephew’s personal stashes. Where could he possibly conjure up records at a moment’s notice? Crucially, the subordinates were all aware of the situation. Everyone knew who had taken whose resources. If merits were truly to be recorded and commendations announced, whose merits would they be? To whom would they be given? What kind of example would that set? He and his nephew were truly done for!
"Sis... Brother-in-law..." Jun Jia stammered, wiping his sweat. He needed to stall for a few hours, to think of a solution.
Coughing, Jin Tianci got up. "Vice Chairman Jing, Old Zhou, please wait a moment. I’m going to the restroom. Jun Jia, I want to see that data when I return." With that, he left for the restroom, assisted by Mrs. Jin.
Indeed, he was a man of his word.
The maids stood at a distance. Soon, only Jing Shu, Zhou Bapi, Li Yuetian, Gold Dominator, and Jun Jia remained in the main hall.
At this moment, the plump, middle-aged man finally reacted. He pointed at Jing Shu, his hand trembling. "What exactly did you mean by those words you said earlier?"
Li Yuetian cleared his throat, also having pieced it together. "Those supplies you confiscated yesterday, the ones from the Imperial Capital? They belong to this Vice Chairman Jing!"
Once Li Yuetian explained, even the slow-witted Gold Dominator understood. So, this had been her overt scheme all along!

chapters.title: Chapter 459: Jing Shu Makes Bold Demands
chapters.content:
Chapter 459: Jing Shu Makes Bold Demands
Zhou Bapi was thoroughly perplexed. Hadn’t they just been praising this Demon Lord of Mayhem? Why was Gold Dominator reacting so strongly now?
Li Yuetian contemplated whether Jing Shu was trying to threaten Gold Dominator with this method.
Although she hadn’t directly offended Jin Tianci and Mrs. Jin, she had still managed to offend Gold Dominator.
But to retrieve the supplies, offending someone was inevitable. Offending two fewer people now was an unexpected outcome,
but Li Yuetian had never imagined that Jing Shu would make such a huge demand.
Young and inexperienced, Gold Dominator paced back and forth anxiously, looking down at Jing Shu as he spoke,
"You... What good does this do you! Do you think you can get those things back by doing this? You’re wrong! Even if you exaggerate the situation, at most I’ll just alter the records to cover it up. And you all, having surrendered everything, will end up with nothing! If need be, I’ll just confess."
Indeed, Jing Shu hadn’t said that Gold Dominator had extorted everyone’s possessions by taking advantage of Jin Tianci’s critical illness. Instead, she claimed Gold Dominator had collected five times the supplies and received everyone’s praise, stating these supplies were for the Wu City granary and the civilians. Now, with Jin Tianci auditing the accounts, even if this charade were to be taken as truth, the items could only go to the granary. This had nothing to do with Jing Shu.
Given she would suffer such a loss, what was the point of her doing this?
Having navigated bureaucratic circles for half his life, Jun Jia sighed and shook his head.
They had fallen into her trap. It was an overt scheme they had no choice but to follow; this young woman’s promises were simply too enticing!
"Oh? Are you really willing to see the disappointed look in your parents’ eyes after you confess? Can you bear to return all the supplies you’ve gathered during this time? Even if you’ve used some of them, do you think your father wouldn’t empty the family coffers to compensate and return everything, setting you right back to square one? I, however, have a solution that benefits everyone." Jing Shu’s triple blow left Gold Dominator breathless.
He finally felt a pang of fear, his once arrogant expression now tinged with dread.
If his mother found out, it might not be a huge deal, but if his father learned of it, he would undoubtedly demand the return of everything immediately and insist on compensating for whatever had been used!
Gold Dominator stared at Jing Shu, a mixture of fear and resentment in his eyes, yet he knew he couldn’t afford to antagonize her.Dressed in a suit, Jun Jia wiped the cold sweat from his forehead, managed a strained smile, and said, "President Jing, please, tell us your thoughts directly."
These Government officials certainly loved to beat around the bush, disguising pleas for mercy with such convoluted phrasing.
Jing Shu chuckled softly and took a step forward. "First, return all my supplies, untouched. If any have been used, you will compensate me at three times their value."
Jun Jia nodded. "Of course, that’s not a problem."
Gold Dominator clenched his teeth in hatred.
Just you wait, he fumed internally. Once this is over, I’ll deal with you. Trying to snatch meat from my, your lord’s, mouth? You must be tired of living!
Jing Shu completely ignored the seething Gold Dominator and continued smoothly, "Second..."
The spacious hall created a slight echo, amplifying Jing Shu’s voice, but it couldn’t mask Li Yuetian’s occasional, shocked gulps.
He hadn’t imagined Jing Shu’s goal was not merely to retrieve her supplies, but to also brazenly make exorbitant demands of both Gold Dominator and Jun Jia. She had struck their vulnerabilities with precision, yet skillfully managed the pressure, careful not to push them into complete desperation.
Jun Jia’s cheeks flushed as he held back his words, while Gold Dominator, after grudgingly weighing his interests, caved in once more. Even Zhou Bapi wore a look of profound realization.
It seemed he was finally grasping something: Jing Shu hadn’t come to treat Old Jin’s illness at all, had she?
"COUGH. COUGH. That should be all for now. Don’t forget to take me to the armory later to choose weapons. After all, we need to make this charade convincing," Jing Shu said calmly.
Li Yuetian observed Gold Dominator’s expression,
deeply afraid Jing Shu might provoke him into fainting. How would he explain that if it happened?
Like an old man in his twilight years, Jin Tianci slowly climbed back into bed. Jun Jia handed him the latest data and said, his smile bitter and his heart feeling as if it were dripping blood, "Brother-in-law, these are the items collected yesterday from Li Yuetian’s unit in the Second Team: red worm cake valued at four million Virtual Coins and other supplies valued at one million Virtual Coins. The red worm cake has been logged into the West Mountain Reserve, and the other supplies into the granary."
Gold Dominator lowered his head, his fists clenched. The supplies worth one million Virtual Coins had been procured from Li Yuetian, but before he could even properly register them as his own, they had to be transferred to the public warehouse. What was hardest to accept was that to cover for the red worm cake this malicious woman supposedly contributed—which he was effectively paying for from his own pocket—he now had to reimburse her with other supplies of equivalent value, likely at a disadvantageous conversion rate for him.
To put it bluntly, this malicious woman hadn’t spent a single Virtual Coin yet had earned the esteemed reputation of contributing four million. Plus, she was receiving supplies far more valuable and superior to the red worm cake. He had suffered a massive loss, like a mute tasting bitter herbs—all suffering, no words to express it. He had given everything and received nothing, while this woman had contributed nothing yet gained a hoard of benefits! Still, he couldn’t disagree. Agreeing meant he could at least keep some things; disagreeing meant he would...
"The official commendation for Li Yuetian has been drafted and is awaiting approval," Jun Jia continued. "Additionally, the Second Team will be exempt from soliciting sponsorships and submitting supplies for the next four months. As for public commendation for Jing Shu, well..."
Of course, there could be no public commendation for her, he thought. Otherwise, those previously extorted by Gold Dominator would undoubtedly explode in fury and rush forward with complaints. The consequences would likely be far worse.
Li Yuetian also lowered his head.
He wanted to laugh but couldn’t; restraining himself was incredibly difficult. The supplies he’d turned in yesterday were destined for the public warehouse anyway. Gold Dominator had extorted far more than that—supplies originally meant for next month’s quota—but now, in return, his team wouldn’t have to secure sponsorships for the next four months.
In effect, Gold Dominator had personally sponsored his team for four months’ worth of supplies and had contributed four million Virtual Coins’ worth of grain to the granary. His ’over-fulfillment’ of the task would also be officially recognized, paving the way for a future promotion.
Li Yuetian glanced at Gold Dominator with a touch of sympathy; their positions had completely flipped in an instant.
"Conveniently," Jun Jia elaborated, "the red worm cake, valued at four million Virtual Coins, was actually contributed by President Jing. Of course, we acquired these valuable red worm cakes from her through a perfectly fair exchange, which included providing weapons and satisfying all the conditions she stipulated. So, during the short time you were away, President Jing subtly indicated to me that if she were publicly commended, she’s worried it might attract some unwanted resentment..."
As long as this transaction was recorded in the readily verifiable central database, it signified the existence of tangible goods, which would be audited monthly. Otherwise, everyone in the relevant department would be held accountable. No one dared to make careless errors or fraudulent entries in these records. Jun Jia didn’t have enough authority to tamper with such things; at most, he could ’delay an item’s official entry into storage.’
Moments ago, they had quickly prepared a supplementary docket before officially logging the items. Combined with yesterday’s records of collecting and depositing supplies, the total ledger value of five million Virtual Coins and the timing of the deposit could now be made to match the warehouse’s official logs.
Since Jing Shu’s red worm cake had always been physically located in the West Mountain Reserve, transferring ownership was a simple matter of adjusting the accounts, much like a bank transaction. If Jun Jia had tried to use the supplies Gold Dominator had actually confiscated to create the new record and then log them, he would have certainly been exposed.
Jing Shu had perfectly exploited this narrow half-hour window, correctly calculating that Jun Jia wouldn’t be able to complete all the necessary paperwork and official transfers for Gold Dominator’s actual haul within that timeframe. And at that critical juncture, wasn’t everything effectively dictated by her terms?

chapters.title: Chapter 460: Accidentally Bought a Piece of Land
chapters.content:
Chapter 460: Accidentally Bought a Piece of Land
So Jin Tianci hadn’t noticed anything unusual. With this hurdle passed, he couldn’t help praising Gold Dominator once more, allowing Gold Dominator, who had suffered significant losses, to finally recoup some interest.
Speaking of declining the commendation, Jin Tianci looked at Jing Shu with a hint of surprise and smiled gently. "I know you. I once chatted with you using that girl Mary’s WeChat account, about the... Honeysuckle that time."
"Hey, and me, old man! I was also watching you guys chat via video on the other side," boasted Zhou Bapi, quite pleased. At the time, he was in Guangdong searching for Honeysuckle and couldn’t believe someone could grow it so well.
Jing Shu’s mouth fell open. She certainly remembered the odd behavior Su Malie had exhibited that time. It hadn’t occurred to her that there were so many sleazy old men on the other side of the chat. Jing Shu didn’t know that it wasn’t just them; a one-eyed man called Bald, and Su Malie’s father... were also there.
Jin Tianci then became interested and turned to ask Jun Jia, "What were the conditions for the donation of supplies? Make sure to satisfy them and implement them properly. Even if it’s difficult, make it happen. Pull some strings if necessary."
A bitter taste filled Jun Jia’s mouth.
This is truly like I’m sewing a wedding dress for Jing Shu, all for free!
Despite this, she smiled and said, "It was a bit difficult, but once you gave the order, I’d certainly find a way."
Jin Tianci raised his eyebrows. "Let’s hear it."
"President Jing wants to rent a large piece of land and has set her sights on that suburban factory industrial land in the new district. It’s about twenty mu in size—the equivalent of two soccer fields—and she wants to set up a feed factory there. But there are already several thousand people who have made it their home, and without relocating them, the work can’t start. Also, both the site and equipment are privately owned. We wanted to requisition that area recently, but the owner insisted on selling the equipment before moving out. We are not completely unreasonable, you know."
Like I’d believe you,
Jing Shu rolled her eyes.
You call yourselves reasonable?
"Whose is it?" Jin Tianci asked directly.
"The Second-in-Command’s," Jun Jia coughed. "For those with connections, it’s a matter of ’being reasonable’; for those without, it’s simply ’requisitioning’."
Jin Tianci pondered. Gold Dominator, on the other hand, couldn’t contain his indignation on several occasions.
On what grounds? This woman has contributed nothing, and now she gets to take such a large piece of land for free? After the apocalypse, usable land has become even more precious, even though industry has collapsed and many factories have closed down.
Meanwhile, Jing Shu was thinking about her current plan.
Renting that piece of land was unexpected, but the reason I want it is to develop it into a second sanctuary for the apocalypse. Indeed, if the villa was a safe haven for the first five years, then that piece of land became the Golden Land after the relocation. In the years I know of, that Golden Land survived disasters unscathed, gradually becoming a central gathering point. It’s like playing that battle royale game: if you know where the safe zone will be after the circle shrinks, wouldn’t you hide there in advance to survive safely until the end? Besides, to prevent the tyrant from turning Stone Garden into a slaughterhouse in the fifth year, I have my own plans for this factory land. This Golden Land is crucial to me. Even if I don’t get it this time, I’ll find a way to secure it next time. And I must sign the contract before the tyrant comes to power.
After a while, Jin Tianci finally asked, "Why rent it, instead of buying this piece of land?"
Jing Shu was stunned. "Didn’t you just say that we could sign a lease for ten years, with the first three years for free? Buy it? That must be very expensive; I can’t afford it.
Before the apocalypse, billions were invested here. How many Virtual Coins would I need now? Besides, it’s the apocalypse; buying land is like buying a house. If a natural disaster destroys it, there’s nowhere to even cry. I only know the trends for the next ten years; I can’t guarantee anything beyond that.
""How about this," Jin Tianci said. "You buy the land plot, the factory, and the equipment. The factory and equipment are ready-made, with a 70-year property right. I will act as an intermediary and give you a half-price deal. This is to protect against the possibility that I... am no longer in office and the lease becomes void."
Jin Tianci was afraid that if he died, the lease might not be recognized by a subsequent administration and could be revoked. Who knew who the next person in power would be? If this area really became valuable in the future, taking it back would be a trivial matter. They could jack up the rent or impose restrictive conditions that would ruin Jing Shu. A half-sale, half-gift arrangement was better.
Jing Shu was somewhat moved and tempted. "How many Virtual Coins? But I don’t have enough Virtual Coins..."
"You make a down payment of half the price, and then I’ll give you a loan. But let’s make this clear: the down payment can be in Virtual Coins, but the monthly repayments must be made with food and supplies of equivalent current value, to guard against future inflation."
"Okay."
「....」
"Brother-in-law is really impressive, exchanging so much food for a piece of land and some scrap equipment in just a few minutes."
"This is a triple-win situation; nobody loses out. Go and process the paperwork for President Jing quickly."
"Alrighty, let’s go, Daddy. Follow me and learn a bit more; it will be good for you to get into this field in the future."
Jun Jia took Gold Dominator away, with Li Yuetian also going along to settle the accounts. Only Mrs. Jin, Jin Tianci, Jing Shu, and Zhou Bapi remained in the vast living room.
Zhou Bapi complained softly,
Finally, that’s settled. Can we talk about my business now? Seriously, this girl Jing Shu has some nerve! It’s the apocalypse, and she dares to take out such a huge loan. I don’t get what she’s thinking. There are so many abandoned factories, yet she insisted on that one with connections. What, is it some kind of special feng shui treasure land or something?
Never mind Zhou Bapi; even Jing Shu was still a bit bewildered.
Initially, I just wanted my supplies back. Then I got greedy and thought about leasing that Golden Land for ten years to secure my family’s future and plan my next big move. But I never, ever imagined that during the apocalypse, I’d take out a massive loan to buy an abandoned factory larger than a soccer field! And now, today’s windfall—Gold Dominator’s supplies worth four million Virtual Coins—will all be poured into it. Virtual Coins used to be just numbers to me. Now, those numbers haven’t just hit Zero; I’m also saddled with a massive debt. Every month, I’ll have to make repayments with supplies, making me a genuine negative-asset holder. Of course, I *could* provide various supplies, including those brought back from the United States later, but that wouldn’t be worth it, and I’m not willing to part with them. I’ll just use the cheapest red worm cake to settle the debt.
Logically, after the apocalypse, the value of houses and land should have dropped. However, the destructive power of natural disasters was too strong, submerging a large part of the city and causing many buildings to collapse. The number of usable buildings and plots of land had decreased by more than half. Many real estate agents had secretly built simple prefabricated houses for low rent. Otherwise, people had to live in the Government-distributed ones, where more than a dozen people shared a single house, unless they had connections and Virtual Coins to afford a private room.

chapters.title: Chapter 461: Mr. and Mrs. Jing’s Promotion and Wealth
chapters.content:
Chapter 461: Mr. and Mrs. Jing’s Promotion and Wealth
Huaxia’s wealth gap was still gradually widening.
"Miss Jing, I heard that this time you went to the United States and brought back a special medicine called ZS-880? And now, you are the only one who has it; they haven’t figured it out over there," Big Yellow Teeth Zhou Bapi leaned in. Old Jin’s survival now depended entirely on Miss Jing!
Jing Shu raised her eyebrows, not expecting the old man to be so well-informed. Seeing the hopeful look on Jin Tianci’s face, she understood. His preferential treatment wasn’t just because of Zhou Bapi; it was definitely also connected to the medicine she’d brought back from the United States, a drug capable of increasing cell division.
Jing Shu couldn’t help but ponder. In her previous life, the tyrant took office in either the fourth or fifth year, and Jin Tianci had died around that time. If it weren’t for her butterfly effect, perhaps Yang Yang, in her previous life, would have also gone to the United States and brought back this medicine. She might have given it to Jin Tianci, thus prolonging his life. However, ZS-880 had limited effects. Given Jin Tianci’s later physical condition, further absorption would have been futile, so ultimately, he only lived about a year longer before dying. That would explain why Jin Tianci died after the fourth year in that timeline.
If I extend Jin Tianci’s life in this timeline, will the tyrant still come to power in Wu City? She continuously weighed the pros and cons. If the tyrant doesn’t come, can Wu City survive the immense difficulties it’s facing? What would the consequences be? And even if I do extend Jin Tianci’s life, will the tyrant ascend to power anyway?
"Miss Jing?" Zhou Bapi quietly interrupted Jing Shu’s pondering.
"Oh, the medicine you mentioned... I do have a few doses. When I was in the Imperial Capital, I lent one to ’Seeking Donations for Research’ for their studies. They have the formula, but it might take some time for them to produce it. I’m just not sure about any side effects or adverse reactions. Plus, it has to be used with that cauldron, but the cauldron... it’s in the Imperial Capital," Jing Shu said.
Just then, Big Yellow Teeth Zhou Bapi shiftily pulled out an old handkerchief, the kind from the eighties. Inside the handkerchief, wrapped in wax paper, was a fine layer of rust powder beneath the smooth surface.
"This is powder scraped from the cauldron," he said. "Mix it with the medicine, and it can be injected. This stuff is extremely precious; they say scraping it a few hundred times could wear the cauldron out completely."
Jing Shu was rather taken aback, not expecting this ’medicine’ to be so crudely prepared. "Injecting this rusty iron... is that really safe?"
"Hah, compared to living a little longer, a few side effects are nothing!" Zhou Bapi said. "So, how about it? You can make any demands to Old Jin. Didn’t you just take out a loan for a big plot of land? Maybe have Old Jin reimburse you for it."
Jin Tianci interrupted Zhou Bapi. "That plot of land can’t compare to the value of this medicine. President Jing, please feel free to make any other requests. As long as I, Jin, can fulfill them, I will."
Even Mrs. Jin nodded excitedly. "Whatever you want, we’ll try our best to arrange it."
Jing Shu still had nine doses of the medicine. Its miraculous life-restoring effects, akin to bringing the dead back to life and fleshing out bones, definitely weren’t on par with the Spiritual Spring. However, possessing this item also provided a legitimate reason for her to save lives in the future. Therefore, the best use for this substance was to trade it at a high price, maximizing its value. Besides, Jin Tianci had to be saved. If he died prematurely and someone other than the tyrant came, or if his death drew the tyrant out ahead of schedule, it would be disastrous.
Now it was a matter of setting the price. It had to be reasonable; after all, Jin Tianci had previously done her a personal favor. What should she ask for?
"The medicine is at home," Jing Shu said. "I’ll bring it over, and then we can discuss terms."
"Good! You are indeed straightforward," Jin Tianci said, a trace of pleasure in his eyes. Indeed, who would want to die if they could live? Mrs. Jin turned away, tears streaming down her face; the news had come too suddenly for her to fully believe it yet.
"Let’s go, Miss Jing, I’ll go with you," Zhou Bapi offered.
Throughout the journey, Zhou Bapi kept advising Jing Shu. As a middleman, he didn’t want to see her get the short end of the stick. However, food wasn’t what Jing Shu needed right now; she was pursuing ’fine products.’ High-quality livestock or rare Domestic Poultry would be somewhat valuable to her. As for weapons, once this matter was settled, she could always go with Jun Jia—who had suffered a loss he couldn’t complain about—to pick from the armory.
Jing Shu’s current weaknesses were ’influence’ and ’authority.’ Soon, she began devising a plan.
After retrieving the medicine and returning to Jin Tianci’s villa, Jing Shu said, "I hear Minister Niu is due for a promotion soon. His position is being contested by Director Liu from the old district and Director Zhang from the Lingshan District, both recommended by higher-ups. However, I believe my mother, Minister Su from the new district, is more capable."
Somewhat drowsy, Jin Tianci pondered then nodded. "I also believe Minister Su is more capable of handling the ministerial post. After some more training, she can then follow Minister Niu to help manage Wu City’s agricultural affairs. You don’t need to worry about this; capable people, even if briefly overshadowed, will eventually shine. Your mother is a prime example."
"By the way, Jun Jia just sent over a document. The livestock farm has been performing well, showing exceptional efficiency, and has recently expanded. Therefore, they are promoting someone to deputy farm manager and have recommended the top performer, Jing An, to be the new farm manager. I only just realized Jing An is your father. What a coincidence!"
"What a coincidence indeed," she said. "But I’m well aware of my father’s professional abilities; he’s been ranked number one in evaluations every year."
The liquid in the glass bottle, initially a faint, starry color, turned a beautiful gilded hue after being mixed with the rust powder. The viscous fluid made the syringe barrel seem much wider; the thought of injecting this unknown substance into the body was daunting.
Once the last drop of liquid was injected, Jin Tianci fell into a deep sleep. The injection site began to swell and turn purplish. It was evident the medication was far from perfect. Zhou Bapi and the medical staff immediately got busy, and Jing Shu took her leave.
Another day was drawing to a close. Before heading home, Jing Shu found Jun Jia, Wu City’s third-in-command. Despite his disdainful and dissatisfied expression, he fulfilled his duty, escorting Jing Shu to Wu City’s legendary armory.
Jing Shu was filled with joy. Weapons were a dwindling resource these days; hoarding as much as she could was undoubtedly the right move.
"Here we are. Go in and choose, choose whatever you want," Jun Jia said, rolling his eyes.
The armory was indeed impressive, clearly built to withstand even bomb blasts. Its thick walls exuded a sense of security; if any disasters struck later, taking refuge here would surely be safe.
The massive, heavy iron door creaked open. Under the dim light, Jing Shu’s initial joy lasted less than two seconds before she stared in shock. The vast armory was almost completely empty!

chapters.title: Chapter 462: Move! See How Much You Can Take Away!
chapters.content:
Chapter 462: Move! See How Much You Can Take Away!
"What, that’s it? That’s all?" Jing Shu ran around the empty storeroom; it contained only worthless handguns and some scattered weapons.
"This is just the corridor of the armory; we haven’t reached the actual weapon storage yet."
"Then let’s go, take me inside," Jing Shu urged.
Jun Jia looked at Jing Shu as if she were a fool. "This is confidential. You can’t just walk in. The directive states that decommissioned weapons are to be exchanged for supplies, and these are all that’s left. You can only choose from these. Even if you go to my brother-in-law and cause a scene, you’ll still only get things from here. Besides, to take it a step further, you wouldn’t be able to get a permit for items from the main armory anyway."
Jing Shu deflated like a punctured ball.
She had hoped to score big, but she hadn’t expected the armory to be almost empty after several months of exchanges with over a dozen districts.
However, Jing Shu didn’t give up.
She still hoped to find something overlooked here.
But aside from an unwanted RPG, there was nothing else of value.
"Fine, add 20 RPGs."
"You’ve used up a quota of five hundred thousand," Jun Jia said with schadenfreude. After all, Jing Shu hadn’t paid anything and was about to take weapons that would normally have been part of several exchanges. The critical point was that he had to use his own supplies for Jing Shu to take the weapons; this made the fatty even more upset.
"Otherwise, I could take some broken guns too. After all, we’ve managed to get quite a few weapons from the United States," Jing Shu pondered,
almost ready to give up.
Then, she suddenly noticed an entire wall of wooden crates! There were rows upon rows of them, in all sorts of sizes!
"What are these..."
"This is the ammunition depot."
Jing Shu’s eyes suddenly lit up.
Ammunition, now that was something incredibly hard to come by! She had plenty of weapons, but because ammunition was so precious, she had barely used any.
"How come there’s so much ammunition left if the weapons are gone? Weren’t we told that after the apocalypse, bullets wouldn’t be manufactured anymore and that each one was precious?"
Jun Jia huffed, looking at Jing Shu as if she were an idiot. "Before the apocalypse, Huaxia had over 60 billion rounds of ammunition, with tens of billions more in reserve. Even though we’ve stopped production now, there haven’t been any major events lately, so there’s still enough for ordinary use."
"In that case, I’ll exchange the rest of my quota for bullets," Jing Shu rubbed her hands together, thrilled. Since new species began invading in the fifth year of the apocalypse, Huaxia’s ammunition supplies had become tight. Later, due to material shortages, few bullets could be produced, making them increasingly valuable.
Having these logistical support bullets was essential for Jing Shu to keep her arsenal well-stocked; otherwise, her weapons would become useless without bullets.
Frowning, Jun Jia thought about how the decommissioned weapons had been traded to prompt people to barter with the Government for bullets. The real prize wasn’t the weapons but the ammunition. It’s like how a car needs gasoline to run; petroleum is a global strategic resource. Consumables are what’s truly valuable. Similarly, by controlling ammunition, these merchants couldn’t stir up trouble. The nation truly controlled the outflow rate of ammunition.
"No. First, bullets are too expensive; it’s not worth it. Second, it’s impossible to release that much ammunition for your quota all at once," Jun Jia said firmly, shaking his head.
"How much Virtual Coin per round? And how much do these crates hold?" Jing Shu asked curiously.
"Thirty Virtual Coin per bullet. These crates hold one thousand rounds each, making them worth 30,000 Virtual Coin."
Jing Shu’s mouth fell open.
The price was indeed outrageously high. Before the apocalypse, a bullet cost only four cents to produce, but now 30 Virtual Coin could buy 10 steamed buns. Food prices had risen dozens of times in the apocalypse, and bullets were valued more than ten times higher than food. But this was a tactic to make merchants exchange bullets at high prices; to put it bluntly, it was still about collecting food and material reserves.
"If you don’t let me exchange for bullets, then even if I take all the weapons in this storeroom, it probably won’t meet my quota, right? Besides... Mrs. Jin has already told you about today’s incident, right? If things go smoothly, her husband might live a lot longer..."
Jun Jia remained silent, wiping the sweat from his forehead. What should he do? This girl was tough to handle, threatening not to leave without bullets and ready to go complain. He detested people who resorted to crying and complaining, just like her sister when she was young... Besides, the items in the storeroom truly weren’t enough for her quota... hmm...
"This is what we’ll do!" Jun Jia suddenly got an idea. "You can exchange for these bullets. Take as many as you can move today. However, the conditions are that you can only move them once, you can’t ask for help, and you must move them before the next shift change. Don’t say I’m being stingy. You can stack them, drag them with ropes, use leverage—any tools you currently have on you are fair game.
Now, you have thirty minutes to move them from here to the exit, which is about five hundred meters away. If you agree, you can start now. If you don’t, then I really can’t help you. Just take the other assorted weapons in the storeroom and leave."
Meaning, from now on, she could use any method she could think of to move the ammunition from its storage place to the exit in one go, and any bullets she got out would be hers.
Jing Shu raised an eyebrow and lifted one of the crates. It weighed about ten-odd kilograms and contained 1,000 bullets.
Ten such crates stacked together would weigh over a hundred kilograms—impossible for an ordinary person to move, even with tools.
A thousand bullets, what good would that do? A machine gun could fire thousands of rounds a minute, and a rifle’s rate of fire was about 650 rounds per minute. Even with burst fire, a few hundred rounds would be gone in minutes.
Of course, this didn’t count someone like Jing Shu, who was so frugal she’d only used a few hundred rounds in total over the past one or two years, and only when absolutely necessary. After all, Jing Shu was planning for the future. Opportunities to use bullets in these past few years had been few, as she hadn’t encountered any particularly dangerous situations.
But things would be different later on. Plus, with bullets becoming scarcer... Jing Shu felt this was a rare opportunity; it would be best to stockpile as many bullets as possible in one go.
At the current market price, one crate was worth 30,000 Virtual Coin (an inflated price). If auctioned later, the price would only get higher. Her quota could get her 120 crates, which was 120,000 bullets. But judging by Jun Jia’s earlier expression, there was absolutely no way he’d let her take that many.
"Fine. So I can’t go out to call for people, nor can I find other tools; I can only use what I have on me, and I can only move them once. I agree. I’ll start now. Let me confirm one last time: no matter how much I can move by myself, it’s all mine?"
Jun Jia nodded. "That’s the idea."
CLICK.
"Alright, you better keep your word. I’m recording this."
Jun Jia chuckled. "Go ahead and record. Let’s see how much you can move."

chapters.title: Chapter 463: Bullet as a Wheel?
chapters.content:
Chapter 463: Bullet as a Wheel?
The bullets and the boxes were deadly heavy. Even if she were Hercules, how much could she possibly move? Could a person move several tons of bullets without any mechanical help? The exit was hundreds of meters away. Even if she were Hercules, did she have the endurance to carry them that far? And how much could she actually carry?
"Fifty kilograms at most. The best record in our team was someone carrying ten boxes, 120 kilograms, which is about 10,000 bullets, roughly equivalent to 300,000 Virtual Coins."
Jun Jia found a spot to sit down and leisurely shook his leg. He guessed that the woman would drag them using her clothes, but a normal person would run out of energy after just a hundred or two hundred meters. Even someone trained might not be able to carry ten boxes of bullets that far, let alone how such a petite woman could manage to drag the bullets to the main gate.
Time was pressing. Jing Shu first confirmed the type of bullets she needed and, to her surprise, found there was even large-caliber ammunition for the German MAN roof-mounted recoilless guns.
Then, according to her needs, she stacked up the boxes one by one. The saying ’a snake trying to swallow an elephant’ perfectly described Jing Shu in this moment. She stacked boxes ten high, reaching two meters, and arranged them into sixteen rows in total, forming a small mountain of ammunition. To move 2 tons of bullets and boxes all at once was impossible for Jing Shu. Not only would she die of exhaustion, but it would also draw unwanted attention.
Shocking! A woman in Wu City lifted 2 tons of bullets and strode briskly, only to be captured by the [Sponsorship-Seeking Research Institute] for study, suspected of having evolved a new gene! Such news would be nothing but trouble for me. The greatest advantage humans have is their brains, after all. And the brain is a fantastic thing.
"Just asking, will these bullets explode if they’re crushed?"
Jun Jia made a ’PFFT!’ sound of contempt. Shaking his leg, he informed the ignorant Jing Shu, "Only black powder would explode. These are treated with desensitized TNT. They only explode with a detonator."
"Then I’m relieved." Jing Shu clapped her hands and took out some special steel wire she had gotten from Qian Duoduo. She chose the large-caliber bullets, placed them one by one under the bottommost ammo box, and then gave it a test push.
"SQUEAK!" The bullets were slightly deformed by the pressure. Their altered, now somewhat elliptical, shapes made it difficult to push the stack any further; it got stuck. This implied that stacking the boxes so high made them too heavy and would impede progress.
Jing Shu began to adjust the positions, placing only eight boxes in a stack.
"Hurry up, you only have fifteen minutes left, and you haven’t even started moving." Jun Jia frowned.
What is this little girl trying to do? She spent ten minutes moving out all these boxes of bullets; is she planning to take them all? Is she crazy?!
She has spent another five minutes tying things up, conducting various experiments. Is she planning to bind bullets beneath those boxes and use their rounded heads to move forward? However, such smooth bullets can’t be fixed in place. Once fixed, they can’t be rolled like a cartwheel, just as her experiment showed—at most, she could only push the bullet-supported boxes forward a meter. How long would it take to push them to the door that way?
In the end, bullets are not wheels; they are oddly shaped, pointed at one end and flat at the other. How could they possibly serve as rolling wheels? Dream on!
Heh, it’d be best if she dawdles a bit longer. When time’s up and she can’t take a single bullet, I’ll just give her some random stuff to send her away,
Jun Jia thought.
Having completed her trial, Jing Shu began to assemble rapidly, weaving two narrow but very long tracks. In Jing Shu’s hands, the large-caliber bullets swiftly transformed into tracks. Jun Jia’s mouth hung open.
These large-caliber bullets, dammit, are good stuff! Well...
Anyway, she can’t take them out. At worst, we’ll just have someone clean up and put them back later,
Jun Jia mused.
Jun Jia checked his watch. "Only five minutes left, and you haven’t even left yet! Even if you run, you won’t make it out. Just give it up and pick something else so you can leave."
Jing Shu let out a long sigh, having just fitted the last section of track. She clapped her hands and said, "Perfect timing. Let’s go."
As she spoke, she pulled forcefully. The first row of boxes started moving. Then, under Jun Jia’s stunned gaze, these stacked boxes began to roll forward, one row after another, like a train. A faint creaking noise accompanied the movement, as the square-ended bullets, pieced together to form the tracks, created indentations that perfectly cradled the four corners of the boxes above, holding them securely.
Each ’car’ was a stack of only eight boxes, but there were a total of twenty such ’cars,’ all connected by steel wires. The lowest layer comprised large-caliber bullets woven into two long tracks on the ground. These tracks continuously propelled them forward. It looked as if twenty train cars, each with its own tracks and linked by steel wires, were being powered by a locomotive. Jing Shu was that locomotive.
Jing Shu ran ahead joyfully while Jun Jia chased after her, sweating profusely. A mix of fear, a sense of the absurd, and disbelief surged within him.
Has the world gone mad, or have I? What the heck is this woman doing? Can bullets actually be used as wheels?
Though Jun Jia kept cursing, hoping the rope would break midway or that the entire assembly would just fall apart, the ’train’ seemed as steady as a rock.
"Slow down, I can’t keep up!"
Wasn’t she supposed to be a simple porter, just using her own strength? And yet, she’d sneakily added wheels!
"We won’t make it on time if we don’t hurry."
"You’re cheating! This doesn’t count!"
"I used the method you mentioned, dragging with a rope, right? I also used the tools I had on me; I didn’t leverage any outside force. As for the bullets underneath, there were no rules saying they couldn’t be used as a base. If you want to cry foul, we can go talk to your brother-in-law and see what he says."
Jing Shu was a seasoned pro at this, moving quickly, precisely, and steadily. Jun Jia, the greasy, middle-aged, chubby man, simply couldn’t keep up. By the time he huffed and puffed his way out, Jing Shu was nowhere in sight.
Only the old gatekeeper remained, scowling as he held out his hand. "You need to settle the bill for the ammunition that was just taken."
Oh, nephew, it looks like your uncle might have to dip into your little piggy bank again. I’m so sorry...
Jun Jia lamented internally.
「 」
"Suddenly, a directive came from higher up today, swapping my name in for a deputy director slot that was meant for someone else. Now even the director is very polite to me."
Mrs. Jing added, "A while ago, Minister Niu said his successor for his position was already decided. But today, I was suddenly notified that I will take over his position after some time! Minister Niu said that my backer must be incredibly powerful to have pushed out the internally decided candidate so easily. He also remarked that I’d jumped four ranks in just two years, a faster rise than even he had managed!"
Mr. Jing and Mrs. Jing exchanged looks.
What a coincidence!
they thought, then glanced toward Jing Shu, who was arranging ammunition in the warehouse.
Could it be our daughter’s doing again? Yet today, our daughter is unusually excited. She didn’t even mind that Su Long ate all the baked gluten and cold skin noodles Grandma Jing had made especially for her.
Instead, she smiled tenderly at Su Long and said, "If it’s all eaten, no big deal. We’ll just make more."

chapters.title: Chapter 464: Jing Shu’s Plans and Intentions
chapters.content:
Chapter 464: Jing Shu’s Plans and Intentions
This abnormal behavior made Su Long immediately beg Grandma Jing to teach him how to wash flour and make cold skin noodles and wheat gluten. He promised that he would soon let Sister Jing eat her beloved cold skin noodles so she would no longer say such horrifying things. He was wrong; he would not overeat again.
However, Jing Shu was genuinely in a good mood today. Although the process had not been entirely pleasant, the result was a bountiful harvest. After briefly updating Mr. Jing and Mrs. Jing on the situation and finishing their meal, Jing Shu locked herself in her bedroom on the second floor of the German MAN RV. She began to thoroughly tally her supplies and the items that could be openly declared. This, of course, included everyone’s gifts.
The fat chicken lay in its nest, fiercely staring at the Sulfur Ant Queen, which was busily laying eggs, and at these Sulfuric Acid Ants continually taking over its territory, making it quite agitated.
While tallying her existing supplies, Jing Shu continued to plan for the future. After all, she sometimes had so many things that she would forget what she possessed and their uses.
First were the 120,000 various kinds of bullets they acquired today, which should last for a long time without issue. They could even support Jing Shu’s side to fully engage in several small-scale wars.
Next were today’s supplies. They didn’t take up much space, so she categorized and placed them accordingly. Daily necessities were stored in the villa area, and industrial goods were put in the warehouse. However, since most of the food lacked Spiritual Spring essence, Jing Shu didn’t care for it. She planned to use it for fostering relationships and as gifts, considering it suitable for her extended family and even friends.
Products with Spiritual Spring characteristics were reserved for her own family’s use.
Later, she had exchanged 4 million Virtual Coins’ worth of red earthworms and Gold Dominator for supplies also valued at 4 million Virtual Coins. However, she then used these 4 million Virtual Coins to purchase that 20-acre plot of prime land. Additionally, she had to use all the Virtual Coins she had saved over the years just to make the down payment. From now on, she would have to make monthly loan repayments using food and supplies.
Jing Shu began to jot down her current issues and plans:
1. Renovate the factory land and put it into production as soon as possible. Resolve the accommodation problem for the thousands of nearby people with Jun Jia.
2. Find a suitable place in the factory to breed a batch of Sulfuric Acid Ants and extract sulfuric acid from them.
Jing Shu already had a plan for the primary use of the purchased land: the Spiral Fish Stink Algae Wu You’ai had given her yesterday.
Second Form!
With a shift of her consciousness, Jing Shu saw her Magic Cube Space packed to the brim. She passed by the ’herds of cattle and sheep’ and squatted in a corner of the Magic Cube Space, observing what she had cultivated the previous day.
It was covered in layers of rotten corpse insects, which were now ubiquitous, feeding on the algae. Jing Shu had scooped a large number of these from a stinking gutter the previous day, killed them, cleaned them, and placed them with the Spiral Fish Stink Algae as food.
Wu You’ai had said that as long as they had protein, these algae could grow and reproduce like crazy. To accelerate the process, Jing Shu had also supplied them with Batch No. 2 spiritual spring liquid.
And now, in just a single day, one cubic meter of space had been completely filled by this seaweed!
Once the seaweed was cultivated, Jing Shu placed a portion of it, less than half, with the red earthworms. This seaweed served as feed for various fish, as it could autonomously synthesize protein and assimilate nitrogen. However, Jing Shu didn’t plan to use it just for feeding fish; she intended to use it for breeding red earthworms.
Previously, the red earthworms had multiplied like crazy without any feed, but the current ones needed something more. Despite Jing Shu’s many attempts, they still couldn’t breed as they once had. Solely using the Spiritual Spring for reproduction was impractical. How much Spiritual Spring did she possess? And how much would be needed to breed them on a large scale?
In the end, individual power still seemed too insignificant.
I hope this algae doesn’t disappoint me.
3. If the algae proves to be a viable feed for red earthworms and boosts their reproduction rate, implement the next phase: recruit workers for the factory site. Designate one area for the low-cost collection or breeding of rotten corpse insects, another for cultivating algae, and a third for feeding red earthworms to expand their breeding scale.
There are too many rotten corpse insects. If I can truly find their value and utilize them, perhaps I could alleviate some of the disaster in Wu City’s fifth year, right?
Indeed, Jing Shu acquired that plot of land not just for herself but also to mitigate the scenario of a total crop failure in the fifth year. Back then, Government was recklessly cutting budgets everywhere, even going so far as to confiscate Qian Duoduo’s Stone Garden and kill Qian Duoduo—all because of the pressure from food shortages.
If Jing Shu’s factory could mass-breed and cultivate red earthworms and align with the Government, perhaps when famine struck, fewer people would die, and the Tyrant wouldn’t be pushed into a corner.
In that case, the Tyrant probably wouldn’t target Stone Garden anymore... right? After all, I also hold shares in Stone Garden.
But who knows, with the Tyrant’s temperament.
4. Investigate if the drug ZS880 can enhance the reproductive ability of red earthworms and algae if they reach their natural reproductive limits, based on the knowledge that cell division is finite.
Thus, Jing Shu initiated the second batch of experiments with the algae and red earthworms.
5. Await the arrival of the second batch of supplies, Seeds, and rare minerals from the Imperial Capital. Discuss with Jin Tianci upon their arrival.
6. Address Hao Yunlai’s unconscious state. Study the withered tree and red liquid. After consulting with Yang Yang, begin experiments to verify her guess...
or rather, begin treating Hao Yunlai. Yes, everything I do is to save my companion.
7. Breed lion-headed geese. Remodel the family’s newly acquired large courtyard. She was quite looking forward to the 300-square-meter space.
8. Prepare for the mudslides expected in six months. The villa and the large rear courtyard will be the first to be submerged. Recall the effective method someone used in her previous life and devise a plausible reason for constructing such a large protective structure.
Jing Shu, biting her pen, had a sudden flash of inspiration.
No need for reasons. I’ll do it just because I like it, because I’m extravagant!
9. Address recent mental fogginess, memory lapses, and forgetfulness—likely a new ability from the Magic Cube Space’s impending upgrade. Cautiously welcome and expedite this upgrade, as the current Magic Cube Space is always insufficient!
10. Acquire an armed helicopter for transportation. Set this as a near-term goal.
That’s enough for now; I’ll add more if I think of anything else.
Jing Shu, satisfied with her recent plans, stayed up late to record all the supplies and place them in the Magic Cube Space before finally going to sleep.
「The next day」
Jing Shu, sporting her ’panda eyes’ with satisfaction, began distributing the gifts she had sorted out the night before.

chapters.title: Chapter 465: Eternal Love
chapters.content:
Chapter 465: Eternal Love
These gifts had either been transported across the ocean from the United States or collected by Jing Shu in her space. For her closest family members, Jing Shu always chose the best to give.
However, as the chief contributor this time, fat chicken naturally had to be the first to be rewarded. Its favorite Fried Chicken Legs arrived by the basketful. Not only that, Jing Shu also rewarded it with a whole drop of Spiritual Spring. Clutching a chicken leg in its beak and having swallowed the drop of Spiritual Spring, it strutted off to show off to Number 3.
"Mom, you’ve always wanted luxury items. Here’s a Hermes bag, Chanel perfume, and Estee Lauder cosmetics... Oh, and if Youai and Third Aunt like them, they can take some too."
Wu You’ai adjusted her glasses and shook her head. "Neither Mom nor I like these things."
Mrs. Jing examined them and adored them, much like a child who finally gets a longed-for toy they couldn’t afford. She sighed, "The quality isn’t even that great. Why do so many people like them? This is the same bag Yu Caini carried before the apocalypse. Oh, and this fragrance is a bit overpowering..."
Things she couldn’t afford before were now easily accessible.
Jing Shu felt that truly possessing them was just so-so; people indeed chase what they can never obtain. Yet, the joy of the wealthy was something she couldn’t have imagined before. This feeling of doing as one wished—Jing Shu had become addicted to it. Thus, she craved even more power and possessions.
"Dad, here’s the Rolex watch you always wanted. I casually got you a dozen or so; you can rotate them. Oh, and these are various red wines and whiskies from the United States. You and Grandpa can decide how to best store them."
"Alright, my girl really gets me."
"Grandpa, these are luxury cigarettes from the United States. Try them and see how different they are from ours. Oh, and this is a whole piece of crocodile skin. See if you can make something suitable with it."
Mr. Jing examined it for a while. "Such a large piece of crocodile skin! Let’s just make leather gun holsters and quivers for each of us."
Wu You’ai received a pair of live king crabs, which were very valuable for her research. Third Aunt received a lot of fabric brought back from the United States, as she liked to make her own clothes. Moreover, Jing Shu had also contacted Zijin, who would be returning in a couple of days. Jing Shu also had a batch of cowhides and sheepskins and wanted them to hurry and make several more sets of gloves, socks, and leather shoes for everyone. After all, the harsh winter of the fifth year was rapidly approaching.
The temperature in Wu City was already below zero, so cold it was unbearable. Making more quilted cotton clothes and fur-lined coats was perfectly timed.
For her Uncle’s family, she brought household goods and various meats from the United States. Their house had just collapsed in the earthquake, so they needed many things for resettlement. At the same time, Jing Shu was also considering where her Uncle’s family would live next.
Jing Shu finally looked towards Grandma Jing, who was looking at her expectantly. Then, as if performing a magic trick, she produced a candlestick. "Grandma," she said, "this is an ever-burning candlestick for you. It’s powered by a chip and magnets, so theoretically, it will never go out. This way, you won’t keep saying it’s a waste of electricity and refuse to turn on the lights anymore."
Grandma Jing took it, astonished, and examined it from all angles. The brightness was soft and just right. "This is truly magical! Good, very good! I’ll put it by my bedside. Grandma needs this."
"Oh, Grandma, you might be quite busy from now on. Look, I brought back lobsters, sea urchins, and king crabs from the United States; they all need to be raised in the pond. There’s also longan, large hams, tuna, foie gras, and caviar that I put in the large refrigerator the day before yesterday. I also brought plenty of olive oil, peanut oil, and rapeseed oil. When you cook, use more oil; don’t just wipe the pan with a piece of pork rind and call that oiling it."
This elicited a burst of laughter from the whole family. Grandma Jing’s thriftiness was legendary, especially since the apocalypse. But hearing about so many supplies, her eyes crinkled with so much joy they nearly disappeared. What’s most comforting during a famine? It’s when, after days of anxiously watching the food in the storehouse dwindle bit by bit, your heart burning with worry, especially when fat chicken isn’t around, Jing Shu returns and completely refills everything. That fills people with an immense sense of security. This was Grandma Jing’s greatest happiness. She would even scatter a few extra handfuls of feed for the chickens now.
Yesterday, Jing Shu had brought back an astonishing amount of food from Li Yuetian, surprising the entire family. Today, Jing Shu told them a second batch of supplies was on its way.
At this point, the family wondered if Jing Shu had gone robbing abroad. Or were resources in the United States truly so plentiful that you could just pick them up off the ground, like in Dubai where luxury cars supposedly littered the streets, unwanted?
"Oh, Grandpa, these are coffee tree saplings I brought back from the United States. Could you please transplant them?"
"You child, why didn’t you bring these out yesterday? Let me quickly check if they’re still alive."
In just two days, Mr. Jing had already built a shed in the backyard, connecting it to the boiler room’s underfloor heating. It was specifically for breeding Jing Shu’s lion-head geese. When the family learned that these two precious birds were rented for breeding, they couldn’t have been more attentive.
However, they hadn’t been fed for two days. Jing Shu said it was to break these two pampered geese of their habits. After all, in the Imperial Capital, they were coddled like pandas, not only constantly fighting but also being picky eaters. Most annoyingly, they wouldn’t even deign to look at you properly.
But fat chicken was well-trained. It frequently dangled juicy chicken legs in front of the two geese, eating with relish until its beak was oily, and it wasn’t long before the blockheaded geese capitulated. Thus, they received the same treatment as the other chickens and ducks at Jing Shu’s house: ordinary feed, vegetable roots containing Spiritual Spring, and leftover bone broth from the family’s meals—nothing was to be wasted, they ate whatever was available.
After Jing Shu added the Spiritual Spring from Number 8, she left them to it. Fat chicken, with its sheepdog-like instincts, had an obsessive dedication to managing the domestic poultry. It loved being the ’class monitor,’ showing off and bossing others around, exactly like Jing Shu herself ten years ago. Regardless, the task of breeding the lion-head geese proceeded smoothly. Now, it was just a matter of waiting for the ’silly geese’ to lay eggs and hatch goslings.
The next day, Zhou Bapi called, asking when Jing Shu would return to work at the Medicine Association. He also mentioned that Jin Tianci’s treatment was very effective. After a full day of diarrhea, he had expelled a lot of toxins. Although he looked haggard, his complexion had improved, and his various indicators were much stronger. He would be back to normal after another week of rest.
Only then did Jing Shu feel relieved. "I need to extend my leave for a while. I don’t have time to go to the Medicine Association recently. Just call me if there’s a competition."
Jun Jia didn’t dare to neglect the factory matters. Jing Shu received a notification that in five days, she could go to take over the factory and handle the various procedures. During this grace period, Jing Shu didn’t waste time. Instead, she repeatedly conducted experiments with seaweed, rotten corpse insects, and red earthworms.
Jing Shu had succeeded in the first step: with the help of the rotten corpse insects, she could indeed propagate seaweed in large quantities and quickly. It was currently unknown how many propagation cycles this original liquid could sustain. However, the second step was somewhat difficult. When the seaweed (to be used as feed) and the red earthworms were placed together, the red earthworms’ reproduction rate was not as fast as the seaweed’s.

chapters.title: Chapter 466: Raising Chickens Improperly Brings Tears to Loved Ones
chapters.content:
Chapter 466: Raising Chickens Improperly Brings Tears to Loved Ones
Within just one day, the space was filled to the brim with seaweed, yet the red earthworms had only about doubled in number.
We definitely need to speed up the experiments. It’s a pity the Magic Cube Space is only this large. Now I can’t even section off a few extra spaces to conduct trials.
Jing Shu felt somewhat disheartened. If the Magic Cube Space were a bit larger, she could have used dozens of separate, small spaces to conduct these experiments simultaneously. Unfortunately, the space was now so crammed that she couldn’t free up any more room. This was the biggest drawback of the Magic Cube Space: although it could be freely combined into a large space, the smallest it could be divided into was a single cubic meter.
Now, many spaces were exactly half a cubic meter, filled with half-eaten foods like Crucian Carp Tofu Soup and Seafood Shrimp Porridge. One-cubic-meter spaces couldn’t be partitioned further. If the Magic Cube Space didn’t upgrade soon, she would have to gather these miscellaneous foods to resolve the crowding.
Forget it. While I still have time, I might as well resolve the issue with Hao Yunlai.
Jing Shu had originally planned to wait until Hao Yunlai’s family all agreed to the risks before attempting such a dangerous method, which was why she had delayed for some time. However, she hadn’t expected Yang Yang to say that Hao Yunlai had jinxed his entire family to death. And these past few days, the people of Wu City could do nothing. So, Jing Shu decided to try a desperate remedy, like treating a dead horse as if it were still alive.
Thus, after Jing Shu prepared the materials, she arranged to meet Yang Yang the next day to find Hao Yunlai.
「The next day.」
Jing Shu, still dreaming, was woken by her family’s chattering inside the RV. The weather outside remained gloomy, and a chill hung in the air. She wondered if the people in the tents on the back mountain had frozen stiff. The weather had been getting progressively colder, driving many who had previously braved the elements back into houses.
Walking from her bedroom to the first floor of the RV, she saw her whole family excitedly gathered around the TV near the dining area.
The TV was broadcasting Wu City’s morning news. The female anchor, her face clean and clear, was presenting live without makeup.
"According to data submitted by Wu City’s deputy livestock farm director, Jing An, Wu City has now issued licenses for 50,000 chickens, 2,000 cows, and 5,000 pigs. Sixty thousand people have received chicken breeding permits after training. Deputy Director Jing An says..."
The scene shifted to Jing An at the gloomy livestock farm, dressed in a breeding uniform, saying, "For just an additional five Virtual Coins, you could spin for a lucky number like 8888 or 9999, boosting your prestige while walking your chicken. We urge all owners who haven’t registered to come and get their chickens tested, vaccinated, and licensed, and to earn your chicken breeding certificate after training. This ensures the safety of you and your beloved chickens. Reject unlicensed chicken breeding that spreads viruses.
Wu City Livestock Farm’s Jing An reminds you: There may be thousands of chickens and ducks, but safety is paramount. Unregulated chicken farming brings tears to your loved ones."
The scene cut back to the news anchor, who said, "The rampant virus has infected many domestic poultry, and some criminals are selling this infected poultry at low prices on the Black Market. The public must remember: [Any chicken without a license is not a good chicken.] Reporting is rewarded..."
Jing Shu’s lips twitched. Mr. Jing had actually made it on the news and had said such things! It was truly a case of looking at someone with new eyes after just three days’ absence.
CLAP! CLAP!
The family clapped, cheering for Mr. Jing. Rubbing the back of his neck with his broad hand, Mr. Jing laughed and said, "We should also get a license for our Fat Chicken, though I’m not sure which category it falls under. And those two Little Black chickens need to be registered too. Oh, and the lion-headed goose—should it get a Wu City license or one from the Imperial Capital? I heard it’s tough to get a license in the Imperial Capital; people are even queuing up for a lottery."
Jing Shu sat down and voraciously devoured Grandma Jing’s breakfast: bite-sized, translucent, and savory Shrimp Dumplings; soft, meaty, steamed pork dumplings; crispy-shelled egg tarts; and giant soup dumplings as large as a bowl. Inserting a straw, Jing Shu slurped the crab-roe-flavored soup, scalding her tongue. It took her a while to answer, "If it’s licensed, does that mean we can’t kill and eat it anymore?"
I never raised chickens in the previous apocalypse, only knowing they were gold-devouring creatures that laid eggs whenever they felt like it.
The Fat Chicken looked over in terror, backing away relentlessly.
What did that mean? Was that something a human would say? I’m already selling eggs to survive, so why are there always troublemakers trying to kill me?
Mr. Jing laughed. "Of course, chickens and ducks bought from our legitimate ’4S store’ can’t be killed. They have to be brought in for annual inspections, and when registering their feather patterns, dyeing isn’t allowed. If there are too many violations in a year, causing the chicken to get sick or lose weight, not only will the chicken be confiscated, but various certificates will also be revoked. However, home-bred chickens aren’t under our jurisdiction, so you can kill them as you please."
The Fat Chicken shivered.
Jing Shu continued to wolf down her food and nodded in understanding. "Then, for the Fat Chicken, just register it as you see fit. As for the lion-headed goose, register it for Wu City."
Whether we’ll even return to the Imperial Capital is still uncertain.
After finishing her meal, Jing Shu left, leaving the Fat Chicken’s mournful little eyes behind her.
A chilly wind gusted as deep night fell upon the desolate wilderness.
"Does Hao Yunlai live here?" Jing Shu looked up, pulling her thick cotton coat and bulky cotton pants tighter around her, staring at the sinister, horrifying mansion. She glanced around.
This damn place is built right on top of a graveyard!
Yang Yang exhaled, a puff of white in the cold air, and put on his military-style leather cap, which made him look much more handsome. "This used to be Hao Wangjiao Village, home to Wu City’s famous pharmaceutical family, with a hundred or so members. Hao Yunlai jinxed everyone in the village who shared his surname to death. Naturally, their ancestral tombs are all buried here."
"Second Form, activate!" A ripple of air spread out, and the Magic Cube Space expanded outwards from Jing Shu. Soon, the mooing of cows and the diligent buzzing of Bees could be heard. Only then did Jing Shu feel much better.
Hao Yunlai is truly terrifying!
Just then, Yang Yang looked down and kicked his leather boots. His tight pants made a creaking sound as he spoke, his cool voice tinged with regret, "Did you know? Hao Wangjiao Village got rich making fake medicine, committing all sorts of unconscionable deeds. After Hao Yunlai was born, he successively jinxed all his clansmen to death. When they discovered he was a Heavenly Slaughter Star, they tried to kill him, but to no avail. He lived on, bearing the curses of his clan and the scorn of the outside world, receiving neither familial love nor compassion from others."
Jing Shu remained silent. She hadn’t expected the sleepy, Zen-like man to have such a tragic past. Indeed, it was thanks to Hao Yunlai that she had escaped with her life in the United States.
Even so, that doesn’t offset this time’s medical expenses.
Yang Yang chuckled lightly, and the atmosphere warmed slightly. Jing Shu entered the gloomy old mansion with her suitcase. It was filled with various precious mahogany furniture, all covered in dust and shrouded in a dead silence.
Hao Yunlai lay in a cold room. Wrapped in thick blankets, he was still shivering, yet soft snores escaped him. Yang Yang shook his head; Hao Yunlai had been sleeping like this for more than ten days.
An old, hunched, deaf, and mute man was taking care of Hao Yunlai in the house.
"That old man is Hao San’er, the only one who wasn’t jinxed to death," Yang Yang explained.
Jing Shu set down her medical box. She curiously watched the old man sitting by the stove, warming himself and completely ignoring the freezing, shivering Hao Yunlai. She asked, "Is it because his sins were the lightest, so he wasn’t jinxed to death?"

chapters.title: Chapter 467: The Rapidly Growing Spiritual Spring!
chapters.content:
Chapter 467: The Rapidly Growing Spiritual Spring!
Yang Yang shook his head. "Because he committed the gravest of sins; he was the one who concocted the fake medicine’s recipe. He is the root cause of everything. Perhaps because his sins are too profound, he must live to be 99 and endure all manner of suffering before going to the Eighteen Levels of Hell."
"Alright." Jing Shu shrugged and opened the medical box to perform some routine checks, making her appear very professional. In Hao San’er’s eyes, however, this was met with a look of disdain. He even scoffed, "Pfft!" then spat, sending a glob of liquid flying a considerable distance. His expression clearly said: "Someone as half-baked as you trying to figure something out? That’s a joke. The Hao family lad’s soul is suffering in the Eighteen Levels of Hell right now."
The Spiritual Spring couldn’t wake Hao Yunlai, so she wouldn’t waste it.
Jing Shu coughed twice, dropped the pretense, and took out the withered tree soaking in the red liquid.
Yang Yang pointed at the withered tree, surprised. "Isn’t that the thing from the billionaire Job Sibus’s research institute in the United States? The one you exchanged for 50 Contribution Value?"
Jing Shu nodded.
Yang Yang is indeed observant,
she thought, which made her even more cautious.
Carefully, Jing Shu took out a knife and sliced open the withered tree. Indeed, after soaking for several days, the withered tree—which was neither Undead nor growing, and which even the billionaire’s research institute couldn’t manage—not only responded to Jing Shu’s treatment but had also sprouted a Blood-colored Crystal the size of a fingernail!
Jing Shu had long suspected these withered trees acted as converters, slowly transforming the red liquid into crystals. However, she didn’t know the difference between the Blood-colored Crystals and the red liquid, nor their specific uses or methods of application.
She carefully stitched up the wound on the withered tree and hesitated while holding the Blood-colored Crystal. Back then, she had touched the gate to the fourth dimension and nearly died, lacking a point of support. The Magic Cube Space had provided that support, and it was the Blood Crystal that had changed the timeline of her life.
It allowed her to return to the moment just before her body collapsed. However, her body would still feel agonizing pain. Time could not change memory, nor could it alter the fact that Jing Shu’s body had already been torn apart—the body retains such memories. It was just like when she had returned to ten years prior after dying in her previous life.
If my guess is correct,
Jing Shu mused,
such crystals should possess the trait of ’allowing a person to return to a certain timeline.’ For instance, if your body was riddled with bullets and beyond saving, the crystal could return you to the moment before you were shot. However, your body would still feel the pain of being pierced by countless arrows.
So, after all that, how is this supposed to be used?
"Right, the crystal can only exert its effect inside the withered tree! Back then, I felt it melting in my brain," Jing Shu clapped her hands. She drove the knife into Hao Yunlai’s left shoulder—the closest point to the heart and thus conducive to absorption—then quickly stuffed the Blood-colored Crystal into the flesh. Blood gushed out, and Hao Yunlai’s lips quickly turned ashen as his face paled.
Is it working? What on earth is she doing?
Yang Yang didn’t understand.
What Jing Shu is doing can’t be called a risk anymore, can it? Forcibly inserting something into his body... what on earth was that?
Jing Shu quickly stitched up the large incision and applied a rolled Black Pill before she breathed a sigh of relief. She then began to vigorously massage the wound, hoping the Blood Crystal would fuse quickly.
Hao Yunlai’s wound occasionally spurted blood, but that wasn’t particularly troubling. These things didn’t come with instruction manuals; she had to figure everything out herself. If the Blood-colored Crystal proved useless, she could cut the flesh open again in a few days and retrieve it. After all, the crystal was quite precious.
She had painstakingly collected the red liquid in the United States for over ten days, managing to gather only this small amount. Although she didn’t know what it could do, it was undoubtedly very precious.
After pressing a few times, Jing Shu felt the crystal shrink.
"There’s hope!" Jing Shu exclaimed excitedly. But unexpectedly, in the very next second, her mind was bombarded with wave after wave, as if someone were furiously ringing a bell by her ear. Jing Shu’s head thundered, seeming to resonate intensely with something else, and then she fainted.
Yang Yang: "???"
What’s happening?
It was Jing Shu’s second ’soul out of body’ experience. She watched, wide-eyed, as ’herself’—dressed in a dowdy, padded cotton jacket—fell to the ground.
Even I think this outfit is too old-fashioned...
From a God’s Eye View, Jing Shu observed the entire house, still not understanding what had transpired.
What’s wrong with me? Did I trigger something again? But I didn’t do anything.
Jing Shu rested her chin in her hand, starting to feel a little anxious.
I’m not going to die just like this, am I?
"DRIP, DRIP, DRIP..."
At that moment, the sound of dripping water reached her ears. Jing Shu looked towards the center of her Magic Cube Space. She discovered that the central cubic meter—the very spot that produced only 20 drops of Spiritual Spring a day, no more and no less than exactly 1 gram daily—was now frenziedly gushing Spiritual Spring. Jing Shu could clearly hear the wonderful sound of each drop of Spiritual Spring landing.
What’s going on? The source that usually produces only 1 gram of Spiritual Spring a day is now producing like crazy? That must be dozens of drops already, three or four days’ worth!
Jing Shu was both shocked and delighted. The preciousness of the Spiritual Spring went without saying. Every day, Jing Shu would dilute the Spiritual Spring according to a numbered sequence and distribute it for various needs. She and the fat chicken required a significant daily intake. Now, there was also ’Number 3’ to consider, in addition to the villa’s vegetable garden, her family, the pond, and so on—all of which needed Spiritual Spring.
The production of Spiritual Spring was already failing to keep up with Jing Shu’s consumption.
However, the Spiritual Spring was now dripping rapidly, making Jing Shu’s jaw drop in astonishment. But then she quickly realized what was going on!
The Blood-colored Crystal in her space, which she had risked her life to obtain from the gate of the fourth dimension and had been reluctant to use on Hao Yunlai just moments ago, was now visibly dissolving. It was converting into Spiritual Spring at an approximate ratio of 1:100.
While Jing Shu was thrilled by the explosive growth of the Spiritual Spring, her heart also ached; the Blood Crystal she had worked so hard to acquire was being devoured and transformed into Spiritual Spring. However, this also indicated that the Spiritual Spring’s volume could be increased not just by its own production but also by using other substances, like this crystal, as a substitute. The cost was a bit high, but then again, who could deny how amazing the Spiritual Spring was?
Jing Shu soon noticed that the newly produced Spiritual Spring seemed incompatible with the existing Spiritual Spring and was instead segregated into another corner. Even its color was a shade deeper.
Does this mean the quality is better, or perhaps slightly inferior? Or does it have other uses?
Jing Shu pondered.
This frenetic production lasted only a few minutes, and then a fist-sized quantity of new Spiritual Spring quietly floated into a corner of the Spiritual Spring Pool.
All the Blood Crystals were completely consumed. The red liquid, however, still lay undisturbed in the space. At that moment, Jing Shu finally began to regain consciousness, her head still feeling somewhat ethereal.
"OUCH, OUCH, OUCH..." Hao Yunlai also awoke, roused by the pain.

chapters.title: Chapter 468: Testing the New Spiritual Spring
chapters.content:
Chapter 468: Testing the New Spiritual Spring
The lingering smoke arose because Hao San’er, staring dumbfounded, had left his hand on the stove until the scorching became a drilling pain.
