I didn’t add anything else. I knew it would be researched for the competition, so I didn’t add a single drop of Spiritual Spring water. If it were to be mass-produced later, I wouldn’t be able to provide the Spiritual Spring; it’s too precious,
she thought.
Minister Zhao was puzzled. "Ordinary Bodhi doesn’t have such a high inhibition rate."
Group Leader Liu grew even more excited. "The vitality molecules in the Bodhi juice of this spray are ten times that of ordinary Bodhi! This means that for some reason—be it the cultivation environment or something else—its vitality is far higher than that of normal Bodhi!"
Ah,
it dawned on Jing Shu.
When I planted Bodhi and other herbs at the Wu City Pharmaceutical Association, I secretly added a tiny bit of Spiritual Spring. And the Bodhi in my space, needless to say, has always been watered with Spiritual Spring.
No sooner had Group Leader Liu finished speaking than the eager eyes of Minister Zhao and everyone else turned to Jing Shu.
Minister Zhao spoke kindly, "Young lady, may I ask how much more of this kind of Bodhi you have? And where did it come from?"
Smiling, Jing Shu extended her hand. "Let’s formally introduce ourselves. I am Jing Shu, the Vice Chair of the Wu City Pharmaceutical Association, and I’m also the leader of the team representing the Wu City Pharmaceutical Association in the Imperial Capital competition. The large batch of Bodhi I mentioned earlier was cultivated by me, and I’ve brought it all with me. Whether or not the Bodhi is good, you can all be the judges."
"This Bodhi is amazing! We need it so much!"
"Oh my goodness! This... this is truly... such great news! A fantastic development indeed!"
"She’s from the Medicine Association? Look at that, she’s one of us!"
"An entire batch of Bodhi like this? We’re saved! We’re saved!"

chapters.title: Chapter 580: Sorry, Bodhi no longer offers this service.
chapters.content:
Chapter 580: Sorry, Bodhi no longer offers this service.
The entire tin house burst into excited cheers. Minister Zhao, thrilled, shook hands with Jing Shu and repeatedly exclaimed, "Excellent, excellent, excellent!"
Group Leader Liu, too, was excited, saying, "Goodness, it’s truly a case of ’peaks and rivers may hide the path, but shady willows and bright flowers reveal a village beyond!’ These days have driven us crazy. Minister Zhao even made a military vow."
Minister Zhao sighed and nodded. "There’s no time to delay. We need to stop by Boss Zhang’s place first, then head straight to the competition venue; otherwise, Boss Zhang is going to lose it."
Jing Shu raised an eyebrow. "Boss Zhang?"
Who’s that?
Minister Zhao coughed. "An older brother of mine. It’s just a habit calling him that."
Group Leader Liu laughed heartily, mysteriously pointing upwards. "You could see him as the Chief Referee of this competition. Although his jurisdiction isn’t in this field, his title is higher. His only grandson was infected after consuming a red earthworm early in his life, and that’s why he took on this task. Otherwise, who would handle this mess?"
Jing Shu suddenly understood.
Was this the grandson of the person mentioned earlier whose life was being sustained by Bodhi?
She also couldn’t help but be curious about what effect her Bodhi would have on a real parasite infection.
"Miss Jing, Miss Jing, your phone! Yes, yes, Miss Jing is fine, nothing happened!"
In the midst of the noise, a somewhat recovered Song Bin called out with a peculiar expression and handed her his phone, adding, "It’s Jun Bao... That person couldn’t find you anywhere, so he called me."
Jing Shu nodded and took the phone. These past few days, as part of her plans, she had cut off all communications routed through the Medicine Association. "Hello? This is Jing Shu. What’s up?"
Over the phone, Jun Bao’s voice came through. "Jin Tianci wanted me to ask if you’ve been mistreated or if something has happened. If so, it’s alright if you don’t participate in the Imperial Capital competition. Don’t worry about resources; I’ll manage to get Wu City’s resources. If anything has happened, have Song Bin approach the Biological Research Center. They’ll figure out a solution."
Jing Shu: "???"
What are you talking about?
"What? No... What happened? We are all fine here, don’t worry," Jing Shu said, bewildered.
Although they had faced some minor unfairness earlier, it hadn’t been severe enough to warrant skipping the competition. Could there have been a misunderstanding?
From the other end, Jun Bao responded in surprise, "Don’t you know? Two hours ago, the Imperial Capital Pharmaceutical Association announced the disqualification of Wu City Pharmaceutical Association. They even posted it in a major data announcement. After that, Old Zhou and Jin Tianci couldn’t reach any of the contestants. I thought maybe something had happened to you."
Hearing this, Jing Shu was instantly filled with warmth and an indescribable feeling.
Being disqualified was unexpected, but Wu City’s response was also beyond her expectations. The burden of Wu City’s resources for next year rested on her shoulders, and she absolutely could not betray their trust.
"Oh, I see. I’ll make my own decision on this matter... That’s it, then."
Over the phone came a quick reply, "If you need any help, just say so," and the call ended.
Just after hanging up, Minister Zhao approached with a smile but encountered Jing Shu’s chilly expression. He asked in puzzlement, "What’s the matter?"
Jing Shu retrieved her homemade spray from Group Leader Liu and said lightly, "Minister Zhao, I’m sorry, but this batch of Bodhi might have to be returned tonight in the same way it came. I regret I can’t provide them to you."
Minister Zhao’s face showed shock. "Xiao Jing, what’s the matter? Everything was fine, right? We agreed that this batch of Bodhi would be used as the competition entry, didn’t we? It’s all recorded and can’t just be changed! Moreover, this concerns the entirety of Huaxia; everyone is awaiting this medicine for salvation! Or did you encounter some difficulty? We can discuss it!"
Jing Shu scoffed. "What’s there to discuss now? It’s absurd how we from Wu City Pharmaceutical Association, despite all hardships, came to the Imperial Capital only to be given such a hard time. Other associations were welcomed upon arrival, but we waited in the snow and mud for a whole day with no one attending to us.
"Later, we found a place ourselves to wait. Then, Team Leader Zhang, who was supposed to pick us up, said the venue was full and told us to wait where we were, promising to pick us up for the competition...
"We didn’t complain, intending to contribute Wu City’s best specialty medicinal herbs to address the crisis. Until a minute ago, I was still planning to donate all the Bodhi... But to our utter astonishment, while we were waiting to compete, Wu City was disqualified!"
Then someone immediately started looking into it. An exclamation of disbelief rippled through the room, "Are you kidding me?! The only people with a life-saving medicine were disqualified from participation?!"
"It’s true! It’s in the notice! Wu City Pharmaceutical Association is red-flagged! The reason given is that the competition had started, and they hadn’t arrived at the venue!"
Upon hearing this, Minister Zhao immediately became enraged.
How could they treat people like this? Disqualify them just because they hadn’t arrived yet? Weren’t they right here conducting research?! Which damn fool authorized this disqualification?!
"That’s outrageous!" Group Leader Liu slapped his thigh in fury. "They are our only lifeline!"
Jing Shu shook her head regretfully. "Just now, Wu City called. They said since we’ve been disqualified, then so be it. They’ll find another way to secure resources next year. Taking the Bodhi back might be good too; at least it can protect the entirety of Wu City."
As she said this, Jing Shu signaled for Song Bin to head back with her.
Group Leader Liu’s legs went weak, and he nearly collapsed. Just as they saw a glimmer of hope, it was abruptly shattered.
Minister Zhao slapped the tin wall of the building. "Xiao Jing, wait a moment! I’ll call Boss Zhang right away to sort this out. Don’t worry, I will give you an explanation!"
Without waiting for Jing Shu’s response, he immediately made the call. He started yelling the moment it connected, holding nothing back, regardless of whether he was talking to his old leader or his old brother. "If you want to save your grandson, then fix this, and fix it now! Our savior is here, and you bloody well disqualified them! What kind of screw-up is this?!" he ranted, going on and on.
Minister Zhao then contacted the Pharmaceutical Association. "Has the competition started? What? You dared to disqualify people based merely on pre-competition reports and rehearsals? I’m telling you, you’ve got a huge problem on your hands! What competition? Halt everything and solve this issue first! And you tell that Old Witch, if this isn’t resolved, we’ll all be finished!"
Jing Shu’s lips briefly curved into a smile, then she quickly composed her expression, waiting for Minister Zhao to finish his calls. Only then did she say politely, "Minister Zhao, what’s been done is utterly disheartening. However, I trust you will provide Wu City with an explanation. I’ll go back and wait for your explanation now. Oh, and this is where we are currently staying."
Seeing there was still room for negotiation, Group Leader Liu wiped his sweat and excitedly replied on Minister Zhao’s behalf, "Ah, yes, of course, of course."
Jing Shu left, accompanied by an adoring Song Bin. They returned to their current residence, greeted by the Pharmacists from Wu City Medicine Association, who had been bottling up their frustrations for days. She commanded Danai, "Danai, have everyone pack their things. We’re going to participate in the competition this afternoon."
"Aye, will do, Jing Shu! You have no idea how frustrated we’ve been, just itching to go out there and show our skills! Don’t worry, I’ve already told everyone. The Imperial Capital is a place with deep waters, so we’ve all been keeping a low profile and not causing trouble. When others provoke us, we endure it."

chapters.title: Chapter 581: Let’s Go Participate in the Competition
chapters.content:
Chapter 581: Let’s Go Participate in the Competition
Song Bin wiped his sweat.
Not stir up trouble? After today, you all might be leaving horizontally.
「That very day」 was originally slated for the Imperial City Pharmaceutical Association’s live-streamed competition. However, rumors were flying, and everyone online who was keenly following the competition was also bewildered. "Come on, start already! This is about next year’s resource distribution! Otherwise, why would everyone go to such lengths to send their precious medicinal materials here?"
Indeed, a competition that had already started was abruptly halted. Rumor had it that one Medicine Association had caused the stoppage, leaving the others to only stand by, idly checking the barrage of messages on the big data screens.
Many dissatisfied individuals paced around the hall, while the well-informed relayed updates non-stop. Word had it that the Chief Referee had personally intervened, and even the Epidemic Prevention Department had gotten involved.
Of course, news from these bigwigs wasn’t enough to shock the participating Medicine Associations. After all, not all of them were from Imperial Capital, so they neither fully understood nor particularly cared about the extent of these individuals’ influence.
What actually brought a sudden silence to the venue was a flashing message on the big screen. It announced that the Fuhai Pharmaceutical Association had been disqualified from the competition for ignoring the rules. Furthermore, the Fuhai Association President had been directly removed from his post by the Emperor City General Pharmaceutical Association! The Fuhai Pharmaceutical Association was also publicly named and criticized.
This was immediately followed by another announcement: "The cancellation of the Wu City Pharmaceutical Association’s participation was due to an operational error by Team Leader Zhang and his group from the Imperial City Pharmaceutical Association. Team Leader Zhang and his group have now been dismissed. We apologize for the inconvenience caused to the members of the Wu City Pharmaceutical Association and the general public! We will learn from this lesson and improve our logistical support in the future..."
As soon as the news broke, those attentively following Wu City’s situation immediately reported it, causing another huge stir there.
「Imperial City Pharmaceutical Association Competition Venue.」
"Wu City Pharmaceutical Association got disqualified? I didn’t even notice."
"Now everyone knows! Holy shit, this is like an indirect apology, isn’t it? That’s so badass!"
"You’re telling me there’s no inside story? I don’t believe a mere operational mistake could lead to disqualification."
"That’s what you all don’t know. A while ago, Fuhai came to us seeking an alliance. They wanted to take first place and offered many benefits, but our president didn’t agree. Did they think we were fools? First place this time wins New Energy!"
"So what? What does that have to do with this?"
"Fuhai bribed the investigation team. They knew Wu City had reported a batch of Bodhi and were probably planning to seize Wu City’s Bodhi to win the pharmaceutical rights this time... But speaking of risks, Bodhi can’t completely suppress these parasites."
"Hmph, I guess Fuhai really messed up this time. They didn’t manage to take anyone down but got themselves kicked out instead."
"Sigh, none of that’s important now. What you need to know is that the Wu City Pharmaceutical Association might have indeed had their participation canceled, but now they’re back, apparently ignoring their disqualification. This competition, tsk tsk, is going to be quite a show."
"That just shows Wu City really has something valuable, something useful. Otherwise, who would bother with them?"
「While both sides were in a flurry of activity, things were much calmer on Jing Shu’s end.」 First, she compensated poor Song Bin. Then, she arranged the renewal of various agreements with the tank merchant regarding the Great Goose. After they all had a lively meal, a LOUD RUMBLING sound of vehicles approaching came from outside.
From afar, Danai’s excited voice could be heard, which then turned to surprise and panic. "Jing Shu, there are so many vehicles outside! So many... This doesn’t seem normal."
Song Bin, now full and much calmer, glanced at Danai.
Your president has caused such a commotion; it’s definitely alerted many influential people. In all his years in Imperial Capital, he’d never seen these genuine academics act so deferential. True researchers are usually quite arrogant, but today, their attitude towards Jing Shu was exceptionally polite.
Song Bin looked at Jing Shu again and shook his head.
It was just about examining a corpse, wasn’t it? How on earth did this person manage to win over the biggest BOSS?
The Pharmacists from the Wu City Pharmaceutical Association watched eagerly, whispering among themselves, "Could they be here to pick us up?"
"You’re overthinking it! This convoy is too grand for that!"
Just then, a man stumbled out of one of the vehicles. It was none other than Team Leader Zhang, the very person who had deliberately ignored the Wu City Pharmaceutical Association’s calls.
Spotting Jing Shu, who was calmly watching the spectacle, he rushed forward intending to embrace her but missed, grabbing at empty air. Unfazed, he began to cry and laugh simultaneously. "President Jing, you must have been waiting a long time! We’re here to escort you! I’m so, so sorry, this is all my fault! I’m not asking for anything else now, just please, come with us to the competition!"
If they go to the competition, I’ll only be dismissed. If they don’t...
Team Leader Zhang shivered.
The Pharmacists widened their eyes.
What... what on earth is happening?
But even more shocking developments were to follow. Several more people disembarked, led by an individual being supported by Minister Zhao. They approached quickly. Minister Zhao, though his expression was stern, spoke in a surprisingly polite tone, "We’ve investigated thoroughly. The Imperial City Pharmaceutical Association made an error; your association did not violate any regulations. Therefore, the Wu City Pharmaceutical Association’s eligibility to compete will not be revoked. The individuals responsible for the mistake have been dealt with, and this matter has been announced publicly online. This is Brother Zhang... the Chief Referee of the competition."
The elderly man being supported, though his legs were unsteady, was in high spirits. He nodded with a cheerful smile. "Everyone responsible has been dealt with. If you have any other concerns or suggestions, please feel free to bring them up for discussion!"
Upon hearing this, Team Leader Zhang trembled violently.
Who the hell could have imagined that an obscure, small place like Wu City possessed such immense influence? All these top figures were personally coming to extend an invitation! Did that Undead Chairman Wang still want to play dirty and double-cross them? Hah! Truly overestimating her own capabilities!
The Wu City Pharmacists were dumbfounded, finally realizing something was very wrong.
It’s just a competition, so why have all these important figures shown up? And more importantly, do they seem to be here to apologize?
After enthusiastically greeting everyone and exchanging some pleasantries, Jing Shu suddenly asked, "Team Leader Zhang, what about Chairman Wang? The one who said she’d teach me what rules truly are? Didn’t she come along? Today, I wanted to share this principle with her: it’s not about who shouts the loudest or who has the grandest title. It’s about who possesses more value—that person *is* the rule."
Team Leader Zhang gave a wry smile.
Just the other day, they were the ones high and mighty, the self-proclaimed Rule Makers who had cast aside the Wu City Pharmaceutical Association, capable of revoking Wu City’s participation with a simple scheme. And today? He’d heard Wu City had discovered the antidote, which explained this treatment. Their loss wasn’t unfair.
What were rules, anyway? This woman before him had shown him! So, the bold words she’d spoken that day weren’t just empty boasts; she truly possessed the power to back them up.
"Her? I’m afraid she won’t be able to make it. She’s already been escorted back to Fuhai. The Fuhai Pharmaceutical Association’s eligibility was revoked due to irregular operations."
Jing Shu raised an eyebrow, slightly surprised.
Quite ruthless. But she liked it.
Team Leader Zhang then asked tentatively, "So, shall we depart? To the competition?"
"Alright, let’s go then," Jing Shu agreed, clapping her hands. "Take good care of our medicinal ingredients!"
"Absolutely, absolutely!"
「Later, at the competition venue...」
"They’re here, they’re here!"
"Who’s here?"
"The Chief Referee is here! Minister Zhao is here too!"
"And the Wu City Pharmaceutical Association is with them! Heavens, why are they together? So the competition halt really *was* for them!"

chapters.title: Chapter 582: We Are All Looking for the Wu City Pharmaceutical Association!
chapters.content:
Chapter 582: We Are All Looking for the Wu City Pharmaceutical Association!
The noisy competition venue suddenly quieted down. As one influential figure after another walked in, the scene began to buzz again. Those in the know started introducing their companions to others. These included tycoons from the Imperial Capital and the person in charge of this event.
Some speculated that the young woman, unfamiliar to many, walking beside the Chief Referee must be the president of the Wu City Medicine Association.
As the influential figures took their seats, the members of the Wu City Medicine Association were also guided to the foremost area. To their surprise, this was where the disqualified Fuhai Medicine Association had been seated!
Feeling the intense, envious, and jealous stares from both sides, the pharmacists of the Wu City Medicine Association were also very confused. Everything that happened today seemed too surreal.
The venue for the competition was quite simple, just the previous grounds of the Imperial City Pharmaceutical Association, slightly modified. However, the key was that the venue now housed many valuable medicinal materials, shockingly displayed behind each Medicine Association.
A glance revealed medicinal materials, nearly extinct since the apocalypse. It was clear that those who brought more materials possessed slightly more confidence.
Spotlights suddenly turned on, and various machines whirred to life.
"Silence! Cough, cough! Hello? Hello?" A voice came through the microphone, and a man wearing glasses and holding a microphone walked out from the glare of the lights. He continued as if nothing had happened, "Take your places... Now, I declare that the competition officially starts!" It was as if the several-hours-long prelude to the competition had never occurred, with no explanations whatsoever.
Of course, the presidents of the Medicine Associations and the rest of the staff onsite also dared not speak. They were mindful of the precedent set by the Fuhai Medicine Association.
"Firstly, I am the presenter for this competition, also known as the host. You can call me Xiao Ai. In the upcoming time, I will convey the thoughts of the large online audience watching this competition and clarify any doubts for the audience here. Audience members can vote for the Medicine Association you favor. However, no matter how many votes you cast... Heh, it doesn’t count. This competition will be decided by one Chief Referee and five other judges."
The host moved briskly across the competition grounds, clapping his hands and saying, "Everyone should be clear on the rules by now. Alright, let’s bring on the props!"
The pharmacists from the Wu City Medicine Association, who had just settled into their positions, blinked and quietly asked, "What rules?"
Jing Shu raised her eyebrows.
She had been so busy these past few days gathering information about various things that she had completely forgotten to learn the rules. However, she seemed to recall hearing they were supposed to be very simple. Just one word: act.
That was when the props rolled in.
Startlingly, the props were patients carried in on stretchers! There were exactly thirty patients, corresponding to the thirty Medicine Associations, and they arrived quickly. Soon, an old man was placed before Jing Shu, lying on a stretcher, groaning and clutching his stomach. Numerous tubes were inserted into him, their ends leading to sealed bags filled with parasites extracted from his body.
Indeed, the patients on the other stretchers were in similar states, all wailing. Without intervention, they would likely be exsanguinated by the parasites in about ten days.
These intense pains were characteristic of patients whose internal organs were being consumed by parasites.
Things hadn’t been this dramatic during the rehearsals. They hadn’t brought out actual parasite-infected patients then. Oh God, and this was being live-streamed to a massive audience... Though the competition hadn’t been publicized, those tuning in were mostly influential figures from various places.
The thought of medicinal materials potentially agitating the parasites into a frenzy during treatment was unsettling. The faces of the onsite pharmacists darkened. This was not the rule they had been briefed on. During the simulations, they had only been told to present their researched medicinal materials for testing.
"As you all know, this competition aims to select a Medicine Association capable of providing a large quantity of Bodhi materials, or an alternative to them. The selected association will be granted a monopoly on the production of these scarce drugs, with all resources concentrated for this purpose.
Now, please use the medications you’ve prepared over these past few days on the patients. Anesthetics were already largely ineffective for these patients. This round of the competition mainly evaluates the substitutes in terms of pain relief and suppression rates.
Oh, and using Bodhi materials is prohibited in this round."
Jing Shu touched her chin, instantly understanding the significance of the competition.
So, the first round was about finding an alternative to Bodhi? From her memories of a past life, it seemed that other than Bodhi, no other antiparasitic or insecticidal drugs were effective against these parasites.
Danai stood slightly trembling next to Jing Shu. She felt a bit dizzy.
The judges on the platform had just cast welcoming looks in her direction, and most unbelievably, they had smiled at her. Were today’s tycoons always this approachable? She turned to look at Jing Shu, shaking her head. Jing Shu was the real tycoon here, right?
"Ah? Why is it like this? They won’t allow Bodhi in the first round, so what should we use? Many in our Medicine Association who listened to you planted Bodhi. They all wanted to showcase their skills this time."
"President, following your instructions, we experimented with several other medicines these past few days. However, theoretically, they were useless, and in practice, even more so..."
"If that’s the case, we can only try to boost their immunity and hope they can hold on for a few more days on their own."
"What’s the use if it doesn’t provide a complete cure? They’ll still be suffering."
Jing Shu shook her head, then raised her hand and said, "This round, Wu City forfeits!"
The scene burst into an uproar.
"What do you mean, ’forfeits’?"
"Wu City is forfeiting this round? What are they thinking?"
"I heard Wu City has a large stockpile of Bodhi, so they aren’t concerned about this round’s focus on alternatives. They’re a strong competitor."
"So what? No matter how much Bodhi they have, it won’t be enough. Besides, Bodhi can only suppress the parasites, not eradicate them. The urgent task now is to find an alternative to Bodhi and replace it."
The old man lying on the ground screamed, "Ah? What about me? It hurts so much! Who can stop this pain? I’d rather die!"
Mocking laughter erupted nearby. "Old Zhou is really miserable! Haha! He came all this way for a trial medication, and they just gave up on him! Ouch, that hurts! Can’t you be gentler?!"
The host, Xiao Ai, nodded, not at all surprised. The large screen scoreboard then showed Wu City’s score for the first round as zero points.
The judges seated on the platform conferred in hushed tones, but they were too far away for anyone to hear what was being said.
The small disturbance quickly subsided. The other Medicine Associations began to work with the professionals, focusing on their tasks and paying no further attention to Wu City.
Meanwhile, Jing Shu quietly gave a few instructions to her team, then sat to one side, ready to watch the show.
Wang Danai nodded excitedly in agreement. Then, she pulled a small black Wanzi from her pocket and fed it to the elderly patient assigned to Wu City.
While the Medicine Associations were busy working up a sweat, an excited voice suddenly announced, "I’m cured! I don’t feel any pain at all! I’m completely healed! Who was mocking me just now?"
"Who’s cured? Is it that old fellow, Old Zhou? He’s cured?"
"Nonsense! Didn’t Old Zhou’s team forfeit the competition?"
The old man, previously on the ground, sprang to his feet, full of vigor. He walked over to the person who had just mocked him and nudged him gently. "Old Yu, after all the years we’ve known each other, you still mocked me! See? I’m cured! Even though they forfeited the competition, they have the antidote! Well? Do you want me to ask them for you?"
"Old Zhou, if you’re cured, of course, I want their help too! I don’t want to be treated here anymore! Damn it, they’ve been tormenting me for ages!"
"I also want treatment from Old Zhou’s Medicine Association!"

chapters.title: Chapter 583: The Second Round of the Competition
chapters.content:
Chapter 583: The Second Round of the Competition
"Let’s go, let’s go, everyone go to that side for treatment; we can’t do it here." Old Zhou was a very enthusiastic old man, pulling people along as he ran.
"Hey, wait a minute! We’re in the middle of a competition here. If the patients run off, how can we proceed with our drug trials!" Seeing his competition "props" about to run off to another place, how could he not panic?
Of course, the chaos didn’t stop there. Even those far away who heard the news couldn’t help but clamor to go to the Wu City Medicine Association for treatment. These were people who had endured pain for several days and couldn’t bear even one more second of it.
Before long, Old Zhou had brought over quite a few patients who could walk; those who couldn’t were protesting on their stretchers. Crucially, many Pharmacists trailed behind them, desperately trying to reason with them. A proper competition turned into a farce, and soon the Wu City Medicine Association was surrounded and impenetrable.
There were those demanding antidotes, those cursing the Medicine Association, and even a scene of the host crawling on the ground searching for his glasses after they were knocked off. In short, it was a complete mess, an unexpected turn no one had envisioned.
Jing Shu had a headache, and Wang Danai was completely at a loss. The referees not only didn’t intervene but also watched with great interest.
"Alright, alright! Everybody quiet down for a moment," Jing Shu had to shout. "Let’s do it like this, dear patients, why don’t we give others a chance first? Just twenty minutes. If the other Medicine Associations can’t cure you, we in Wu City will treat everyone free of charge!" She saw the eyes of the other Medicine Associations practically ready to devour the Wu City Medicine Association.
It’s still early in the contest, and the animosity has already peaked.
And it’s not just happening at the competition; it’s also being live-streamed! Although not many people are watching, influential figures from various places are surely paying attention. Just thinking about it makes my scalp tingle. They probably think: Everyone came here to compete, minding their own business. Wu City forfeited, fine. But then their patients suddenly stop treatment and rush to your side for an antidote? What’s that supposed to mean? Are you looking down on us? Think you’re so great, huh?
This was when Old Zhou jumped in, "Exactly! Don’t make it difficult for them. Go get treated first, and if it doesn’t work, then come back here."
"Really? Weren’t you the one who called us over just now, Old Zhou?"
"But I don’t want to delay for even a minute! Old Zhou, you know how painful that bite is, right?"
"Everyone, please, do me a favor, okay!" Old Zhou said this time with vigorous enthusiasm.
"Alright, alright. Then you all hurry up. Quick! If it doesn’t work, I’m coming over here."
And so, the farce finally came to a close. Jing Shu sighed in relief, and the other Medicine Associations did the same, hastening their drug trials.
Hadn’t they heard it was only twenty minutes? Was there some mistake? Who was the real referee here, anyway?
But many still believed the substitutes here were effective. After all, a lot of theoretical work had already been done. With powerful computer data calculations, they could predict the rate of inhibition these drugs might achieve—this was now merely the final testing phase.
Host Xiao Ai eventually found his glasses. Under the light, they refracted a curious beam.
He knew that although Wu City had withdrawn from the competition, they had already scored a significant victory in the first round.
"Old man, is it still very painful? It shouldn’t be!"
As time ticked by, second by second, the appointed time was nearly upon them. However, these Bodhi substitutes still had no effect, not even reducing the pain by a fraction.
"We told you it wouldn’t work! Can we switch places now?"
"This is really unbearable!"
At this point, without needing anyone else’s consent, these patients, driven by a strong will to live, made their way to the Wu City Medicine Association, crawling if they had to, all begging for medicine. The scene descended into chaos once again.
Xiao Ai subtly glanced at the referees, who nodded and did not intervene. So, with all the "props" gone, he proceeded to explain the various medications prepared by the Medicine Associations to the online audience.
Old Zhou carefully placed each tiny black pill into the mouths of the patients. In just five minutes, the people who had been in severe pain, tormented by parasites, all calmed down.
"I’m better! I’m really better!"
"This medicine is miraculous! It’s an antidote, an antidote!"
...
"Now, I declare the first round of the competition over! The judges have already posted the scores for all Medicine Associations on the screen. Please look!"
The screen, filled with red Zeros, was shocking. No surprises there; all Medicine Associations scored zero. Alternative medicines were indeed not that easy to find. Although some Medicine Associations were dissatisfied, there was nothing they could do; the scores were given by the judges.
The patients who had just been carried in were now mostly lively and walking out on their own. It was a good start.
"Then, the second round of the competition begins now! This round is also simple. A Medicine Association is judged on the total quality and quantity of its medicinal materials. Simply having one outstanding material is not enough. To possess the right to emergency pharmacology, one must have corresponding strength!
This round will compare the total number and quality of medicinal materials from each Medicine Association!
Now, I will announce the names of the medicinal materials submitted by each Medicine Association, and the judges will personally assess their quality."
"This is good. We should aim to score more points this time. We might not be sure about other things, but when it comes to medicinal materials, we’ve brought our entire stock."
"We got the news early and even borrowed some from other places. If it’s about quantity, you definitely can’t compete with us."
Hearing these whispers, Wang Danai snorted and said to Jing Shu, "What do they count for? Even if they have more, what use is it? Our Wu City’s materials are top grade."
Jing Shu smiled without saying a word.
While Wu City might not have the advantage in quantity, she was very confident about the quality.
A few referees were each responsible for some Medicine Associations. Only Boss Zhang, the Chief Referee from a different field, still sat on the platform—he wasn’t familiar with medicinal materials, after all. However, he kept glancing at Jing Shu, his gaze growing more and more intense, and he continually urged Minister Zhao and the others, "Hurry up! Get it done quickly and announce the results!"
The Wu City Medicine Association was, as luck would have it, assigned to Minister Zhao. He walked over laughing, and the first thing he examined was Wu City’s Bodhi. Upon seeing the abundant, lush green, and dewy-fresh Bodhi, Minister Zhao exclaimed, his eyes filled with pleasant surprise, "Fantastic! Top grade, all of it is top grade! Record it, record it all!"
"All top grade?" the recorder asked hesitantly.
"All of it!"
At this time, Old Man Zhang, the Chief Referee, was also helped over, excitedly asking Minister Zhao, "These are the ones? My, they look delightful."
"Is there a mistake? Is there a full top-grade batch over there?"
"Let’s go and see."

chapters.title: Chapter 584: The Third Round of the Competition
chapters.content:
Chapter 584: The Third Round of the Competition
No one present understood the meaning of "top grade" better than they did: it signified a level that only the most precious, highest-quality herbs of the apocalypse could achieve. Due to geographical locations, various high-quality herbs would grow, but only a small fraction would reach top grade.
Top grade was extremely rare, its worth in the apocalypse determined by value, quantity, and quality.
Pandas were unique to Huaxia—rare, and therefore national treasures.
But if these herbs were as common as cabbages, how could they be treasures? Yet, the referee declared them all top grade. What was he implying? Was he trying to pull some strings? This was blatant favoritism.
"All the herbs are top grade?"
"It’s Bodhi. You all know how precious Bodhi is now."
"Even if it’s Bodhi, it can’t all be judged as top grade, can it?"
A group of Pharmacists from other Medicine Associations gathered to watch, creating quite a scene. They were full of disbelief, ready to challenge the claim, and eager to see these supposed top-grade herbs.
Minister Zhao didn’t stop them. Instead, he sighed and brought out the Bodhi for everyone to see. "By these standards, let alone under the harsh conditions of the apocalypse, even before the apocalypse, this would have been considered top grade. Smell this. Look at this. You all understand herbs, so you should be able to tell."
The herbs were passed around, followed by exclamations of surprise. In the challenging environment of the apocalypse, farming food was already difficult, let alone cultivating herbs that required higher standards and years to grow.
However, Bodhi was not considered an herb before the apocalypse; it was more of a tree species that could reach medicinal standards in as little as four months. But the Bodhi cultivated during the apocalypse had much-reduced vitality and, naturally, greatly diminished medicinal properties, barely reaching the medicinal threshold.
Thus, seeing truly high-quality, potent Bodhi astounded the knowledgeable Pharmacists. Initially, they had assumed that Wu City merely possessed a large batch of Bodhi, nothing more. But now, it was clear it wasn’t that simple; this batch of Bodhi was of excellent quality!
The onlookers fell silent. Minister Zhao smiled without saying a word; there were even more surprises in store, things these people probably didn’t know. This quality of Bodhi could perfectly suppress parasites, completely rendering obsolete their months of frantic searching for antidotes and substitutes.
Minister Zhao even thought to himself,
If it weren’t necessary to follow procedures, I’d declare this batch of Bodhi the champion right now!
He didn’t want to delay another minute; the sooner it was done, the more people could be saved. That would be far better!
Although the raw Bodhi was available and could perfectly suppress parasites, the subsequent steps were very cumbersome. The actual process of producing medicine using the techniques currently available in the apocalypse was quite problematic.
Jing Shu’s method of directly crushing Bodhi into a liquid, for example, was frankly wasteful. After all, even with such a large batch of Bodhi, it was necessary to produce at least several million doses of medicine. In principle, every Bodhi leaf could undergo repeated refinement to extract more medicinal properties.
Little did they know, Chief Referee Boss Zhang shared Minister Zhao’s urgency. He had almost spoken up several times but stopped himself, maintaining a smile while nodding and agreeing with whatever Minister Zhao said. Inwardly, however, he was fuming,
Damn it all, get a move on!
Of course, Wu City had more than just Bodhi; they also had dozens of Pharmacists cultivating various other herbs. Minister Zhao spoke quickly, instructing the record keeper, "Mid-grade!" "Suitable for medicine!" "Qualified!" and so on, his tone finally returning to normal.
Observant people could see Minister Zhao’s perfunctory and lenient assessments; he often announced grades without even looking closely. Nearby, Jing Shu knew Minister Zhao was indeed inflating the quality of some herbs.
Is he trying to curry favor?
she wondered.
Many people noticed, but what was the use? It didn’t affect the results anymore. On the screen, the top-grade medicinal herbs from the Wu City Pharmaceutical Association had already filled most of the display. There was no need to look at anything else; the Wu City Pharmaceutical Association’s score was tens of times ahead of second place.
This rendered the competition a farce.
In past competitions, this second round was the most thrilling and competitive. The screen would constantly update with whose herbs were more plentiful and of higher quality, each change eliciting exclamations of surprise. Typically, there would be announcements about various precious herbs like ginseng and Lingzhi, all invariably top grade.
But this time? One or two top-grade items were hardly worth announcing anymore. Look at Wu City: Minister Zhao had declared all their herbs top-grade, directly securing first place in the second round for them.
This is so frustrating! Was it our lack of preparation? Did we not bring enough herbs?
This competition is so dull, so stifling.
That’s what most of the Medicine Associations thought.
Seeing that Minister Zhao’s side was almost finished, the other judges sped up their assessments, quickly categorizing the quality with a mere glance. Since not all their herbs were top-grade, they were losing anyway. Further judgment seemed pointless.
At that moment, Chief Referee Boss Zhang, supported by someone, excitedly stood up. "Now, I announce that the second round is over! The rankings are displayed on the big screen. Let’s proceed to the final round!" he declared as he began to walk. The other judges followed suit, and they all departed.
The crowd looked on, utterly confused. "What in the world...?"
Then, the host Xiao Ai said, "Hurry up and follow! We are moving on to the third round now. Oh right, I forgot to mention, the third round isn’t held here. Grab your equipment and come along! Lights and cameras, follow!"
"Ohhh!"
"What are we competing in for this third round? Why isn’t it here?"
"Maybe there’s a chance. I thought, with Wu City suddenly emerging and crushing us... but in the next round, if it’s not about herbs, maybe we can fight for a spot."
"Forget about first place, but second might be within reach. The rewards for second place aren’t bad either, just lacking that red mysterious energy. What a pity."
...
The journey wasn’t far, and everyone had to bring their equipment. Fortunately, transport vehicles were on standby nearby. A large contingent moved towards the Imperial City Pharmaceutical Association, only to discover an abandoned stadium there.
The air was foul, filled with a nauseating odor. Jing Shu knew this smell all too well—it was just like the one she had encountered that morning.
"This... This place is?"
"Yes. This is where the heavily parasite-infected patients in the Imperial Capital are housed. Without new drugs developed, these people are here to... wait to die."
Those who couldn’t survive, who died, were taken to the crematorium for incineration. Reality was that harsh.

chapters.title: Chapter 585: Er Qiu
chapters.content:
Chapter 585: Er Qiu
As they walked, many people were overwhelmed by the strong smell and vomited uncontrollably. The intense aroma, similar to that of a decaying corpse, especially affected those who had never encountered it before, causing them to throw up without warning.
Of course, for Jing Shu, who had endured the year-long disaster of super stinky eggs in her previous life, she was much calmer this time around. Among the crowd, she kept her composure and pulled out a protective mask from her trouser pocket to wear, while also distributing them to the Wu City Pharmaceutical Association members near her—handing out one to each person so that they wouldn’t be overwhelmed by the stench and faint during the competition.
Upon arriving, the situation was much more horrific than Jing Shu had imagined, with the sound of miserable cries audible from afar.
The abandoned stadium was massive. Countless makeshift beds were partitioned off in the center, packed with people lying on them, so many that one couldn’t see the end at a glance.
How many people must there be?
If the first batch, at least, could still manage to curse and scream loudly, the majority of those here could only lie on the ground groaning. Only a few with severe reactions were screaming loudly.
This place was filled with people infected by parasites!
Arriving here, if the members of the various Medicine Associations didn’t understand what the third round of the competition was about, they would have been living in vain, though they could mostly guess what it entailed.
But with current methods, they could only intervene. The effectiveness of medications was not very significant. Consequently, doctors were seen ceaselessly moving among the parasite-infected patients.
In just a short while, the incessant BEEPING echoed through the hall. Two waves of resuscitations were conducted, and the atmosphere was incredibly tense since at any moment, someone could die from organ failure or various other causes.
Having lived through the apocalypse for so many years, most disasters resulted in instant death. If victims weren’t found already deceased, it was rare to witness such anguished, tortured departures from life as these.
Jing Shu’s eyes narrowed into slits as she recalled her previous life when numerous disasters struck. She shivered, praying desperately for everything to pass quickly, praying to survive. Her parents were still alive; how could she dare die? She wanted to become strong, but the times were harsh. Apart from silently following the Huaxia Government, they had no other lifeline.
Back then, they were just like the people here today, living in pain and difficulty. But as long as they had the will to survive, they struggled to hang on. Unfulfilled wishes and family ties meant they dared not die. Those without the desire to live had passed away early, which could be considered an early reincarnation.
Taking a deep breath, Jing Shu felt for the first time that her decision was right. In this life, she had encountered and planted a large number of Bodhi trees early on.
However, the Chief Referee didn’t seem to have any intention of stopping and continued to walk forward.
Could everyone have guessed wrong?
"Isn’t it here?"
"We need to go to the back."
"The back?"
"This area is just a part of the parasite-infected patients; further back, there is a section dedicated to children."
A realization dawned on several people all at once.
The number of children infected by parasites was not small, and they were also segregated into a separate area. However, this section was much more eerie. The children lay quietly on the ground, as if... they were asleep. In any case, it was far quieter than the other section, with hardly any groaning or screaming.
If it weren’t for the doctors’ intermittent check-ups and the BEEPING of the ECG machine, everyone would have doubted whether these children were...
What’s going on here?
The Chief Referee finally stopped. "These are the future hopes of our Huaxia," he said. "Now, use whatever methods you have at your disposal and prioritize the children. Save as many as we can."
Then another referee said, "According to the procedure, we have to first enter into the drug trial, check the records, and so on. But now, resources are scarce, and we can’t afford to delay any further. Children are not like adults. Even if these children are hanging on by a thread each day with the aid of Bodhi and precious drugs like anesthesia and sleeping aids, they won’t last much longer. We can administer the medication directly."
Minister Zhao wiped the moisture from the corner of his eyes. "The third round of the competition is very simple," he said. "Over here, we have the new drug formulas that our team has developed, which will be made public for everyone’s reference."
"Next, there are no restrictions on any means, including the red New Energy that you obtained from other channels. Use whatever you have. This round of competition is about your methods and how high a suppression rate for parasites you can achieve."
Soon, the various pharmacy ratios were published, followed by detailed data. The current highest suppression rate was 86%. With the data from the epidemic prevention department and various precious medicinal materials and Bodhi gathered these days, the members of these Medicine Associations were quite confident.
The Chief Referee looked excitedly at Jing Shu, recalling Old Zhao’s claim of a 99% suppression rate.
Although he knew Old Zhao wouldn’t lie, the tension was still nerve-racking.
He then announced, "So, let the third round of the competition begin. Everyone, please do your best. The results will be based on the suppression rate."
"Grandpa! Grandpa! I’m over here!"
Just then, a clear but weak voice rang out. A pair of bright eyes stared this way, neither innocent nor naïve, but unexpectedly wise. The small head tilted as if seeing right through everything.
"Er Qiu, what nonsense are you spouting? How did you wake up?" The Chief Referee, flustered, strode over, anxiously looking at the doctor.
The little boy wiped his sweat and shook his head with effort. "Grandpa, I refused the anesthesia and sleep medicine," he said. "I’m afraid that after taking the medicine, I might never wake up again and never see this beautiful world."
Even Boss Zhang, a tough man who had been through wars, couldn’t help his tears.
His grandson was truly...
"That’s not true, Great-grandfather!" a skinny child suddenly piped up. "He said he wanted to save the medicine for other children, that he can bear the pain."
Boss Zhang nodded, knowing it was the truth. Then he suddenly glared at the skinny child. "How are you awake too?"
"It’s... it’s all my fault Er Qiu is like this. If only I hadn’t fed him red earthworms back then, he wouldn’t have gotten infected. If Er Qiu isn’t taking the medicine, I won’t either!"
"Good, good, you are both real men!" Boss Zhang bowed his head, taking the chance to discreetly wipe a tear from the corner of his eye.
It was at this moment that Jing Shu, accompanied by the pharmacists from Wu City, approached. Minister Zhao introduced them brightly, "Xiao Jing, let me introduce you. This young friend here is Boss Zhang’s grandson, his nickname is Er Qiu. And this is his good friend, Tie Dan."
Jing Shu smiled and squatted down. Er Qiu was still sweating from enduring the pain. It pained her to see such a sensible and well-behaved child, only ten years old, suffering so much. She couldn’t help but pat his head. "So you’re Er Qiu? I’m Jing Shu," she said gently. "I know a smart kid named Niu Yanben, just like you. Once you’re better, I’ll introduce you two. Oh, and you too, Tie Dan. You can all play together."
Er Qiu’s lips cracked into a smile, and he nodded gently. "If such a day comes, I would be very happy."
At that moment, Danai retrieved her secretly made Black Pills.

chapters.title: Chapter 586: Testing Medicine
chapters.content:
Chapter 586: Testing Medicine
Jing Shu shook her head. "Let me do it. The usual treatment you use is fine for those elders from today, but its therapeutic effect is lacking for these cases."
The Bodhi used by Danai and the others had been transplanted by Jing Shu. Later, without a single drop of Spiritual Spring water to nourish it, its effects certainly couldn’t match the top-grade Bodhi Jing Shu took from her space today, which boasted a 99% inhibition rate.
Danai scratched his head and laughed. "That’s true. Let’s not waste the medicine then. But later, we need to go treat those with mild parasite infections."
Jing Shu nodded. Minister Zhao was incredibly excited, and even the Chief Referee’s breathing grew labored.
The Wu City Medicine Association’s efficacy had been evident before, but only for mild cases. Even the drugs they developed themselves showed decent effects on mild conditions. However, for these severe, prolonged cases—especially the children whose lives depended on daily doses of Bodhi—their conditions were deteriorating day by day. Furthermore, because parasites could share genes and evolve, any emerging drug resistance would drastically reduce all therapeutic effects.
Now, it was time to see just how effective Wu City’s medicine truly was!
Jing Shu was then seen carefully taking a finger-thick glass vial from her pocket. She gently swirled the liquid inside. This concoction seemed much more potent than the spray she had produced that morning.
It was remarkably small, though, wasn’t it? Probably only a few tens of milliliters.
Jing Shu casually pulled out the cork. Instantly, a peculiar, fresh fragrance permeated the air. The bystanders felt significantly refreshed, and even the revolting stench that filled the area seemed to dissipate, as if purified. Er Qiu, who had been sweating profusely from pain, visibly relaxed.
"This looks promising!"
"This medicine seems very powerful."
Minister Zhao asked in surprise, "This... what’s in here?"
Jing Shu swirled the vial again; the liquid roiled, looking as if it might spill at any moment. Minister Zhao quickly extended his hands underneath, ready to catch any spill. This substance looked anything but ordinary.
Jing Shu handed the vial to Minister Zhao. "This is a concentrated essence—the original liquid of Bodhi. I performed extensive refinement to achieve this purity. Today’s spray was merely a byproduct of this process." It was fortunate Jing Shu had recently learned the purification and extraction methods from Jun Bao; otherwise, she truly couldn’t have completed this step. It was also fortunate she had kept this as a contingency.
Minister Zhao’s hand trembled, nearly spilling the precious liquid.
What extravagance! Such an astonishing concentration! How much Bodhi must have been used to produce this?
"Take one drop of the original liquid and dilute it with 250ml of saline for injection," Jing Shu instructed. "Er Qiu, what do you say? Do you dare to be the first to test this medicine? I must state clearly, this medicine is being presented without any prior trials."
Er Qiu’s eyes widened. After scanning his surroundings, he said, "Based on my observations, Miss, your medicine is the most reliable one here."
Jing Shu smiled, somewhat surprised. "And how did you observe that?"
Er Qiu sighed softly. "Because of the way my grandfather looks at you. And look at Uncle Zhao’s eager expression. If there wasn’t some confidence in it, why would he appear so anxious?"
Jing Shu laughed.
This child is truly observant. So young, yet he understands so much. Such a perceptive child is bound to be sensitive, and the more sensible children are, the more they tug at one’s heartstrings.
"Er Qiu, this medicine might cause some very strong reactions..."
"It’s okay, Miss. Let’s do it!"
"I want to try the medicine too!" Tie Dan piped up, unwilling to be outdone. Whatever Er Qiu did, he had to follow; he couldn’t show weakness.
Jing Shu nodded. Minister Zhao quickly made arrangements, and ultimately, Er Qiu and Tie Dan were chosen to test the medicine. IV drips were set up for them according to procedure.
DRIP. DRIP. DRIP...
The tense atmosphere silenced the entire hall once more; it was so quiet that the dripping from the IV bags was audible.
Large beads of sweat began to form on Er Qiu’s and Tie Dan’s faces, their expressions contorting fiercely. Tie Dan was the first to break; he couldn’t help but scream in agony and began to thrash on the ground.
"Quick! Hold him down!"
The nearby adults immediately restrained them, preventing any violent movements that might dislodge the IV needles.
Er Qiu, too, eventually cried out, his veins bulging and his lips turning purple.
"Get an oxygen mask! He’s hypoxic!"
The shrill beeping of the EKG monitor was particularly jarring. Jing Shu frowned, not having anticipated such a severe reaction.
"Should we continue? It doesn’t look good; the reaction is too strong."
Minister Zhao hesitated. After all, this wasn’t his grandson. He looked towards Boss Zhang, the Chief Referee.
"Continue! I... I can take it!" Er Qiu’s voice, though strained and hoarse, rang out. His eyes were bloodshot, looking as if they might burst from their sockets.
"Then let’s continue," Boss Zhang sighed.
Er Qiu and Tie Dan’s struggles intensified, and the sounds they made grew louder. Observers from other Medicine Associations, hearing the commotion from afar, even wondered if a fight had broken out.
Suddenly, as if on cue, dense swarms of parasites erupted from Er Qiu’s and Tie Dan’s eyes, noses, mouths, and ears—from every orifice.
To say they ’sprayed’ would be an understatement; it was more akin to them frantically fleeing their hosts’ bodies.
It’s important to understand that parasites typically never leave their host, as they cannot survive outside. The only exception is when mature parasites leave to reproduce. It seemed Bodhi contained an element that inhibited the parasites’ growth and maturation, though Jing Shu wasn’t entirely clear on the specifics.
For parasites to frantically abandon their host usually meant the host itself was beyond saving! Such a violent expulsion would undoubtedly destroy numerous internal organs; it was as brutal as having one’s insides churned indiscriminately.
This phenomenon instantly threw the scene into chaos. The people holding the boys down were so startled they cried out and recoiled instinctively.
Yet Jing Shu stepped forward boldly, utterly unfazed by the expelled parasites, showing no fear. With one hand on each, she easily subdued the two boys, who had previously required a group of adults to hold down.
Just as startled cries erupted, an even more astounding scene unfolded!
The tide of ejected parasites, as if ensnared by some terrifying force, was violently dragged back the moment they had all burst forth.
The ensuing sight was horrifying: the parasites desperately tried to flee but were inexorably dragged back. Ultimately, they were slowly devoured by an unseen force, their insect heads thrashing about as if wailing in futile despair.

chapters.title: Chapter 587: The Drug with Severe Side Effects
chapters.content:
Chapter 587: The Drug with Severe Side Effects
It was only a matter of seconds before the parasites were dragged back into Er Qiu and Tie Dan’s bodies. Their bodies began to cave in at certain spots, then swell out again as if something was moving inside!
Those who had regained their senses quickly pressed down on the two men again.
But everything had quieted down. When the last of the liquid from the IV dripped into their bodies, Er Qiu and Tie Dan were completely silent, taking deep breaths.
Everyone who had been terrified seemed to gradually calm down as well.
Just then, Er Qiu began to cough violently again, sending everyone’s hearts back into their throats.
"COUGH, COUGH, COUGH, COUGH!"
"RETCH!"
SPLASH! Almost at the same time, they both spewed a large amount of vomit, one bout after another. The dark brown liquid was filled with stringy objects coiled together like strands of hair.
At first glance, one might think they’d vomited up a pile of hair.
"It’s the parasites! Dried up, dead parasites!"
"Quick, Old Wang, get it tested."
After vomiting a large puddle, the two seemed much thinner, but their spirits improved remarkably. Only then did everyone truly relax.
"How do you feel? What’s your status?" asked Boss Zhang, trembling as he moved forward. His heart hadn’t settled yet; it felt like it might jump out of his chest.
The Zhang family only had this one precious child, and if something were to go wrong...
"Feels like I’ve been gutted," Er Qiu said jokingly, wiping the filth from the corners of his mouth.
"You rascal! At a time like this," Boss Zhang laughed as well, finally relieved.
Minister Zhao was ecstatic. The morning had already brought enough of a surprise with a 99% suppression rate, but he hadn’t expected this. Now, the lab results could reveal the full extent!
But they couldn’t afford to let their guard down, especially considering these children had been infected for so many days. Whether it was their internal organs or other parts, they must have sustained significant damage, and repairing that damage would be a major issue.
Regardless of whether they could be cured completely, they would inevitably suffer serious long-term effects.
The mess was quickly cleaned up. Samples that needed testing were taken away, and the children began receiving additional treatments and follow-up care. Only a group of tense individuals remained standing, cautiously waiting for the results.
Minister Zhao and the others were especially anxious. They watched the test results come in but dared not look at them. Sometimes, the greater the anticipation, the greater the fear—everyone dreaded the results might fall short.
In short, they were nervous and eager, yet fearful to know the outcome. It was a tense contradiction that Jing Shu found somewhat amusing to watch from the side.
Just as everyone was anxiously awaiting the results, the silence was suddenly shattered by commotion.
"It worked! Our medicine cured them! It can practically eradicate the parasites!"
This announcement startled many, who were eager to see what was happening. But before joy could take hold, strange howling noises arose.
Everyone rushed to see what was going on, and Jing Shu also went to observe the excitement.
「Scene change.」
What should have been a scene of anesthetized children quietly lying on the ground for drug testing was now chaotic. A child, whose gender was indiscernible, was wildly dashing about. He had torn off all the syringes from his body. His cheeks were severely hollowed, and long hair was growing on his hands, face, and other parts of his body. He was crouched low, pushing off with his back legs, moving on all fours in a bizarre manner.
Fortunately, the area was enclosed, and the frantic child was quickly captured. Several people struggled to hold the child down and ended up binding him to a bed. He still thrashed ceaselessly, baring his teeth and grimacing.
Minister Zhao strode forward, examined the child, and then asked, "What’s going on here? What medication was used? Where is the person in charge? Show me the prescription, and also check the child’s condition." Among everyone present, Minister Zhao was by far the most authoritative and influential. He had overseen the development of all drugs at the Ministry of Epidemic Prevention and was a learned, experienced researcher himself.
"It’s medicine from the Yunzhou Pharmaceutical Association. Probably a side effect."
"But the side effects shouldn’t be this severe! Look at what’s become of the child—he’s lost his mind! What good is a cure then?"
"I heard they used the most precious, newly developed energy source."
At this, the head of the Yunzhou Pharmaceutical Association stepped forward with some trepidation, handing over the prescription and the medicine. He said with a frown, "We didn’t expect such severe side effects. We just added a little more of the red energy mixture..."
"Right, here is our result sheet. The results showed it could kill 99.9% of the parasites."
Minister Zhao sniffed the medicine and frowned at the prescription. "The red energy’s side effects are too great," he said. "Your ratio is over a hundred times what it should be, which makes the treatment meaningless. First of all, we don’t have that much red energy, and it’s still in the developmental stage—we don’t even know the correct way to utilize it. Secondly, these side effects are not sustainable. This formula isn’t viable. Please stop the experiment."
"No way!"
"How is that acceptable! Didn’t we agree that no matter what we used, even this red energy, it would be okay as long as it cured them? Shouldn’t the results be based on the suppression rate?"
"Yes, we’re using this precious energy regardless of cost! As long as it proves effective against the parasites, we’ll win this round!"
The people from the Yunzhou Pharmaceutical Association suddenly became agitated. They had spent a considerable sum on this; how could they simply accept defeat? The competition rules were clear, and there could be no backtracking. Moreover, they were confident, backed by powerful resources. Otherwise, they wouldn’t have obtained such a precious substance right before the competition.
Then someone from another pharmaceutical association said, "You’ve cured him into senselessness. What’s the point if he survives like that?"
"We don’t care! The rules clearly state that the outcome is based on the suppression rate. We’ll experiment with a few more subjects, and we’re bound to find the best formula."
"You’re planning to render a few more senseless?"
The commotion quickly drew even more people, as well as all the referees. Elder Zhang was helped over too. After hearing the full account of events, he nodded and said, "You all have valid points. Since I’m the Chief Referee of this competition, let me say a few words."
Finally, everyone quieted down again, except for the child who was still thrashing restlessly on the bed to which he was tied.
"The outcome of this competition is determined primarily by the final suppression rate; this will not change. Whoever ranks highest will be the winner of this round," Elder Zhang declared.
The members of the Yunzhou Pharmaceutical Association smirked smugly. "Indeed, initial losses are inevitable. Just give us a few more samples, and we can do even better. Reaching 100% is not impossible."
"But!"

chapters.title: Chapter 588: The Competition is Over, Hurry Up and Leave
chapters.content:
Chapter 588: The Competition is Over, Hurry Up and Leave
Before the crowd could process Boss Zhang’s words, a single "but"—an unexpected turn—forced everyone to perk up their ears and listen closely.
But what? What’s there to ’but’ about? If we’re going by the rules, what’s left to ’but’? Seriously.
Nobody dared to speak these words aloud,
but those from the Yunzhou Medicine Association thought them, all the while nodding and smiling. "Please, do tell," one said. "Whatever it is, as long as it’s within the rules, we’re open to discussion." The Chief Referee had given them a way out; they couldn’t very well ignore the gesture, could they?
Victory seemed within their grasp. Anything was acceptable as long as it didn’t affect the outcome.
Members of the other Medicine Associations looked on with unpleasant expressions. They had heard that if the inhibition rate was the deciding factor, then the 99.9% figure would likely clinch the victory. Even if the Chief Referee had additional demands, it seemed too late for them to turn the tide.
Is the Chief Referee also biased?
everyone wondered. They all knew this drug had been developed with a massive amount of money. Using it was frankly out of the question—not to mention its lethal side effects, especially considering the precious red energy source was rarer even than Bodhi.
At that moment, all eyes turned to the Chief Referee.
Elder Zhang continued, "However, since this result has been obtained, we will record your data on the competition’s score sheet. You may conclude your participation now. As Old Zhao mentioned, this drug isn’t suitable for mass production. Even continuing trials for this formulation is unnecessary, given the waste of human and material resources... Let’s stop here."
The faces of those from the Yunzhou Medicine Association flickered with indiscernible emotions. Although their data had been acknowledged, and they might end up champions, the inability to mass-produce or even continue research left them with a hollow victory.
Won’t we become the subject of ridicule once we return?
Boss Zhang coughed a few times, waved his hand, and began walking away. As he walked, he said firmly, "Rest assured, the results will be based on the inhibition rate. If yours remains the highest, then the championship is yours." His demeanor brooked no further argument, showcasing the Chief Referee’s decisiveness.
"Good! Then, we will take our leave."
"Wait. That child will be your responsibility. If you can’t cure him, his life from here on out is in your hands. I will send people to check in regularly."
The person in charge from the Yunzhou Medicine Association lowered his head. When he raised it again, his eyes were filled with joy and smiles. "Of course, it is our responsibility."
The delegation from the Yunzhou Medicine Association quickly left the scene, taking all their belongings and leaving behind only a messenger. The competition continued; this was but a minor episode. Despite the 99.9% figure looming over them, other Medicine Associations did not give up. Fighting for second or third place was still worthwhile, as it could lead to good resources for the following year.
「Yet, another wave arose before the first had settled.」
The drug testing stage had just begun. They hadn’t even had the chance to administer the injections when the competition venue became noisy again. The sight of children lying neatly on the ground, apparently unconscious from the anesthesia, was somewhat unsettling.
"One hundred percent!"
"It’s one hundred percent!"
Each shout was more excited and louder than the last.
"What one hundred percent? One hundred percent what?"
"Who knows? Let’s go see. Could it be a one hundred percent inhibition rate?"
"Are you crazy? What was the highest the Epidemic Prevention Department achieved after months of research? Today, a drug with a 99.9% rate, developed with sheer money, has been shocking enough. And its side effects are so severe it could practically turn people into imbeciles. How could there possibly be one hundred percent? That would be a huge slap in the face for the Epidemic Prevention Department!"
As they talked, the growing excitement and impassioned cries drew the others back in. Of course, some diligent participants continued to focus on the competition. They did not join the commotion.
As everyone knows, those who merely watch the drama unfold and gossip never accomplish great things.
"Ahem, wait a moment, let’s pause the competition," Minister Zhao announced through a megaphone, but he didn’t expect Boss Zhang to snatch it from him. Boss Zhang then declared, "What competition are you talking about? The competition is over; there’s no need to continue! Whether you’ve yet to start, are halfway through the drug trial, or are about to begin, please stop all actions. I now announce the competition is over!"
Everyone was bewildered.
What in the world is going on? Had the competition even properly started? We went to see what the commotion was about after that sudden announcement of a 99.9% inhibition rate. We just got back to the competition area, not even warmed up yet, and now they’re declaring it over?
"But some of us haven’t even started... Why is it over?"
"What happened?"
"Why stop the competition?"
Overcome with excitement, Boss Zhang spoke through the megaphone, "What is the purpose of hosting this competition? It’s to find a complete cure for the parasite! Now that we have found it, the competition must end! Just moments ago, we discovered a drug that has no side effects, an inhibitory and kill rate of 100%, and can be mass-produced! This horrific parasite infection will soon be over!"
"Really? Is it true?"
"Quick, look! Wu City! Their data just updated on the big screen!"
"Wu City? The one with a huge supply of Bodhi? But... how could the rate be that high?"
"It’s real! Truly real! This is so unexpected!"
The lab results were in. Although the two children were very weak, with their organs damaged to varying degrees, and would need further treatment, the conclusion was undeniable: the parasites had vanished completely, eradicated without a trace!
"Quick! This drug needs at least five hundred clinical trials! Start treating these children now! I ask the other Medicine Associations to stop their work and clear the premises!" Minister Zhao urged. He sounded much like an exam proctor announcing the end of an exam when the bell rings, shouting, "Alright, pens down! Leave the classroom!" afraid someone might write an extra word.
This was undeniably real. The people of Wu City had actually produced a cost-free drug with a 100% efficacy rate!
Was this competition some kind of farce from beginning to end? What had we actually accomplished, if not just playing a supporting role?
they thought.
"So, even if the first-place winner is decided, and second place too, shouldn’t we at least determine third and fourth place?" someone asked.
"Exactly! We should have a proper ranking, right? You can’t just stop the competition halfway through!" another added.
How will we explain this when we get back? What about the resources?
Boss Zhang waved his hand dismissively and said authoritatively, "Apart from the data just recorded, all other Medicine Associations will score Zero for this round. We’ll then determine rankings based on the combined scores from the first and second rounds."
That was quite generous of him,
some thought.
Fine, so everyone scored Zero this round—what a frustrating mess,
they grumbled inwardly.
But at least there will be a third place.
People started to trickle out. Now, the delegation from the Wu City Medicine Association really had to scramble. They, too, were still bewildered by the outcome.

chapters.title: Chapter 589: This Is My Explanation for Everyone
chapters.content:
Chapter 589: This Is My Explanation for Everyone
They hadn’t done anything at all up to this point. So how had the competition stopped so inexplicably, leaving them as the ones who remained? Not only that, but the judges were also looking at them with such eager eyes, as if...
Hmm, lambs to the slaughter? No, no, no, they must have been mistaken.
With the competition halted, the Wu City Pharmaceutical Association and the judges all pitched in. They diluted the original liquid with saline before infusing it into the children. At least four people were needed to restrain each child during the intense reactions caused by the drug, while specialists recorded various data.
In short, a competition evolved into a large-scale emergency treatment scene, resounding with calls and shouts.
As for Jing Shu, she had almost forgotten her original reason for coming, having joined the team using the original liquid to treat these children and quickly becoming skilled at it.
Jing Shu might not have known how to administer injections. Indeed, if not for her Spiritual Spring—her ’golden touch’—she was the type who couldn’t even keep a flower alive. She relied on it to grow such impressive medicinal herbs. Aside from that, Jing Shu wasn’t particularly skilled in much else, but she did possess brute strength.
Even when diluted with saline, the Bodhi Original Liquid was formidable. The insects within Er Qiu’s body had almost burst out in violent resistance. The sedated children showed no pain response, but the insects within them reacted violently.
If they weren’t properly secured and controlled, the consequences of allowing the trial subjects to resist would be severe.
...
...
"This is the remaining original liquid..." Minister Zhao reluctantly passed the small bottle of original liquid to Jing Shu and solemnly promised, "Rest assured, President Jing. Aside from the original liquid used on the first two children, which counts towards the drug trial competition, we will include all subsequent uses in our procurement list. You will not suffer any loss. Moreover, we will purchase all Bodhi from your Wu City Pharmaceutical Association from now on. In addition, the production rights for this class of drugs will be wholly handed over to the Wu City Pharmaceutical Association to manage."
Jing Shu waved her hand dismissively and checked the time. Her stomach was already growling with hunger.
Because I wanted to keep a low profile, I didn’t bring Fat Chicken; revealing such a large bird in front of hundreds of people would have been too ostentatious. And I didn’t bring any food for myself either. More than half the day has passed; Fat Chicken must be starving too. This won’t do; I need to finish up quickly and head back.
Besides, she had brought the original liquid precisely to treat people this time. Jing Shu felt a great sense of accomplishment being able to save these future seeds of hope within her capabilities. Therefore, she said, "There’s no need to return it. Didn’t you say that a drug trial requires data from at least several hundred people? There are more severely ill patients outside. Before the new medicine is ready, we can use this for them. Consider it my personal donation. Let’s not make a big deal out of it."
Stay low-profile. Be discreet,
she thought.
"Great, great! That’s wonderful! Your donation isn’t just an item; it’s literally saving lives! We won’t publicize it, but this must be recorded in the big data archives. Although doing good deeds anonymously is commendable, this honorable deed of yours must be recorded as an example!"
Minister Zhao, looking like he wouldn’t take no for an answer, insisted on recording this event in her personal file. Oddly enough, despite having only known Jing Shu, this young woman, for a day and the considerable age difference between them, he always felt she was to his liking—a person with whom he could get along and work well.
Meanwhile, Boss Zhang, the event’s overall person in charge who had jumped departments to forcefully take over, was already happily taking his precious only grandson for convalescence. His objective was clear: he had taken on this mess entirely because of his infected grandson. Now that they had found the antidote and cured his grandson, Boss Zhang, being out of his field and understanding none of it, naturally relinquished all responsibility, instructing, "Second Zhao, you will take full responsibility for this matter from now on. I, this old man, am not feeling well and will head home first."
With those words, he was gone. And just like that, Minister Zhao from the Epidemic Prevention Department was naturally in charge of everything that followed. Therefore, regarding the drug production rights, Minister Zhao directly delegated them to the Wu City Pharmaceutical Association.
"Oh, I forgot to make an announcement! Aren’t the people from the other Medicine Associations still waiting outside for the results? Lao Miao, update the big data and publish the results. In my excitement, I completely forgot about that! Quick, find a few more people. Distribute this original liquid to the group on the other side, and prioritize treating those with serious conditions there first. It will take some time before the new medicine is ready. You’ll also need to personally supervise the new drug’s formulation and comparisons... Ah, never mind, never mind. Time is tight and the tasks are heavy; I’ll have to handle these things myself!"
As he spoke, Lao Miao, who had been holding out his hand waiting to receive the original liquid for a long time, was stunned for a moment to see the proffered hand retract. Minister Zhao hurried off again, with Lao Miao shouting from behind, "Wait for me! Wait for me, Minister! Sigh, when will you ever change this impulsive nature of yours..."
Jing Shu also smiled and shook her head. Minister Zhao, who had just been excitedly discussing matters with her, had vanished in a puff of smoke.
But the country needs people like him to persevere and go further in the apocalypse,
she thought.
"Danai, the rest is up to you now—coordination, drug manufacturing, contract signing, and so on," said Jing Shu as she too made her exit.
Removing her gas mask and taking in the fresh air, Jing Shu took deep breaths. Just as she was about to relax, her phone urgently rang. "Hello?"
