This kept Jing Shu extremely busy, making her finally grasp just how many enterprises she currently owned.
And this perfectly illustrates the saying: the scary part isn’t telling one lie, but having to tell thousands more to cover it up, endlessly spinning falsehoods. For instance, initially, it was just about starting the Red Worm Factory. But look at what followed—to supplement the factory, I had to collaborate with West Mountain for energy and Fuel supplies, and plan for the factory’s future development and its relocation after the fifth year. Because the factory had some open space, and for various other reasons, I started breeding Sulfuric Acid Ants. They produce a stable supply of sulfuric acid, which can be used as fertilizer or provided directly to the Township Government. I also took over the waste plant in Banana District, becoming its manager, all to reduce costs and secure more Fuel for the factory, as well as to prepare for the fifth-year relocation. Later, I collaborated with the insect woman, Xiao Wei, acting as a middleman. I gave Xiao Wei some rice and flour, oil, and daily necessities. In return, I arranged for hundreds of her super-sized insects to be slaughtered and made into meat patties. The profits from these insects were then reinvested into the factory, continuing the cycle.
In the end, was all that effort for nothing? Pah! Actually, not really. These industries have snowballed, growing larger and larger. It reached a point where, to support one part of the industrial chain, I had to establish others. Breaking a single link would disrupt the entire operation. I now also understand the essence of it: if you’re in trouble, go to the Township Government. If you’re out of money, go to the Township Government. Always use borrowed resources if possible, never your own. I’m living the life of the capitalist I despised in my past life. But I also once said, ’I despise those big corporate capitalists. Of course, if it’s me, then pretend I never said that.’ My current industries also include shares from West Mountain and in biological research. And that’s not even counting the smaller ventures.
Jing Shu had been lost in these self-satisfied thoughts for the past few days. Of course, Jing Shu’s return had definitely stirred the whole family, especially with the items she brought back—weren’t each of them nearly extinct?
Furthermore, she had also brought new breeding stock, like bamboo rats. The fact that these creatures were to be kept in Jing Shu’s room for her personal care showed just how much importance she placed on them.
At the same time, various feed insects were also being produced in batches.
Mr. Jing had work to do again: setting up a special breeding compartment for insects in the backyard. With the outside temperature already below minus twenty degrees Celsius, Jing Shu’s house needed its furnace and underfloor heating running 24 hours a day to maintain the temperature of the entire villa and backyard. So, there was no need to worry about these creatures freezing to death.
Jing Shu, meanwhile, had already prolifically bred a batch in her space.
I’m prepared. In the coming years, these feed insects might substitute other fresh grains. Plus, there won’t be as many fresh vegetable roots available during the relocation. So now, I’ll breed as many insects as possible—the more, the better. Eventually, I’ll freeze-dry them all to save space.
The Wu City news did indeed feature a video welcoming the Medicine Association’s triumphant return. However, it didn’t elaborate, only generally mentioning the competition in the Imperial Capital. The inside details and involved contents were not publicly disclosed.
But that didn’t really matter. The key point was that they also broadcast footage of Jing Shu disembarking from the plane in a thick padded jacket, smiling and waving, and shaking hands with Jin Tianci.

chapters.title: Chapter 622: Just For Fun
chapters.content:
Chapter 622: Just For Fun
The Jing Shu in this video looks so unsophisticated!
she thought.
Even if they say the ultimate in plainness can be beauty, this is just too much. I can’t even bear to look directly at it. Thankfully, my face isn’t very clear due to the darkness.
Jing Shu comforted herself.
I’m just trying to keep a low profile, so there’s nothing much to it. Besides, the lighting is bad, so ordinary people wouldn’t recognize me anyway.
Her family didn’t feel the same way. Urged by Mr. Jing, the whole family eagerly gathered around the TV, watching the local news from Wu City with great interest. Mr. Jing would occasionally point at the scenes on the TV, talking about how he had been right there at that moment. When the camera swept over him, he bounced excitedly, pointing at the screen and shouting loudly.
But Mr. Jing rapped him with a chopstick, forcing him to sit. "Stop shouting, sit down! You’re too loud."
Mr. Jing grunted.
Jing Shu’s thoughts wandered far again.
Actually, I’m not too worried about this. There aren’t many people who still watch TV and news at this hour, since everyone is now watching short videos about big data on their smartphones.
Just then, her phone started BEEPING non-stop. Jing Shu suddenly had a bad feeling. After unlocking her phone, her suspicions were confirmed: the high school group chat was fervently discussing something. When she scrolled up, she indeed found the video of herself in a bulky coat, shaking hands and smiling.
"This looks like Jing Shu @Jing Shu, is it you?"
"Looks a bit like her, but this is the news..."
The chat was generally focused on whether the person was Jing Shu. Some said it was her; despite the dim lighting, Jing Shu had worn that exact bulky coat before. Others said it wasn’t, arguing that this was the news, unlike that incident with Xishan shares.
Both sides presented their arguments. Of course, the biggest source of disbelief stemmed from the titles mentioned, such as being photographed with Wu City’s leader and being the President of the Medicine Association.
Who would believe that an old classmate has climbed to such a position now? Did you see that person, Big Yellow Teeth? He’s so old and is just the vice-president of the Medicine Association, yet the person in that bulky coat is so young and is already a vice-president...
Jing Shu had already given everyone the impression of being mysterious and capable. Her family didn’t seem very influential, yet she always possessed a strong, enigmatic aura. She could even befriend Su Malie, who notably admired her. Of course, everyone later found out that Jing Shu actually had a share in the coveted West Mountain Stone Garden.
But even with all this, it seemed implausible that someone so young could become the vice-president of the Medicine Association or be personally greeted at the airport by a powerful leader. Most people found it hard to believe, or rather, were unwilling to.
Jing Shu shook her head.
Even though several people mentioned me and Su Malie in the group chat, since there’s no concrete evidence, I’ll just act oblivious and stay silent. Su Malie seems to be absent. I have no idea what she’s up to; she seems busy recently. Grandma Jing did mention the neighboring villa has been empty for days.
It had to be said, Jing Shu had perfected the art of playing aloof, as if she’d mastered a player’s handbook.
The group’s attention quickly shifted to a new topic. To stimulate consumption and find new food sources during the apocalypse, Wu City had organized a "New Apocalypse Food Competition." The premise was simple: anyone, whether they were digging in the soil or just going about their day, could submit any new species they encountered to the competition judges. These judges would then determine if the species was edible. Furthermore, if someone could cultivate a new edible plant, discover a new edible species, or synthesize new food, they could enter their creation into the competition, provided it was edible.
The prizes included a wealth of Virtual Coins, a standalone home, and many other smaller prizes and participation awards.
Indeed, lured by the rich rewards, people discovered quite a few new edible species from the apocalypse. Although they weren’t very tasty and some even had potential side effects, that hardly mattered anymore.
The news broadcast had finished, and Jing Shu was almost done with her second meal at home when the university group chat started BEEPING with notifications again.
Jing Shu, already irritable, was about to close the chat.
I’m not very familiar with my college classmates anyway. To be honest, with over ninety people in one class, aside from large lectures and shared electives with other classes, I can hardly remember most of their names now. So much time has passed; I’ve almost completely forgotten them all. That’s why, since I joined the group, there’s seldom been any conversation. Even after all this time since the apocalypse, there’s hardly been any interaction.
Jing Shu’s college was a tier-three institution in Wu City specializing in performing arts. The tuition fees—goodness, they were expensive! Consequently, the families who could afford it were generally well-off, inevitably leading to comparisons. Moreover, most students paid meticulous attention to their appearance and physique. Premium makeup, skincare, and personal trainers were considered basic necessities, not to mention various nutritional and beauty supplements.
The former campus belle, with her flawless white skin and nearly perfect figure, had spent millions on upkeep. Yet, some always naively believed that such a "pure" campus belle would actually fall for something as absurd as love.
I used to like that feeling too, and I envied everything about them,
Jing Shu mused.
But ten years in the apocalypse have worn down all my sharp edges and illusions. It’s better to be simple and down-to-earth now. So in this life... I have a more detached view on these matters.
Jing Shu frowned as notifications tagging her kept popping up.
Who could it be?
she wondered. Upon checking, she saw it was that news story again, and it had clearly sparked a strong reaction.
Jiang Changke: "@Jing Shu, the woman in this news, it’s you, right? She looks a lot like you."
Liu Xia: "There are many people who look alike. By the way, who is Jing Shu? I don’t remember her."
Cheng Long: "How could it possibly be someone from our school, let alone Jing Shu? I know that girl; I even chased her once, hahaha."
The conversation started from there and, surprisingly, even escalated into an argument. Jing Shu scrolled down, perplexed.
Liu Xia: "Cheng Long, your kids are old enough to be running errands for soy sauce, and Sister Tang Yuan is also in this group. How can you still talk like this? Aren’t you afraid Sister Tang Yuan will smack you?"
Cheng Long: "...It was just for fun back then. I only chased Jing Shu because I lost a bet; it was nothing serious."
Now I vaguely remember this Cheng Long person,
Jing Shu thought.
He did seem to pursue me back then, but I was solely focused on becoming an actor and had no interest in such matters. The reason I remember is because my dorm mates tricked me into a gathering. I went, only to find Cheng Long was the only one there. He told me to order first, saying everyone else would arrive soon. So, naive little me ended up having a meal with him, utterly confused.
Zhen Hu: "I remember now! Jing Shu became an internet celebrity and was endorsing products online. Nothing much was heard after that. But how could she possibly represent the Wu City Medicine Association in a competition? Besides, the Medicine Association isn’t easy to get into."
Liu Xia: "Exactly! Jing Shu has no background in pharmaceuticals or medicine. That’s a completely different field!"

chapters.title: Chapter 623: Otherwise, do you still want to hit me?
chapters.content:
Chapter 623: Otherwise, do you still want to hit me?
Actually, up to this point, everything had been normal, with no strange comments. The only exception was Cheng Long’s remarks, which made Jing Shu uncomfortable... she just found them annoying.
Jing Shu has become more sensitive these days; it can’t be helped, as she rarely faces any grievances anymore.
Jing Shu quietly made a mental note of Cheng Long’s name.
Words shouldn’t be spoken so carelessly.
The discussion should have ended there, as there was nothing really to fuss about, but then Jiang Changke had to pop up again.
Jiang Changke: "Hehe, check out this comparison. I dug up a graduation photo from a few years ago and some other old pictures. After comparing them with the person in the video using professional software, I realized it’s the same individual! @Jing Shu, Boss, my stomach is weak, so I’m perfect for living off someone. Are you looking to be a sugar mama?"
Liu Xia: "Jiang Changke, cut it out! Even if you want to be a sycophant, this isn’t the way. You really think a few photos prove anything?"
Sweet Dumpling: "Hey, it’s not like you don’t know him. Jiang Changke is always deceiving people. Back in university, he claimed a family member was seriously ill and borrowed money from everyone. He then invested it in some shares, lost everything, and ended up owing people money. He still owes me five hundred bucks!"
Cheng Long: "But Jiang Changke’s data analysis seems to be correct... Now that you mention it, she *does* look a bit like Jing Shu... Incredible! If our class really produced someone like that, it would be freaking awesome! @Jing Shu, for old times’ sake, considering I treated you to meals before, how about introducing us to a few good jobs? I hear that among all the official positions, the Pharmaceutical Association Hospital and its cafeteria offer the best benefits."
Sweet Dumpling: "You shameless bastard! You even treated *her* to a meal? You regret being with me, don’t you? Cheng Long, you scumbag! Since she’s made it big, why don’t you just go be with her!"
Jiang Changke: "@Sweet Dumpling, you’d better keep an eye on your husband. Look at this photo—Cheng Long secretly took it back in the day. And that first photo of a meal on his social media feed? That was him eating with Jing Shu. Hahaha."
Jing Shu finally frowned.
That damned troublemaker! What is he trying to do? Is he deliberately saying these things to provoke people?
As expected, the next second, Sweet Dumpling exploded and began to curse furiously.
Sweet Dumpling: "Fine! You despicable couple! The woman is shameless enough to casually dine with other men, and the man goes around fathering children everywhere! Even with kids now, he still hasn’t deleted those photos from his social media feed! @#¥%..."
Then Cheng Long, unable to bear the loss of face, also started cursing profusely, "I’ve indulged you enough, day in and day out! If you spout one more damn word, I’ll go to your workplace right now and deal with you!"
Jiang Changke: "@Cheng Long, go for it, bro! How are you planning to ’deal’ with her? Is it the way I’m thinking? In broad daylight, though? That might not be such a good idea, right?"
Sweet Dumpling: "Scram!"
Cheng Long: "Scram!"
...
Liu Xia: "Oh, I get it now! Everyone, stop arguing. Jiang Changke has a motive for saying Jing Shu is the person in the news. He must have received some benefits from Jing Shu to say such a thing. @Jing Shu, hurry up and clarify! Don’t make things up for this; it won’t do you any good."
Jing Shu: "???"
This group is freaking toxic! Why would I need to fabricate something like this?
Liu Xia continued her analysis: "Have you all forgotten? Recently, there’s been a bankruptcy liquidation auction called the Celebrities Gathering. It’s for auctioning off assets from those who owe Virtual Coins to the Township Government, those with pre-apocalypse debts, criminals, and others for various reasons. The court auctions off these items, so many people are looking to snap up bargains."
Celebrities Gathering? Jing Shu genuinely didn’t know about that. After all, she had only just returned and hadn’t heard about this event. Oh, right, that’s because she hasn’t really interacted with anyone lately.
Liu Xia: "But not just anyone can get in. The entry barrier is very high; you need an invitation card. As you all know, in our group, only Young Master Lan has access to invitation slots. So, Jing Shu must have given Jiang Changke some benefits to ’confirm’ this whole thing. If we all acknowledge her status, she can then conveniently ask for an invitation to go to the Celebrities Gathering and snap up some bargains at the auction."
Jiang Changke: "You sure can spin a complicated tale! I didn’t even think that far ahead. But let me tell you, the person in the news *is* Jing Shu. Just wait and see how she deals with you all for offending her."
Liu Xia: "Ooh, I’m so scared."
Sweet Dumpling: "Me too, I’m terrified! Does this mean she won’t help us find good jobs anymore?"
Wang Miao: "Speaking of the Celebrities Gathering, the way you guys describe it, just getting in sounds like picking up free money. I’m so envious! I want to go too. Unfortunately, I don’t have the connections to get in. @Young Master Lan, could you perhaps lower the requirements?"
Liu Wen: "I want to go too! It would be great just to witness it. I heard many items are sold at their base price and are mostly snapped up internally."
Guo Qiran: "I heard there’s everything from large properties, estates, and villas, down to small second-hand items and daily necessities. New, old, even move-in ready places... so much stuff..."
Jing Shu raised an eyebrow as she read this.
Actually, she already had plenty of things. She wasn’t really interested in events like this Celebrities Gathering anymore. After all, she had already splurged big time twice in the Imperial Capital. There were only a very few specific items she still needed to acquire.
Jing Shu gave a sarcastic smile.
She hadn’t expected the question of whether or not it was her in the news to stir up so many other issues. So what if it was her? And so what if it wasn’t? These people really overthink things, don’t they? Jing Shu wasn’t some saint with infinite patience. After being inexplicably berated like this, she really felt like hitting someone. Jing Shu wasn’t fond of cursing people; she preferred to take direct action.
If you have a problem, don’t just run your mouth. Don’t hide under your covers cursing people out.
Jing Shu’s fists were CRACKLING. Just at that moment, someone else spoke up in the group chat.
Young Master Lan: "Let’s not be so extreme, everyone. The truth will always come out; fakes can’t become real. If Jing Shu is truly the Deputy Chairwoman of the Medicine Association, then she wouldn’t need my invitation card; she could come and go from the Celebrities Gathering as she pleases. If it’s a lie and she still asks me for a slot, then that would be too blatant, wouldn’t it, @Jing Shu?"
Liu Xia: "So, you’re saying that on the day of the event, we’ll know if she’s the real deal just by seeing if Jing Shu shows up?"
Jing Shu’s ’all energies’ finally erupted.
She had to admit, sometimes cursing people out was quite satisfying. No wonder there were so many keyboard warriors.
Jing Shu: "@Liu Xia, whether I’m real or fake is none of your damn business! Is it that important to you? Instead of wasting your time on this, you’d be better off figuring out how to sneak into the event yourself. That’s more practical. And you, @Jiang Changke, retract those chat logs right now! You’ve violated my privacy. If you don’t, you’d better consider the consequences yourself.
"@Sweet Dumpling, @Cheng Long, I don’t want to comment on your personal drama. However, you both need to apologize to me and retract all your statements concerning me.
"Never mind. I know you definitely won’t apologize. I’m just going through the motions here."
Jing Shu’s rapid-fire barrage of messages immediately sent the chat into an uproar; she had tagged every single person who had spoken about her.
Sweet Dumpling: "So what if I don’t apologize? Are you going to hit me? Come on then! This is a perfect chance for everyone to see how you used to seduce men."

chapters.title: Chapter 624: I’m Sorry for My Lack of Spine
chapters.content:
Chapter 624: I’m Sorry for My Lack of Spine
Jing Shu said, "It’s too late for apologies now. I’m already angry, so don’t say I bullied you later."
Jing Shu really didn’t want to do this; it was too much like bullying. Why did some people always insist on provoking powerful opponents?
Sweet Dumpling retorted, "What, are you going to come here and hit me? Try it! See if I don’t kill you. Who dares to mess around without connections these days? Even if you’re just some broke president, how powerful can you be? You think you can manage me across industries? I work at the power grid. Come at me if you dare!"
Jing Shu replied, "I won’t hit you. Later, you can hit yourself. You’re shouting so fiercely now; just make sure you don’t apologize later. Have some backbone."
Sweet Dumpling scoffed, "Bullshit! Only morons apologize. Come on, come now, or everyone will look down on you. Trying to play tough with me? I’ve seen this trick a million times before."
Jiang Changke quickly typed, "Alright, alright, Boss, I was wrong! I’ll take back everything I said immediately. You guys better apologize quickly too. If you offend the Boss, you’re done for! Do you know how powerful the Vice President is? A flick of her little finger could crush you! And those in the group acting like big shots, stop calling Young Master Lan so affectionately. He’s nothing in front of Jing Shu! And what about the Wu City Four? Do you think following Gold Dominator makes you so incredible?"
The Wu City Four? Jing Shu had no idea such people even existed.
Jiang Changke really knew how to stir up hatred; he was a natural-born troublemaker. His words offended everyone, causing widespread dissatisfaction and strong condemnation. They immediately lumped Jiang Changke in with Jing Shu, rendering her speechless.
Where the heck did this idiot come from? I have absolutely no impression of him.
"Jiang Changke, who do you think you’re fooling, acting like this is real? You borrowed money from us, claiming misfortune, and never paid it back, you little wretch!"
Guo Qiran sneered, "Act, go on, keep acting. It’s quite believable. You must have made a good amount of Virtual Coins from this, right? Scammer!"
Liu Xia chimed in, "Each of the Wu City Four is impressive. Gold Dominator’s dad is the big boss of Wu City. Young Master Lan calls Gold Dominator his brother; isn’t that impressive? Young Master Lan’s family also holds a high position in Wu City, and he even helped our school secure many job positions. Tell me, just how impressive is Young Master Lan? Even Jing Shu can’t possibly match his status, can she?"
Jing Shu understood now. Gold Dominator? Jin Tianci’s son? He was the one who stole her supplies that year, angering her so much that she stormed directly into Jin Tianci’s house. So, she had a score to settle with Gold Dominator too.
When did this guy even form the Wu City Four?
The group chat completely exploded.
Even Young Master Lan of the Wu City Four started @-ing Jiang Changke, warning him to watch his words or face the consequences.
Young Master Lan clearly had significant influence, as many people in the group depended on him for their jobs. Once he spoke, the tide immediately turned in his favor.
However, Jing Shu’s problems weren’t solved. Many in the group supporting Sweet Dumpling had started attacking Jing Shu, accusing her and Jiang Changke of being deceivers of the same ilk. They taunted, "Now that Young Master Lan has spoken, why aren’t you keeping quiet?" Some even dug up Jing Shu’s old influencer materials, mocking her for failing as an actress and becoming an influencer instead. At first glance, Jing Shu seemed to be at a disadvantage, but that wasn’t really the case.
Look at how frequent online bickering still was. Keyboard warriors, so frustrated in their real lives, became incredibly brazen online. They acted as if they were God Almighty, believing they could not only destroy someone online but also snuff them out in real life whenever they pleased.
It made this apocalypse seem as if it weren’t even a society governed by law anymore.
But the war of words continued. Liu Xia and a few others kept making snide and mocking comments. Some cursed Jiang Changke while simultaneously fawning over Young Master Lan, who seemed to enjoy having the whole situation under his control. Sometimes, he would interject, "Okay, I’ll just add a few more spots for Celebrities Gathering. But as I’ve always said, those who are truly capable don’t need my spots to get in, and I wouldn’t invite fakes anyway."
Liu Xia gushed, "Wow, did you see that? That’s Young Master Lan for you, able to add spots to Celebrities Gathering just like that! It must be run by your relatives, right? Can you take me with you so I can broaden my horizons? Not like some people who resort to faking things and tricking others, thinking that pretending to be some vice president will get them in."
"It’s a classic case of trying to steal a chicken only to lose the rice bait. Hiring Jiang Changke must have cost a fortune, right?"
Young Master Lan said modestly, "It’s not run by my relatives. I just pulled some strings through Gold Dominator. He calls the shots for these things. After all, isn’t Wu City still under his dad’s control?"
Just then, Sister Tang Yuan, who had been quiet for a while, suddenly posted a video and @-all, causing everyone to pause and open it.
SLAP! SLAP! SLAP! SLAP!
A series of crisp slaps rang out. It was a video of Sister Tang Yuan slapping herself, one after another, each blow leaving a red mark. She was being incredibly harsh on herself.
While hitting herself, she choked out, "I’m sorry, I was wrong! I was reckless before, that’s why I spoke that way about someone. I’m just jealous and couldn’t get over it. I’m an idiot! I’m really sorry, Jing Shu... Please, let me go! I beg you, I know I was wrong... I was talking big; I thought you wouldn’t dare do anything to me... I’m sorry, I have no backbone. I’m scared..."
After watching the video and hearing her words, everyone was stunned. They were utterly shocked.
What the hell was going on? What was this situation?
Liu Xia typed, "@Sister Tang Yuan, what nonsense are you spouting? How can you bow down to evil forces? Did she threaten you? Speak up, and I’ll stand up for you!"
Sister Tang Yuan shot back, "Fuck off! You’re the one stirring up trouble here. You’d better apologize, and fast!"
Liu Xia fumed, "Seriously? How can there be people like this? I’m damn well trying to help you, and you’re siding with the enemy? This is a true case of offering a warm face only to get a cold shoulder!"
Just moments ago, Sister Tang Yuan had been the loudest with her curses. She disappeared for only a few minutes, and then suddenly, she completely changed her tune. Just as everyone was puzzled by this, it wasn’t long before Liu Xia also posted a half-minute-long voice message apology, her tone filled with extreme fright, terror, and shock.
The students then realized something was truly amiss. Jing Shu’s influence was indeed significant!
It had only been a few minutes, hadn’t it? People were cursing happily just moments before, and now, in no time at all, Sister Tang Yuan was slapping herself while apologizing. What on earth had Jing Shu done?
Jiang Changke laughed. "Hahaha, @Sister Tang Yuan, why are you caving in and admitting your mistake now? The worst they could do is use their connections to get you fired. Are you really bowing down just for a lousy job? Look at your husband, @Cheng Long. He hasn’t said a peep! He was silent when you were hurling abuse, and now that you’re practically on your knees, he’s still nowhere to be seen. Tsk, tsk, what a scumbag."

chapters.title: Chapter 625: Should I Go to the Celebrities Gathering?
chapters.content:
Chapter 625: Should I Go to the Celebrities Gathering?
Honestly, that Cheng Long really is something, staying quiet from start to finish.
Young Master Lan: "@sweet dumpling, Liu Xia, you guys really don’t need to worry about your jobs. No one can interfere with your positions. Since it was me who arranged for you to be there, I wouldn’t allow anyone to slap me in the face. @Jing Shu, joking is joking, even if you do have some clout, don’t make jokes about other people’s jobs. Rest assured, even if you did make a call, their jobs won’t be lost. After all, I still have a say in the power grid."
Jing Shu: "Do I need to stoop to such lowly tactics?"
Jing Shu chuckled. Threatening people was something she was least good at. What she excelled in was killing—with stones, knives, guns, all methods of killing, but there were many others as well.
A soft knife is still a knife, and it can kill without shedding blood.
Using a job as a threat was a trifling tactic Jing Shu disdained to use. Moreover, it was very easy to hit a snag, just like facing someone like Young Master Lan who wouldn’t give face. Why humiliate oneself?
sweet dumpling: "No, no, no, Young Master Lan, Jing Shu really didn’t threaten me, really. Don’t ask anymore, I was really wrong. I beg your forgiveness, Jing Shu. I was blind not to recognize a great person. This Devil wants my life!! My life!!"
sweet dumpling regretted it, regretted provoking this devil, this Devil!
Young Master Lan: "We’re all classmates here. Let’s talk things out. Jing Shu, no matter what connections you used, why make things so tense? It’s better to leave some room for maneuver when dealing with people, since we have to face each other in the future."
Jing Shu then asked, "@sweet dumpling, @Liu Xia, I heard I threatened you guys? Well then, let’s have a heart-to-heart and see if I really did threaten you. I have nothing to fear if I’m in the right... to prevent anyone from thinking I’m bullying."
sweet dumpling: "Don’t, don’t, please don’t say it, please. I was wrong. Please stop. I really was wrong. What can I do for you to forgive me? I’ll come to the group every day to confess, to apologize, just hoping for your forgiveness."
The university group members couldn’t help but grow curious. What could have scared sweet dumpling to this extent?
Could sweet dumpling have done something unspeakable?
Jing Shu must have some kind of secret on sweet dumpling; otherwise, she wouldn’t be acting like this. Even with Young Master Lan backing her up, there was no reason to be so frightened unless Jing Shu had a grip on her lifeline.
Jiang Changke: "The big boss is really powerful. Just showing up determines who has clout. With a flick of a finger, she can crush those little ants. Weren’t these people being so defiant just a few minutes ago? Now look at them, this is what happens when you cross the big boss, huh, let’s see who still dares to speak out of turn."
"Shut up, don’t talk anymore." Jing Shu was truly speechless at this troublemaker.
If it weren’t for Jiang Changke, none of this would have happened today. Honestly, how could I have no impression of this person at all? It seems I didn’t even borrow money from him in college.
Young Master Lan: "Alright, alright, it’s not a big deal. Let’s do this, we’re all classmates after all. I know this incident was triggered by everyone’s concern for the Celebrities Gathering. I will try to secure five more spots for everyone, and I can also fight for ten spots for temporary workers on the day of the event. Even though you can’t participate in the auction as waiters, you’ll get to see the event and a free meal.
"Jing Shu, whether it’s true or not, I invite you to join the Celebrities Gathering. How about it? Let’s give them a break? If you do know something, then you surely know that I also have a lot of say in Wu City Power Company. Can we all get along well after this?"
"Wow, Young Master Lan is so awesome, so powerful, to be able to secure that many spots. I want to go too, I want to go."
"I want to work there, count me in for a spot, please."
Jing Shu couldn’t help but chuckle.
If it weren’t for turning to Heng Jin to check on sweet dumpling, I wouldn’t have known that this girl had already ’started exercising’ with people from Young Master Lan’s circle—you catch my drift, ’exercising.’ Of course, sweet dumpling has more dirty secrets than just that, or she wouldn’t be so scared out of her wits. She’s practically a double agent, involved not only with Young Master Lan but also deeply connected with his arch-rival. I was quite shocked after going through the files. What a pro! 666! No wonder Young Master Lan is putting on a show of protecting them here. Poor guy, he doesn’t even realize he’s already been betrayed, and sweet dumpling is truly terrified of their relationship coming to light, because the consequences would indeed be very dire. As for sweet dumpling’s husband, Cheng Long, he’s no saint either. What a chaotic world the apocalypse is, what a messy circle they’re in.
Jing Shu looked at Young Master Lan with a bit of sympathy and said teasingly, "Leave the invitation to someone who needs it more; I don’t want it. Let’s call this matter closed. In the future, you should be more careful not to invade others’ privacy. After all, I’m not the kind of person who speaks nicely, and I might do things that would terrify that person.
"Next time, if you provoke me again, things won’t be so simple."
Her words were audacious, but at that moment, no one dared to argue any further.
Even Jiang Changke didn’t dare to speak.
But Young Master Lan’s offer was still too enticing; the Celebrities Gathering’s influence was just too significant, and the topic quickly shifted in that direction.
"Just perfect, there’s one extra spot now, we all want to go!"
With more than a hundred people in the group chat, more and more people began scrambling for the spots. Young Master Lan reveled in the power to decide who could attend, feeling a different kind of thrill, as if he were the boss in another classmate’s domain.
All conversations about whether Jing Shu was the vice president of the Medicine Association were now buried, and sweet dumpling and her group didn’t dare to cause any more trouble. Jing Shu also soon forgot about the whole incident.
After all, as for the Celebrities Gathering, I really don’t need it. Besides, with these rather unsociable university classmates around, I don’t want to be in the spotlight. After all, back in university, everyone was accustomed to constant comparisons.
There are also hidden dragons and crouching tigers among them. Besides Young Master Lan, there are definitely others. Although I don’t know who they are, it’s already the fourth year of the apocalypse. It’s best not to be conspicuous or have people remember you; otherwise, it’s just trouble.
It’s strange sometimes; the very things you don’t want to do are precisely the ones that end up happening.
Not two days had passed since things calmed down when Jing Shu received an invitation from Li Yuetian to attend the so-called Celebrities Gathering.
"I’d better not," Jing Shu refused, making up an excuse. "The factory’s facing difficulties, and we still owe the Township Government a lot of Virtual Coins. I can’t afford the auction."
Li Yuetian was sipping the Turtle Snake Wine that Jing Shu had given him, his happiness almost making him feel like he could fly. It was only after gulping down a satisfying mouthful that he said, "Is that so? That’s a shame. We’re going out there with a mission this time, to recover some resources for the New District. But I heard that this time, there will be a lot of mobile villas. Didn’t you ask me to keep an eye out for you before?"
"Mobile villas???" Jing Shu’s eyes immediately lit up, practically turning into 15W light bulbs.

chapters.title: Chapter 627: You haven’t got eyes? (First Update)
chapters.content:
Chapter 627: You haven’t got eyes? (First Update)
The other members of the family didn’t seem very interested in the Celebrities Gathering either. Mr. Jing was still busy making worm nests, and Grandma Jing had her hands full with chores from morning till night. After all, just feeding the domestic poultry was a huge undertaking. That settled it; Jing Shu would go alone.
Besides, buying a house and increasing her assets were minor matters, not worth mentioning to them yet. She would surprise everyone later.
「The next day」
Jing Shu left the house fully prepared and formally dressed.
Finally, she took off the thick cotton jacket and switched to a fluffy black open-front down jacket. Underneath, she had to wear a bulletproof vest and put on a bulletproof hat. These were standard gear for Jing Shu whenever she left home.
What if some villain targeted her, wealthy as she was in this post-apocalyptic world?
But if anyone harbored ill intentions, they had better not blame her for punching them in the chest with her little fists.
The venue for this Celebrities Gathering was the New World Mall in Wu City. This mall had just been constructed in the development zone before the apocalypse. It had only just opened when the apocalypse struck, after which most of its supplies were moved out.
So, what was being auctioned was a parcel of land. This land was now very valuable, given that Wu City and several nearby towns had been flooded, making living spaces limited. Finally, someone had set their sights on this entrepreneur’s mall.
Jing Shu had been here in her past life. It was extravagant, praised as surpassing Wanda Mall—a one-stop spot for entertainment, sleeping, eating, and playing.
Coming to the New World Mall again in this life, things were starkly different. It had survived a second-year flood, a third-year earthquake, and now mudslides. Located in the suburbs, it still stood, though its interior was now very dilapidated.
But now, whoever could buy this mall—a nine-story giant—could use it as a factory or residential building. Either way, it was still very appealing.
Jing Shu’s goal this time was simple: a movable villa. She only had eyes for the movable villa and considered nothing else.
The first-floor exhibition hall of the New World Mall had clearly been cleaned up, as there had been a huge uproar in the university group the day before.
The students who went to work at the Celebrities Gathering had been called in early. Their tasks included cleaning mud, scraping off algae and plankton that had soaked for over a year, transporting debris, and wiping down and setting up tables. They had been exhausted for days. Fortunately, they were provided daily meals, and the tantalizing prospect of broadening their horizons at the Celebrities Gathering kept them going; otherwise, they would have quit long ago.
Virtual screens were hung up, carpets laid down, signs displayed, and the power was turned back on, providing air conditioning and lights. That made it look somewhat proper.
Upon entering, the vast, seven or eight hundred square meter open space was still very impressive. In the middle were rings of open-air escalators going up from the second floor to the third and fourth floors and beyond. This place had been very popular when it first opened.
Of course, what caught Jing Shu’s eye the most was not this, but the central exhibition hall. Three different villas stood there, exquisitely styled, luxurious, lavish, and grand...
Jing Shu spotted the largest and most luxurious movable villa right away. It had to be said, this movable villa was built very extravagantly, even better than she had imagined. It was the perfect ideal in Jing Shu’s mind, completely captivating her just from its appearance.
I wonder what it looks like inside,
she thought.
No matter how expensive, I must get this movable villa!
Jing Shu nearly drooled, staring longingly at the villa. It took several calls from someone nearby for her to snap out of it.
"Stop looking around and find your spot. I’ve got mine over there and have some mingling to do, so I’m heading over," Li Yuetian said as he left. He left Jing Shu alone—oh, along with Liu from the Red Worm Factory’s finance department.
Jing Shu wiped the drool from the corners of her mouth and pulled down the brim of her hat, trying to make herself less conspicuous.
Low profile, still need to keep a low profile,
she thought.
But just at that moment, someone came charging recklessly toward her. Jing Shu didn’t notice in time and bumped into him. The impact sent the person flying several meters away, landing with a THUD. Just from the sound, you could tell it hurt. His screams of agony immediately followed, and the faces of those around him turned pale.
The attention of the spectators, who were originally admiring the exhibition, was instantly drawn to this scene.
"How do you walk? Don’t you have eyes? Are you blind? Apologize immediately! Waiter, where’s the waiter? Come and help!" someone shouted.
Jing Shu frowned and took a closer look.
Well, what a coincidence. Isn’t this an acquaintance? TSK TSK.
Lying on the ground and wailing was none other than Gold Dominator, the son of Wu City’s ruler, Jin Tianci. He and Jing Shu were old enemies, and their previous grievances had not yet been settled.
If it hadn’t been for Jin Tianci’s sake, this little rascal would have already...
she mused.
Gold Dominator clutched his chest, feeling as if all his ribs had shattered. It was like crashing into a block of iron; the pain was so intense it brought tears to his eyes. He opened his mouth to curse, but upon looking up and seeing who it was, he swallowed his words.
Gold Dominator glared fiercely at Jing Shu.
Enemies truly do have a way of crossing paths,
he thought.
At this point, several of Gold Dominator’s Gou Tuizi rushed over to help him up. They barely managed to get him on his feet as he continued to wail in pain, trembling as he stood. Seeing this, the people around Gold Dominator immediately started cursing loudly.
"How is it? You didn’t hurt yourself too badly, did you? Need an ambulance? TSK TSK," Jing Shu said with her arms crossed and a mocking tone.
A young man supporting Gold Dominator demanded sternly, "Didn’t you see how badly Little Overlord fell? You vicious woman, aren’t you going to apologize? If anything happens to Little Overlord, can you afford to compensate him?"
"Oh? Little Overlord, HAHA! Did you have an accident? Do you need me to apologize? It seemed like you were the one who ran into me, right? I should be the one shouting ’indecent assault!’"
Although Gold Dominator looked fierce, he dared not say much, just gritting his teeth. He vaguely remembered his uncle telling him not to provoke this woman, that she was very difficult to deal with. Of course, he knew how difficult she was; she had made him suffer secretly twice, and he couldn’t even complain. Recently, she had even been on good terms with his cousin Jun Bao...
This is so infuriating! It’s maddening!
The young man supporting Gold Dominator said disdainfully, "Who do you think you are? Shouting ’indecent assault’? Who would believe that? Maybe you’re just trying to take advantage of our Little Overlord."
"That’s Jing Shu! DAMN IT! Isn’t this Jing Shu? Guys, look, doesn’t she look just like in the photos?"
Just then, another young man dressed as a waiter shouted excitedly. He took out his phone, showing it to the male and female waitstaff around him, and even to a man in a suit in the crowd.
Jing Shu frowned.
This loudmouth, what’s his deal? Who is this guy anyway?
"I’m Jiang Changke, Big Shot! I’m Jiang Changke! I’ve studied your photo hundreds of times; I’d recognize you anywhere!"

chapters.title: Chapter 628: Brother Tyrant Spares Your Life (Part 2)
chapters.content:
Chapter 628: Brother Tyrant Spares Your Life (Part 2)
It’s not like we have some profound feud, but it feels like I’d recognize him even if he turned to ashes!
Jing Shu felt utterly helpless.
How did I run into this buffoon again?
The tall and skinny Jiang Changke dashed out of the crowd, ceaselessly bragging and introducing her to his university classmates as if they wouldn’t recognize her otherwise.
"See that? The great Jing Shu came by herself! Yes, that’s the great Jing Shu, I guarantee it. She came without even asking Young Master Lan for an invitation. A boss truly is a boss. What do you say now, Young Master Lan? Anything else to add?"
Jiang Changke asked the refined Young Master Lan, who was dressed in a suit.
Young Master Lan adjusted his glasses and politely asked Gold Dominator, "Brother Tyrant, is there anything I can do for you? Are you alright? Do you need a Doctor? Let me handle this matter; I’ll ensure you receive a satisfactory outcome."
Gold Dominator haughtily turned his head away. "I’m fine. No, no need to handle it."
Rub, rub, rub... My fucking toe hurts like hell! I really want to rub it, damn it! But I can’t show I’m in so much pain. I need to find a secluded spot to rub it properly...
The suit-clad Young Master Lan frowned again and asked Jing Shu, "You are Jing Shu, correct? I don’t know how you managed to get in here, but as for hitting someone at this trade fair, we have the authority to ask the organizers to remove you. You must apologize for this incident."
"Right, apologize! How dare she offend Brother Tyrant!"
"Do you even know who my Brother Tyrant is? You’re screwed!"
"Not even the King himself could save you today!"
"Oh, look, that’s Jing Shu. She’s dressed quite nicely; perhaps she’s a golden phoenix after all. Too bad, it seems she’s provoked someone she can’t afford to."
Jing Shu’s finance assistant, Liu, was frowning and about to call for backup, but Jing Shu stopped him with a shake of her head, signaling him to remain calm and not act rashly.
Among the crowd, some remained silent, merely clenching their fists with their heads bowed. Sweet dumpling and Liu Xia stood near Young Master Lan, too afraid to speak, but inwardly, they felt a little pleased, hoping Jing Shu would be taken down.
Jing Shu took a look around. Young Master Lan really was something else, getting almost all their university classmates to work here as waitstaff. And those in plain clothes must have been using the extra entry quotas.
So, having a bigger crowd and a louder voice makes you right?
The manager in charge also arrived. Seeing that Gold Dominator was involved, he immediately scurried over to inquire about the situation.
Gold Dominator looked thoroughly impatient. He wanted them all to clear out; they were keeping him from rubbing his foot.
"What, Gold Dominator, you want me to apologize?" Jing Shu wasn’t known for her good temper either. She dropped the playful demeanor, her brow furrowing slightly as she pressed forward step by step. Her aura immediately suppressed everyone present. Publicly, Jing Shu wouldn’t cause Jin Tianci to lose face, but privately... she’d ensure Gold Dominator suffered in silence, unable to even lodge a complaint.
"Disperse, disperse! This matter ends here!" Gold Dominator shouted, exasperated, then immediately turned and limped away towards the restroom.
With the main party involved no longer pursuing the matter, the people around him immediately followed, leaving behind a crowd that had been eagerly waiting to watch a good show.
Young Master Lan was a bit puzzled. He glanced at Jing Shu.
This person dared to address Gold Dominator by his full name, and Gold Dominator wasn’t even angry? This doesn’t make sense.
The manager in charge also let out a sigh of relief. "What’s with Little Overlord today? He used to cause trouble every day. He truly is a Devil."
"If it weren’t for Brother Tyrant sparing your life, you’d be dead today."
"Let’s go, let’s go."
"Consider yourself lucky."
Jing Shu snickered.
Yes, lucky for Gold Dominator he ran off quickly.
The crowd dispersed quickly. Some felt regret, others pity, but as the Celebrities Gathering was about to begin, everyone’s attention was once again captivated.
"I’ll serve the big shot, shall I? Boss, whatever you need, just say the word. Boss, where are you sitting? What’s your seat?" Jiang Changke followed eagerly.
Jing Shu, nursing a throbbing headache, ignored him and took another look around before finally finding her own seat.
Jing Shu’s spot was known as the "privileged seating" area—the best in the house, not even in the same section as Li Yuetian. This meant it was very close to the display stage, allowing for a much clearer view of the items up for auction. This was important since this wasn’t the Imperial Capital; there were no 3D virtual screens, and even the lighting was subpar.
The key was that there weren’t many people, and the area was divided into four small sections, each with its own screen, making it quite private. It was akin to having a front-row box, with each box seating around thirty people.
Just as Jing Shu settled into her chilly chair, the door curtain was flung open. Gold Dominator, gingerly rubbing his chest and then his rear end, limped in with a large group in tow.
Both parties looked up, equally surprised.
"You’re in the wrong place, aren’t you?" Jing Shu asked.
"I’m not! This is the spot my dad arranged," Gold Dominator replied subconsciously. After speaking, he grew angry again, then quickly realized that if his dad had arranged it, then it must be correct; it was very likely he had arranged for Jing Shu to be here as well.
Upon hearing this, everyone’s eyes lit up.
"He must be one of the authorities, right?"
"Looks like it. Although this isn’t an auction run by the Township Government, all earnings here still go to them, I’ve heard. They say the assets are either from those who have committed crimes or are bankrupt and liquidating."
"Brother Tyrant is incredible, booking such a large space in such a prestigious place! We definitely came to the right event."
Young Master Lan asked, "So she’s the one in the wrong? Manager, could you come over here, please? And waitstaff, waitstaff!"
Annoyed, Gold Dominator waved his hand dismissively. "Forget it, forget it, she’s not in the wrong. Let’s get on with it; I still have tasks to attend to."
If I had known, I would have let my Little Uncle come. I really shouldn’t have taken on this crappy task.
Jing Shu and Liu, without a doubt, chose the best seats in the center of the front row. Gold Dominator sat nearby, while Young Master Lan and Gold Dominator’s Gou Tuizi took the second row. The remaining quota spots were filled by others further back.
This place didn’t provide food or water; it was quite bare-bones. The chairs were all ice-cold.
The attentive Liu, having already wiped the chairs clean, had laid down blankets and set up an extra chair for Jing Shu as a small table, covering it with a pink and white tablecloth. He then took out a thermos, poured Jing Shu a cup of coffee, and added two large pieces of crystal sugar.
He also presented four small plates laden with banana chips, dried fish, peanuts, sunflower seeds, and cherry tomatoes, among other things.
"Have a little something to tide you over," Liu said, then stood to the side holding his briefcase, like a bodyguard.
Forget the onlookers in the background, who were gaping, muttering, "Holy shit! Holy shit!" and swallowing audibly; even Jing Shu was astounded by this scene.
It’s the freaking apocalypse, and he’s bringing all these snacks just to observe the event? Does he think this is a theater show?
This Liu... he’s really getting the hang of things. Bringing his own food for the boss like this?
Jing Shu swore she hadn’t brought any of these items herself.

chapters.title: Chapter 629: Auctioning the Jinhua Sow
chapters.content:
Chapter 629: Auctioning the Jinhua Sow
Jing Shu took another look at Liu. He handled finances and was a young man in his twenties, looking gentle and quiet. From the way he was ready to make a phone call the moment he was scolded, it was evident that this young man had his own opinions.
"Promising," Jing Shu commented nonchalantly as she sipped her coffee, then lightly furrowed her brows. This was the Nestle coffee that used to cost one coin a packet, a bit astringent in taste.
To be honest, it couldn’t compare to the top-notch coffee she had brought from the United States, but to find coffee at all these days was a rarity. Since things had become so exaggerated, Jing Shu didn’t want to force her taste buds, so she silently took out a packet of milk and squeezed it into her coffee. With milk added, the flavor became much richer and aromatic.
Liu silently gave Jing Shu a thumbs-up.
Look at that, truly fitting for a factory manager—awesome,
he thought, impressed.
"Holy shit."
"Awesome."
"Such class."
"Quick, give Xiu’er a throne."
Gold Dominator complained unhappily, "Young Master Lan, how are you handling things? Didn’t you say I’d be enjoying myself comfortably today?"
In comparison, my own prestige is completely gone! Look at her—sitting on a chair with a blanket, a table with a tablecloth, legs crossed while eating snacks, and even a bodyguard standing by!
Then look at me, completely outdone in display. Damn it, that’s already two losses today!
Young Master Lan nodded rather awkwardly. "I’ll arrange it right now."
Damn it... what is there to eat in this dump? The Celebrities Gathering is so poor they’re practically losing their pants; otherwise, I wouldn’t have tricked my college classmate into working as unpaid hired labor,
he thought.
Gold Dominator grumbled with extreme dissatisfaction, but the Celebrities Gathering had already begun.
"Ladies and gentlemen, good afternoon. I am Xiao Shuai, your host for today’s Celebrities Gathering. No more nonsense; since we’re all familiar faces here, let’s get straight to business," said a host clad in a big black cotton-padded jacket, covered in mud, clearly not one for formalities. This, of course, was because the organizers were extremely poor and had a limited budget.
Xiao Shuai tapped the microphone.
He had to hurry; who knew if the battery would even last until he finished hosting?
He sped up his speech: "Alright, I know what everyone’s been waiting for! The first item up for auction today is the incredibly awesome and nearly extinct Jinhua Sow! Bring in the sow!"
"Buy a sow now, and get a boar for free. Struggle to find quality ’Seeds’? Prices too high? Being controlled by others? Now, you don’t need any of that. All the hassle you’d face for breeding will be taken care of, as we provide services directly to your doorstep.
Take home a sow and a boar, and next year, they’ll produce piglets. The year after, the piglets will have their own litter, with piglets galore!"
As Xiao Shuai spoke passionately, waiters huffed and puffed as they brought in two pigs. They were not large and rather lean, but clean.
It wasn’t that they didn’t want to raise them fatter; having pigs meant needing feed. This was the reality of the apocalypse, much like the situation with the geese at the Imperial Capital Grain and Oil Bureau. Good things were available, but everything was affected by this apocalyptic environment. I even suspect there might be some unknown gases or elements in the air harming all living creatures,
Jing Shu mused.
Gasps of amazement rose from the audience. In these times, pigs weren’t just pigs; they were two Ferraris or Maseratis on the hoof. No, they were two gold mines capable of Qian Shengqian.
"Alright, the auction for the nearly extinct Jinhua Sow begins. We do not accept Virtual Coin and will not tolerate fraudulent bidding. We have personnel from the Township Government present to check your assets. If you engage in sham bidding, your property will be confiscated. So think carefully before you bid.
To reiterate, this Celebrities Gathering is of a special nature; we only accept commodities or other materials of equivalent value. In the case of items of similar value, we reserve the right to decide which party’s goods to accept.
Alright, the sow is valued at goods equivalent to 10,000 Virtual Coins! The auction starts now!"
When Virtual Coins can’t buy anything, how terrifying would that scenario be?
Someone bid quickly; these pigs had too much investment potential, it seemed impossible to make a loss on them.
"Fabrics valued at 20,000 Virtual Coins!"
"Petroleum valued at 25,000 Virtual Coins!"
"Right, to save time and prevent malicious bidding and disruptions, each person can bid a maximum of three times per auction item. Everyone should think carefully before bidding. Each item also has a tracking code. If you’re bidding for someone else and later transfer ownership, a 2% handling fee is required." Xiao Shuai rolled his eyes, emotionlessly reciting the rules.
These shameless, money-crazed organizers!
he cursed in his heart.
Put simply, this meant: don’t mess around bidding in small increments. Be quick and bid in multiples, raising the stakes substantially. If you had connections, you could have someone bid for you; just pay a handling fee afterward.
The entire hall fell silent for a few seconds. No one raised the bid. Then, after several more seconds, someone finally called out:
"Food valued at 200,000 Virtual Coins!"
"Goods valued at 400,000 Virtual Coins!"
The hall began to buzz again. Such high prices instantly dashed the hopes of 99% of the people for the Jinhua Sow.
Are we really here expecting to find a bargain?
many wondered.
These items are truly excellent, though!
This caused the group of classmates behind Jing Shu to exclaim in shock.
What did goods worth several hundred thousand Virtual Coins even represent?
Currently, an entire house cost only several thousand to tens of thousands of Virtual Coins. These classmates’ families weren’t poor; in the apocalypse, they had all managed to secure single-occupancy houses, but that was about the extent of it. Even those with high salaries earned only a few hundred Virtual Coins a month.
"Goods worth 700,000!"
The bidding calls grew quieter. It wasn’t that these people didn’t have money; the wealthy had plenty of Virtual Coins, all ’forcibly’ exchanged by the Township Government at that time. But now, the thought of exchanging so many actual goods felt a bit painful.
No one bid on the Jinhua Sow anymore, and just as Xiao Shuai was about to finalize the deal, Gold Dominator called out, "Goods worth 1,000,000!"
At this call, the entire venue erupted again.
A breeding pair exchanged for goods valued at 1,000,000! How many truckloads would that take? Is it worth it? Not at all! Even if the sow has piglets, and those piglets have more piglets, it wouldn’t be worth this much! Ordinary pigs aren’t this expensive!
After calling several more times and receiving no further bids, the host, Xiao Shuai, announced, "Sold for goods worth 1,000,000! Please proceed with the on-site transaction. Our professionals will now come for the handover. Everyone, please wait a moment. If the payment isn’t genuine, we’ll have to re-auction the item."
"Wow, Brother Tyrant is so amazing."
"A million from Brother Tyrant! He bought it just like that—so badass."
"Did I hear right? Did Brother Tyrant really spend a million on a pair of pigs?"
Professionals arrived promptly for the inspection. Two servers also came, leading the two pigs. These servers were college classmates, and they seemed very excited, exchanging winks and glances.

chapters.title: Chapter 630: Please Start Your Performance
chapters.content:
Chapter 630: Please Start Your Performance
After all, these were two living pigs. How long had it been since anyone had seen a live pig? Now, pigs were limited editions, and getting to see one was considered an eye-opener.
Professional staff quickly inspected the goods and, after confirming everything was in order, they branded the two pigs with traceability codes and numbers. The pigs were officially owned by Gold Dominator.
"Brother Tyrant, your old man is the boss of Wu City. To put it bluntly, isn’t Wu City practically yours? You can have whatever you want. Why even bother bidding for pigs at an auction?"
Couldn’t you just intercept them outright?
"Yeah, yeah."
Gold Dominator snorted disdainfully. "My home is my home, Wu City is Wu City. Do you think I am an Emperor?" But regardless, having regained the upper hand, Gold Dominator looked somewhat smugly at Jing Shu, who had sat through the auction calm and collected.
Did she see how I threw around a fortune so effortlessly? Wasn’t I suave?
Staff members and Gold Dominator’s men went outside to transfer the goods, leaving behind the two pigs that were rooting around and squealing in their cages. Attentive waiters periodically fed them with the feed in their hands. At this moment, everyone’s gaze in the private room was drawn to the pigs.
"Brother Tyrant, can I touch them?"
"Brother Tyrant, can I take a photo with the Jinhua Sow?"
Gold Dominator waved his hand, looking even more smug. "Easy there, these pigs are rather finicky."
With that, everyone cheered and turned their focus to the two pigs.
The Celebrities Gathering continued with the auction.
The host, Xiao Shuai, cleared his throat. "Alright, the highlight of the evening has arrived! Have you seen the three mobile homes on display? These are the mobile homes we’re going to auction next!
"They were built by Wu City’s largest real estate company, Greenland Company. They are fully furnished and ready to move in. Firstly, the quality is guaranteed, as the materials have been professionally certified by the Township Government as the best available. Greenland Company can’t pay back what it owes to the Township Government, so they’re using these homes to settle the debt.
"The functionalities of mobile homes need no further explanation, right? The promotional posters had outlined them quite clearly. Nowadays, disasters are frequent, and no one knows what the next one will be. Over the years, countless people have lost their homes due to disasters, so owning such a mobile home would be preparing for the unknown.
"Now, ten mobile homes are up for auction, and the Township Government is only accepting food-related goods. Other items are ineligible for bidding. Alright, the starting bid is 300,000 Virtual Coins in food-related goods. Let the auction begin!"
Swapping houses for food would have seemed insane before the apocalypse, but that was the current reality. The Wu City Township Government had even started to rack their brains to gather food from all around.
It’s hard to imagine that circumstances will only get worse next year. But now that Jing Shu is here, and she has quietly done so much, maybe it won’t end like before, with many people starving to death.
Many in the audience felt a silent regret. Mobile homes were nice, but firstly, the houses they already had were good enough, and they didn’t need to exchange so much extra food for a mobile home, especially when food was really scarce.
Secondly, by requiring payment only in food goods, the Township Government had effectively eliminated many people who only had other types of assets. This was frustrating for those holding non-food items, but there was no way around it. Now, food was the hard currency, even more precious than gold.
So, anyone who could still use food to bid on mobile homes was definitely wealthy.
Indeed, it turned out there were quite a few wealthy folks in Wu City. Before long, the ten homes were auctioned off for 500,000 each. Compared to the Jinhua Sows, the homes also showed great potential. Just the mobility aspect alone was significant. Being able to move the house in the face of danger was an enormous safeguard that could provide a strong sense of security.
Even those playing with pigs in the private room shifted their attention to the ongoing bidding, exclaiming in wonder. Thanks to their proximity to the display stage, everyone could clearly see the interior of the homes when the host, Xiao Shuai, opened them up for viewing.
The luxurious decor and exquisite interior design made it seem like they were entering a mansion. If one had such a luxurious mobile home in these apocalyptic times, they would want for nothing more.
Host Xiao Shuai read from his script bit by bit, but the crowd of bumpkins listened with stars in their eyes, their faces full of longing and envy as the prices rose systematically.
"Brother Tyrant, aren’t you considering getting a mobile home?"
"Yeah, Brother Tyrant, it looks so great. No matter the disaster, with a mobile home, you can go wherever you want."
Gold Dominator hummed disdainfully.
His father hadn’t given him the authority, so how could he dare to bid on these?
Irritated, he said, "Hasn’t Young Master Lan arrived yet? Is it that hard to get something to eat?"
The atmosphere immediately turned cold, and nobody dared to speak again.
Liu took out his calculator and began tapping away, reporting in a soft voice, "Boss, based on the anticipated final transaction price and the goods we brought, buying five homes shouldn’t be a problem. However, some units have already been claimed by others, and a few more are reserved by insiders. So, I suggest we just go for three."
Jing Shu raised an eyebrow, just about to say something, when Liu continued, "Boss, I’ll start the bidding for you. After I’ve made three bids, you can jump in to finish it off."
How thoughtful, he’d even considered that.
Liu’s voice was soft, but as the private room was eerily quiet, his words were overheard.
"Tsk, tsk, tsk, thinking of buying five mobile homes? Who do you think you are, puffing yourself up with such big talk."
"I couldn’t bear listening to such wild claims any longer. I almost couldn’t hold myself back."
"They wouldn’t even dare to make this up in movies—what an exaggeration..."
These hushed whispers could be heard, suggesting that mentioning wanting one mobile home might have been believable, but claiming to want all of them was just showing off.
Right then, the price for three of the mobile homes skyrocketed to 1,000,000 each, a full 500,000 higher than the other villas.
Someone had made a move!
Two more homes were quickly bid up to 1,000,000 as well, and in the blink of an eye, only five lower-priced homes remained.
Jing Shu could no longer be bothered with the group of youngsters behind her, her attention caught by a familiar-looking bidder—it was the housekeeper from Qian Duoduo’s family.
The person who grabbed two homes also looked familiar: a meticulous man in his seventies, known to be Su Malie’s compulsive housekeeper.
Well, these were the truly formidable ones.
Jing Shu waved her hand and said, "Liu, start now. No need to wait."
Let the show begin.
The group behind her nearly covered their mouths, struggling to hold back laughter, curious to see what was meant by ’start.’

chapters.title: Chapter 631: Three Villas, I’ll Take Them
chapters.content:
Chapter 631: Three Villas, I’ll Take Them
Was it time to start showing off, or would it end in a slap to the face? Truth be told, they were all quite eager to see what would happen.
"Hahaha, come on, let’s get this started. I can hardly wait," someone laughed.
"We can also shout out a few bids, right? After all, someone will raise the starting price."
"Hmph, do you know there are specialized bid recording staff outside? If these people whimsically decide to inspect your worth afterward and find out you were bidding wildly, the consequences would be severe." Just at that moment, Young Master Lan arrived, carrying a huge platter of food. Heaven knows he had swallowed his pride and begged high and low to buy this at a steep price last minute. But to cling onto Gold Dominator’s powerful coattails, any expense was worth it.
Murmurs of surprise filled the air. It seemed things were quite strict after all.
"That’s still a matter of chance; they can’t possibly check everyone, haha." Jiang Changke carefreely sang a different tune from everyone else.
The crowd had already lost interest in Jiang Changke because Liu had already raised a placard and called out, "Three villas, each for 800,000 Virtual Coins."
The voice wasn’t loud, but it was steady, as if he were discussing something trivial, yet it truly dropped the jaws of the group behind him.
"Holy shit, this guy really dares to bid! Badass! Just for that swagger, I give him 99 points."
"Isn’t he afraid of being checked? Even if he’s Jing Shu’s bodyguard, he shouldn’t own that much property."
Young Master Lan adjusted his glasses. "If someone guarantees the bid, then it’s possible to auction."
"The question is, does Jing Shu really have that much money?"
"Yeah," someone interjected.
Gold Dominator nonchalantly munched on the food Young Master Lan brought and held back his criticism of Jing Shu.
That woman was richer than anyone; he was envious just looking at the resources she had last time. So much time has passed, who knows how much she has stockpiled? But he couldn’t admit defeat; he was determined to be just a bit more formidable than her.
Paying 800,000 Virtual Coins for a villa was clearly unrealistic. The price for the ten villas rapidly rose to around 1.1 million Virtual Coins before slowly coming down.
Liu also bid precisely every time, raising the price by 100,000 Virtual Coins, pushing it right up to 1.1 million Virtual Coins, just a bit less than the price of the other villas.
"Number 567, three villas, each for 1.2 million Virtual Coins!" Jing Shu conveniently added the final bid, successfully pushing it to that point, making it a losing deal for anyone else to raise the bid.
Even Jing Shu had to admire Liu’s precise calculation ability.
Although she didn’t need Liu and could call out a high bid at the end by herself, having someone to cover for her from the start was convenient and also saved a lot of Virtual Coins.
The classmates behind them slowly gaped in disbelief.
Was this... for real? They really bid 1.2 million Virtual Coins for a villa and instantly went for three? What for? Even if they had the money, wouldn’t one be enough?
Young Master Lan furrowed his brows, growing more and more baffled.
Some things seemed to go beyond his comprehension.
"If I may be so bold to ask..." Young Master Lan’s demeanor softened considerably, missing the previously hidden smugness and sense of superiority.
Liu stood erect and said indifferently, "Since you know it’s presumptuous, then don’t ask."
Young Master Lan: "....."
Everyone: "...."
Damn, what an awesome attitude.
Someone quickly sent this sacred moment to the university group chat and started live updating: "Jing Shu has already called for three villas."...
Gold Dominator covered his mouth, trying not to laugh.
After all, Young Master Lan was one of his associates, but for some reason, Gold Dominator found it immensely satisfying to see someone struggle under that woman’s control...
"Sold!" With Xiao Shuai, the auctioneer’s final strike of the hammer, the ten villas were ultimately sold for an average price of 1.2 million Virtual Coins each, though there were slight differences in price, of course.
"Now, please wait a few minutes to let the parties finalize their transaction. After all, this is not a small sum. But these villas are really a bargain because the Greenland Company will also provide two free moving services. Later, you will just need to provide an address."
Liu started punching numbers into the calculator rapidly, while Jing Shu sipped her coffee boredly, waiting for the staff to come and settle the accounts. The atmosphere quieted down behind her.
It seemed some were still in disbelief, but others had already begun to spread the story of the event through their phones.
Gold Dominator had already disrupted their understanding by purchasing two pigs for 1 million Virtual Coins, but now, Jing Shu was about to buy three villas with 3.6 million Virtual Coins?
Money shouldn’t be spent like this, right?
Most critically, this time, it wasn’t Virtual Coins being spent, but food supplies!
"I told you the boss was awesome, but you didn’t believe me. How rich do you think the vice president of the Medicine Association must be? Do you know how expensive medicines are these days? How could they not have money? If you ask me, it’s already too late to cozy up to them now, haha. Lucky I started early," boasted Jiang Changke, about to ramble on when Jing Shu silenced him with a glare.
While waiting, the auctioneer Xiao Shuai regretfully announced, "Now, a villa that failed to sell for 1.18 million Virtual Coins will be disposed of to the last bidder. After verification, Mr. Li’s food supplies were insufficient, and the case has been handed over to the Township Government for serious handling..."
This was just a minor incident, yet it sparked excitement among some college classmates in the background. "Do you think Jing Shu’s food won’t be enough either? After all, food worth 3.6 million Virtual Coins – how much would that be?"
"Who knows," they speculated.
"It might be medicinal herbs, you know. Medicinal herbs are so expensive – just a few ginseng roots would cost a fortune."
"That’s got to be the result of corruption."
Liu cleared his throat. "Who just said that? Say it again so I can record it, and then we can proceed with legal action right away."
Subsequently, even the whispering ceased. Jing Shu shook her head with a smile.
Some things she didn’t care much about, for the gap in their statuses was as vast as that between an eagle and an ant. However, having someone who cared about her was quite nice.
Finally, it was Jing Shu’s turn.
SWOOSH. The door opened, and more than a dozen staff members walked in. To expedite the process, each had their specific task. These people, uniformly expressionless, began in a businesslike tone, "Jing Shu, please scan your face to confirm your identity and prepare the supplies. Our team will need to tally them."
This was quite a show of force; the people in the entire private room dared not speak, except for the two pigs that kept GRUNTING.
Then someone murmured from behind, "Brother Tyrant is really something after all. The staff who just came in were so courteous to him, smiling so widely it crinkled their faces."
BEEP...
The lead staff member’s expression suddenly changed, and he froze.
The atmosphere in the private room tensed once again.
What was happening now?
"Could it be... that they’ve been caught making things up randomly?"
The next second, the lead staff member smiled again, his happiness as clear as the creases of a blooming chrysanthemum. "Hello, hello, your records show approval, but we don’t actually know what kind of food supplies you’re trading?"
Such a high level of authority is terrifying – they can’t see anything! So this is a true big shot!

chapters.title: Chapter 632: Even If You Beg, My Boss Won’t Care
chapters.content:
Chapter 632: Even If You Beg, My Boss Won’t Care
What... what’s happening? Can this worker change faces? One second he was so serious, and now it’s like he’s changed into a completely different person without any warning!
Liu gave a slight, formal cough and stepped forward like a bodyguard, saying, "The red worm cakes, worth 3.6 million Virtual Coins, are in the parking lot outside. Our people are already waiting there to coordinate. Please hurry; after all, this is a big project."
Insect Cakes aren’t valuable individually, so there’s a large quantity of them.
"Okay, okay, I’ll call someone to handle the collection right now. You all rest here for a bit. Wang Hong! Tell them not to be so strict. Just do a rough count; we’re in a hurry here. Besides, these large quantities of Insect Cakes are exactly what we need right now. Miss Jing, you’re truly too kind! You’ve just solved our most pressing problem. If you have more Insect Cakes, would you be able to sell us some more?"
Not only was the worker enthusiastic, but he was overdoing it, even showing hints of fawning. This absolutely stunned Jing Shu’s university classmates behind her.
Jing Shu herself was surprised. She repaid her debt to the Township Government with Insect Cakes every month. She asked, "I thought we had a partnership with the Township Government?"
The worker gave an embarrassed smile. "We’re part of Administration, Enforcement, and Logistics. Your partnership is likely directly with the higher-ups. We’re in different departments. Although the higher-ups allocate some supplies to us, it’s becoming difficult to distribute food to our staff these days."
"So this transaction, is it for your department’s benefit, or...?" Jing Shu asked again.
The worker replied honestly, "As long as we pay off the original debts from bankruptcies and business closures, the rest of the profit belongs entirely to our department. The higher-ups only want the previous debts settled; no matter how much is left over, it’s all ours."
Jing Shu nodded in understanding. "Liu, see how many red earthworms are left."
After a flurry of keystrokes on his device, Liu said, "Boss, there’s still over 2 million Virtual Coins worth of stock, which converts to roughly two hundred tons of red worm cake."
Tons and tons? Damn, in the apocalypse, they’re still measuring food by the ton...
The group behind her seemed dumbfounded. Although they usually didn’t eat this kind of basic food, they knew that one Insect Cake cost 1.5 Virtual Coins, making it very cheap.
But several hundred tons... Is this terrifying number actually real?
Now, everyone looked at Jing Shu in a new light. Young Master Lan’s body seemed to stiffen for a moment; he lowered his head, his expression dark as he pondered something.
"Several hundred tons of red worm cake... how much is that?"
"Isn’t Jing Shu from the Medicine Association? How did she get into the Insect Cake business?"
"Yeah, don’t tell me she’s monopolized all the Insect Cakes in Wu City?"
While these classmates were still reeling from the shock, the worker on the other side was blinking, gazing at Jing Shu with star-struck eyes.
She truly lives up to her reputation as a big shot!
If it were rice, he would have been lamenting his inability to afford it. But this kind of cheap, filling food was truly scarce and desperately needed right now.
Jing Shu nodded. "Regarding these additional cakes: if my total spending here today is high enough to cover their value, you can count the revenue from them as your department’s profit. If my spending doesn’t cover their value, I’ll sell the remainder to you at the standard Virtual Coin price."
In any case, she wasn’t planning on taking any of the Insect Cakes she brought today back with her.
"Really? That’s wonderful! Thank you, thank you so much! Wang Hong, hurry and get those bastards ready to unload! Have they finished counting? Good, I understand. Miss Jing, your initial transaction is complete on our end. We’ll report it right away... Oh, right, my name is Wang Miao. If Miss Jing ever needs help with administration or logistics in the future, please feel free to call on me anytime... You lot, so clueless! Hurry up and get a stove heated for Miss Jing!"
In the blink of an eye, a few more people rushed in, carrying a small stove. They placed it near Jing Shu’s feet and added some coal.
"Miss Jing, please rest for now. They’ve finished the inventory over there. Later, just give Wang Hong the villa’s address; he’ll be in charge of transporting your items there. If you have any other needs, feel free to ask Wang Hong. I’ve assigned him to assist you. Now, I’ll go handle the relevant paperwork for you."
Wang Miao left, but a man specifically assigned to serve Jing Shu remained.
The crowd was left staring agape. People could operate like this? This was just too slick!
Now, Jing Shu was even better equipped: a small stove, tea and snacks, and a comfortable chair. The only thing missing was someone to give her a massage.
"Boss! Boss, you’ve really been keeping a low profile! I never imagined that the economical and affordable red worm cakes I eat every day are from your business! Boss, seeing as we’re classmates, could you give us a bit of a discount? Food’s been tight at home lately, and I’d like to buy some Insect Cakes wholesale," Jiang Changke piped up excitedly, stepping forward.
