"Bah! Jiang Changke, what shady business haven’t you been up to these past few years? You expect us to believe you eat Insect Cakes? I bet you just want to resell them! Shameless! Sucking up to anyone with an advantage. You’re mad for money!"
"Yeah, Jiang Changke! Pay back your debts!"
Jiang Changke waved his hand dismissively. "Get lost, all of you! I’m talking to the Boss. What’s it got to do with any of you? You didn’t recognize the situation sooner, and now it’s too late for you to even try sucking up!"
At this moment, Young Master Lan stood up and cleared his throat lightly. "Jing Shu, so you’re the one behind the red worm cakes, eh? That’s quite impressive. It seems we’ve misjudged you all along. I would like to formally apologize to you now. Due to my oversight these past few days, you’ve been subjected to some unfair treatment. I am truly sorry for that, really, and I hope you can forgive me. I will also explain this matter in the group chat. Furthermore, as compensation, I’d like to give your family 500 units of electricity. From now on, if you need anything, I’ll do my best to make it happen."
"Wow, Young Master Lan is so generous!"
"Electricity is so expensive these days. Half an hour a day isn’t even enough time to charge our devices."
Jing Shu closed her eyes to rest.
She was somewhat surprised; these people were much more yielding than she had imagined. Still, it was understandable. If she dealt in something other than Insect Cakes, Young Master Lan probably wouldn’t have humbled himself like this. It was precisely because she controlled a large supply of this cheap food that he was likely hoping to acquire some from her at a very low price. After all, even the Township Government was struggling to feed its people, let alone how he could sustain his power grid.
Liu stepped forward, blocking Young Master Lan’s view, and said firmly, "Your apology comes too late. It might have meant something if you had apologized when we first faced that injustice earlier today. Our Boss does not accept your apology. Please return to your seat and do not disturb our Boss while she rests. And don’t get any ideas about our business. The red worm cake operation has a fixed contract with the Township Government; it’s not open to external parties right now. So, even if you beg our Boss, it will be useless."
These few sentences cut off all his avenues, shattering Young Master Lan’s plan to apologize, offer some gifts, and then secure some food in return.
Insect Cakes were so cheap, whereas rice was far too expensive and completely unsuitable for distributing as wages.
In all his years, Young Master Lan had never been humiliated like this, let alone by a university classmate’s lackey.
For a moment, Young Master Lan’s face turned livid, veins bulging on his temples. "You... you’re not Jing Shu! Since when do you have the right to speak?"

chapters.title: Chapter 633: Someone Coming to Rob Us?
chapters.content:
Chapter 633: Someone Coming to Rob Us?
At that moment, Jing Shu spoke with half-closed eyes, her words imbued with nonchalance, "What Liu said is exactly what I wanted to say."
The atmosphere in the private room grew colder once again. No one had expected Jing Shu to be so dismissive and domineering. She didn’t even seem to consider Young Master Lan. In their eyes, he was the campus big brother—a person of wealth, status, and power, who now controlled the coveted electricity network.
That was old Niu at his peak of power; but where did Jing Shu get the resources to stand up to Young Master Lan?
In the past few years, Young Master Lan had even become the proverbial breadwinner, the boss, the big brother for many people.
"Young Master Lan has humbled himself to seek peace, Jing Shu, why are you still acting like this?"
"Yeah, really, what’s all this about? It’s just a bunch of insects; is it necessary to be so impressively intense?"
"Exactly, you really think too highly of yourself. Who in Wu City doesn’t need electricity? Who doesn’t end up asking Young Master Lan for help?"
Young Master Lan’s face grew even darker, turning a shade of purple as he clenched his fist and pointed at Jing Shu, nodding angrily, "Fine, fine, Jing Shu! You just wait!" But he didn’t dare to utter harsher words, because, after all... they were really in desperate need of food right now!
Jing Shu remained languid, clearly not taking Young Master Lan seriously, not even bothering to shift her position or change her posture.
Gold Dominator watched the drama unfold with glee, munching on the food from the tray in his hand. In the end, he shook his head in disdain, as if he was just making do with the meal. He was actually hoping for a fight to break out between the two.
As the tension between both sides escalated, the atmosphere one of drawn swords and aimed crossbows, the door suddenly burst open.
A chubby man rushed in frantically, shouting, "Daddy, Daddy, quick, we have to get out of here, follow me!"
Gold Dominator, who had been enjoying the show, frowned. "Uncle, what’s all the panic about? What happened? Is it a robbery or something?" As he spoke, Gold Dominator grew excited.
It’s been years since the apocalypse; could there still be such brazen acts? We’ve put on such a big show this time, and of course, we’ve taken precautions. There are plenty of armed forces hidden away. If anyone is foolish enough to try something, then there’ll be quite a spectacle!
As if to confirm the uncle’s words, the entire New World Building trembled slightly, and a rolling rumble could be heard from outside.
Uneasy murmurs filled the hall, and even the auction was temporarily halted. Xiao Shuai, the host, told everyone to stay calm and remain in place without panicking. He then activated the alarm and reassured everyone with a steady voice, "Don’t be afraid. No matter what we encounter, there are powerful armed forces outside... Our job is not to add to the chaos... blah blah blah..."
Jun Jia, sweating bullets, urged, "My ancestors, don’t add to the chaos, just come with me, hurry!"
It would be too late if they didn’t leave now!
The surroundings grew quiet as everyone seemed to realize the gravity of the situation.
If even a figure like Gold Dominator is about to ’seek refuge,’ this probably isn’t a good sign!
Gold Dominator was completely unconcerned.
What kind of violent storm haven’t I seen? There’s even a military unit from the Township Government here today, my father’s men. What’s there to be afraid of?
"Let’s go, let’s go! Oh right, what about the people I brought? Should they come along too?" Gold Dominator didn’t forget to look out for his underlings before leaving. This made Young Master Lan, whose face was an iron-blue, feel a bit better, though he also started to feel nervous.
Could this really be a once-in-a-century robbery? If so, it would be safer to follow Gold Dominator.
Jun Jia tugged on Gold Dominator, heading towards the exit. "These friends of yours will have to wait for the next trip. There are only a few spots available now. I’ve arranged for Xiao Zhang and the others to look after your friends; don’t worry... Oh, Jing Shu, you’re here too? Let’s go, hurry up and follow me..."
Jing Shu furrowed her brow but then nodded. She quickly stood up, picked up the ever-present black case in her hand, and signaled Liu with her eyes to follow. The other man assigned to serve Jing Shu spoke briskly, "I’ll go check on Captain Wang Miao’s situation first."
Jing Shu realized something was amiss. True to her fearful and cautious nature, she had placed several snakes and insects at the entrance and around the area when she arrived, just in case any danger arose.
Although it doesn’t seem like we’ve encountered a ’robbery,’ these creatures are all sending out feelings of unease—intense unease!
Something significant might be about to happen!
Gold Dominator was pulled and dragged away. Even then, he was reluctant, saying, "Let me at least bring someone! Young Master Lan, let Young Master Lan follow me first."
Among all these people, Young Master Lan is the best at saying pleasing things, and he’s comfortable to have around.
"There’s no time, hurry up and go. I’ll have someone look after your friend," Jun Jia said, getting impatient.
Gold Dominator protested, "Why does Jing Shu get to bring someone and I can’t? I want to bring someone too! Young Master Lan, come with me, hurry up! I can’t believe this!"
Young Master Lan scurried after him like a clingy plaster that couldn’t be shaken off, clinging tightly to Gold Dominator.
They left behind a crowd with complicated expressions.
"They’re gone, they’ve all gone... It seems this time the situation isn’t good."
"They actually didn’t take us with them! It’s too infuriating!"
"What exactly happened?"
At this moment, Jiang Changke stepped forward. "We’d better not run around wildly. If something happens later, let’s follow the host Xiao Shuai; I think he’s definitely safe. Besides, we’re so poor, the robbers probably won’t even look twice at us. Women, make yourselves look uglier; men, make yourselves look more pitiful..."
Jiang Changke, like a lone star appearing in the pitch-black night, suddenly offered these classmates a brilliant idea.
Elsewhere, Jun Jia frantically led Jing Shu, Liu, Gold Dominator, and Young Master Lan out of the building.
At this moment, Young Master Lan had a realization.
Does Jing Shu have some connection to Gold Dominator’s family? Otherwise, why would Gold Dominator’s uncle specifically call for her and no one else? Jing Shu’s identity... it’s truly a mystery. What kind of person is she really? I always thought she was just an unremarkable person, not even popular enough to be considered an internet celebrity.
While running, Jing Shu sent out more snakes to find out what was going on, but soon, she understood the situation.
Outside the New World Building, everything was a chaotic mess.
So, it’s not a robbery.
Jing Shu felt somewhat relieved.
Not that I was afraid, but it wouldn’t have been worth it if I had to expose my strength or anything else.
But soon, Jing Shu cursed aloud. If her feelings at that moment had to be described in two words, it would be "Damn it!"
"It’s over, we can’t make it! We’re completely separated! You kid, you were dawdling!" Jun Jia scolded Gold Dominator, who, still looking bewildered, asked, "What’s wrong? What happened that has you so worked up?"
"A mudslide! It’s coming!"

chapters.title: Chapter 634: The Mansion Was Swept Away...
chapters.content:
Chapter 634: The Mansion Was Swept Away...
A massive mudslide approached from all directions, seemingly poised to engulf the area, but that was merely an illusion. The real crisis wasn’t the mudslide—it was just a visual effect.
Jing Shu, who had night vision, could see clearly. The New World Building seemed like a new tectonic plate, having been sliced off and set adrift.
The building was like an isolated island, floating on the sea, moving away from its original location at an incomprehensible speed. The surrounding scenery began to change, becoming unfamiliar.
Jing Shu had survived the apocalypse for ten years. While she was unclear about this specific situation, she roughly knew it must be the ’plate movement’ that had begun in the second year. These movements were possibly random or due to other factors, perhaps involving a mountain or a tract of land. In any case, they disrupted the maps, meaning original locations were no longer where they used to be.
Unfortunately for Jing Shu, the land beneath her feet was one such plate; it had begun to move.
Jun Jia pulled out his phone, cursing aloud, "Reports had come in earlier of massive mudslides approaching, potentially engulfing the New World Building, and we were preparing to evacuate people. But our signals were blocked in this remote area, so we couldn’t broadcast any distress signals. I knew something was wrong. Then cracks began to appear around us... Every exit began to break off bit by bit."
Jing Shu took out her phone, found no signal, and asked, "After the signal was blocked, did anyone go out to call for help?"
"Come on, let’s ask Wang Miao if he sent anyone out." Jun Jia, frustrated, kicked the prepared off-road vehicle and ran with a few others to the other side, shouting, "Wang Miao, what’s the status? Did anyone escape?"
This was Wang Miao, who had just arrived in charge of administrative and logistical management. He said, his voice filled with pain, "It was too late to evacuate. Only three convoys got out, and one of them was engulfed by the mudslide. We couldn’t launch a rescue in time from here. It’s uncertain whether the other two vehicles could escape the mudslide."
Gold Dominator stood with his mouth agape, vehicle headlights illuminating the surroundings. Only then did he clearly see that the area was no longer the suburb it had once been. They seemed to be floating on a ship, the relentless mudslide pushing the building around—this was surreal!
It was more accurate to say the building was like a small boat, propelled by a vast river of mudslides surrounding it.
"All signals are blocked. We just tried the transmitter, and it’s completely useless," Wang Miao said, somewhat despondently. "It’s too late for any distress calls."
Everyone was dumbstruck. Although they had considered everything during the planning, including potential disasters, no one had imagined they would be separated like this, with the entire building adrift on a sea of mudslides. What in the world was happening?
"They wouldn’t dare to make a movie like this," Gold Dominator finally blurted out after a while.
Jun Jia patted Wang Miao on the shoulder. "So many of us are missing; the higher-ups will definitely take it seriously. Just wait for the rescue now. If only we’d had a helicopter then."
If there had been an aircraft, they could at least determine their location and expedite the rescue.
Wang Miao continued to sigh. "The problem now is we can’t be located. I have no idea where we’ve been moved to. There are no landmarks around, and those who escaped to seek help don’t know which direction we’ve drifted... In this situation, searching for us is too difficult."
The whistling wind indicated their rapid speed. Jun Jia frowned. "We must be going dozens of yards per second, right? We can only pray it stops soon." Their constant change of position further complicated the rescue.
At that moment, Li Yuetian arrived with an armed force, panting. "I’ve just sealed off the building. No one will come out, and our men are stationed everywhere.
I’ve also scouted around. There are no dangerous objects. I’ll arrange for the perimeter to be fenced off shortly to prevent anyone from falling if there’s a collapse. Now, let’s agree on a plan and then go inside to explain the situation to everyone."
Young Master Lan quietly breathed a sigh of relief.
As long as it isn’t a robbery... Even though the entire building is being pushed to an unknown location, with Gold Dominator and countless celebrities inside, the higher-ups will definitely make a great effort to rescue us. So, what we need to do now is...
"Just wait for rescue calmly, and reassure the people in the building," Jun Jia declared. "Before that, no casualties or other mishaps are to occur, and no infighting is allowed." In this setting, his administrative rank was the highest. After all, he was part of Wu City’s leadership.
"Yes!"
"Received!"
"Wang Miao, compile a list of all attendees at the Celebrities Gathering and all our personnel. Coordinate with the head of logistics to figure out food and accommodation. Determine what existing supplies can be used and what’s missing. Report back so we can decide on a course of action." Jun Jia, true to the Jun Family name, even if he was a bit of a greedy bastard, still had real skills in managing his subordinates.
Jing Shu frowned throughout the entire ordeal, sensing unease.
This situation... it wasn’t her first rodeo; it was too familiar, too similar.
The situation might not be as straightforward as just waiting for rescue. If this is due to plate movement, it would completely disrupt our geographical understanding. It was like this in the United States and in the mountains as well. It’s highly probable we’re no longer within Wu City’s bounds!
Wang Miao took out his phone and said, "There are a thousand people attending the Celebrities Gathering auction, three hundred in services and security, over a hundred in administrative and logistics, and six hundred in armed forces, totaling two thousand people. But there are also more than two hundred people who have always resided on the upper floors, led by Boss Lu, the original developer of the New World..."
"Because we thought the auction would be over in two hours, other food supplies weren’t prepared. Currently, the food and water supplies are only enough for these two thousand-plus people to last a day or two...
Because just before, all the food supplies and other goods of the Celebrities Gathering attendees in the parking lot were separated from the building. Although Boss Lu might have some food, water is a serious problem! If we are trapped in the building for more than seven days, then..."
In other words, the New World parking lot, designated for storing supplies, was not part of the section that was moved. Only the bare building itself, devoid of anything, was separated and carried away.
"Boss, Finance Director Liu!"
Just then, Wang Miao’s driver excitedly ran over. He said, patting his chest, "I was scared to death just now! The ground split open while I was handing over duties there. Luckily, our trucks were inside. Otherwise, we wouldn’t have seen you."
Liu’s eyes lit up. He nodded, quietly pulling the driver aside and asked some further questions.
This means my trucks of red worm cakes are still here!

chapters.title: Chapter 635: Trapped in the Building
chapters.content:
Chapter 635: Trapped in the Building
However, no one seemed in the mood to care about Jing Shu’s truck driver at the moment. Hunger wouldn’t kill anyone immediately, but life couldn’t last long without water.
"We can’t just die of thirst waiting for rescue that might never come; we must make preparations in advance!" Jun Jia might not have known much, but he believed in collective effort—that many minds working together could surely devise a solution. "Wang Miao," he instructed, "we must be ready with at least other sources of food and water! Right, let’s quickly return to the auction and start a crowdfunding effort to secure a water supply."
Li Yuetian interjected, "Wait! As for the water source, we can simply filter it. Let’s send a group to dig through the mudflow, find some stones, activated carbon, sand, and so on. We can dig several pits and set up a makeshift filter. The method is crude, and the muddy water will be hard to swallow, but with many hands on the task, we surely won’t die of thirst. Right now, we are overlooking one point: we don’t have much fuel left. The temperature is dropping to minus thirty degrees, and it gets even colder at night. We must boil water before drinking it. Without enough blankets and such, it’s very easy for people to get sick..."
Jun Jia nodded. "Wang Miao, I’ll leave these matters for you to figure out. Start with the logistics director. Take stock of how long each supply will last and how many usable supplies we have right now, including the public and private goods from this Celebrities Gathering. Then, find whatever else we can use and report back to us.
Captain Li, you go and rally all the armed forces. Give this your utmost attention, issue weapons, and ensure our people are stationed everywhere, patrolling 24 hours a day without any slack. Keep a close eye on Boss Lu and some individuals from the Celebrities Gathering to prevent them from causing trouble.
I’ll lead a team to seal off the auction house and inform them of the situation. We can figure out what to do next after that!"
Young Master Lan said with envy, "Brother Tyrant, your uncle is really impressive."
Gold Dominator hummed proudly, "My dad is even more impressive. Everyone in our family is impressive."
Jing Shu weighed the black case in her hand. Thankfully, she had the habit of carrying it whenever she left the house—firstly, as a cover for her, and secondly, given her cautious and timid nature, she always went out fully armed. The black case contained weapons and various foods, so taking them out later wouldn’t seem abrupt. Of course, the contents of her personal space were all-encompassing. She had everything she could need, so Jing Shu wasn’t troubled about food, clothing, drink, or even various other necessities.
What she worried about was when she could return home.
Jun Jia led his people quickly back to the auction house. Jing Shu quietly instructed Liu with a few words, telling the driver to take the goods and follow Li Yuetian, who would naturally arrange everything. In these chaotic times, Jing Shu didn’t want others knowing that, by a stroke of luck, she still had several truckloads of Insect Cake.
Jing Shu released more insects around her and scattered them throughout the entire New World Building. It was as if she had countless eyes watching every move there, ensuring she’d be the first to know if anything unusual happened.
During these times, she couldn’t afford to be the slightest bit careless. Not only did she have to guard against the natural disasters outside, but she also had to be wary of anyone among the two thousand people who might have malicious intent towards her, or who might seek to take advantage of the chaos.
Jing Shu followed Jun Jia without drawing attention to herself and quickly returned to the unruly auction scene.
The host, Xiao Shuai, sat by the fire on a chair, legs crossed, sipping tea. He was perfunctorily chatting with the anxiously whispering crowd about various trivialities. It was Xiao Shuai’s outwardly casual demeanor that prevented the situation from descending into complete chaos.
"Oh? Look, the boss has arrived. Come on, let the leader of the Township Government tell us what’s happening outside and if we are in any danger," Xiao Shuai quickly stood up, offered his seat, and handed over the microphone.
Outside, everything was quiet, and there was no sound of gunfire. It appeared there were no major problems.
The room immediately fell silent.
Gold Dominator, with Jing Shu and Young Master Lan in tow, returned to their previous private room and said with a brazen air, "All good now, I’m back. With me here, you don’t need to worry about anything. Regardless of what happens, rest assured, I’ll protect you all."
"Brother Tyrant, you’re back! Thank goodness, we were just scared to death."
"What exactly happened outside?"
Young Master Lan coughed once. "It’s not a big problem. Right now, Brother Tyrant’s uncle, who is the highest official here, is about to make arrangements. As long as we follow the instructions from our superiors, nothing will go wrong."
"No problem, we will follow orders."
A group of people chattered as if Gold Dominator had never left with Young Master Lan. The truth was, even if Gold Dominator had really abandoned them, they would have had no choice but to suck up to him later, smiling as if nothing had happened.
Liu took out the blanket again, laid it out for Jing Shu, brought back the stove, and set out a platter heaped with assorted snacks. Jing Shu comfortably sat down, putting her feet up on a stool, and Liu offered her a cup of coffee. Jing Shu, her eyes half-closed, let her thoughts race as she simultaneously controlled the small insects around her to continue gathering information.
Next, she needed to know how many people were in this entire building, what factions existed, if there were any dangerous individuals, and... what supplies and weapons were still available.
Jun Jia clearly had much more experience with such matters. Especially at times like this, it was crucial not to divulge the truth and to stabilize public morale. Thus, Jun Jia said in a very relaxed tone,
"Sorry to have kept you all waiting. In reality, nothing serious has happened—it isn’t a robbery or riot as you may have thought. You all know about mudslides, right? It’s just that since we’re in the suburbs, the mudslides are a bit larger here..."
So large it swept the entire building away.
"What?!"
"Then what are we waiting for? Let’s run!"
The hall grew noisy again. With mudslides coming, wouldn’t they be waiting for death if they didn’t flee?
"Stay calm! Listen to me. This mudslide is somewhat special. We originally intended to clear a path, but the road has been cut off. Now, this building is being pushed by the mudslide. We’re no longer in our original location, which is why there’s no signal. But don’t worry, we’ve already sent out satellite signals for rescue, and I believe rescue will arrive before long.
Rest assured, professionals have checked and confirmed there are no other dangers.
For now, the auction is suspended. Xiao Shuai, take some people to seal up the items currently up for auction. We will continue the auction after this is over. What we need to do is simple: just wait for rescue to arrive," said Jun Jia with a natural and sincere expression.
The hall quieted down again. Reassured by the promise of rescue and the knowledge they were only temporarily trapped without immediate danger, everyone finally relaxed completely.
"But!" Jun Jia raised his hand again. "Since this is only a temporary base and we don’t have an adequate water supply, we’ll still have to filter some water ourselves. And, since there are many of us, we might have to stay in this building for a few days."

chapters.title: Chapter 636: Allocating Accommodation
chapters.content:
Chapter 636: Allocating Accommodation
"As for food... Boss Lu, since you have 200 people staying in the New World, could you please supply us with some food?" Jun Jia asked directly.
Boss Lu, the person Jun Jia was referring to, was half-reclining in a reflective glass room with an openwork design on the second floor. Hearing the voice, Boss Lu, clad in a bathrobe, lazily got up, took the microphone, and said, "Sure, no problem at all. We’ve got a big restaurant on the second floor that can provide different kinds of food. However, I am a businessman. I’ll have to sell each meal at market price. It doesn’t matter that we don’t have internet right now; we can just keep a tab. Not raising prices during these special times is already an act of charity."
"That’s fine. We’ll go by market price. How much water do we still have?"
Regretfully, Boss Lu shook his head. "Someone just reported that a water pipe has burst. Although some water was saved, not much was left, and the filtration equipment is all broken too."
Jun Jia nodded and continued, "I know many of you are temporary workers and don’t have Virtual Coin to buy food. Don’t panic. We’re going to dig pits outside to filter muddy water, and these tasks will be compensated. Those who have money can stay in the building; those who don’t can choose to work. Our people will keep the accounts."
A sigh of relief could be heard throughout the hall. In the apocalypse, food was the most expensive commodity, but as long as there was work to be done and food to eat, it was enough for the moment.
"Alright, now let’s arrange the accommodation issue... It’s foreseeable that we might have to stay here for several days. Honestly, this is a commercial building, and right now over two thousand of us are trapped here, but there are only about fifty vacant rooms with beds. Who gets to stay? Who doesn’t?"
"To be fair, let’s auction them off now. The highest bidder wins. We’ll use the money raised to pay for tasks like digging pits and filtering, as well as some labor reformation. Boss Lu, is that okay with you?"
Boss Lu waved his hand dismissively. He had planned to auction off the building today anyway, but who would have thought that it would be swept away by a mudslide? Honestly speaking, he was bankrupt with substantial debts, so the building no longer belonged to him.
Do you want to live in a room with a bed, or are you willing to sleep in the cold, hard, dirty hall with many others crowded together?
The hundreds of people from the Celebrities Gathering were real auction bidders, and right now, for those fifty rooms, they started bidding immediately.
Gold Dominator clearly didn’t want to inconvenience himself; he quickly raised his bid and added, "I’ll bid for a room for you girls. You can all live together, which is better than sleeping on a hard floor."
"Brother Tyrant is mighty! Brother Tyrant is awesome!"
"Brother Tyrant, you’re my idol."
Gold Dominator became even more proud.
Liu quietly asked from the side, "Boss, do we need to bid?"
Jing Shu shook her head. "We have a ready-made villa."
She never expected that the mobile villa, which was bought for future unforeseen needs, would come into use on the very first day of the auction.
Liu’s eyes lit up with understanding, and he gave a thumbs-up.
The boss is truly incredible!
The fifty rooms were quickly auctioned off. Just then, someone asked, "What about these three villas? They can accommodate a lot of people, right? There are dozens of rooms inside. Can we arrange an auction for them?"
Jun Jia frowned.
Right, there are three villas readily available here.
Then he said, "The ten villas have all been auctioned off and the handover is complete, so we won’t be auctioning them to the public."
"But there are only three villas. How are we going to split them?"
"Yeah! If only three families can get them, wouldn’t the others be at a disadvantage?"
Only three villas were on display here. The rest were with Greenland Company.
Jun Jia waved his hand and explained, "We’ll divide them according to who has spent the most money in total. First is Jing Shu, who bought three villas for a total of 3.6 million, and second is..."
This method was somewhat fair. After all, Jing Shu alone had bought three villas, so she definitely had the right to one of them. The other two were allocated, one to Qian Duoduo’s group and one to a family of three whom Jing Shu did not know.
In any case, during the days they were trapped here, Jing Shu finally had a large private space to live in and wouldn’t have to sleep on the floor.
At this time, even Gold Dominator was looking enviously at Jing Shu.
Such a large two-story villa, with so many beautifully decorated rooms... Living alone in there is truly a luxury!
Having divided the villas, Jun Jia started organizing living arrangements for everyone.
The New World followed the layout of a large mall, so the open counters and clothing stores without actual rooms could also be used for sleeping. Larger shops could accommodate more people, smaller shops fewer. Wang Miao, along with the logistics director, started assigning spots and carefully recording them.
Where everyone stayed was meticulously documented. If anyone wanted to move, they needed to state their intention in advance. Crossing boundaries and roaming around were not allowed. Each floor and each designated area had supervisors from the Township Government to prevent chaos, poetically referred to as ’Life Coaches.’
"During these days we’re trapped, to ensure everyone’s safety, we will gather daily for roll call and hold a meeting in this very spot. We will report on our current situation.
"Moreover, everyone must report daily information to their Life Coach. All matters regarding clothing, food, accommodation, and transportation fall under the Life Coach’s purview. Each floor is equipped with a military instructor, whom you can contact in case of any danger. Fighting and brawling are prohibited, and violators will be punished according to the new law."
Soon, everyone trapped in the building found themselves under a military-style management regime.
However, with thousands of people involved, dividing accommodations wasn’t going to satisfy everyone so easily.
Jun Jia passed the subsequent issues to Wang Miao. "Alright, let’s leave it at this for now. If anyone needs to make a change or has other issues, you can go see Wang Miao."
Suddenly, the hall buzzed as many people went to find Wang Miao, including those who wanted to change their living placements, those who wanted to work, and others with various miscellaneous issues.
At this moment, Young Master Lan stood up and said, "Jing Shu, with so many rooms in your villa, how about you let some of the girls from our class stay there? That way, we can give the room Brother Tyrant won to our principal. I just heard from the list that our principal is here too, but he didn’t manage to get a room and has been assigned to sleep in a common sleeping area."
The private room once again fell silent, all eyes turning to Jing Shu. In fact, Jun Jia had divided rooms according to teams, so there were, overall, no major issues. All the people in their section, including the hundred or so volunteers Young Master Lan had brought, were grouped together.
Liu frowned, about to say something when Jing Shu opened her eyes and said indifferently, "Sorry, I have a bit of germophobia. I don’t like other people touching my things."
Young Master Lan’s face soured as he pressed, "Our principal is a good man, and at his age, sleeping in a communal area could easily make him sick. Can you bear to see the principal suffer? Otherwise, since your villa has so many rooms, why not give the principal one?"
"I’ll say it again: I don’t like other people touching my things. If you enjoy playing the good Samaritan so much, why don’t you find a room for the principal?" Jing Shu replied offhandedly.
"It’s such a waste to leave the rooms in your villa empty..."
"Never mind us. The principal is such a good person."

chapters.title: Chapter 637: Moving into the New Villa
chapters.content:
Chapter 637: Moving into the New Villa
"Exactly. They said we might not even get any bedding. How are we supposed to cope in this cold weather?"
Jing Shu raised her eyes, stood up, and signaled Liu to pack up. Then, she picked up her suitcase and walked out. "If you want to be good people, go ahead on your own. Don’t drag me into it. Don’t try to be a hero if you don’t have the ability."
As she spoke, she left the private room, leaving everyone with a view of her cool and impressive departing figure.
Gold Dominator clicked his tongue and shook his head. When he first met this woman, she had seemed somewhat cautious, deliberately keeping a low profile. But now, she was truly revealing her sharp nature.
"I can’t do anything about the room situation. You all saw how tight resources are this time. Either the girls give up their rooms and sleep on the cold floor, or your old Principal sleeps there. Okay, I’m not going to play around with you all anymore. I’m going to check my room first. By the way, Young Master Lan, those two pigs will be in your care for the next few days."
"Ah, got it, Brother Tyrant, don’t worry. Oh, I’ll call you at mealtime."
...
The girls discussed it briefly and ultimately decided not to give up their rooms. After all, it was too inconvenient for so many of them. Thus, they had to let the old Principal endure the hardship.
Jing Shu, accompanied by Liu, went outside to find Li Yuetian. He was sitting on the ground, wearily sipping Turtle Snake Wine. This wine had kept his rheumatism at bay ever since he started drinking it.
Around them, people had already begun digging pits and filtering water.
"I’ve arranged for your truck and driver; they’ll be under my management for now. By the way, I’ve also assigned your driver and this colleague who came with you to a two-bed room," Li Yuetian said, smacking his lips. He was thinking about how much he would rely on Jing Shu in the future.
Li Yuetian now practically wished Jing Shu would ask for his help.
Sigh, is it really so hard for me to be of some use while I’m still alive?
"Thanks, I was worried they wouldn’t have a place to stay. By the way, weren’t there only fifty rooms with beds?"
Li Yuetian touched his nose and smiled. "You just set up a frame, throw some bedding on it, partition off a section, and there you have another room, don’t you? Right now, bedding is what’s really in short supply. We’ve had to distribute old curtains and pieces of cloth as well. Even so, many people still won’t have blankets to cover themselves. Luckily, our team members always carry their packs and bags when we go out. So, if you still want a ’single room,’ it’s no problem for me to spare some more. Don’t worry, I’ll use our Second Team’s own resources."
Jing Shu nodded in understanding. "Coincidentally, I was hoping for a single room myself..."
"No big deal. Just give me the name, and I’ll have my nephew, Li Chenglong, go and set up a fully equipped single room for you on the spot."
After giving the old Principal’s name to Li Yuetian, Jing Shu told Liu, "Liu, take the old Principal there first. Explain the situation and see if he needs any more help. We’ll meet back in the auction’s private room later."
"Sure thing, Boss." Liu adjusted his glasses, his admiration for Jing Shu growing.
A boss who operates so calmly and subtly is the most impressive kind.
The others could never have imagined that what was a matter of desperately scarce resources for them could be arranged so simply by Jing Shu.
Li Yuetian continued to sip his wine leisurely, supervising the work. Reports on the situation on each floor came through his walkie-talkie intermittently.
The wind howled, chillingly cold, signaling that the building was moving faster and faster.
To others, only reflective surfaces revealed any scenery. But with Jing Shu’s full night vision, she could see everything around her clearly.
"Damn it." Jing Shu stood for a while before she couldn’t help cursing.
Li Yuetian cautiously asked, "What’s wrong?"
"Nothing much." Jing Shu sighed. Li Yuetian, being in the dark, and ordinary people might not understand this feeling, but Jing Shu could see it clearly. The building, much like a ship, was advancing at a speed of about 20 kilometers per hour.
The building they were in was currently wedged in a muddy, rocky river flowing between two large mountain ranges. It was surrounded by seemingly endless mountain ranges. Beneath these ranges lay an endless flow of mud, all shrouded in pitch darkness.
For any rescue team to find the New World Building in these vast, boundless mountains would be incredibly difficult, almost impossible.
If it drifted to the end of its course or collided with something, the consequences would be dire.
Sigh... but at this rate, even if we wanted to hit something to stop, it’s probably impossible. It’s too desolate out here, completely bare, nothing at all. This feeling is so oppressive.
"I’m heading back." Jing Shu shook her head. Even with her abilities, she couldn’t stop such a massive building. After all, it wasn’t just a few houses. Jing Shu briefly considered getting some large stones from her storage space to see if she could somehow wedge the building to a stop.
But this damn thing is like a small island!
As luck would have it, Jing Shu’s villa was placed right next to the private auction rooms!
Passing the private auction rooms, one went straight onto the display platform, and then could enter the villa’s door. Although it was right under everyone’s noses, there was currently no better place to situate the villa. The New World’s exterior parking lot had been detached, so there wasn’t much usable land left, and other areas weren’t safe.
Right under everyone’s noses then, so be it.
Her classmates watched with envy, jealousy, and hatred as Jing Shu walked into the villa alone. SLAM! The door shut.
Fortunately, the interior was a sealed, private space, designed according to pre-apocalypse standards. Upon entering, there was an enclosed courtyard. The garage was on the right, and the main hall was on the left.
It had two floors in total, with four rooms, two bathrooms, a large living hall, and two kitchens—fully equipped, much like any other typical villa. Most of the furniture was fixed in place—cabinets, the dining table, sofa, beds, and the like were all immovable.
There was no electricity or running water, so cooking was out of the question.
Upon entering the villa, it felt as if the doors to the outside world had closed. All the arguments and noise faded.
In the pitch-black interior, Jing Shu stood straight, suitcase in hand. She half-closed her eyes and began to concentrate.
Two soft gloves liquefied and slid from Jing Shu’s hands. Gripping pieces of black cloth, they began to seal every window and corner, completely closing off the villa from the outside.
Venomous snakes slithered out one by one, and countless small insects crawled out in dense swarms. They scurried over every inch of the villa, inside and out, covering the floor, walls, roof, and eaves—they were everywhere, checking for anything unusual—any tell-tale red or black lights, or any surveillance and eavesdropping devices.
Jing Shu also conducted her own thorough search. Only after confirming it was safe did she switch on the energy-saving lights in the living room and kitchen.
The entire villa instantly lit up. She started to like having light, even though it was very faint.
The quality of this villa was clearly not as good as those in the Banana District, but its advantages were its light weight and that it was foldable.
The myriad small insects vanished like a receding tide, crawling back into various nooks and crannies. The venomous snakes also disappeared, as if none of it had ever happened.
Jing Shu took out some daily necessities from her storage space. The villa was very cold, so silk quilts were essential, and a stove was also necessary.
Alright, time to set up the foldable bathtub and have a good, long soak in hot water.

chapters.title: Chapter 638: Dreaming
chapters.content:
Chapter 638: Dreaming
Then, she would drink some fresh watermelon juice from the space and savor the grilled meat, sausages, and lettuce salad wraps she had previously stored—delicious and satisfying! At that moment, it felt as if life had reached its peak.
Luckily, Jing Shu was always wary of emergencies. So, whenever she had time, she would make various delicious cooked foods at home. These included different porridges and soups, spicy crayfish, braised meat in sauce, fried steak, braised lion’s head meatballs, oil-braised prawns, roast duck, and chicken cutlets—all measured by the cubic meter.
A rough estimate indicated that the various foods occupied hundreds of square meters.
Therefore, her Magic Cube Space currently held every delicacy imaginable, ready to be taken out steaming hot.
After eating, she would indulge in dessert: yogurt with honey beans, taro balls, and various fruits, making a truly delightful fruit salad.
The leftovers were thrown directly into the space to feed the pigs and chickens, wasting nothing.
Oh, it just feels a bit empty, not having fat chicken by my side is definitely something I’m not used to.
Jing Shu had never been separated from fat chicken over the years, always taking it with her wherever she went. This also provided her a sense of security and lessened her boredom.
This time, she didn’t know how long she’d be trapped here. Jing Shu wanted to go back soon to make more preparations, as she was about to face a real storm.
Besides, there’s not a single person to talk to.
Jing Shu glanced at her watch. It was still early. She tidied up the villa and discreetly set up some... traps, for instance, at the entrances, windows, and surrounding areas.
If anyone dared to sneak around, they shouldn’t blame her for the consequences.
Jing Shu was just that kind of person, always lacking a sense of security.
After setting up all the homemade traps, Jing Shu laid out the bedding in the master bedroom, preparing to begin her practice with the Magic Cube.
Four hours of relentless Magic Cube practice was a must every day. It was a matter of practice making perfect. Though there were formulas, one could only progress through endless exploration and thousands of instances of muscle memory.
Every time she leveled up, she would encounter various bizarre events, and these events were always related to the abilities unlocked after upgrading the Magic Cube.
After summarizing, Jing Shu classified these abilities according to their magnitude and importance into the first realm, the second realm, and beyond.
Currently, the Magic Cube’s abilities all belonged to the second realm. If it reached the third realm, Jing Shu guessed it would fully coincide with reality. This would likely mean that Magic Cube Space could truly exist in reality.
Then, she would truly be invincible and unafraid of the world collapsing.
So, it was peculiar that this time the Magic Cube seemed not to be causing trouble. During these days of Jing Shu’s upgrades, no glitches had occurred. There was no need to get up at four in the morning to practice, nor did she ever forget to practice...
Everything was perfectly normal. The more normal it was, the more uncertain and anxious Jing Shu felt, as if something was stuck in her throat.
Therefore, Jing Shu practiced with the Magic Cube even more frequently.
「A few days flew by.」
The more than two thousand people trapped in the New World Building hadn’t encountered any major issues. This was because, at the onset of the event, Jun Jia had organized a full military-style management, keeping everyone tightly under control.
Of course, various conflicts arose, but with the military as a backdrop, they were generally resolved. People seemed to gradually adapt to this way of life.
Meanwhile, Jing Shu mostly stayed in the villa. She either practiced with the Magic Cube, fed the chickens, cows, and pigs, harvested and stored fresh vegetables, or organized her Magic Cube Space.
Since the building was short on resources, with no electricity or heating, Jing Shu had spent the past few days figuring out how to generate electricity in the space and transfer it to reality.
And she actually managed it. After starting her diesel-powered generator in the Magic Cube Space, she could connect it to reality. The main advantage was that it could be done stealthily, meaning she would never fear running out of electricity again.
The disadvantage was that Jing Shu had to be present and couldn’t move beyond the range of her Magic Cube Space. She had to constantly divide her attention; otherwise, the power line would be instantly severed by the space.
Actually, when the Magic Cube Space reached Tier 5, right when the apocalypse began, Jing Shu had tried to transmit electricity from the space to reality. It was unsuccessful at the time; she couldn’t manage to have things half in the space and half in reality.
Because an item is a whole, it is either in the space or in reality—indivisible. Jing Shu had regretted this for a long time.
However, when the Magic Cube activated its second space, and space and reality became semi-integrated, Jing Shu gained this ability. This led her to speculate: if she upgraded to the third realm, where space fully coincided with reality,
would that mean she, too, could enter the space? By then, if any danger arose, she could hide in the space. And based on her understanding of the space, even if she were inside, she wouldn’t be immobile. She could change locations, drive a car within it, and, using the space as a medium, move in reality...
She was getting carried away with her daydreams.
"Everyone! Please gather immediately in the plaza hall! We have an important announcement! Repeat..."
Jing Shu was awakened by the loud broadcast announcement.
Another meeting in the private rooms. She wondered what had happened.
Jing Shu stuffed her mouth with steak, sausage, and fried egg while hurriedly putting on her bulletproof clothing and bulletproof hat. Finally, after drinking a can of soy milk, she donned a mask and rushed to the private room for the meeting.
Liu had already groomed herself and dressed neatly. She had arranged a blanket in their spot, brought over the small stove from the other day, and was even heating a pot of tea for Jing Shu, waiting respectfully.
"Boss, sit here. Here, I’ve heated the stove for you. Have some tea first. Later, we’ll see what else is available in the cafeteria," Liu said with some concern.
There was no more food; the building was running out. The consumption of two thousand people was enormous.
But the boss’s appetite was so small, like a mosquito’s. She only ate a bite or two each time, and always with a disdainful look. How could she possibly get full on so little?
Jing Shu, her hair a mess like a bird’s nest, sat down. The entire hall was dark, except for a faint light on the stage that allowed Xiao Shuai, the host, to be seen. The rest of the hall was pitch black.
The other people gradually arrived, all shivering with cold.
Jing Shu, wearing gloves, brought her hands close to the stove and exhaled.
Ah, that feels good.
"Why does it smell like fried eggs? It smells so fragrant."
"It clearly smells like steak."
"Nonsense, you’re just imagining things."
Liu’s nose twitched. Indeed, there was a meaty aroma, seemingly mixed with a hint of soy milk.
It smells amazing!

chapters.title: Chapter 639: Dark Creatures Spotted
chapters.content:
Chapter 639: Dark Creatures Spotted
Jing Shu wiped her mouth discreetly.
These people are ridiculous—they can even sniff out what’s at the corner of my mouth. Absolutely twisted. It looks like I’ll need to mask my scent before going out from now on.
"Alright, alright, is everyone here? Now, we’ll start the briefing. COUGH. COUGH."
The moment Xiao Shuai, the host, began speaking into the microphone, the entire hall quieted down, though there were still some whispers. It was just like a regular meeting; there were always people whispering under their breath. Everyone was quite concerned about this matter, as they had been trapped for several days now. The feeling was frankly unbearable...
"What I’m about to say next is very important, so please remember it at all times. Just three hours ago, a man and a woman ignored the curfew and sneaked out, probably to engage in some... intimate activities. As a result, they were dragged into the mire by an unknown creature and vanished. By the time our people arrived to rescue them, all they found were some clothes and the sounds of screams!"
There wasn’t a big commotion at the scene. After all, only two people had died. Wasn’t that normal? More than their deaths, people were actually curious about who the man and woman were. Perhaps actions like theirs could only happen when sleeping in a large communal bunk with no privacy?
Besides, it had been years since the apocalypse started. Wasn’t it normal for such things to happen occasionally?
"Do you think this is normal? Do you disregard this? At first, we only felt regret. The people at the scene were preparing to report the incident and investigate who those two were. However, it’s regrettable to inform you that three hours have passed, and we still haven’t had time to identify them. This is because many more strange-looking creatures, covered in black mud, have climbed out of the rapid mudslide and dragged our people into the mire as well.
Our people opened fire, but shooting them was like shooting into mud; there was no reaction whatsoever. We could only watch as these things dragged our comrades into the mudslide, where they completely disappeared.
We then assembled many people armed with torches, electric batons, and various weapons. After a fierce battle, the creatures left behind ten corpses and scurried back into the mire, disappearing completely. In that fight, we lost three people, and five were injured.
It’s predictable that there are many such creatures. They are like fierce beasts: strong, fast, amphibious, and impervious to bullets, much like mud. However, they are afraid of light, fire, and electricity. Now, let me show you the bodies of these creatures. After our examination, we’ve found that they are likely a new product of the apocalypse."
The host waved his hand, and people began carrying the mutated creatures onto the stage. The spotlight fell on them—grotesque, terrifying, shriveled.
One mutated creature was over six feet tall.
Without the nourishment of mud and water, they soon dried up, becoming like desiccated corpses. However, their skeletons remained, resembling... the skeleton of a fish, yet with horrifying teeth and two claws.
All in all, they had a fish-like body, lizard-like claws, and a head that took up half of its body.
Jing Shu furrowed her brows, rhythmically tapping her chair and producing a patterned sound.
Strange, I’ve never seen this creature before. I slept too soundly last night. My insects and snakes were only sparsely placed around the outer perimeter of the building; they didn’t raise an alarm. After all, these insects and snakes have very low intelligence—they wouldn’t signal unless my safety was threatened, and they certainly wouldn’t record these events.
"After a simple identification, these creatures were identified as Dark Creatures that eat anything. They typically survive on mud. There’s no distinct male or female, and their reproduction methods are unknown. However, they are highly dangerous, capable of capturing any living thing to eat, and possess formidable combat abilities. You can think of them as a mutated evolution of a small shark that has evolved claws, enhanced teeth, and the ability to survive in both water and on land."
Host Xiao Shuai repeated everything he was instructed to say, with no omissions. After discussions with the higher-ups, they initially wanted to downplay the severity to avoid panic. However, they ultimately decided to disclose everything to ensure people took the situation seriously.
After hearing this, Jing Shu quietly released more snakes outside the building and commanded them to alert her if these Dark Creatures approached.
"In this dangerous situation, the truth needs to be told to scare them a bit, to make them stay inside the building and not cause any trouble," Jun Jia had said at the time.
Indeed, after Xiao Shuai finished speaking and the Dark Creatures were brought up, the hall completely erupted.
It wasn’t just that the Dark Creatures were horrific; it was the realization that these man-eating beings were lurking right outside and, importantly, could climb onto the building itself.
Xiao Shuai was pleased and continued, "Do you understand what this means? It’s as if we’re on a large ship floating on the ocean, surrounded by sharks. And these packs of sharks can also climb ashore to prey on any of you who are alone."
HUBBUB! The people in the hall grew even more terrified. Trapped and anxious before, now they were truly panicked.
"Therefore, the authorities have decided that, aside from those with entry permits, no one else is allowed to leave the building. Anyone who violates this will be thrown into the water as shark bait," Xiao Shuai announced cheerfully. Yet, no one objected.
Now, who in their right mind would want to go outside? Better to just stay put inside the building.
"Oh, and because there are so many people these days, food has become quite scarce. Boss Lu, the owner of the building, has decided to double the price of all food," Xiao Shuai announced as the second regulation.
"What? How can this be? We have no money left."
"Yeah, the food is too expensive, doesn’t even taste good, and is hard to swallow."
"It’s already mixed with mud..."
Xiao Shuai nodded understandingly. "So now, we need five hundred people to help dig defensive walls and set up interception mechanisms within the building. These individuals will be provided with three free meals a day."
If they didn’t volunteer, many wouldn’t be able to afford food. However, going outside seemed very dangerous.
"Don’t worry, we’ve found the weaknesses of these Dark Creatures, and we will definitely protect you."
The most conflicted were Jing Shu’s classmates in the private room. After all, they weren’t financially well-off...
"Wait, have you guys seen Cheng Long?"
"Cheng Long isn’t here. It seems no one has seen him this morning."
"Where is he? Wasn’t he with Tang Yuan?"
Tang Yuan’s voice trembled. "Yesterday, he said he was going to help Brother Tyrant..."
Gold Dominator’s voice interjected, "Don’t talk nonsense. If I needed help, I would have asked Young Master Lan."
So, where had Cheng Long gone?
Could he be one of the two who vanished? But Cheng Long’s wife, Tang Yuan, was still here.
Jing Shu shook her head.
This whole affair is truly preposterous.

chapters.title: Chapter 640: The Building’s Food Shortage
chapters.content:
Chapter 640: The Building’s Food Shortage
There definitely needed to be people going out to dig traps and fences, and it was urgent. They had already started counting people over there and had limited the food supply. If you didn’t go out to work, unless you were rich enough to afford food, you would just have to wait to starve to death.
On the other side, the life teacher had finished checking the number of people under each jurisdiction and quickly identified the two missing individuals. One was indeed Tang Yuan’s husband, Cheng Long, and surprisingly, the other was a woman in her fifties who had come to attend the auction.
No one had expected Cheng Long to have gotten involved with the noble lady, become intimate with her, and even had trysts with her in the wild.
"I’ve been saying Cheng Long is always out at night these days," someone remarked.
"And Cheng Long has had so much good food lately. It turns out he was playing the gigolo," another added.
"Sister Tang Yuan, your Cheng Long really is... *sigh*, I don’t know what to say. Look at this mess. You’ll just have to mourn him."
"A perfectly good person, gone just like that."
There were those who laughed at Tang Yuan, those who reveled in her misfortune, and those who sighed at the unpredictability of life.
With a dark face and red eyes, Tang Yuan was partly angry and partly felt an odd sensation. She sneakily glanced at the expressionless Young Master Lan and bit her lip.
Perhaps her future support would be Young Master Lan?
"What are you looking at? Do any of you even have Virtual Coins to buy food? Go register to dig fences now! If some people are dead, they had it coming, but those of us who are alive need to continue living!" Tang Yuan said angrily before running off to register. By going early, and because she was a woman who knew Young Master Lan, she might get an easier job. If she went late, she’d really only be left with digging pits.
A crowd also hurriedly went to register. After all, registering now meant they could snag breakfast, and most of them really had no Virtual Coins left for food. Plenty of them had been living off their salaries from the network, but they always needed to save some...
In any case, Jun Jia was still a sly fox, clearly understanding these people’s minds and making them willingly go to work.
When the people in the private room had mostly left, Gold Dominator came over, humming and hawing, "Hey, Jing Shu, I need a favor."
"I won’t help," Jing Shu said, not wanting to deal with Gold Dominator, then turned her head to Liu, "Let’s go to the cafeteria."
"Wait, wait a moment, Jing Shu! Just a small favor. My little piggies have run out of feed these past few days. Could you spare some Insect Cake? I just found out that my pigs used to eat your family’s Insect Cake... Can I buy them? I know you don’t need money, but just tell me what you want for some Insect Cake?" Gold Dominator said helplessly.
In a corner, Young Master Lan was cleaning the pigsty and feeding them hot water. Both pigs were listless. Hearing this, Young Master Lan looked up towards Jing Shu, his expression complex.
Jing Shu stopped, raised an eyebrow, and spoke, "How about this: I’ll supply food for your two pigs until we’re rescued, and in return, you give me one of their offspring when they breed."
After all, they were nearly extinct Jinhua sows. Although her family also had black pigs, which were delicious too, Jinhua Ham was famous far and wide, and Jing Shu hadn’t properly tasted it yet. Good things, how could anyone have too much of them? It’s like who would complain about having too much money?
"No way, that would be too much of a bargain for you," Gold Dominator immediately refused without thinking.
"Then forget it," Jing Shu said without turning her head and walked away with Liu.
Gold Dominator, fuming in their wake, looked at the dejected Pig Jin Bab and said, "I’ll think of other ways. I refuse to believe there’s no other food available."
Young Master Lan said weakly, "I’ve been feeding them other things for the past couple of days too, but they hardly eat any—probably because they’ve gotten used to Insect Cake."
"They’re just spoiled!" Gold Dominator said angrily and stormed off. He was going to his uncle to demand an explanation. Besides, Gold Dominator had been in a terrible mood these past few days because his daily milk and snacks were gone. All that was left were pitiful biscuits and awful-tasting stale buns.
"Ah, when will we be rescued?"
...
"Boss, this situation doesn’t look too good," Liu said worriedly, following behind Jing Shu.
"That’s putting it mildly," Jing Shu shook her head.
The two of them had just reached the grand dining hall on the second floor of the new world. Boss Lu had converted the entire floor into a cafeteria, with people dishing out food at windows and others taking notes. Whether they were celebrities who had bid high prices at the auction, wealthy individuals, or service staff, everyone obediently stood in line with their bowls.
It seemed Jun Jia had reached some agreement with Boss Lu.
Sometimes, the serving lady’s hand would tremble, leaving hardly anything in the bowl. Though the food wasn’t good, the main concern now was simply getting enough to eat.
A young man pointed to a half-bowl of some dark sludge, made of who-knows-what, and said, "Give me some more, please."
"That’s enough, move along now! The rules from above state that those working outside only get half a bowl! Keep quiet, or you’ll lose your eligibility to work," the serving lady said impatiently, shooing away the young man, who quickly left.
Behind him, a middle-aged man in a down jacket smoothed his slicked-back hair and grinned, "Beautiful, I’ll take six bowls. Just put it on my tab; here’s my identification."
The lady scoffed, "Six bowls? You wish! There’s a limit of one bowl per person now. Take it or leave it."
"Yes, yes, yes..." The middle-aged man bowed low as he handed over his bowl, and the lady filled it generously. After the person next to him had recorded it, the next person in line was served.
Now, whether you were a multimillionaire or a poor fellow, everyone had to keep a low profile. If you were a dragon, you had to coil up; if you were a tiger, you had to lie low.
No matter how many supplies one had, their net worth, whether they lived in a villa or held high authority, if they hadn’t brought their own food, they had to endure.
The cafeteria was crowded. Although there were several windows, a variety of food choices had been available during the first two days. Jing Shu had even reluctantly taken a bite or two back then.
But today, there was only this dark mush, a mixture of all sorts of scraps cooked together, which even smelled indescribably foul.
Liu whispered quietly, "I heard from the driver that Li Yuetian has been leading his men everywhere, gathering insects and any living thing they can find. They chop it all up and cook it together. Apparently, Jun Jia said the situation might turn dire, so they must conserve as much food as possible."
So this is why today’s breakfast is like this? Probably, some people won’t be able to stomach it.
Jing Shu recalled that some of her own insects had mysteriously disappeared recently. Li Yuetian and his men had probably dug them out. It seemed she’d have to be more careful about where she kept them.
Liu continued softly, "I also heard that Boss Lu has begun to secretly hoard food. He doesn’t dare openly resist the Township Government. However, under these circumstances, he’s definitely keeping extra food. The only question is how much Boss Lu actually has left."

chapters.title: Chapter 641: The Tower is Invaded (Added for Susuan Lin Juanjuan)
chapters.content:
Chapter 641: The Tower is Invaded (Added for Susuan Lin Juanjuan)
Jing Shu frowned.
Perhaps I’ll investigate in detail later when I have time,
she mused.
Boss Lu’s room has been made of special materials for the past two days; not even an insect can get in. Otherwise...
"Boss, we still have a lot of Insect Cake. Currently, only Li Yuetian and Jun Jia know the exact amount; no one else does. And Li Yuetian is protecting the truck at their camp. What do you think we should do?"
Jing Shu said as she walked, "Don’t touch the Insect Cake for now. It’s not just Boss Lu; others have hidden food too. Let’s just wait and see."
The emergence of insects and snakes in the past two days had allowed Jing Shu to gather significant information. For instance, she learned that her food supplies weren’t the only ones that hadn’t been confiscated; others had also coincidentally managed to bring supplies into the building and were now keeping quiet about it.
Under these circumstances, Jing Shu was determined not to let anyone else know she still had food supplies.
"Boss, does this mean we can only eat Insect Cake from now on? We probably can’t eat the cafeteria food anymore," Liu said, looking at the dark mush with distaste.
Just then, a group of people surged into the cafeteria, chattering. Jing Shu saw it was her college classmates.
They approached, fuming and cursing.
"What the hell! They said they had enough people and didn’t need any more..."
"Exactly! Didn’t they say they needed five hundred people to dig? How could they be full so quickly? What are we supposed to eat then?"
"Zhang Hao, lend me some Virtual Coin. I hit my limit yesterday; they won’t let me run a tab anymore."
"Get lost! It’s your own fault for not working these past few days. You deserve it."
"Let’s go find Young Master Lan and ask him to arrange a job for us. He’s the one who brought us in, after all."
"Why does Young Master Lan arrange jobs for all the women—and easy ones at that—but not for us?"
"Right, let’s go to Young Master Lan! If he can’t arrange a job, he can at least get us some food. Young Master Lan himself was eating biscuits yesterday."
"Let’s go! Let’s go ask Young Master Lan for food!"
The group departed as boisterously as they had arrived.
Young Master Lan has really gotten himself into a big mess this time,
Jing Shu thought.
Jing Shu shook her head. "Forget the Insect Cake; I can’t get used to it. Come with me."
Since the cafeteria food had become unbearable, Jing Shu stopped pretending. Quietly carrying a black box, she went to the room Liu shared with the driver. The driver was currently at the camp’s truck, guarding the goods with Li Yuetian’s men.
Ever since discovering that the Insect Cake on the truck might be the last food supply in the entire building, the driver had been guarding it practically around the clock. He constantly worried that some troublemakers might try to steal it, even though not even the soldiers knew what was inside the truck.
When hungry, he ate Insect Cake; when tired, he slept in the truck. It was tough.
Liu was also working very hard, running around to gather information and meticulously making all necessary arrangements. Jing Shu wouldn’t let either of them be mistreated.
Once in their room, she closed the door and checked that they were alone. Only then did Jing Shu open the first compartment of the black box, swiftly retrieve two packages, and close the box again before Liu could fully react.
"Boss... what are you planning to do?" Liu’s voice was faint and a little fearful.
The Boss rarely acts this strangely. What on earth did she take out?
"This is for you and the driver, one package each," Jing Shu said. "For the next few days, if you get hungry, eat this quietly. Don’t let anyone else find out."
When Liu opened his package, he found five black, fist-sized objects that looked like rocks.
"Th-this... what is this?" Liu was completely baffled.
"Lick it," Jing Shu said smugly.
"Huh? You want me to lick a rock?" Liu pinched the hard, rock-like object and finally licked it. A sharp, sour taste that made him shiver assaulted his senses, immediately followed by a rich, milky aroma that seemed to permeate his entire being. Liu’s pupils dilated, and his body trembled uncontrollably, as if he had reached some new state of existence.
Liu licked it a few more times. The fragrance in his mouth grew richer and lingered, becoming incredibly addictive. He couldn’t stop.
"Th-this is...?"
"They’re yogurt balls, a concentrated essence made by fermenting pure milk. Each ball contains the equivalent of one to one-and-a-half kilograms of milk. You can eat them slowly. They’re very nutritious and filling, perfect for the current emergency."
"Now open the second package. These are Compressed Biscuits. Usually, half a biscuit is enough to make you feel full. If you eat them sparingly, these will be enough for you both for ten to fifteen days. These are foods that aren’t easily discovered, so hide them well."
Liu was so moved he was beyond words.
The Boss... she really is the Boss!
"Boss, do you always carry so much with you when you go out? If you give these to us, will you have enough for yourself? Actually, one of these packages would have been enough for both of us..."
Jing Shu nodded. "I’ve encountered many situations like this before, so I always make sure to bring enough food when I go out. Don’t worry, I still have enough."
In any case, ever since the unknown Dark Creatures were discovered, work had begun at a feverish pace in the New World Building to dig pits and erect defensive walls. Although it was a case of robbing Peter to pay Paul for materials, within a mere three days, the entire building was enclosed by a one-and-a-half-meter-high low wall, with a deep trench dug behind it.
Due to the cold weather, the low wall quickly solidified. This provided everyone with some sense of security, although no one understood why the subterranean mudslides didn’t freeze in such frigid temperatures.
People didn’t remain idle in the following days either. Jun Jia had them continue to build the wall higher and constantly search for scrap materials to make weapons and traps.
In short, if you wanted to eat, you couldn’t afford to be idle; you had to work constantly.
At this moment, I feel like I’m seeing the tyrant from five years in the future,
Jing Shu thought.
It figures; they’re clearly cut from the same cloth.
During this time, the Dark Creatures didn’t appear again. Everyone quietly breathed a sigh of relief and began to relax.
However, new anxieties soon arose as people were increasingly not getting enough to eat. The food, which used to be a dark mush, had now thinned to a black, watery broth—so insubstantial that it felt like nothing remained after a trip to the latrine.
The worst part was that it contained a lot of sand and grit. Biting into it was gritty and painful on the teeth, but swallowing it directly was... unpleasant, to say the least.
Just as everyone’s focus had shifted to their hunger, and while they were sound asleep late at night, sudden screams shattered the silence inside the building.
Immediately, the entire building erupted into chaos, filled with more screams. The alarm blared, and the night patrol guards outside quickly rushed in.
"Help! Help me!"
"What happened? What’s going on?"
"AAAAHHHH!"
Screams, the sound of trampling feet, and bizarre chewing noises mingled together. The entire New World Building was thrown into chaos!
Jing Shu’s eyes snapped open. In her mind, countless eyes and insects seemed to stir.

chapters.title: Chapter 642: Unfortunately, You Can’t Eat Meat
chapters.content:
Chapter 642: Unfortunately, You Can’t Eat Meat
Only images from heat sources were transmitted through the snake’s eyes, allowing Jing Shu to see many red energy bodies running about. However, the snake’s vision wasn’t very sensitive to the invasion of the Dark Creatures. Jing Shu surmised that these Dark Creatures either had no body temperature or a very low one.
The insect’s vision was even simpler: enormous creatures were rampaging throughout the building!
Jing Shu surveyed the building’s exterior. It was very quiet, with nothing unusual. Even the patrols were currently rushing into the building, torches and weapons in hand. A few days ago, Dark Creatures had invaded; because they feared light and fire, the area around the building had consistently been kept lit.
Jing Shu quickly got up, grabbed two machetes, and carefully opened her villa door. At that moment, people from the other two villas in the exhibition hall also cautiously cracked open their doors to observe what was happening outside.
Li Yuetian’s men told Jing Shu to hide well and call him if anything happened, then hurried off, as the lobby was currently safe.
The first-floor lobby of the New World Building was very quiet. However, since the building’s center was an open atrium, Jing Shu could see someone on the fourth floor desperately fleeing. They were apparently so desperate they had chosen to jump.
But just as they leaped into mid-air, an enormous, blood-red maw lunged and swallowed half their body in a single bite.
Immediately after, the ugly, crawling Dark Creature and the remaining half of the body plummeted from the fourth floor, landing with a tremendous BOOM.
"AAAH!" The people in the neighboring villa screamed, having glimpsed a Shadow in the torchlight from outside.
"Shut up," Jing Shu hissed, but the screaming didn’t stop.
The crawling creature landed near the exhibition hall. It was incredible that such a huge being, after falling from such a height and practically splattering into a muddy heap on the ground, began to crawl again in just a few seconds.
It was as if their bodies weren’t made of flesh but of something like rotten mud.
Jing Shu frowned. This was the first time she had seen such a grotesque creature. The corpses she had encountered before were mere skeletons, but this thing looked like a pile of sludge. It had a fish-like head almost as large as its body and vaguely resembled a Mermaid...
I’ll call it a rotten mermaid for now,
she thought.She watched as this rotten mermaid continuously chewed the flesh in its mouth, then slowly crawled toward the other half of the recently fallen corpse.
Jing Shu, holding her machetes, strode quickly toward it.
"Miss, what are you doing? Run, quickly! Hide in the villa and wait for rescue!" a man from another villa shouted, leaning out to warn her.
If no one else were around, I’d really like to pull out the boulders from my Magic Cube Space and smash these rotten mermaids to a pulp,
Jing Shu thought.
There’s no way they’d survive that.
Too bad there are people around,
she continued to muse.
Since there’s only one rotten mermaid right now, I have to quickly figure out its biggest weakness. In this apocalypse, despite the Township Government’s protection, you can ultimately only rely on your own abilities. Ordinary people die so easily.
That was why these people couldn’t understand Jing Shu.
Why not wait for rescue?
they would wonder.
But Jing Shu wasn’t foolish enough to charge in with just her machetes. After all, she possessed the special ability of her Magic Cube Space: she could control living creatures. As long as a creature was conscious, Jing Shu could manipulate its thoughts or induce illusions, anything to achieve her goals.
This ability was unlocked when she reached the seventh order of the Magic Cube. Initially, she could only control a single organism—or just one human. However, after helping her elder aunt’s daughter-in-law give birth, Jing Shu trained relentlessly and could now control a significant number of creatures simultaneously.
The rotten mermaid noticed Jing Shu as well. It merely emitted a low growl and continued eating. Perhaps, in its eyes, she posed no fear or threat.
Jing Shu moved faster and faster, her eyes fixed on the rotten mermaid. Seizing the moment it bared its teeth, she swung her machete down. The Mermaid’s head was huge; even the largest machete she had bought before the apocalypse failed to sever it in one strike.
Jing Shu’s strength was now tremendous, reaching a frightening level. As she brought the machete down, she felt resistance and a viscous stickiness. She had to exert considerable force to finally cleave through, but it only lopped off half of the rotten mermaid’s head.
There was no blood or fluid. The rotten mermaid seemed to be made of playdough; the separation of flesh from bone didn’t affect its ability to move in the slightest.
Now I understand why they’re not afraid of bullets,
Jing Shu thought.
With a structure like this, being riddled with holes would hardly affect them. Many Dark Creatures in the apocalypse have this trait. To survive, they evolved down dark paths, eating anything, and eventually turned into beings that are neither human nor ghost.
It seemed to feel pain, however. It began to roar furiously, dropped the flesh from its mouth, and charged straight at Jing Shu.
Jing Shu activated her Magic Cube Space ability, exerting control over conscious life forms within its range.
The rotten mermaid stiffened for a moment.
Seizing the opportunity, Jing Shu chopped off the other half of its head, completely severing it from the body. The rotten mermaid twitched a few more times, then fell still.
Jing Shu nodded.
It seems this level of Dark Creature hasn’t reached the invincibility of those from the fifth or sixth year of the apocalypse,
she thought.
It died once its head was gone. Not too troublesome.
Upon death, the rotten mermaid’s body quickly dissolved into a pool of mud, revealing the white bones within.
The screams from the person behind Jing Shu abruptly stopped. That woman stared in astonishment, as did the man from the other villa, both gaping at the scene.
This... this is unbelievable, isn’t it? That woman, with just a machete, split such a huge monster in two with a couple of strikes? That’s way too badass!
The screams from upstairs hadn’t stopped, which puzzled Jing Shu.
Logically, these things should have crawled in from outside and passed through the first-floor exhibition hall first. Shouldn’t we here have been the first to be attacked? Why isn’t there a single Mermaid on the first floor, yet there are so many upstairs?
Fortunately, each floor had management instructors who began to organize an orderly response. The patrols from outside, along with Li Yuetian’s armed forces, were also heading upstairs.
Jing Shu squatted down, touched the huge bones, and said, "What a pity."
The man from the villa cautiously walked out, looked at Jing Shu, and said, "A pity about what? Let’s get out of here quickly. If a few more of them show up, we’ll be helpless. It’s better to hide quietly inside the villa; they probably won’t figure out how to open the doors."
"It’s a pity that such a huge creature has no meat. It can’t be used as rations. Such a waste." Jing Shu shook her head.
If these things were edible, this place would be a treasure trove, and these people wouldn’t have to worry about food. Never mind that, when I get back from this, I’ll probably have to hire specialists to capture these rotten mermaids,
she thought.

chapters.title: Chapter 643: Picking up White Bones (Extra update for the 90-year-old)
chapters.content:
Chapter 643: Picking up White Bones (Extra update for the 90-year-old)
