This was something many people in the south found incomprehensible: how, within the same Huaxia, it could get dark for them at six, while for others, it wasn’t dark even at twelve. But all of this was a thing of the past. After the apocalypse, everything was disrupted, the seasons became chaotic, and there was no longer any regular daytime.
Still, the data Jing Shu had been observing for so many days was viable. She would continue to observe. If a cyclical pattern of time differences emerged, it was very likely they were currently in a giant vortex, with the building spinning in circles. However, this still required further observation. At least now they knew roughly which direction they were drifting, had a general idea of their bearing, and perhaps even how far they had drifted.
"Excellent, truly excellent!" Jun Jia exclaimed, deeply moved. "Who would have thought we had someone as talented as you among us! It’s amazing you could figure this out!"
Jing Shu smiled faintly. "It’s just that the apocalypse completely disrupted the weather, so no one paid attention to this. The simpler things are, the more easily they’re overlooked. Besides, others probably pinned their hopes on waiting for rescue. And to be more precise, I don’t understand the exact geographical relationships based on this method of differentiation either." That was why no one else had thought of it so deeply.
But Jing Shu was different. She was someone who had died once. Having experienced so much during the apocalypse, she profoundly understood that relying on others was never as good as relying on oneself. Therefore, from the very beginning, Jing Shu had been constantly trying to find solutions. Although she had considered some outlandish ideas, like controlling the building, she had ultimately always focused on self-rescue.
"Excellent, excellent, excellent!" Jun Jia seemed to see a glimmer of hope. "I’ll go back and gather people knowledgeable in these matters to analyze this. Miss Jing, you’ve made a truly significant contribution!"
Gold Dominator opened his mouth but ultimately said nothing, just muttering softly,
We learned this in junior high...
Unfortunately, the apocalypse had struck right after they finished those studies, and now there were only online classes. The Township Government still didn’t plan to reinstate the college entrance exams. The content of the online classes had been changed, no longer including the difficult subjects of the past. Instead, it was tailored to cultivate the most needed talents for the current situation and was divided into many fields like humanities, science, practical skills, and sociology. After finishing high school, one could directly apply for temporary jobs with the Township Government.
Ah, I haven’t signed in to water for so many days. The vegetables for my Chinese class homework are going to die. I’m going to fail this semester,
Gold Dominator thought, stuffing his long-dead smartphone into his pocket. The Chinese language class was a separate app, much like certain farming simulation games, teaching different methods for growing fruits and vegetables, controlling temperature and humidity, and even requiring bug catching. Under normal circumstances, Gold Dominator should have been a carefree college student by now. What a pity.
Gold Dominator stomped his feet like a child, listlessly listening as his Uncle and Jing Shu discussed the operational plans and many confidential matters. His uncle clearly valued Jing Shu a great deal.
Suddenly, Gold Dominator looked up as he heard Jun Jia say, "Miss Jing, I have a somewhat awkward favor to ask... I might be very busy soon, perhaps too busy to look after myself. So, I’d like to ask for your help in taking care of Gold Dominator. If, by any chance, something unfortunate happens to me, please, at the very least, ensure he survives. My sister and brother-in-law... they only have this one child..."
Is he entrusting his nephew to my care?
Jing Shu thought. Not just Gold Dominator, but Jing Shu herself was incredibly surprised. This seemed unnecessary. However, seeing Jun Jia’s somewhat agitated expression, she nodded in agreement. "Uncle Jin has always taken good care of our family. Please don’t worry, I’ll look after Gold Dominator."That was her promise. Jun Jia finally set aside his last worry. He trusted Jing Shu. She had managed to survive and return from the perilous environment in the United States. Others might not know the details, but he did. Furthermore, based on the information Yang Yang had brought back, he wouldn’t be surprised if Jing Shu possessed some special ability. More importantly, he had heard from Ling Yi’s own lips about the fear Jing Shu inspired, and then there was the inexplicable appearance of so many skeletons in the hall. Jun Jia knew Jing Shu was far from ordinary. Even if everyone else here perished, Jing Shu surely had her own ways to survive. Entrusting the boy to her, given her character and integrity, he felt he could trust her completely.
"Uncle..." Gold Dominator felt a surge of unease.
His uncle speaking like this... does it mean something bad is about to happen?
"Anyway, I don’t care! As long as I’m alive, you have to be alive too! If something happens to you, I won’t go on living either!"
"What nonsense are you spouting, child? We all need to keep living, to survive this apocalypse!"
Only then did Gold Dominator nod. He turned to Jing Shu and said, "Alright, you’re in charge of feeding my two pigs until we’re rescued. If they have piglets, I’ll give you one." These days, the two pigs’ spirits were declining more and more, and with rescue still nowhere in sight, Gold Dominator had finally relented. Although he could have used his connections to secretly get some pig feed, it wouldn’t have been an upright thing to do.
"I want two," Jing Shu said, gazing towards the sky.
"You- you’re being too greedy!" Gold Dominator grew anxious. He’d heard that a Jinhua Sow usually only birthed a few piglets at a time...
"Then... three?"
"Fine, two it is! Hmph! From now on, the pigs are your responsibility," Gold Dominator relented, feeling aggrieved. There was no choice; he was under someone else’s roof and had to bow his head. For now, everyone was reliant on Jing Shu’s Insect Cake.
"Yes, I’ll take care of them all." Jing Shu glanced at Gold Dominator.
I’ll have to ensure his survival when necessary,
she decided,
considering the astonishing influence Jin Tianci’s family will have in Wu City later on.
Gold Dominator stomped his feet and stormed off in a huff.

chapters.title: Chapter 654: Fishing (Extra for Su Ruan Lin Juanjuan)
chapters.content:
Chapter 654: Fishing (Extra for Su Ruan Lin Juanjuan)
That day, the weather was gloomy, with a cold wind blowing sharply.
It was getting colder, but there was no sign that the mudstone flow would freeze, which was completely unscientific.
Jing Shu had secretly wrapped an extra sweater around herself and put on some thermal underwear, making her look a bit bloated.
Many people in the building were shivering and huddling together for warmth—there was no helping it. The building was as cold as an ice cellar.
They couldn’t run either, as that would consume too much food, so they could only cling to each other in the hall like stacked toys. Everyone had stopped bathing and changing clothes for a long time, and even though it was very cold, there was inevitably an odd smell.
The entire building was filled with this stench.
That day, ever since Jun Jia returned, he had urgently convened a meeting and devised several self-rescue plans. As Jun Jia had said, he became very busy, implementing several plans at once. Consequently, many people could be seen with tasks on their hands.
That day, following the routine roll call in the private room, Jing Shu gave Liu some instructions before she stood up with her tool in hand and left.
"Hey, wait, Jing Shu, where are you going?" Gold Dominator called out from behind.
Jing Shu turned her head and, pointing to the homemade fishing rod in her hand, said, "Fishing."
"Fishing??" Gold Dominator pointed at the rebar in Jing Shu’s hand, wanting to say something but stopping himself, his expression odd. Seeing Jing Shu about to walk away again, he said, "Wait for me, I’m coming too."
He wanted to see what Jing Shu was up to.
Jing Shu walked on ahead without a care, with Gold Dominator closely following behind.
Only after the two had left did their classmates start whispering:
"What are those two up to? Didn’t you see that thick rebar? Jing Shu holding it as if it were a real fishing rod—it’s terrifying."
"When did Brother Tyrant become Jing Shu’s shadow? Young Master Lan, you’re close with Brother Tyrant, what’s going on?"
Young Master Lan rubbed his swollen hands and said through clenched teeth, "I don’t know."
"I really envy Brother Tyrant. He has connections at home, so no one assigns him any tasks. Look at Young Master Lan, even he has to work with us."
"And I envy Jing Shu, too. She can leave the building whenever she wants without having to work."
"Why don’t they have to work?"
"Because we have to eat, so we have to work."
"It seems like Jing Shu doesn’t even go to the cafeteria to eat."
"Maybe she’s running a private cafeteria."
Jiang Changke shifted his sore elbow and said, "The bigshots naturally eat like Brother Tyrant, with small biscuits. Speaking of which, the food these days seems to be mixed with red worm cake. I eat it often and am quite familiar with it."
Many of their classmates’ eyes brightened, especially Young Master Lan, who now also had to eat the same food as everyone else.
"I heard there’s a reward for reporting hidden food supplies."
"But we’re talking about our classmates here."
"Aren’t you curious what Brother Tyrant and Jing Shu are eating? Why won’t they share some with us?"
There was a patrol team outside the building to prevent the tragedy of that day from happening again. No one was allowed to go out, and there were twenty-four-hour patrols both outside and inside, covering every corner.
"Sister Jing, got a moment?" Li Chenglong handed her a steaming hot earthen bowl of water, chuckling. "Have a drink, it’ll warm you up. It’s cold outside."
"No thanks, I have to make a trip to the periphery." Jing Shu watched as Li Chenglong called over dozens of soldiers to start a major project: filtering water. The filtered water was boiled on-site, and the soil nearby was conveniently used to make bowls.
Fuel had been resolved only recently; someone had used professional knowledge to make biogas from feces. However, it was said to be very dangerous, and a careless mistake could lead to a BOOM! Therefore, it was set up on the outermost perimeter.
This was barely a perfect cycle: over two thousand people’s daily feces were used to produce biogas for fuel, mud from the mudstone flow was filtered for water, and the remaining earth was fired into various supplies for everyday life.
However, now that everyone was eating less, even their feces had decreased significantly, with many people only relieving themselves once a week.
"Sister Jing, I’ll go with you. It’s dangerous outside, and who knows, a monster might pop out." Li Chenglong put down his hand-warming cup and walked towards the outermost area with Jing Shu.
Gold Dominator looked disdainfully at Li Chenglong,
Such a sycophant,
he thought, while quickly following Jing Shu.
The wind was strong, and everyone wrapped their clothes tighter. They quickly reached the boundary, marked by a one-meter-high wall. Jing Shu easily jumped up onto it, watching the roiling black mudstone flow continually shake and surge.
It was as magical as waves.
Their current location was akin to the stern of a large ship, with the building traveling at a thirty-five-degree angle upward, so the mudstone flow couldn’t pour in.
Otherwise, I’d really think this building was some kind of powered ship,
Jing Shu mused.
Li Chenglong also easily climbed up, scratching his head. "It’s pitch black, can’t see a thing. But my uncle says, Sister Jing, you are meant to observe the stars and do great things. If you have any difficulties, just find me, and I’ll definitely help you."
"Fishing. Let’s see if we can catch some fish." Jing Shu swung the steel bar in her hand—long, good, exactly what she needed. Then, she twirled her homemade fishing rod a few times and, using inertia, cast out a long steel wire fishing line baited with Insect Cake.
The ’fishing line’ quickly disappeared into the mudstone flow, engulfed swiftly by the black Mudstone Flow Sea as the building swayed.
Gold Dominator’s mouth fell open.
What the hell? Are they really here to fish?
Li Chenglong blinked.
Indeed, everything Sister Jing did was out of the ordinary. Though I don’t understand it, I just need to know she’s doing something important.
RUMBLE...
Li Chenglong’s stomach made an untimely noise, and he coughed awkwardly. "How about I go back for a drink of water?"
At least I can fill my stomach with water,
he thought.
Gold Dominator snorted even more disdainfully and clumsily climbed up.
RUMBLE...
Gold Dominator’s stomach growled too.
He also felt awkward.
I must have overexerted myself just now,
he thought.
The food lately has been worse than pig slop; I can’t even stomach the canteen meals.
RUMBLE...
At that moment, Jing Shu’s stomach growled as well.
This was embarrassing. The three exchanged glances for a while until Jing Shu sighed and took out some black, hard yogurt balls from her pocket, handing them to the two. "Eat this."
Li Chenglong chuckled and took a big bite.
Sister Jing truly is Sister Jing! To still have food at a time like this—impressive!
CRACK.
He almost lost a tooth, the pain bringing tears to his eyes.
"...Suck on it," Jing Shu advised. "These are yogurt balls, hard as rocks. Don’t you want your teeth anymore?"
Soon, the three of them sat on the wall, each holding a yogurt ball, sucking on it. They couldn’t rush it, nor could they bite through.
"It’s tasty but tough on the tongue," Li Chenglong complained a bit.
"Shut it," Gold Dominator said. "You’re training your tongue skills. Master that, and which girl couldn’t you charm?"
"Little Tyrant, you sure know a lot. Can tongue skills really be trained this way? Like this?"
"Be more flexible, not stiff. Use the tip of your tongue."
Jing Shu said, "Keep making such a fuss while eating these yogurt balls, and I’ll kick you both back."

chapters.title: Chapter 655: Mudslide’s Strange White Spot
chapters.content:
Chapter 655: Mudslide’s Strange White Spot
Damn it, a bunch of immature kids discussing such things and getting all worked up about it! As if I, a young woman in her prime, don’t even exist? Aren’t they supposed to be shy?
Then again, how do I know so much about this strange stuff? And why do I suddenly feel the urge to lecture these two? It’s clearly not like that; it should be like *this*, and *this*.
Jing Shu shook her head.
I’m probably overthinking it.
Indeed, after being scolded, both of them sighed in unison.
People always say that after the apocalypse, men can have countless women, one on each arm,
they thought.
Too bad we don’t have the qualifications or the guts. We really envy those novel protagonists.
"I’m just practicing out of loneliness," Gold Dominator muttered, then fell silent. He felt frustrated, pitifully possessing abilities with nowhere to use them.
Li Chenglong focused on nibbling the yogurt balls.
My God, I’ve never tasted anything so delicious! The purity of milk, that tangy, fermented aroma... it lingers endlessly on my taste buds.
The best part is how long these yogurt balls last. A bun this big, I’d usually finish in one bite. But I’ve been gnawing on this yogurt ball for half an hour, and it’s only shrunk by a tiny bit! If I get hungry, I can just take it out for a bite. It’s cold-resistant and keeps hunger away—truly perfect!
"This is so delicious, even better than the milk tea at home!" Gold Dominator exclaimed, then lamented, "If only my family could make yogurt balls too. Ah, it’s a pity. Our cow hasn’t been successfully bred recently, so milk is pitifully scarce. It’s already a blessing to get a little milk each day."
No, no, I can’t look so pathetic,
Gold Dominator thought, deliberately slowing his eating pace and putting on a haughty expression.
Ugh, I don’t want yogurt balls, I want hot pot! When can I sneak off to have some hot pot?
The three of them were each lost in their own thoughts, and for a long time, no one spoke. Only the MUNCH, MUNCH, MUNCH of their eating could be heard.
The steel rod occasionally twitched. Jing Shu arched an eyebrow, a surprised look on her face. It wasn’t that a fish was actually on the hook; she had discovered some strange things in the Mudstone Flow Sea.
Jing Shu slightly closed her eyes. Countless insects, linked one after another, followed the fishing line deep into the Mudstone Flow Sea.
Jing Shu frowned slightly, seemingly dissatisfied.
SPLASH. Jing Shu stood up, tied a dozen more ropes to the steel rod, and cast them into the Mudstone Flow Sea. Soon, the insects followed, spreading out like a net.
Gold Dominator gaped. "I’ve never seen anyone fish like this."
Li Chenglong retorted, "Sis is doing something important; you wouldn’t get it."
Jing Shu ignored the two, squinting her eyes as a pattern formed in her mind. The insects relayed the conditions in the mud, much clearer this time than when she had used only a single line.
Countless little white dots were reflected.
This is the strange part,
Jing Shu mused.
Why are there such peculiar things in the Mudstone Flow Sea?
I need to get these white dots and study them.
Naturally, it wouldn’t be as troublesome as actually fishing. Using the fishing line and the insects’ touch, I can just put these strange things directly into my space.
Just as Jing Shu directed the insects toward one of the white dots, a huge mouth suddenly roared towards them, swallowing both the white dot and the insects whole. Initially, Jing Shu still received signals, but as the huge mouth chewed rapidly, her connection was severed.
All the insects approaching the white dots had died.
Jing Shu’s expression turned grim. She directed the insects toward the other white dots, this time proceeding with extreme caution, waiting patiently near the white dots until she could see clearly.
Near each of the white spots in the Mudstone Flow Sea, there were rows of rotten mermaids!
These rotten mermaids usually remained motionless, completely indistinguishable from the mudstone flow, having become one with it. Only when they opened their mouths to feed could one tell they were rotten mermaids.
In the blink of an eye, several white spots vanished, all devoured by the rotten mermaids, who also swallowed the surrounding mud. It turned out that rotten mermaids ate not only mud but also these white spots.
Jing Shu grew even more curious.
What exactly are these white spots?
With her newfound experience, she directed more insects toward the white lights underground.
As long as they can touch these lights, I can instantly pull them into my space.
However, Jing Shu had clearly underestimated the rotten mermaids beneath the surface. It seemed every white spot was guarded by a rotten mermaid. Anytime something dared to approach the white light, the rotten mermaids would engulf the white spot along with everything around it.
The most terrifying aspect of the rotten mermaids was their teeth: six rows of gear-like structures that churned everything in their mouths like a blender, leaving no blind spots.
I initially thought that my new breed of apocalypse insects, fearing neither heaven nor earth, would at least survive in the mermaids’ mouths long enough to touch the white spots and complete their mission,
she thought.
But alas, the rotten mermaids’ saliva is also a highly corrosive mucus.
Jing Shu’s expression was grim. After several attempts, she hadn’t managed to retrieve a single white spot and had instead lost quite a few of her prized insects.
What a loss, what a real loss.
Speaking of which, just how many rotten mermaids are down there?
Jing Shu felt goosebumps rise on her skin.
It felt like drifting in a small boat on the open sea, with dense shoals of man-eating sharks circling just beneath the surface.
Even someone as powerful as Jing Shu felt her scalp tingle.
She hadn’t realized it before, but now, knowing that the area beneath the building was teeming with rotten mermaids, her mood soured considerably, and she felt a wave of revulsion. It seemed the ones that attacked the building last time were just a tiny fraction; so many more were still lurking below.
But the building is always moving. What about these rotten mermaids? Are they always moving too? Or perhaps...
A thought struck Jing Shu, one she found utterly bizarre. Could it be that these rotten mermaids have never moved? That there have always been this many? That would be truly terrifying.
"Sis, you look a bit pale. Are you cold? Shall we go back? It’s rather chilly outside," Li Chenglong voiced his concern.
Gold Dominator also shivered—it was indeed getting colder. Lately, he had stopped worrying about his appearance, wearing whatever army coats his uncle could find for him.
"Let’s head back," Jing Shu nodded, swiftly began to reel in her steel rod and retrieve the insects from the mud.
As the three of them walked back, Jing Shu turned to look at the black Mudstone Flow Sea, thinking,
I’ll come back better prepared to investigate next time.
Jing Shu suddenly had a premonition.
These white spots... they seem like some kind of treasure. Perhaps they can connect to dimensions, or even represent a form of dimensional linkage.
Upgrading my space can no longer rely solely on practicing with the Magic Cube. It requires absorbing massive amounts of energy—very likely, energy from various dimensions.
Perhaps this is an opportunity,
she thought.
No sooner had they returned to the building than they found the lobby bustling with activity.
Curious, Jing Shu wanted to see what the excitement was about, only to discover, astonishingly, that she was the center of it.
Because someone was about to search Jing Shu’s villa.

chapters.title: Chapter 656: Doesn’t Your Conscience Hurt?
chapters.content:
Chapter 656: Doesn’t Your Conscience Hurt?
I heard it was because they received a report alleging Jing Shu was hoarding food.
Liu eagerly handed Jing Shu her exclusive teacup, adding, "It’s cold outside. Have some hot water." There was no tea; they were just making do with what was available.
Li Chenglong gave Liu a thumbs-up, as if he had learned something.
Look at how attentive Liu is, no wonder Sister Jing didn’t accept my water.
Jing Shu nodded naturally as she took the water. She then looked at the two groups on either side of the villa. One was a squad from the building’s armed forces, with more than a dozen people blocking the villa’s entrance.
The other was Young Master Lan with a group of college classmates, who were there to watch the commotion. Of course, many others were crowding around as well.
"I heard someone’s hoarding food. If we find it, we’ll split it among everyone."
"How much could we even get from a split? When they go in to search, we should sneak in during the chaos and grab something for ourselves."
...
Gold Dominator snorted but instinctively felt the yogurt balls in his pocket. He didn’t want Jing Shu’s private stash to be confiscated; otherwise, he wouldn’t get any.
Li Chenglong also felt the yogurt balls in his pocket and strode forward. "What’s all the fuss about? What happened?"
Li Chenglong was the team’s second-in-command and Li Yuetian’s nephew.
"Captain Li, we received reports from these people that this villa is hoarding food," Zhang Shan replied loudly.
Gold Dominator also walked up, disgruntled, and asked Young Master Lan, "What’s going on with you guys? Got nothing better to do? Who reported it?"
Which fool dares to target my yogurt balls? No, I have to impress Jing Shu today so she’ll give me lots of yogurt balls.
No one in the crowd spoke. Jiang Changke, however, stepped forward, pointed at Young Master Lan, and said sarcastically, "It was Young Master Lan who reported it. He insisted on reporting, and I couldn’t stop him at all. We’re all classmates here; how does reporting her benefit you? You just can’t stand to see others do well."
Young Master Lan’s face turned an ashen red; he was clearly embarrassed.
The plot wasn’t supposed to go this way!
Facing Gold Dominator’s gaze, Young Master Lan stammered, "It’s not... not like that..."
"Then what is it like?" Gold Dominator demanded, hands on his hips. He scrutinized Young Master Lan, visibly dissatisfied.
I thought this guy knew how to read people and make them comfortable. I never expected him to target my yogurt balls!
Weren’t reports supposed to be anonymous? And weren’t true allegations supposed to be rewarded? Isn’t this a setup? So many people are here... And why on earth did my brain short-circuit today and make me file a report? Even if it came to the worst, couldn’t I have just sent that brainless woman, Sweet Dumpling, to her doom?
Young Master Lan couldn’t bear the infamy of ’betraying a classmate,’ so he could only say, "I was just joking. Everyone is taking it too seriously..." he said, signaling with his eyes to a few female classmates.
Jiang Changke wore an expression that said,
You expect me to believe that crap?
Young Master Lan still held a high status in the eyes of the female classmates, especially close ones like Sweet Dumpling. She stepped forward and said, "Exactly! We just wanted to see what Jing Shu had to eat."
"It was purely out of curiosity..."
Gold Dominator nodded in satisfaction and gave Li Chenglong a look. "See? It was all a joke, a misunderstanding. Let’s all disperse."
Li Chenglong was also pleased. "Alright, Zhang Shan, let’s disperse. It’s a misunderstanding."
Zhang Shan was also preparing to leave when two more people stepped out from the crowd.
"No, we can’t just let this go! This guy previously said he had evidence. She never eats in the cafeteria; she must have a private food stash!"
"Right, let’s search first!"
Young Master Lan’s face turned a shade of purplish-black.
When the hell did I ever say those things?
Fuming, Gold Dominator put his hands on his hips, ready to curse.
What the hell is Young Master Lan up to, saying such things?!
Young Master Lan shook his head vigorously. Though he didn’t care about Jing Shu, he didn’t want to offend Gold Dominator.
Strange, when did Gold Dominator start siding with Jing Shu?
At that moment, a few more people started shouting, wanting to search the villa.
Jing Shu furrowed her brows, feeling something odd about the several people who had suddenly appeared. She then glanced at a man in the crowd who had pulled his hat brim low—it was Da Ji, the one who had hidden food in the tunnel under the toilet!
After Da Ji noticed Jing Shu looking at him, he turned and walked away.
Before Jing Shu could get angry, Li Chenglong lost his temper.
Daring to oppose my Sister Jing is like opposing me!
Li Chenglong grabbed Zhang Shan’s megaphone and shouted, "Be quiet! Search the villa, my ass! I bet you just want to use the chaos to steal some good stuff! Don’t any of you want dinner tonight? I’d like to see who today dares to say Jing Shu is hoarding food and wants to search the villa! Come on, step forward, all of you!"
Jing Shu pressed her forehead.
Why has Li Chenglong started cursing people out? And why is he so worked up?
Sure enough, this prompted some people to start pushing back:
"Oh, so you officials are covering for each other now, huh? You won’t let us search the villa?"
"There must be something fishy here."
Even Young Master Lan seemed to sense an opportunity. Sweet Dumpling lowered her head and clenched her fists. She, more than anyone, wished for Jing Shu’s downfall.
Unfortunately, I don’t know what good things Jing Shu has been secretly eating lately; she’s even gained weight!
Don’t misunderstand; in the apocalypse, gaining weight is a compliment, a symbol of envy, jealousy, and hatred.
Go ahead and search,
Jing Shu thought.
Search all you want. If you find even a scrap of food, I’ll believe you. However, the villa is still full of snakes and insects. If you get bitten to death, don’t blame me!
Amidst the clamor, a gunshot suddenly rang out. Then, another team arrived.
Someone shouted, "Captain Li has come!"
Only then did the entire hall fall silent.
Li Yuetian arrived with his men. A single sharp glance from him instantly quieted the scene. He stepped onto a platform and spoke through the megaphone, "You can search. Why not? Those who just said they wanted to report and search the villa, step forward. You, you, you, and you over there—yes, you. Come stand here."
Li Yuetian pointed at several people.
Young Master Lan shook his head like a rattle drum. "I’m not reporting."
I’m not that foolish,
he thought.
The remaining few hesitated.
Li Yuetian continued, "Reporting an ordinary person isn’t this troublesome. But the Jing Shu you want to report is no ordinary person.
Right, I forgot to tell you all something. The food for the more than two thousand people in our building—all the red worm cake—is provided solely by Jing Shu.
Whether you have a next meal, and all the food everyone in our building will eat from now on, depends on Jing Shu. We will be relying on her for many days to come.
Hoarding food? She alone has provided so much food for the building, saved so many lives, and even pays out of her own pocket to give you food every day, yet you still want to report her?
Doesn’t your conscience hurt?!"
Li Yuetian’s rebuke echoed throughout the building. For a moment, the hall was utterly silent; not a soul spoke.

chapters.title: Chapter 657: It’s Because There Are Good Things
chapters.content:
Chapter 657: It’s Because There Are Good Things
Li Yuetian’s description of Jing Shu as so selflessly grand made Jing Shu, who was hidden in the shadows, feel slightly embarrassed.
Giving away food was merely a win-win situation, not charity,
she thought. Even Jun Jia, Wu City’s second-in-command, had assured her that these goods would be accounted for. The food she provided would be exchanged for points, which served as internal currency for trading within the Township Government.
Truthfully, Jing Shu was now inclined to stay here longer and use up more of her food supplies.
After all,
she mused,
the Red Worm Cakes, originally worth only 2,000,000 Virtual Coins, could eventually be exchanged for restricted items using Contribution Points.
It was very difficult to acquire Contribution Points within the Township Government.
Similar to the internal points system of the Wu City Pharmaceutical Association, the Township Government dangled attractive prospects: the highest accumulation of points could be exchanged for unimaginably top-notch items.
But the people in the hall didn’t know that. After hearing this, many felt ashamed.
"So all the food we’ve been eating these days was provided by her."
"We’ve been trapped here so long. We would have starved without food."
"We owe our lives to her."
"Now, all the food we can eat is provided by her; how could that be called hoarding private stock?"
Li Yuetian was pleased with this outcome. He then pointed to the person who had just wanted to report Jing Shu for hoarding food and asked, "To think you would accuse the very person supplying food to the entire building of hoarding...
"Very well, we are the fairest of all. You few who yelled about searching the villa, no more food will be provided to you from now on. Fend for yourselves. Li Chenglong, take these people inside to search and see if there’s any food."
Upon hearing from Li Yuetian that there would be no more food, not even Insect Cakes, and that they would starve to death, these people’s faces immediately changed.
"We won’t search anymore, we won’t!"
"We were just joking. We didn’t know that Miss Jing Shu was the one providing us with food. She is our lifesaver. We were blind and failed to recognize a great person like yourself. Please spare us this time."
"I won’t search either. I was just joining in on the commotion. I don’t know why I impulsively did such a foolish thing just now."
The few who had been clamoring and stirring up trouble instantly changed their tune. They certainly knew they had provoked someone they shouldn’t have and now realized their food supply was on the line.
Li Yuetian’s expression cooled. "Rather than causing a stir here, you’d be better off doing more work. Then you might get to eat more." After saying that, he walked away with his group.
Li Chenglong chuckled. "Have you seen enough? Or shall we invite everyone to cool off outside?"
The crowd’s expressions changed again, and they dispersed quickly.
The college classmates were shocked beyond measure. The new revelation was overwhelming: all the food these past days and the subsequent meals of Insect Cakes in the coming days were sourced from their unassuming classmate, Jing Shu.
Jiang Changke boasted, "Still envious of Jing Shu, the big shot who doesn’t need to work, huh? Well, she indeed has the capital not to work."
Whether she was hoarding private stock or not didn’t matter anymore. After all, so many people in the building depended on Jing Shu.
The crucial point now was that to survive and eat their fill, they would have to rely on Jing Shu.
Jing Shu wanted to keep a low profile and was inclined to say
it was no big deal,
but at this moment, the way her classmates looked at her had already changed. Several were quickly sidling up to her:
"Jing Shu, could you spare a few more Insect Cakes?"
"I can’t believe you’re such a big shot, Jing Shu! Please support me; I can even warm your bed!"
"I’m an electric motor, the frequency of which can be adjusted—fast or slow, shallow or deep. They call me ’Mazda.’ Consider me."
"TSK."
Jing Shu fled. Interacting with her classmates after her identity had been exposed made Jing Shu a bit uncomfortable.
Now when she looked at people, her first thought was:
Are you getting close to me because you want my Insect Cakes? Are you interested in my Insect Cakes, or in me as a person?
Jing Shu admitted that she somewhat understood the Emperor’s feeling of ’it’s lonely at the top’ and his yearning for a true confidant.
But that didn’t stop Jing Shu from hiding in her villa, secretly indulging in extra meals that left her mouth greasy with oil. When she had nothing to do, she would pick a cucumber from her space to eat on the spot, or cut open a watermelon to scoop out and enjoy. Or she might have some fruit after a meal, choosing whatever she fancied—oranges, peaches, lychees, or strawberries.
Her only small regret was that durians smelled too strong, so she didn’t dare to eat them.
The following days were much more peaceful. No one came to trouble Jing Shu, and life seemed to return to an orderly rhythm.
Everyone had things to do.
Jing Shu was woken by the whistle every day, almost wishing she could take back the yogurt balls she had given Li Chenglong. It was he who roused everyone at 7:00 AM daily to gather in the main hall for roll call.
It was just like the militarized discipline of past military training.
She couldn’t sleep in even if she wanted to. Jing Shu’s days were quite comfortable. At night, she slept in a thick silk sleeping bag, with snakes and insects standing guard. Her nights in the silent villa were incredibly peaceful; if only she didn’t have to get up so early.
Jing Shu had gotten used to appearing with bed hair in the first-floor private room for roll call. This was followed by a ten-minute routine meeting, which generally covered yesterday’s progress, today’s plans, and a brief summary.
Afterward, everyone would go to the cafeteria to eat.
Jing Shu used to be more discreet, but ever since that incident, she had Liu openly bring her meals back to the villa. Jing Shu would then return to her villa, take a nap, and then get up to do her ’real work.’
This ’real work’ involved taking a large assortment of tools to go fishing.
These days, Jing Shu’s collection of ’tools’ had grown, and she had even transformed her fishing spot into a proper ’office.’
Indeed, around the perimeter wall outside the building, she had built herself a wind-sheltered earthen hut—of course, hiring the workers had cost her some Insect Cakes. Wanting to keep the opportunity within her own group, she naturally hired her college classmates.
Inside the hut was an earthen kang, heated from below, where Jing Shu usually sat, feeling warm. Next to the kang, she had also built a small earthen stove. She usually kept a teapot on it, boiling water for tea and adding yogurt balls and milk powder.
The tea and milk bubbled and mixed, transforming into a fragrant milk tea that warmed both her hands and her stomach.
In front of the hut now stood a row of steel bars, wrapped with various electrical wires or netting, and beside them were a small generator and a small motor.
These were borrowed from Dr. Chao Zhang. To thank Jing Shu for finding the Bone Powder that had resolved the issue of uncontrollable bleeding, Dr. Zhang had also generously provided the raw materials.
CRACKLE. CRACKLE.
Electricity surged through the wires, extending deep into the soil of the Mudstone Flow Sea. Li Chenglong and the others didn’t understand why Jing Shu was doing this.
Jing Shu never explained.
No one understood, but then again, no one was foolish enough to ask. Nobody could control what Jing Shu did. In others’ eyes, why would Jing Shu forsake the comfort of her villa to endure the cold wind and suffer out here?
Yes, why indeed?
Naturally, it was because there was something good to be found out here.

chapters.title: Chapter 658: White Energy
chapters.content:
Chapter 658: White Energy
"Otherwise, why would we endure such cold weather, spending so much time and so many tools, just to come here and get nothing for our pains?"
Jing Shu had been anxious a few days ago. Being trapped on such a vast, deserted island was daunting.
What if I can never return?
But ever since she discovered this wonderful thing, Jing Shu had actually stopped worrying.
She even began to treat it as a daily job, one to be completed diligently. If not for her inherent laziness and fear of arousing suspicion, Jing Shu would have gladly stayed in the small earthen hut twenty-four hours a day.
Few things could capture Jing Shu’s interest now.
Unexpectedly, the white dots in the Mudstone Flow Sea turned out to be a special type of energy body.
Jing Shu had previously scoured for black energy and red energy. Each demonstrated different purposes and abilities, belonging to a type of Dimension Energy, and each possessed strong regional specificity, rarity, and uniqueness.
Jing Shu found it quite regrettable that she hadn’t encountered anything like those energies again outside of those specific regions.
Therefore, Jing Shu named this elusive Dimension Energy: White Energy. They varied in size. Each newly born white dot was guarded by a rotten mermaid until it matured, after which the rotten mermaid would consume it.
The Magic Cube Space’s ability to upgrade was largely thanks to finding such energies. Naturally, this White Energy also presented an opportunity for it to upgrade.
What was bothersome was the new requirement for the Magic Cube Space to upgrade. Not only did she have to meet the stringent condition of restoring it within a set time, but she also had to infuse it with a type of Dimension Energy.
The appearance of White Energy was therefore like a timely rain.
So, Jing Shu was naturally no longer in a hurry. It would be best to collect enough energy to allow the Magic Cube Space to upgrade.
"It’s a pity, the process is too slow," she said.
Relying on her own snail-like collection speed, progress was too slow. It was nowhere near as fast as that time in the United States when she had directly absorbed crystallized energy into her space.
"Rome wasn’t built in a day; we can only proceed slowly," she mused aloud.
After all, with milk tea to drink and beef jerky to eat, and occasionally indulging in braised lion’s head meatballs and spicy crayfish, life was quite comfortable.
If conditions allowed, Jing Shu really wanted to set up a spit to roast a suckling pig or a whole lamb. She had a new batch of piglets in her space, and lamb was readily available. Besides, in this cold weather, cooking a pot of turnip and lamb stew and sipping the hot broth would be excellent.
Slowly simmering it over a low heat, letting it bubble away, would be perfect right now. Unfortunately, the enticing aroma could drift for hundreds of meters, growing more fragrant as it spread, and Jing Shu didn’t dare risk it.
"Alas," Jing Shu sighed. "In this confined place with no freedom, getting a good meal is so difficult."
Through a few days of exploration, Jing Shu had already discovered some clues about White Energy’s uses. If red energy had an effect related to the ancestral gene, then White Energy possessed Healing abilities.
But it wasn’t merely for healing.
Well, after studying these energies, Jing Shu found they had both beneficial and negative aspects.
The negative effect was that it caused the consumer’s body to become extremely stiff, essentially petrifying them.
A chicken in Jing Shu’s space had been petrified, which made her sad for a long time.
Isn’t Beggar’s Chicken tasty? Or is Dapan Chicken not delicious? What a complete waste of a chicken.
The petrified chicken was useless, like a plain white stone sculpture that would chip if tapped.
The fat black creature in the space ate just as much as before. However, a boar Jing Shu was about to slaughter, having not consumed many White Energy Points, was now completely stiff. It had to hop when it walked, just like a Zombie. Jing Shu even wondered if she had inadvertently invented a new creature: the hopping Zombie pig.
Can it still be slaughtered and eaten?
Jing Shu planned to wait a bit longer.
For now, it seemed White Energy had no other use besides upgrading the space. However, this single purpose was enough to make Jing Shu willingly stay here and collect it.
However, the rotten mermaids in the Mudstone Flow Sea ate the White Energy happily. They were neither petrified nor stiff. Instead, they were invulnerable to physical attacks, like creatures made of mud, yet very sensitive to electricity, as if made of water. Crucially, they had also developed some kind of bleeding ’BUFF’ ability.
Jing Shu gazed at the perpetually flowing Mudstone Flow Sea, lost in thought.
Is the rotten mermaids’ resistance to petrification related to the mud in this area?
Suddenly, Jing Shu sat upright.
She opened her eyes wide, as if she had seen something incredible in this dark world.
"Impossible!" Jing Shu exclaimed.
The long row of rebar was quite a sight. These wires extended deep into the Mudstone Flow Sea, forming a giant net that acted like Jing Shu’s eyes, allowing her to sense the world below.
There was a moderate number of White Energy Points. Each was closely guarded by a menacing rotten mermaid. However, ever since Jing Shu learned how to conduct electricity down into the depths, she had always been able to snatch the energy from right under their noses.
But today, the area beneath the building was densely packed with White Energy Points. In Jing Shu’s sensory perception, the space was almost entirely dominated by White Energy.
Jing Shu didn’t even need to exert much effort; simply dropping some wires down was enough to reach these White Energy Points.
So many of them.
Yet, Jing Shu could not feel happy; her face turned unusually grim.
This was so much White Energy—more than all she had seen in many days combined! It meant the surroundings were teeming with countless rotten mermaids!
Have we drifted into the rotten mermaids’ main nest?
Jing Shu could hardly imagine the scene if all the rotten mermaids were to swarm ashore at this moment. Without a doubt, it would lead to total annihilation for everyone here.
Fortunately, at this moment, the rotten mermaids seemed more interested in the White Energy Points.
No, this is far too dangerous compared to before,
Jing Shu worried, even as she carefully harvested the nearly mature White Energy Points. She would electrocute a rotten mermaid and then snatch the White Energy from its mouth.
According to Jing Shu’s observations, when not threatened, the rotten mermaids would only consume a White Energy Point every few days. This coincided exactly with the time it took for White Energy to regenerate from below.
They continued this cycle endlessly.
Jing Shu moved quickly. The sudden disappearance of the White Energy confused the rotten mermaids. With their low intelligence, once they recovered from being stunned and found the White Energy gone, they would simply swim off to find new sources.
Jing Shu had planned to capture a few live rotten mermaids to study in her space. Theoretically, she should have been able to transfer them directly into her space, but all her attempts had failed. The space strongly repelled some kind of energy they possessed.
Could it be due to dimensional reasons?
Jing Shu speculated.
"Sister Jing Shu, my uncle is calling for you! Hurry and come with me!" Li Chenglong’s voice rang out. He could be seen running from afar, clearly in a rush.
Jing Shu frowned. She didn’t want to leave; the Magic Cube Space needed to be upgraded as soon as possible.
"What’s the matter?"

chapters.title: Chapter 659: Jing Shu, can you solve this problem?
chapters.content:
Chapter 659: Jing Shu, can you solve this problem?
"To be honest, even if there was something, Jing Shu wouldn’t be able to help."
Li Chenglong quickly ran to the front of the house. While inwardly marveling at how his sister, as expected of her, managed such an impressive setup, he said, "After observing for so many days, we have a new development regarding our position. My uncle just asked for you to come over to discuss our next survival plan."
Hearing this, Jing Shu hurriedly got up and followed Li Chenglong to the seventh floor of the building, which was Boss Lu’s territory.
This was Jing Shu’s first visit here; Boss Lu had built a titanium alloy, fully enclosed little house that resembled a safe in this hidden room, and no one knew what was inside. Although Jing Shu was very curious, she hadn’t had the time to pay attention to it until now.
The gathering place today was once a hotpot restaurant before the apocalypse and now lay in ruins. The bright red decor, coupled with faint firelight, seemed a bit unsettling.
Only some large round tables and the empty twin-sided hot pots in the middle remained in the hall.
Many wooden chairs had been taken to be used as firewood.
Even the large red curtains and dividers that were previously for decoration had been taken to use as blankets.
"Just find a seat anywhere," Li Yuetian, who was sitting on the twin-sided hot pot placed on a platform, told the incoming Jing Shu and Li Chenglong.
Jing Shu felt it was a pity—should she swipe a pot later so she could enjoy a twin-sided hot pot meal in the future?
Once everyone in the hall had arrived, some were squatting on the tables while others lay on them. The most extravagant was Boss Lu, who had turned a large round table into a giant bed, comfortably lying on it, yawning under a thick blanket.
Apart from Jun Jia, Gold Dominator, Wang Miao, and other people from the Township Government that Jing Shu knew, the rest were Boss Lu’s people!
An old man with a bald head was holding a door plank, writing and drawing intensely on it. When he turned around, Jing Shu recognized him—it was her old college principal, Wang Zhiren!
"Let me explain in detail our current position. It’s a bit complex..." Old Principal Wang Zhiren, holding his data results, was about to begin his lengthy discourse when he was interrupted by Boss Lu.
Extremely dissatisfied, Boss Lu said, "We don’t understand those things anyway. Don’t make it so complicated. Just tell us bluntly where we are and how to get back to Wu City, and that’s it."
Old Principal Wang sighed awkwardly. "According to the time differences observed in the earliest days, we should have continued drifting westward, but..."
"But what? Hurry up, old man, you’re making us anxious," Boss Lu urged.
"But the time difference was sometimes earlier, sometimes later, according to..." The old principal rambled on and on, and Boss Lu was completely lost, as were the academically challenged folks around him.
So, where were they exactly?
Li Yuetian said in a deep voice, "So what Principal Wang means is, we were drifting before, and now we’ve been circling around this spot in recent days?"
Principal Wang wiped the sweat off his forehead. These people didn’t even understand basic geography. Being a math teacher asked to teach geography was indeed exhausting.
Luckily, he was highly learned and knowledgeable.
These people are even worse than the worst students I’ve ever taught.
Just as he was thinking this, Old Principal Wang saw a familiar figure in the crowd.
Hey, isn’t that student Jing Shu? She’s the one who got me a private room. And afterward, that young man, Liu, diligently helped me move my luggage and has been quite attentive these past few days...
Old Principal Wang cleared his throat and shook his head. "It is not that simple..."
Aiya, these people, no matter how I explain it, they just don’t get it!
He scratched his head, his occupational habit flaring up again. "Miss Jing Shu, please come up and explain this problem to everyone."
After he finished speaking, the principal realized something was a bit off.
But Jing Shu had already walked up. She took the homemade pen from Old Principal Wang, flipped the door plank to its other side, and then drew a large circle, followed by successively smaller circles inside it, spiraling inwards until she finally dotted the very center.
The line flowed uninterrupted until it reached the center of the circles, resembling the ’@’ symbol.
Jing Shu looked very serious. For many days, she too hadn’t understood why. Initially, for over ten days, the time difference indicated they were drifting in one direction. Then, for another ten-plus days, it seemed to revert. Later, the cycle shortened to seven or eight days, then five or six, and finally to a three or four-day period.
It wasn’t until today, after Old Principal Wang’s explanation, that she had an epiphany.
"See this diagram? This is the route we’ve been taking these days.
We are just circling like this, from originally taking ten to twenty days for a big circle to now, where a small circle might not even take a day. That explains why the time difference is so strange."
This diagram of Jing Shu’s was so simple that even someone as academically challenged as Boss Lu could understand it. He nodded in realization. "So, how do we return to Wu City now? How can we get in touch with the people in Wu City?"
Jing Shu shook her head. "Right now, the problem isn’t whether we can return to Wu City. It’s the danger that’s coming next."
"Danger? What danger?" Boss Lu had grown accustomed to comfort. After so many days, aside from that one monster attack, everything else had been quite peaceful.
"We might be pulled into a vortex, and that speed will increase, and then..." Jing Shu didn’t finish her sentence. The current danger didn’t just come from the vortex. Beneath the building swarmed numerous Rotten Mermaids, and if they climbed up again, total annihilation was inevitable.
The Magic Cube Space couldn’t admit people, and by then, Jing Shu herself might be done for.
Although Jing Shu had an ace up her sleeve, she wouldn’t reveal it until everyone else was dead. Her secret couldn’t be disclosed to anyone. Essentially, the worst-case scenario would be total annihilation, and her ace could, at best, only save herself.
Only then did everyone grasp the seriousness of the situation.
Nothing survives the eye of a vortex storm.
Old Principal Wang nodded in satisfaction, having finally conveyed the message he intended to express.
Surely, she was a student he had taught... well, he hadn’t actually taught her, but having spoken to her counts as teaching, right?
"AHEM." Principal Wang cleared his throat and continued, "According to the timeline, we’ll be at the storm’s eye in two days. What conditions will prevail there, I can’t say. The building might sink, or there might be a new way out. My suggestion is, we can’t just sit and wait to die; we at least have to try and control our direction and avoid being drawn into the vortex’s center."
The building was like an island. How could one control the direction of such a building?
"Ships weighing several tens of tons need huge anchors and propellers to steer. How can we steer such a large island?"
Jun Jia spoke up, "Actually, we’ve been fashioning a massive makeshift rudder using all the steel and materials we could dismantle. Maybe we can deviate a bit in our course."
Wang Miao then added, "We have also organized a team and made emergency floating vessels. If it really comes to it, we might have to abandon the building!"
Abandon the building? Jing Shu’s mobile villa was still on the building.

chapters.title: Chapter 660: Jing Shu was Stunned
chapters.content:
Chapter 660: Jing Shu was Stunned
The building couldn’t be abandoned unless absolutely necessary. Even if they considered the worst-case scenario, Jing Shu did not want to experience another migration as arduous as trekking through a landslide, walking all the way back to Wu City.
However heavy a snail’s shell may be, it is still its home.
Jing Shu’s thoughts drifted far away. She hadn’t quite understood what they discussed later; she figured that given the limited conditions, they probably couldn’t have settled on much anyway. It wasn’t until Old Principal Wang gently patted her on the shoulder, reminiscing about the touching incident from the last graduation ceremony four or five years ago—when he and Jing Shu had even taken a photo together—that she snapped back to reality.
"I came to the auction this time too. Who knew it would be such a coincidence?" the old principal lamented his bad luck.
Returning to her senses, Jing Shu asked, "What are you here to bid for?"
Old Principal Wang looked like he had neither money nor power.
"Uh... the authorities agreed that I could take the last batch of wooden desks, chairs, and door panels to auction them off, so we could make ends meet and exchange them for some food... as payment for the teachers who taught online classes..." Principal Wang said with shame. Strictly speaking, they were part of the education department and considered official employees. Yet now, they had been reduced to selling school supplies.
There was no choice. Students now attended school without paying tuition, the supplies allocated by the higher-ups were scarce, and most importantly, the times had forced their physics teachers to learn how to develop APPs, and language teachers had to learn how to farm vegetables and correct homework on APPs.
Even he, as a math teacher, had to keep up with the times.
It’s tough,
he thought.
Jing Shu nodded.
Aside from being a bit of a chatterbox and liking to lecture people, Old Principal Wang is a responsible and good principal.
"Have you sold the items?"
Old Principal Wang shook his head. "It’s not my turn yet."
"Send them to me later, alright? I’ll exchange Insect Cakes for them."
The expanded Insect Cake Factory just happened to need some desks and chairs, and the employee dormitories needed door panels.
Old Principal Wang excitedly agreed.
「...」
The atmosphere in the building was a bit cold. These days, their food was merely Insect Cake boiled with water into a paste; even foods like green algae were gone. It was evident that they were truly eating into their reserves. If they ran out of Insect Cake, they would genuinely have nothing left.
Li Yuetian had increased the workload, and after he dealt with a few people who didn’t want to work, it became even quieter.
Jing Shu could almost see the numbness in these people, their lives as unchanging as those of the walking dead. They didn’t realize that, at this moment, they were in great danger.
Even her usually chatty college classmates had become much quieter. The massive amount of work kept them constantly moving in the cold weather, and hunger and fatigue dominated most of their lives, leaving them no time to dwell on other things.
Except for that pest, Gold Dominator.
Every day, he held two energetic Jinhua Pigs in a private room in the first-floor lobby, talking to himself as he continuously stroked the pigs with gentle movements.
He even brought the sow with him wherever he went, abandoning the little bear he used to carry.
Jing Shu had initially thought Gold Dominator had some strange fetish for pigs. That was until she saw him drooling uncontrollably one time, hastily wiping it away when he noticed her looking.
Only then did Jing Shu realize this boy was craving meat—craving it so terribly he was on the verge of madness, his eyes practically green with desire. Look at this poor child.
That very night, Jing Shu roasted a suckling pig in her space, satisfying her craving. This was a new method she’d devised: barbecuing directly within her space.
The downside is that the smoke and smell can’t disperse, contaminating two cubic meters of my space. I’ll have to wait until I’m in an open area to vent it.
"Hmm?"
Having eaten her fill, Jing Shu had contentedly gone to bed. Tomorrow might bring a tough battle, but just at this critical moment, one of the snakes she had released sent her a signal.
Da Ji? He should be asleep. What mischief is he up to now?
Jing Shu yawned as she got up and gathered her things. Leaving the comfort of her down quilt, Jing Shu shivered.
It’s really cold.
Ever since she had started suspecting there was something off about Da Ji, Jing Shu had one of her snakes watching him. These past few days, he had been relatively well-behaved, aside from occasionally sneaking into the underground tunnel to pilfer some of his hoarded food. Jing Shu didn’t care for such petty thievery, so she hadn’t bothered with it.
Little Snake followed Da Ji out of his single room and up to the seventh floor of the building—Boss Lu’s territory.
Ever since the invasion of the rotten mermaids, the building was patrolled around the clock. But, whether due to Da Ji’s sheer luck or something else, he managed to reach the seventh floor without encountering any patrols.
Jing Shu followed quietly.
I need to see what Da Ji is up to.
Apart from the sound of snoring, there were few other sounds in the building. With so much work to do during the day, not enough to eat, and no entertainment at night, everyone slept like logs.
Da Ji tiptoed to the first room—a conference room converted from a hotpot restaurant. He went to what used to be the back kitchen and began searching the wall, tapping here and knocking there.
Jing Shu followed him in, casually picking up a fairly clean mandarin duck pot from a corner.
I’ll have a hotpot later, spicy on one side and mushroom broth on the other.
Although the building was pitch black due to a lack of resources, the darkness couldn’t obstruct Jing Shu’s vision; she could clearly see Da Ji moving with a specific target in mind.
He’s looking for Boss Lu’s sealed room! The one without even a seam, right behind that wall!
Jing Shu’s expression turned peculiar. She had originally planned to just go back to bed; after all, that room was always kept shut. Her insects had scoured everywhere but had found no way to penetrate it.
Should I have my insects try to bore a hole? But what is that material? It looks like stainless steel rebar that even bullets probably couldn’t pierce.
Just as this thought crossed her mind, a commotion started in the building. Then, Jing Shu heard a rustling sound and, to her astonishment, a rotten mermaid fell from the ventilation duct.
One, two, three...
These rotten mermaids were slightly smaller than the previous ones, but not by much. Their objective was clear: they were all crawling toward that seemingly impregnable room.
Jing Shu was thoroughly shocked.
Holy crap! Holy crap! Could Da Ji be controlling these rotten mermaids?
Just as she was wondering this, a terrified scream pierced the silence.
"Don’t come near! AAAHHH— Help me!" Da Ji’s screams echoed throughout the entire building. He cowered in a far corner, so scared he was trembling. Meanwhile, his voice drew the attention of the patrol and Boss Lu’s men.
Jing Shu clearly saw Da Ji’s terrified expression and his trembling legs.
What in the world is happening?!
Jing Shu was stunned.
So Da Ji *can’t* control these rotten mermaids?
CRACK! A rotten mermaid took a huge bite out of the wall plaster, revealing a bit of the steel room inside.

chapters.title: Chapter 661: Boss Lu’s Steel House
chapters.content:
Chapter 661: Boss Lu’s Steel House
One after another, all the rotten mermaids began gnawing at the outer covering of the structure, revealing the room inside, which was made of unknown materials. This outer covering seemed extremely fragile in the rotten mermaids’ mouths; a few bites were enough to eat away a section. They could even consume materials like dirt mixed with rebar, turning it into food!
This genuinely surprised Jing Shu. She hadn’t expected the rotten mermaids’ biting power to be so formidable. She wondered if it had something to do with their saliva. However, as apocalyptic Dark Creatures that fed on White Energy, their great power likely stemmed from their access to it.
"Such ability not used for digging tunnels is truly a waste."
In fact, Jing Shu had already reached an agreement with insect woman Xiao Wei. If things went as planned, they would increase the reproduction of the Engineer Insects and those specialized in digging tunnels. If everything went according to the normal schedule, the insects should have been bred by now and started digging a tunnel. The tunnel project was massive, stretching from Wu City towards the distant south.
This was one of the preparations Jing Shu was making for the migration of Wu City. However, she had been trapped on this deserted island for one or two months now and didn’t know if Xiao Wei had initiated the project. Furthermore, the task was enormous. Even if Xiao Wei’s insects were proficient tunnel diggers, the project might not reach the south by next year.
"However, if a large number of rotten mermaids could also dig tunnels, that would greatly increase the chances."
"If the migration later took place through the tunnel instead of braving the cold weather outside, fewer people would freeze to death. They also wouldn’t encounter as many terrifying Dark Creatures, and the journey could be much faster."
The most important thing was to scout the route first, as the earth’s plates might shift, and prior knowledge would be crucial for issuing warnings.
When Jing Shu looked at the rotten mermaids again, her eyes lit up. While the rotten mermaids weren’t as versatile as Xiao Wei’s insects—which could both eat meat and dig tunnels—they were at least plentiful.
Regrettably, how could she tame so many rotten mermaids? Even if she used the power of space, Jing Shu could not control too many, which would be akin to a drop in the bucket.
"How can I make the rotten mermaids work for me?"
Jing Shu wondered, resting her chin in her hand as she watched a rotten mermaid snap vigorously at the steel house.
CRUNCH! SCREEECH!
Harsh, straining sounds erupted, like heavy metal clashing. However, the rotten mermaids’ teeth soon snapped off. Many lost their teeth biting the room, which appeared to be made of steel. But they seemed to feel no pain. Even with their teeth broken, they continued to ram their bodies against the house.
Jing Shu could clearly see that the steel room, many centimeters thick, had been dented and mangled by their bites.
The dumbfounded Da Ji trembled and hid in a corner. It was as if a realization had struck him, yet he looked at these rotten mermaids with even greater confusion.
Meanwhile, the patrol and Boss Lu’s men heard the sounds and rushed over with flashlights. Jing Shu quietly found a dark corner to observe, simultaneously releasing more insects to scout the surroundings.
The rotten mermaids below the building were restless but hadn’t climbed onto the shore. So where did these rotten mermaids suddenly appearing from the ventilation outlet come from? Da Ji looked bewildered, then fell into deep thought.
Why were the rotten mermaids ignoring Da Ji and so intent on gnawing this hard building? What was their purpose?
The people in the building already had experience dealing with such creatures. They grabbed electric batons, torches, Fire Bottles, and shields, rushing forward without a word to shock the creatures’ eyes and burn their mouths.
As for this batch of uninvited guests, the eyes of the other rotten mermaids glowed green. They immediately charged, attacking what they saw as delicacies. In that instant, they reverted to their bestial nature and indulged in frenzied violence. However, another group of rotten mermaids continued to attack the steel house.
The two sides quickly engaged in battle. More rotten mermaids kept pouring out of the ventilation shaft. However, the building’s inhabitants were experienced and employed various electrical and fire attacks, leading to a temporary stalemate.
Jing Shu heard Li Chenglong’s shouts and the building’s alarm. The numbers on both sides were steadily increasing.
"So... what was the reason?"
Jing Shu frowned, clearly puzzled. She looked at Da Ji and suddenly saw excitement, greed, and disbelief in his eyes.
Da Ji, who had initially been worried about being bitten, quietly crept closer to a corner of the steel house. He stared intently at the structure as if it were a treasure trove.
What wonderful things might be inside?
he wondered.
Could there be piles of white rice and white flour? Or perhaps mouth-watering hams?
"Sausages! I really want some sausages!" Da Ji muttered, saliva dripping from his mouth.
Jing Shu was speechless.
CRACK...
The fully armored steel room, under the relentless attacks of numerous rotten mermaids, gradually gave way. It was forcibly deformed and dented to an extreme angle before it cracked open, and the rest followed inevitably.
An incredulous Da Ji’s face lit up with wild joy. Amidst the chaos, he crawled inside, and his uproarious laughter soon followed. Jing Shu, hidden in the darkness, slowly approached him. No one paid attention to this area. Everyone’s focus was on the rotten mermaids.
In the dim light, Da Ji felt bag after bag of sealed rice. He looked around the small room, which was filled with a variety of foods. The light was too dim, so he fumbled to identify each item. It was unbelievable! "Smoked chicken! My favorite smoked chicken! My favorite sausages... This is wonderful, so wonderful!"
This place was a food paradise, filled with foods that were almost extinct in the apocalypse. Almost everything he loved to eat was here.
My God, am I dreaming?
A dim light suddenly switched on, and a gun was pressed against Da Ji’s head. Da Ji struggled to lift his head and saw Boss Lu, his face ashen, wearing a bathrobe.
"Do you think you’ll live long enough to eat any of this?" Boss Lu snarled through gritted teeth. He scrutinized the oblivious man before him, then mournfully looked at his ’Doomsday Fortress.’ It had cost a fortune to build and had just been breached by these creatures after only a few minutes of continuous attack.
He had whimsically constructed this impregnable secret place when he renovated the building before the apocalypse. Originally, he’d thought that if he were ever chased for debts or attacked, he could hide here. He had prepared enough supplies, food, and weapons for one person for ten years. After the apocalypse, he had secretly continued to stock it with good things, never daring to indulge himself. He had endured the hardships of the apocalypse for so long, yet he’d never brought himself to use the supplies inside. Instead, he had guarded the building, refusing to leave, largely because this iron behemoth was immovable. But today, unexpectedly, these creatures had pried it open. And the worst part? This man before him was trying to freeload?

chapters.title: Chapter 662: Da Ji’s Miraculous Ability
chapters.content:
Chapter 662: Da Ji’s Miraculous Ability
Whoever dared to target his prized possession was after Boss Lu’s life! Especially at this moment, the sudden intrusion into his carefully constructed Doomsday Fortress signaled that his secrets could no longer be concealed.
Boss Lu’s face was filled with malevolence. He wanted this person dead!
Da Ji’s cold sweat came pouring down. He hadn’t expected that even after opening this contraption, there would still be someone inside. He pleaded with a mournful face, "Wait, don’t kill me... This is a misunderstanding, listen to me..."
Unperturbed, he pulled down his hat brim and touched the lumps around his neck, all the while screaming in his mind,
Help, help, someone come save me, can’t those damn monsters come to my rescue?
In a dark corner, Jing Shu squinted her eyes, quietly observing everything. She wanted to watch a bit longer, feeling that there was something odd about this man named Da Ji. She had a premonition that this disaster, as well as the rotten mermaids, might be related to him.
Perhaps he really possessed some peculiar ability. One could not be too careful.
Just then, several rotten mermaids at the doorway suddenly began hammering against the iron scrap like mad. Given how small the opening was and the larger bodies of the mermaids, the big heads of the rotten mermaids got stuck halfway through the hole, their grotesque faces pushing forward as they opened and closed their mouths.
They wanted to come in, but couldn’t.
Boss Lu was also startled, nearly dropping his weapon. However, seeing the situation, he slowly exhaled. He glanced at the intruder in front of him, narrowed his eyes, and decided to deal with this immediate trouble first—his secret inside could not be exposed.
Previously, the Township Government knew he was hoarding things, but they didn’t know he had hoarded so much. Both parties needed to exploit each other, so stepping back was feasible. But now, if this were to be discovered, it would not be so simple. This was his assurance for the latter half of his life. He couldn’t take risks.
The gun was slowly raised.
Da Ji’s face fell, looking even more miserable than if he were crying.
Even though Da Ji seemed to have predicted something—that these monsters would indeed do something he desperately wanted—the monsters couldn’t enter right now and couldn’t save him.
Da Ji suddenly knelt down, began to beg for mercy, and started saying nice things. He absolutely had no designs on the things inside. He just wanted to be let go...
At this life-or-death moment, Da Ji’s memories flashed through his mind like a fast-forwarded movie.
The oddity of it all started the day of the auction.
As an outsider, bluntly put, he was a merchant in the apocalypse who shuttled back and forth trading local apocalyptic products to earn a meager livelihood, handling his business carefully and cautiously.
So on the day of the auction, he checked every nook and cranny, and thus accidentally discovered a special place on the seventh floor.
He originally thought it was just a secret compartment. Unable to resist the urge to investigate, he chiseled at the corner of the wall and accidentally unearthed a fist-sized white insect.
The sight gave him a huge fright. He chiseled it down instantly, splashing white fluid all over his face. Irritated, he prepared to throw away the insect, not expecting it to still be alive. It suddenly sprang up, wriggling its body, hopping around like a shrimp, and leapt onto his neck...
It bit into his neck. OUCH!
Da Ji reached to pull the insect off, but to his dismay, it burrowed directly into his flesh. Soon after, the building began to shake...
It was only after Da Ji was summoned to the hall that he discovered a lump on his neck, which, no matter what he tried, could not be removed, as if it had grown into his flesh.
Later, Da Ji discovered something unusual. Whenever he had a strong desire in his heart, for some reason, it would come true through various coincidences, and it would involve those monsters.
Those who mocked him, the people who teamed up to bully him—all died, bitten to death.
Oh, one did not die, but he lost his lower body, which was almost the same as being dead.
Da Ji tried three times, and three times his wishes came true, except for once when he wanted to see what was in that woman’s villa, and it didn’t happen.
I want to survive, save me, I don’t want to die!
Da Ji shouted in his mind, frantically pinching the tumor on his neck.
All of this is related to that white insect!
CRACKLE... The rotten mermaid at the cave entrance was electrocuted. Then, a faint light revealed another woman walking in—it was her!
Da Ji’s pupils shrank sharply. "Save me, save me!"
"Who is it!" Boss Lu pulled out another gun and aimed it at the person coming in. He was very sensitive now. More and more people were learning his secret!
I should kill them all!
Jing Shu slowly walked in. It was chaos outside, so temporarily, no one had noticed this. However, with such a large secret room exposed, it was no longer a secret.
"Ah. I guess when they finish fighting outside, they’ll come over," Jing Shu said, staring at Boss Lu and then glancing at Da Ji on the floor, a hint of confusion in her eyes.
"Don’t be nervous, Boss Lu. It’s me," Jing Shu said softly. Her voice carried a calming quality, and under its subtle influence, Boss Lu paused, momentarily stunned.
In the dim light, a droplet shot out, a strange smell spreading throughout the small room.
In just those few seconds, the fluids from the two little cuties in her hand had covered the entire room, and they had silently transferred into Boss Lu’s body.
For a long time now, Jing Shu’s little cuties had not had a chance to be used, which was a pity. They had a great advantage, capable of completely controlling a person in a short time, killing invisibly; even professional Doctors couldn’t detect the cause of death.
The biggest disadvantage was that they could only control one person at a time and had a limited range; for instance, they couldn’t control Boss Lu from such a distance just now.
While Jing Shu’s additional ability of suggestion was also very functional, it could only guide, not achieve complete control like this. And for what came next, she would need Boss Lu’s cooperation.
The two little cuties had completely taken over Boss Lu. Jing Shu quietly exhaled. When the rotten mermaid had suddenly rushed in like mad only to get stuck and block her view, she’d had no choice but to reveal herself.
The controlled Boss Lu said in a harsh tone, "It’s you! What are you here for?" This indicated that the two of them at least knew each other.
Jing Shu did not answer but instead asked Da Ji, "Do you want me to save you?"
Da Ji nodded frantically. "Save me, I don’t want to die!" Da Ji looked outside; the monsters couldn’t get in. With a gun pointed at his head, his only hope lay with this woman.
"Agree to a few conditions, and I will save you," Jing Shu said to Da Ji, using the power of suggestion from her Magic Cube Space combined with mental interference.
Unexpectedly, the usually effective ability hit a wall with Da Ji. His eyes darted around as he seemed to be thinking of something, clearly not influenced by the suggestion or control.

chapters.title: Chapter 663: Da Ji Exploded
chapters.content:
Chapter 663: Da Ji Exploded
Da Ji’s identity had become even more intriguing—if a mere threat could elicit some answers from him, that wouldn’t be so bad.
Thus, the manipulated Boss Lu impatiently said, "He has uncovered my secret and must be completely eradicated! However, if you agree to that matter of mine, sparing this lad’s life is not out of the question..."
Da Ji no longer dared to hesitate and immediately agreed to whatever it was. "You say, you say—whatever I can do, I’ll definitely do it for you. It’s just that I don’t know what you would want..."
What?
He was now penniless and out of Virtual Coins—what could he possibly be made to do?
"But first, we must see if this person is worth the price..." Jing Shu slowly approached Da Ji, eyeing him carefully, while also remaining on guard.
In this vast and mysterious world, there were some in Huaxia with strange abilities, such as Hao Yunlai and Zhen Nantian. Da Ji may have appeared to be a weakling, but she could not afford to take any chances.
Privately, she had already deployed all her trump cards, prepared to silence him at the first sign of trouble.
Once Da Ji heard there was a chance, he quickly nodded. "Useful, useful, I must be worth..." He subconsciously pulled down the brim of his hat, wondering what this woman could possibly want from him.
"Very well, I’ll start by asking you a few questions to see if you’re of any value," Jing Shu said deliberately.
"You ask." Da Ji suddenly had a bad feeling.
He had hoped to stall for time, waiting for the monsters outside to come and save him. At that time, who knew what would happen? But it seemed the two individuals before him were not easily fooled... More importantly, neither of them was ordinary. Would he have to kill everyone? But then he wouldn’t be able to return. Should he try to control everyone instead?
For a moment, Da Ji considered many possibilities.
The first question Jing Shu asked was, "The rotten mermaids outside... that’s the name I’ve given those monsters. Why don’t they bite you? It’s no coincidence—I noticed it last time."
Da Ji was startled, not expecting anyone to have taken note of that. In fact, he had also somewhat disbelieved it at the time. His eyes darted around as he stammered, "That... I don’t know about that. I kind of noticed too, but as for why, I’m not quite sure. Perhaps there’s something special about me."
Da Ji spoke half-truths and half-lies.
Suddenly, several more rotten mermaids outside tried to rush in, getting stuck at the entrance. However, this time they seemed smarter, forcefully hitting and widening the opening. It looked like they might be able to squeeze through before too long!
Surprise flashed in Da Ji’s eyes.
"I see. You’re useless, not worth me paying a high price to Boss Lu to spare your life. Boss Lu, you can dispose of him as you wish. I had thought he could control these monsters. What a waste of my time," Jing Shu waved her hand, her gaze fixed on the frantic rotten mermaids outside, feeling a slight stir within.
BANG! A gunshot rang out.
It seemed Boss Lu had missed, the shot hitting Da Ji in the leg instead, causing him to scream in agony.
"Sorry to have startled you," Boss Lu said. "My aim was off; I’ll do my best next time." He raised his gun again, taking careful aim.
"I’ll talk, I’ll talk! Don’t kill me—I can control the rotten mermaids you’re talking about. Really, really, don’t kill me!" Da Ji realized this man was not joking, nor could he afford to stall for time any longer.
If he doesn’t reveal something compelling to prove his worth, this man will truly kill him!
"Boss Lu, let’s give him another chance. Let me hear what he has to say, to see if there’s anything valuable... You only have this one chance. I hope you won’t waste our time talking nonsense. Make it quick, so I can still find a Doctor to treat you," Jing Shu said, frowning slightly. After all, if he truly could control the rotten mermaids, it was indeed a good opportunity, as she needed many to dig tunnels. Although their flesh was not edible, it still had other uses.
The rotten mermaids outside had become even crazier.
