Could this person truly control them?
Jing Shu wondered.
Da Ji, clutching his wound, started speaking, "Here’s what happened..."
Jing Shu frowned as she listened, while Boss Lu showed no expression throughout because he was completely controlled by Jing Shu’s pet.
"...So, it’s not like I can control them for sure, but as long as I have a strong desire, these mermaids can help me realize it," Da Ji said, glancing at the iron mass.
Why hasn’t a mermaid managed to come in to rescue him yet? To kill all these people?
Jing Shu slowly approached Da Ji, continuing to ask, "You’re saying a white insect bit you and you turned into this? Where’s the white insect then?"
"The white insect... I threw it away," Da Ji’s eyes darted around, as he lowered his hat brim again.
"You keep pulling down your hat brim. Are you trying to cover something up? You’ve been like this since I first saw you," Jing Shu said, and with a swift motion, she yanked off Da Ji’s hat, revealing a grotesque, fist-sized tumor on his neck.
The tumor was constantly writhing, as if it were alive.
As Da Ji backed away, clutching the tumor and shaking his head, he held onto the squirming lump, unsure of what to say.
Just as Jing Shu frowned in thought, wondering if the tumor was that insect, a sudden change occurred!
Whether it was because Da Ji was bleeding too much or the tumor sensed danger, the tumor swelled visibly and rapidly.
Da Ji managed only a scream before his head was grotesquely twisted 180 degrees against his back by the expanding tumor. Not only that, but his entire body also began to swell.
And it began petrifying in a strange way.
Jing Shu retreated rapidly and, without a second thought, summoned half a stone slab to block her front.
Safety first,
she mused. However, the space within the iron mass was too confined to accommodate the entire slab.
The moment after Jing Shu finished summoning the stone, a loud BOOM erupted.
Da Ji exploded!
Countless stone shards flew like shrapnel from a hand grenade. Despite Jing Shu’s quick reflexes, the powerful shockwave and flying stones from the side still caused her considerable injuries.
Boss Lu, who was controlled and standing behind Da Ji, fared even worse. His face was entirely unrecognizable, with a third of his flesh shorn off.
The whole fortification suffered even more. Sealed bags of rice were slashed open and spilled out, while the dried ducks and chickens were impaled with various stone shards.
If I’m not mistaken, these are from Da Ji’s petrified remains,
Jing Shu thought.
Her two little darlings quickly retreated to Jing Shu’s hand.
Da Ji was gone.
In his place was a white insect, looking like a large, arm-sized tadpole.
Gazing at it, Jing Shu thought,
This white insect must be related to the White Energy and the rotten mermaids, right? The negative effect of the White Energy, petrification, is perfectly manifested in it.

chapters.title: Chapter 664: Jing Shu is Seriously Injured
chapters.content:
Chapter 664: Jing Shu is Seriously Injured
This must be something good, right?
Before Jing Shu could ponder it further, the insect—oh, it should be said, an insect resembling a tadpole magnified countless times—appeared. Strictly speaking, Jing Shu thought it looked like a miniaturized version of the rotten mermaid.
It extended its tendrils... what seemed like a tiny tail suddenly grew several meters long in that instant, reaching into Boss Lu’s body in the blink of an eye.
It began to absorb his blood with satisfaction.
Jing Shu immediately threw a fishing net.
Anyway, the first thing is to control this insect and see if it can be tamed. With the Magic Cube Space, I’m very confident.
The net precisely covered the giant insect. The seemingly dull-witted creature didn’t react at all, much like a rotten mermaid, which ignores everything else while eating.
Get in here!
Jing Shu intended to put the insect into her Magic Cube Space first and then tame it, but to her utter surprise, she failed.
Jing Shu couldn’t help but frown. The rotten mermaids from the Mudstone Flow Sea couldn’t be pulled into her Magic Cube Space from a distance. However, the short time she had spent experimenting outside just now proved that by making physical contact with the rotten mermaids via an object, she could still bring them into her Magic Cube Space.
Now, two rotten mermaids are sleeping soundly in the Magic Cube Space. Da Ji wasn’t affected by my Magic Cube Space a moment ago; it must be because of this insect’s presence.
So, based on what’s been said, this insect is a product of a Dimension Space. Does that mean my Magic Cube Space, aside from not admitting humans, also can’t take in living products from a Dimension Space?
"CHIRP CHIRP! CHIRP CHIRP CHIRP CHIRP!"
In the few seconds Jing Shu was contemplating, Boss Lu was drained dry. The insect in the net struggled, emitting a sound so piercingly shrill it nearly ruptured Jing Shu’s eardrums. Blood instantly flowed from them, and her ears began to ring.
However, that wasn’t the worst of it. The rotten mermaids, which had been silently surging beneath the building, seemed to receive some kind of signal. They began to crawl up from all sides. The meter-high walls and traps couldn’t stop their advance as the terrifying rotten mermaids climbed up, one after another.
Then, they charged into the building.
Jing Shu’s insects and snakes nervously transmitted information from underground. Some unlucky snakes were trampled to death, while others, upon discovery, were immediately eaten.
The transmitted information indicated that all the rotten mermaids around the building had been roused!
They swarmed in teeming, innumerable masses!
Jing Shu clutched her ears, which were filled with a roaring sound. The earlier piercing cry had made her dizzy, but she felt much better immediately after swallowing a drop of Spiritual Spring.
This is leading to a total wipeout; this insect can’t be kept alive,
Jing Shu gritted her teeth.
I have to deal with it first because it can control the rotten mermaids!
What can’t be obtained must be destroyed.
The sturdy fishing net instantly petrified and shattered, falling to the ground. The chirping insect twisted its body, its tail lashing towards Jing Shu like a whip.
Jing Shu quickly reviewed several plans in her mind. According to Da Ji, he had seriously wounded the insect with just a chisel when it was only fist-sized. That was merely two months ago, and today it had grown this large.
I don’t know how long its tail can stretch.
The rotten mermaids’ weakness is their fear of fire and electricity, so I’ll start with an electric shock!
Just as the tail whipped towards her, Jing Shu threw another dense, electrified wire mesh at it. This electric net was something she had used in her villa during the first year of the apocalypse for defense against people. After security improved, Jing Shu had retrieved part of it.
The electric current CRACKLED, and the net smashed the insect directly onto the ground.
Strangely, while such a strong electrical current would immobilize rotten mermaids, this insect seemed unaffected. The tail, despite being smashed back, not only drilled out from the wire mesh and continued towards Jing Shu, but the section of the mesh on its body also turned into milky-white stone at a visible rate before shattering.
Jing Shu cut off the electricity, her heart aching at the loss. Two nets, gone just like that.
Ruthlessly, Jing Shu materialized a huge rock and smashed it down on the insect, flattening it. However, it was still alive and recovered within a few seconds.
The blood-sucking tail could drain a person in seconds. Jing Shu instinctively pulled out her pig-slaughtering knife and chopped at the appendage, which was as thick as a pig’s tail.
Her strike was fast, accurate, and ruthless.
With a crisp SNAP, the white tail broke off at Jing Shu’s feet.
Jing Shu exhaled, only to see the severed tail tremble and rapidly regenerate. It then continued towards her as if nothing had happened.
Jing Shu looked at the knife in her hand; its edge had petrified slightly. SNAP! She chopped down again. The tail broke off, then grew back...
Jing Shu was speechless.
What the hell? When will this end?
The army of rotten mermaids had already broken through the main gate, breached the first line of defense, and was pouring in. Such a vast number of them...
Never mind the people currently here; even the military’s concentrated firepower probably couldn’t stop them. Perhaps only a bomb capable of total annihilation would work.
They were like locusts, leaving devastation in their wake, consuming everything.
Jing Shu panicked.
The worst-case scenario has arrived. I must quickly deal with this insect that can heal itself incessantly.
The function of White Energy is Healing and petrification. Is there a way to use White Energy against it? But would that be like delivering food to its mouth?
Irritated, Jing Shu kept chopping at the regrowing tail while moving closer to the insect.
Should I just hack it to pieces? Chop it into hundreds of bits; surely it can’t survive that?
Set it on fire? Or just throw a bomb in here and blast it to smithereens?
Jing Shu decided to try fire first. With an aching heart, she poured barrels of oil onto the insect and ignited it. The area around the insect began to petrify. While the fire blazed, a huge, round stone quickly formed, completely enveloping the creature.
It was unclear whether the oil itself had petrified or if this was due to the insect’s own ability, but gradually, the fire died down.
Its tail stretched out again, heading towards Jing Shu like a straw searching for something to drink.
It’s not afraid of fire, unlike the rotten mermaids who recoil at the sight of flames. It shows no reaction. It’s not afraid of electricity either. So, what is it afraid of?
Screams began to erupt throughout the building. The number of rotten mermaids was many times greater than before. The nooks and crannies of the first-floor lobby were quickly overrun, and they were spreading upwards, floor by floor.
Jing Shu’s palms were sweating.
What should I do?
The knife in her hand completely petrified and broke with a SNAP. Jing Shu took out another pig-slaughtering knife from her Magic Cube Space; she still had quite a few.
Suddenly, looking at the severed tails scattered on the ground, Jing Shu impulsively swept them into her Magic Cube Space.

chapters.title: Chapter 665: Magic Cube Space Upgrade?
chapters.content:
Chapter 665: Magic Cube Space Upgrade?
Jing Shu simply wanted to know what effect putting the body of an insect related to White Energy into the Magic Cube Space would have. Could it be utilized?
After all, with so many tails lying around, it felt wasteful not to use them.
Ten years into the apocalypse, the scarcity of resources had made Jing Shu exceedingly frugal.
Who knew that this simple act would cause the tails, upon entering the space, to be automatically compressed and transformed into concentrated energy essence, which the jubilant space then promptly absorbed.
There was no room for negotiation. Jing Shu only saw a flash of light, denser than White Energy, before it vanished...
Only when the Magic Cube Space encountered something that could help it upgrade would it act without Jing Shu’s consent, directly assimilating it.
Jing Shu’s eyes lit up. When she had previously put White Energy into the space, she knew it could upgrade it. However, the Magic Cube Space had barely reacted then; whether she fed it the energy or simply stored it, the space had seemed indifferent.
But these insect tails were absorbed by the Magic Cube Space immediately, indicating their energy was of higher quality and purity.
Overjoyed, Jing Shu immediately put all the severed tails into the space. Strands of pure energy, compressed by the space, flashed and then vanished.
Hunger, excitement, more, I need more...
The sensations flooded her mind, and Jing Shu knew that the Magic Cube Space’s upgrade this time would likely depend on this.
Jing Shu’s eyes gleamed. She switched to using both hands, chopping with relentless KACHA KACHA sounds. However long the insect’s tail grew, she hacked it off. She even moved closer and chopped off half its head, followed by a frenzy of indiscriminate hacking.
With the hand speed honed by thirty years of being single, her arms became a blur. Whether it was a nose or an eye, she just chopped. When a knife petrified, she discarded it and immediately took out another.
Most importantly, she threw every part of the insect she could into the Magic Cube Space.
Jing Shu discovered that the faster she chopped, the faster the insect regenerated. Satisfied hums continuously emanated from the space, which demanded even more of this energy.
Scouts from the first floor of the building sent word: the rotten mermaids weren’t even sparing the furnished villas. Previously, they had just clumsily bumped around, simply capturing people to eat. But now, they were advancing like destroyers, crushing everything bit by bit.
"I still have a little time," Jing Shu murmured.
To test her hypothesis, Jing Shu reluctantly brought out the hopping zombie boar.
There’s no way I can eat this half-petrified thing. What if I turn to stone myself? Better to use it for an experiment.
As soon as the zombie boar appeared, before it could even hop twice, the insect beneath Jing Shu bit into it.
So it’s not just the tail that can suck blood; its mouth can too.
The several-hundred-pound fat boar was drained dry in just over ten seconds. Blood and flesh gone, only a layer of skin remained. Jing Shu’s guess was correct: the insect’s regenerative abilities had become even more formidable, healing almost instantly after she chopped it.
The insect’s attacks suddenly intensified, forcing Jing Shu to fend them off while simultaneously trying to collect the severed parts into her space.
If not for the years of drinking Spiritual Spring, which granted her immense strength and excellent stamina, Jing Shu would have collapsed from exhaustion long ago, given the speed at which she was wielding her knives.
The rotten mermaid army lingered a little longer on the second floor, as it was the cafeteria and stored food for over two thousand people. They devoured everything edible within minutes, even gnawing clean the chairs and tables that had been intended for Fuel.
This delay also bought some escape time for the others. Amidst the chaos, Li Yuetian had his men carry the last of the provisions upstairs.
Li Yuetian ordered, "Block all stairwells! Set them on fire, or use electricity—whatever it takes, we must stop them!"
As soon as the chaos erupted, Liu had started looking for Jing Shu. He went to her villa, but naturally, it was empty; even her black box was gone. Seeing this, Liu immediately had the driver and other soldiers start moving out a portion of the Insect Cakes.
Unfortunately, they couldn’t move much.
...
Jing Shu was drenched in sweat, engrossed in her painful yet joyful task. She had spent so long fishing outside in the wind and rain, yet the White Energy she’d collected was minimal. It was far less efficient than these few minutes spent directly chopping the insect.
When the insect’s regeneration slowed, Jing Shu knew it was out of energy. Wincing at the loss, she threw out another cow.
It doesn’t matter if I have to eat less beef jerky for a while. I need to upgrade the Magic Cube Space quickly so I can take more things with me when we migrate.
Unexpectedly, the insect’s recovery abilities grew even stronger. Almost instantly, its tail lashed out and struck Jing Shu’s skin, sucking a large amount of her blood in that split second!
Jing Shu’s face paled instantly, but her hands didn’t stop; she continued to hack wildly, her speed increasing even more.
Fortunately, this frenzied state only lasted for a few minutes.
The space faintly conveyed a sense of being full and satisfied. Only when the insect’s recovery rate slowed down again did the space finally stop absorbing its energy, instead choosing to store the compressed energy.
Jing Shu slowly exhaled. Gritting her teeth, she consumed another drop of Spiritual Spring, and some color returned to her cheeks.
Just as she was despairing, wondering how this insect was still alive and when it would finally die, a sudden BOOM echoed in her head, followed by a persistent BUZZING. Jing Shu felt dizzy, yet she also experienced a strange sense of mental clarity and openness.
But in that moment of distraction, the insect’s tail snaked out again, pressing against Jing Shu’s neck. It was preparing to suck directly from her carotid artery!
However, before Jing Shu could react, the insect that should have been sucking her blood suddenly shrieked in agony. It struggled violently, as if being forcibly pulled towards Jing Shu. In the next second, the insect continuously shrank until it was the size of a fingernail. Then, as if unwilling, it completely merged into Jing Shu’s neck.
A small, white, tadpole-shaped mark appeared on Jing Shu’s neck.
SQUEAK SQUEAK SQUEAK SQUEAK...
It felt as if tens of thousands of SQUEAKING voices flooded her mind. Unable to bear it, she collapsed to the ground.
The iron fortress was a scene of utter devastation. Of the three people originally there, Da Ji had turned into rubble, Boss Lu was nothing but a flap of skin, and Jing Shu lay collapsed in a pool of blood. Meanwhile, the battle outside raged on...
Jing Shu had only been unconscious for ten to fifteen minutes when she abruptly opened her eyes. Her head still throbbed, and her ears were still ringing. The insect’s earlier shrieks had damaged her eardrums, and the Spiritual Spring she drank hadn’t fully healed them yet.
But in the next second, an expression of delighted surprise appeared on Jing Shu’s face.
My Magic Cube Space actually upgraded?! Just like that? This was entirely achieved by bombarding it with energy!
Previously, with every upgrade, the Magic Cube Space had to shut down, repair, and restart. This time, however, it seemed like none of that had happened; Jing Shu even had the illusion that it hadn’t upgraded at all.
Not good, those things have reached the seventh floor!

chapters.title: Chapter 666: Escape
chapters.content:
Chapter 666: Escape
Even though the Magic Cube Space upgrade was much simpler this time, without the usual lengthy repair routine that took several hours, a massive number of rotten mermaids had already advanced layer by layer, quickly reaching the seventh floor during the brief moment Jing Shu was unconscious. It was the last bastion of survival for the people inside the building!
The thousands of insects and snakes Jing Shu had released were now almost completely wiped out. They didn’t dare show their heads, except for a few insects quivering in wall crevices, having narrowly escaped disaster.
The building was crammed with rotten mermaids that devoured everything. Despite Li Yuetian leading his people to desperately defend every passageway, even resorting to all sorts of methods, they were simply no match for the rotten mermaids that surged like a tide, forcefully overwhelming them.
Jing Shu didn’t have time to understand what had happened. When the last of her insects were about to draw blood, she had clearly felt some of her own blood being taken.
But what transpired after that?
Subconsciously, she touched her neck.
I was afraid of being possessed and developing tumorous growths like Da Ji, but that hasn’t happened. There’s just a small bump, much like a mole.
I can’t worry about that now!
She couldn’t even focus on the upgraded Magic Cube Space. Jing Shu knew she had to first organize a defense against the incoming rotten mermaids.
Otherwise, what am I supposed to do once all the rotten mermaids swarm over and devour everyone?
A continuous chirping echoed in her head, incessant, as if countless rotten mermaids were speaking. She couldn’t understand them; it was as annoying as tens of thousands of ducks quacking nonstop!
If only they would quiet down,
Jing Shu thought.
Then, as if by magic, the noise from a moment before suddenly vanished. Now, all she could hear was a ringing buzz in her ears and the faint sounds of screams from outside.
Jing Shu’s mind raced. She emerged from Boss Lu’s secret treasure chamber. Rotten mermaids were still continuously dropping into the passageway there. Li Chenglong was retreating with a group of people to the next exit. Consequently, no one nearby had witnessed that scene. Instead, many rotten mermaids passed by Jing Shu, targeting the area Li Chenglong’s group defended. Not only that, but the rotten mermaids also consciously cleared a path for Jing Shu.
Jing Shu speculated.
Am I receiving the same treatment as Da Ji? The rotten mermaids are no longer attacking me. Does that mean I have the same privileges as him?
All of you, stop! Don’t move!
Jing Shu thought, recalling what Da Ji had said. He couldn’t control these rotten mermaids, but if he had a strong desire for something, they would help him achieve it.
「」
"Hold the line! We must hold the line!" Li Yuetian shouted, ordering people to grab anything that could burn. "As long as we survive, until the very last moment, there’s hope!"
"Bedding, items from the private rooms, doorframes—bring them all here to burn!"
"Tie Dan, secure the other passage!"
"Captain, staircase number four is lost! They’re in, they’re pouring in!"
Upon hearing the news, Li Yuetian ran over frantically. The central hall on the seventh floor was overflowing with people. There was no room to stand; everyone was shivering. If there were only a few hundred, they could still put up a fierce resistance. But these teeming creatures numbered at least in the tens of thousands, and more kept squeezing their way toward them relentlessly.
"AHHH, help!"
"Monsters are breaking in!"
The already cramped hall erupted with screams as people tried to flee. But with the crowd packed so tightly, where was there any space to run? A rotten mermaid charged into the crowd, and with one huge bite, devoured a person.
It’s over,
Li Yuetian thought blankly. He then shouted at Li Chenglong, "Still no sign of Jing Shu?"
Li Chenglong replied, "I don’t know. I’ve been here from the start."
Jun Jia, pinching Gold Dominator’s hand, sighed. "Under these circumstances, she’s probably more dead than alive."
Li Chenglong then yelled, "She’s so powerful! She must be doing something we can’t imagine. She’ll definitely be fine!"
Li Yuetian murmured, "If only she were here. Perhaps she’d have a way."
Suddenly, another monster lunged over from a different blockade. Stepping on the bodies of its companions, it plunged into the crowd from above, jaws wide open, heading straight for Li Chenglong.
It’s over,
was Li Chenglong’s first thought. Then, clenching his teeth, he grabbed a torch with his bare hands and shoved it into the mermaid’s mouth, resigned to mutual destruction.
But then, unexpectedly, events took a sudden turn.
All the monsters suddenly stopped moving, as if stuck. The attacking monsters froze. The feasting ones stopped. They were like statues. Li Chenglong had just stuck a torch into a monster’s mouth; normally, it would have reacted, but at this moment, the monster didn’t move, allowing the torch to burn it to ashes.
"Huh?"
Immediately afterward, everyone else in the hall noticed. "What’s going on?"
"These monsters have stopped moving! Hurry, kill them all, no matter what!" Li Yuetian was the quickest to react.
「」
Jing Shu walked forward, gazing at everything in disbelief. Indeed, all the rotten mermaids had stopped, just like statues, exceedingly obedient.
It wasn’t as Da Ji described, requiring a strong wish to be fulfilled. I merely thought about it silently. It was a piece of cake.
"All of you, retreat underground!" Jing Shu commanded this time. But after giving the order, her head felt like it exploded with a BANG, almost bursting. It felt as if something had been completely drained from her.
The next second, the mermaids began to leave, just as they had come. Their minds were dull, lacking intelligence, yet they knew the path and turned to go back the way they came.
The recently quieted hall erupted with cries of alarm again. This time, however, the monsters truly receded like the tide.
Only when every living rotten mermaid had returned to the Mudstone Flow Sea underground and completely exited the building did Jing Shu, who had been holding on with difficulty, finally exhale.
This matter is finally resolved,
she thought.
But are there conditions for ordering these monsters? That still needs to be verified.
"Who’s there?!" Li Chenglong, who had just come out to check the situation, immediately realized someone was in a dark corner.
Jing Shu, holding the mysterious black box she had summoned from the Magic Cube Space in advance, said weakly, "It’s me."
"Sister? Sister Jing! It’s you! Thank goodness, you’re not dead! I knew it!" Li Chenglong ran over excitedly. In the dim light, he smelled the thick scent of blood. He turned on his flashlight and was shocked by how pale Jing Shu’s face was.
"What’s wrong? Let me support you, Sister. Are you okay?" Li Chenglong carefully helped Jing Shu up, taking the black box that she never went anywhere without.
"What is this thing? It’s so heavy!" Li Chenglong could barely lift it.
Back in the crowded hall, no one dared to go out. Who knew if the monsters had truly gone?

chapters.title: Chapter 667: Without Food
chapters.content:
Chapter 667: Without Food
"I’m fine."
All I wanted was to get some good rest. Who knew that upgrading the space wouldn’t give me a break? It felt like after I gave the last command, I was completely drained.
"Sister Jing, where did you go? We looked everywhere and couldn’t find you!" Li Chenglong complained a little, yet his tone also carried concern.
It was so dangerous; why didn’t she know how to take care of herself?
Jing Shu remained silent.
"I knew it, Sister Jing! You must have been up to something big. Maybe all the monsters retreated because of you," Li Chenglong said as he helped Jing Shu sit on the ground. He then switched to "loudspeaker mode," announcing to his uncle that Jing Shu had been found. Soon after, Jun Jia arrived with a large group of people.
Seeing Jing Shu was all right, Li Chenglong also felt relieved.
My Turtle Snake Wine is secured now,
he thought.
Otherwise, this chronic rheumatism could kill me.
Gold Dominator, still carrying the two pigs, was trembling uncontrollably. He grunted, "Look how scared you got. You’re not much better off than me."
Gold Dominator never forgot about the Jinhua Sows he carried, especially if one was the last of its kind. He’d even decided that in a dire situation, he’d eat them.
He was practically salivating at the sight of the two pigs now.
"It’s good that you’re okay," Jun Jia said, noticing the blood covering Jing Shu. "Chenglong, take the patrol team and check the surroundings. Once it’s confirmed safe, we’ll go down." Then he asked, "What happened earlier when we couldn’t find you?"
After resting for a moment, Jing Shu took a sip of the hot water Liu had handed her—her "special" supply—and then called everyone to follow her to the hot pot restaurant where they had been earlier.
Jun Jia assigned some temporary tasks: Dr. Zhang was to lead a team to check if the injured could be treated, and Wang Miao would lead another to take stock of the current situation. After every battle, things were chaotic, with many small matters to address. However, the most pressing concern for everyone now was whether the monsters would return.
The hall was a mess. Many people, understandably, had been so scared they’d wet their pants. Not to mention, quite a few had been constipated for weeks, wanting to relieve themselves but unable to. The fright had just made them lose control. A warm stream ran down their legs; it had been a long time since they’d felt such warmth, albeit a bit sticky.
The hall reeked of an indescribable odor.
Jing Shu quickened her pace.
Liu followed, head held high, unfazed by the strange looks he received after handing Jing Shu the water.
He was proud; he’d never forget his leader’s hot water bottle, no matter where they went. He just knew it: the boss, with her black box, must have been attending to important business.
Everyone stared in surprise at the storage room, which had a large, forcibly created hole in its wall.
"This is it." Jing Shu kicked aside a pile of rotten mermaid skeletons blocking the large hole in front of what looked like a secret safe.
Gold Dominator felt a chill run down his spine. The others quietly swallowed, a sense of awe washing over them.
It looked like Jing Shu had killed a significant number of monsters.
Once inside, they couldn’t help but gasp. The secret storage room was small, barely fitting the few of them standing, and supplies were piled high everywhere. But the supplies were now in a sorry state. Rice and flour were scattered everywhere. Sausages and smoked ducks hanging from hooks were embedded with many small Shi Zi and stone flakes, and everything was spattered with bloodstains.
This itself wasn’t devastating. It seemed as if a shockwave had ravaged the place; most of the supplies had been shattered by the force.
Jing Shu figured Da Ji’s explosion must have destroyed some supplies. Then came the insect’s screech, so powerful it nearly ruptured her eardrums. That must have been the shockwave that did the rest of the damage.
The others weren’t Jing Shu, and their focus was different. When Jing Shu first saw the storage room, she had been a little surprised by the sheer amount of food and meat. However, most of it was common stuff, things she could already produce in her space.
If it hadn’t been contaminated, I might have considered taking it into my space,
Jing Shu thought.
But now it’s stained with blood and riddled with countless small Shi Zi. What’s more, it’s all mixed with Da Ji’s remains. The very idea is disgusting. Who knows what problems eating it might cause?
She immediately lost interest.
However, the storage room also contained some weapons. Amidst the chaos, Jing Shu had already stashed them into her space, a considerable bounty.
I’ll take a good look when I get back and see what kinds there are,
she planned.
In the apocalypse, these weapons are almost top-notch treasures. The main problem is the lack of ammunition.
"My God, so much food!"
"This is Boss Lu’s storage room, right?"
Jing Shu nodded.
Jun Jia clenched his teeth. He had been wanting to ask, "Where is Boss Lu?"
Jing Shu pointed to the ground.
Only then did the others look over and realize Li Yuetian was standing on a shriveled husk of skin and some clothes.
Jun Jia staggered back, landing his backside on a bag of rice and flour. He yelped as something sharp pricked him.
Without changing his expression, Li Yuetian kicked the remains aside.
Disgusting,
he thought.
Jing Shu explained, "He was drained dry by a powerful monster."
Nobody asked where the powerful monster had gone. After all, only Jing Shu had emerged. Seeing the gruesome scene, everyone couldn’t help but regard Jing Shu with newfound respect.
Her black box is like a treasure chest, with many compartments and all sorts of supplies. And she herself is even more mysterious—not only immensely strong but also possessing unexpected abilities.
"Sausage!" Gold Dominator dropped the cage—
he couldn’t care less how powerful Jing Shu was right now
—grabbed a sausage, and started gnawing on it. He immediately yelped, a tooth snapping, and blood gushed from his mouth. "PTOOEY! PTOOEY! PTOOEY! Why are there so many sharp Shi Zi in this?!"
Jing Shu didn’t have the heart to tell him they were fragments from Da Ji’s remains.
Just then, Li Chenglong rushed over. "Uncle, they’re all gone! Vanished without a trace! But the second floor... all the food on the second floor has been eaten! Nothing’s left! What are we going to do?"
"All of it?"
"All of it! Including Sister Jing’s two truckloads of Insect Cake! Even the tables, chairs, kitchenware, and the clay stoves we built—all gone! There’s just a pile of droppings left!" Li Chenglong was near tears.
They were trapped on this isolated outpost, relying on Jing Shu’s two truckloads of Insect Cake to survive. As long as they had food, they could keep living. Now, they had nothing.
Jun Jia pointed to the storage room. Any hope he’d felt was instantly doused with cold water. He asked, "With what’s in this room, how long can the survivors last?"
This time, the casualties had been severe. It was unlike the last attack, where Jing Shu had blocked most of the monsters, with only a few dozen reaching the upper floors and scattering across the seven levels.
Li Yuetian surveyed the remaining supplies and said, "Even with 1,500 people, if we ration carefully, this food will only last three or four days."
The supplies here were varied, mostly personal stashes with limited quantities of each item. Some were filling, others merely snacks.
Liu spoke up hesitantly, "I had the driver and a few others move out dozens of boxes of Insect Cakes earlier, but with so many people, it’s only enough for one day..."
Jing Shu was powerless this time. The rotten mermaids had eaten all the Insect Cakes from her truck, and she couldn’t conjure up any more food.
"Let’s distribute the spoils of war first," someone declared. "We have to survive!"

chapters.title: Chapter 668: The Villa is Gone
chapters.content:
Chapter 668: The Villa is Gone
Survival first. That’s the rule of the apocalypse. No one can divide everything selflessly, but you can always take a bit for yourself first.
It was foreseeable that wherever monsters roamed, nothing would be left.
Li Yuetian clutched his heart, aching for a long time. His last bottle of liquor, the one he had hidden in the second-floor camp, was now nothing but a pool of excrement.
The spoils of war were the contents of this storage room. With Boss Lu dead, they became unclaimed goods.
Jun Jia then said, "Jing Shu found this place first, so you pick. The rest of us will each take only what we can carry. Logistics will make communal meals from whatever is left and distribute it."
This was what they called ’finder’s share.’ Li Chenglong rubbed his hands together, chuckling. He had arrived just in time; following Sister Jing was definitely the right choice.
Boss Lu could never have imagined his treasured supplies would be divided up so easily.
At this moment, no one questioned the night’s events. What mattered was the sight of so much food—the hope for survival.
Luckily, not many people were present. Even at full capacity, one person couldn’t carry away too much. Although it was enough food to last one person ten years, it wouldn’t last long once divided among thousands.
Honestly, Jing Shu wasn’t interested in these things. Otherwise, she would have stashed them in her Magic Cube Space long ago, just as she had with the weapons.
However, she absolutely couldn’t show disdain. After all, in these apocalyptic years with so many species extinct, Boss Lu’s treasure was quite substantial. From the current perspective, these were definitely valuable items that couldn’t be bought.
Hadn’t Jun Jia’s eyes lit up at the sight of them?
"Sister, you pick first. Once you’ve chosen, I’ll help you carry it," Li Chenglong urged with an eager smile. "Since Jing Shu discovered the stash, of course, she should pick first.
There were only so many good things. What if everyone wanted the smoked sausage? That’s what priority was for, wasn’t it?
"
Jing Shu then carefully searched for food that hadn’t been damaged by Da Ji’s corpse, selecting items from a corner.
Fortunately, her night vision was excellent. She finally found a batch of undamaged, sealed apocalypse-era canned goods and military rations from various countries, distinguishable by the different languages on their labels.
Great! She had never tried most of these things before, only seen them in various review videos. These strange and varied foods seemed quite fun, and she was rather curious about them.
Jing Shu didn’t stand on ceremony. She lifted six large boxes filled with all sorts of peculiar apocalypse rations with one hand and declared, "I’ll take this much."
There really wasn’t any other food as perfectly intact, or any other useful supplies, left to find.
Li Chenglong’s enthusiasm deflated.
He had forgotten that Sister Jing was a Hercules; she effortlessly managed these items, weighing over a hundred pounds, with just one hand.
The others weren’t polite either. Jun Jia immediately grabbed a leaking bag of rice. Gold Dominator, still spitting blood, was determined to take all the sausages and even snatched a few smoked chickens at the end.
Li Yuetian was also a pragmatist. He went straight for rice, then rummaged through the supplies, found a large quantity of instant noodles, and promptly took two boxes.
Liu imitated Jing Shu, searching in a corner.
He didn’t want to be eating and suddenly bite into a stone.
He finally found food that satisfied him.
The group first hid their chosen food supplies together before beginning the true post-battle distribution work.
Jun Jia went to reassure everyone. After all, they had just experienced such a terrifying event. He had to paint a grand picture for them to lessen their fear, explaining that although the food on the second floor was gone, Boss Lu had secretly hoarded much more, which could now be shared.
Li Yuetian led several teams to start sifting through the food in the storage room. There was too much rubble, mostly sharp. The large pieces were only fingernail-sized, while the small ones were like sesame seeds. Biting down on them would genuinely shatter teeth and cause bleeding.
Pools of water and blood mixed on the floor, and a sweet smell permeated the air from shattered glass jars, spilled drinks, and condiments.
Flour and rice were scattered everywhere—a complete mess.
But with food so scarce, nothing on the floor could be wasted. It naturally had to be meticulously picked clean by people, ground down bit by bit, and added to the communal pot for cooking.
Li Chenglong had to lead people to patrol, inspect, and dispose of the bodies—both human and monster. Jing Shu went with him for the time being.
Dr. Zhang had already begun treatment, checking for any survivors who had been bitten but were still alive.
Wang Miao, while taking inventory, also directed the evacuation of the crowd, getting everyone to start tidying up with just a few succinct words.
He needed to arrange the current living accommodations, so he had no choice but to first follow Li Chenglong to check the situation on the lower floors.
Sixth floor: A pile of excrement.
Stepping on it felt soft and still warm.
Fifth floor: A layer of excrement.
Fourth floor: A thick layer of excrement.
Third floor: A very thick layer of excrement.
Second floor: Excrement up to their knees.
With each floor they descended, Jing Shu’s expression darkened further. Fortunately, back on the sixth floor, she had silently pulled two black plastic bags from her pocket and slipped them over her shoes.
Perhaps these rotten mermaids had overeaten. This time, they had devoured everything—furniture, doors, bedding, anything edible or inedible—to create such a grand spectacle.
The place was as empty as Li Chenglong had described; absolutely nothing remained.
Li Chenglong shook his head. "Now, there’s really nothing left."
Jing Shu, as if remembering something, hurried to the first-floor lobby.
She froze. The once-crowded first-floor lobby, which had been filled with tables, screens, and chairs, and had even housed three prefabricated villas, was now completely bare.
Jing Shu felt like she was wading through a swamp as she struggled forward, staring in disbelief at where her villa had once stood. Only some broken walls and steel frames remained; everything else was gone. The lobby was a chaotic mess, with leftover trash strewn about, and the stench was unbearable.
The villa she had spent a fortune on was gone. Jing Shu couldn’t even describe her current mood; it felt like she’d been royally screwed.
But not only had her Magic Cube Space upgraded, it seemed she had also gained an incredible ability. If she could truly command the rotten mermaids in the future, it would be a net gain.
Jing Shu consoled herself with this thought.
Wang Miao hadn’t expected it to be this devastating. Floors one through six were utterly empty. Cooking utensils, eating utensils, sleeping arrangements—all gone.
"Director Wang, how should we arrange the accommodations?" Jing Shu asked.
She wanted to be alone for a bit and needed to sort out living arrangements quickly. She had to check her Magic Cube Space; the devastation outside was too heartbreaking.
Wang Miao suppressed the urge to vomit and said, "Everyone will stay on the seventh floor for now. The other areas are uninhabitable. We’ll have to squeeze in..."
Jing Shu, however, said, "Let’s clean up the sixth floor first. There isn’t as much excrement there, and it can be made habitable. This excrement isn’t entirely useless either. Let’s see if we can use it as fuel.
At least we won’t be cold then.
"
With so much excrement, the fuel problem should be solvable. But where would they find food?
Jing Shu temporarily pushed these headaches aside. Then she turned to Gold Dominator and asked, "What do you mean by following me around with your Jinhua Sow, never leaving my side?"
Liu discreetly positioned himself in front of Gold Dominator.
He had been feeling lately that many people were vying for his position; he had to be on guard!
Just then, Li Chenglong came running back, followed by many skeletons.

chapters.title: Chapter 669: The Most Awesome Function After Upgrading
chapters.content:
Chapter 669: The Most Awesome Function After Upgrading
"Sister Jing, there were so many skeletons this time! I’ve cleaned them all up and brought them over. Dr. Zhang finished the headcount; no one was bitten by the monsters, so there was no need for the Bone Powder. I know you like this stuff, so I brought it all to you," Li Chenglong said, his voice conveying a sense of accomplishment. Those who had been bitten by the monsters had died. So this time, apart from the deaths and injuries from being trampled, there were surprisingly no other casualties.
Li Chenglong spoke as if seeking praise. After all, during that life-and-death battle, he had only seen Jing Shu collecting these skeletons, doing nothing else.
Jing Shu: "..."
It didn’t take long for the skeletons to fill up the old hot pot restaurant. When the rotten mermaids died, nothing was left except for these useless skeletons.
"Then I’m off. We still have to clean up layer by layer, and then filter the water. We need to figure out how to make more clay pots and bowls since all of those are gone now," Li Chenglong said before hurriedly leaving.
Dawn was breaking; the day had arrived. Although it was still gloomy, there was at least some visibility now.
But no one could sleep; everyone had to work. They had to clean the building’s waste, filter water, boil water—there was plenty to do. Everyone was busy.
Not just the ordinary people; even the managers were overwhelmed with work. Wang Miao had to take care of the post-battle headcount and also consider where everyone would sleep at night. With so many people, and all the private rooms, bedding, and private food supplies gone, what were they to do on such cold nights?
Jun Jia still had to direct the sorting of food inside the iron chunks. It was the last resort for survival; how could it be distributed to maximize its use?
In the blink of an eye, only Jing Shu, Liu, and Gold Dominator—who was clutching a pig and staring with wide-eyed innocence—were left in the hot pot restaurant. This time, Gold Dominator was determined to stick close to Jing Shu. His brother-in-law had told him: to survive the apocalypse, you must stick close to Jing Shu.
Jing Shu, however, was momentarily stunned, gazing at the mountainous pile of bones before her.
Not only can these bones quickly heal wounds inflicted by the rotten mermaids and cause petrification, but they’re also edible! Yes, bones are too hard to chew without meat, but once ground into powder, they can be cooked into mush. What is most abundant in the Mudstone Flow Sea? Naturally, it’s the endless rotten mermaids!
Jing Shu became excited.
Following this line of thought, as long as there are rotten mermaids, there will be food; people won’t starve in the apocalypse! With only one or two thousand people now, won’t there be even more rotten mermaids in the future, which could then support even more people? Thinking about it this way, every part of the rotten mermaids is a treasure!
Speaking of this, Jing Shu recalled experiments she had conducted before.
Animals that ate too much White Energy would petrify, but people who ate rotten mermaid bones showed no abnormalities. The chickens and fish tested inside the Magic Cube Space were the best proof, though there were no other effects.
Right, there are still a few rotten mermaids left in the Magic Cube Space; they’re perfect for some experiments,
Jing Shu thought, sharpening her knife with great zeal. She first made a cut on the pig’s rear, then let the mermaid saliva from the rotten mermaids she had captured into the Space drip into the wound to observe the reaction.
There’s no choice; the only creatures in the Space with abundant blood flow are these Domestic Poultry, and besides, I have many pigs to spare,
she mused.
The blood wouldn’t stop flowing, gushing out. Jing Shu made sure to collect some pig blood, not letting it go to waste.
It can be used to feed the chickens; the chickens in the Space aren’t picky eaters.
She then sprinkled the ground Bone Powder little by little onto the wound. The pig’s rear petrified and healed. The pig was lively again—a truly good outcome.
It seems this Bone Powder is really effective, just as I thought! From now on, if someone gets a wound, they won’t need medicine. They can just apply mermaid saliva, then dust it with the powder, and it will quickly stop the bleeding, petrify, and scab over. Who would have thought that in this apocalypse, 99% of people can’t afford medicine? It’s basically like an AB glue; both components need to interact to be effective.
Jing Shu was very satisfied, truly satisfied.
Rotten mermaid saliva is easy to collect—a big bucket can be gathered just like that—and there’s an abundance of Bone Powder. If I ever package and sell this stuff... tsk tsk, it would be a blessing for many.
So how do rotten mermaids reproduce?
Jing Shu quickly figured it out: rotten mermaids are hermaphrodites, mating with themselves to produce as many offspring as they desire.
But there is a prerequisite: they can spawn only when they are well-fed and have access to White Energy.
Jing Shu wandered around the Magic Cube Space with a strange expression. The space, which was supposed to have expanded significantly, hadn’t grown much. Instead, an additional, smaller, different space had appeared.
Immediately, Jing Shu called Liu to have people grind all the bones into powder. Then, she quietly found a spot to sit down, closed her eyes, and decided to investigate the peculiarity of the space.
After the upgrade, the space was supposed to be 10x10x10, totaling 1,000 cubic meters. Aside from the 1 cubic meter Spiritual Spring and 60 cubic meters of land, there should have been 939 cubic meters of blank space left. In short, besides the 6 cubic meters of land gained with each level increase, I should have obtained an additional 265 cubic meters of blank space. But now, there’s an extra 4x4x4, so 64 cubic meters, of milky-white space below the Spiritual Spring. The remaining 261 cubic meters must be what I actually gained from this upgrade.
In the center of this new space, there’s a milky-white liquid bubbling just like the Spiritual Spring. However, the Space Spiritual Spring is... well, spring-sized, while this milky-white liquid is only the size of a fist. The milky-white space, like the Magic Cube Space, can also be pieced together at will. But its use... when eggs and other materials are put into it, they slowly dissolve into something like white water. When living things are placed inside, the result is similar. Chickens scream and then perish, dissolving as if being digested.
Jing Shu’s eyebrows raised. Then, she placed one of the captured rotten mermaids into it. The rotten mermaid cheered joyfully, emitting sounds of pleasure...
Jing Shu’s eyes reddened.
While others were busy, Jing Shu began her frantic experiments. After the new upgrade to her space, she hadn’t gained any additional passive abilities, but she did get this extra little space. After several experiments, Jing Shu named it the Cultivation Space.
True to its name, its primary function was to rapidly and crazily propagate rotten mermaids, preserving their eggs within the space and making them available when needed.
At first, Jing Shu didn’t realize it, but after feeding just a tiny drop of the milky liquid to a rotten mermaid, it spat out eggs like bullets. With a CRACKLING sound, it laid hundreds of thumb-sized eggs, which were perfectly preserved in the milky-white space.
Like the Spiritual Spring, the milky liquid increased by only one drop automatically each day, making it very precious.
As for whether it can stimulate other beings... my attempts have been unsuccessful so far. Perhaps it only works on Dark Creatures. That will have to be tested later.
It also had a huge advantage: within a one-kilometer diameter of the activated Second Order Rubik’s Cube space, it could directly absorb the surrounding White Energy, saving Jing Shu the trouble of fishing for and collecting energy.
Of course, it had one more incredible feature that made Jing Shu kneel in awe.

chapters.title: Chapter 670: King’s Ace in the Hole
chapters.content:
Chapter 670: King’s Ace in the Hole
This function is so practical.
In the previous two months, Jing Shu had come up with the idea of electrifying the rotten mermaids underground to take away the White Energy and even conducted experiments. It was through touch that she captured some rotten mermaids for experimentation, to thoroughly understand this new species of the apocalypse. But after eating the White Energy, the rotten mermaids became dimensional products. Unless personally touched and taken into the space, it was impossible to capture them.
The most impressive feature of the upgraded milky white space is that within a one-kilometer radius of its expansion, as long as there are rotten mermaids, they can be collected into the space and then released unexpectedly. This distance is not fixed. When the Magic Cube Space upgrades next time, it will be 11x11x11 = 1,331 cubic meters, and this kilometer radius will expand as well. In other words, the milky white space is also akin to a summoning gate. Within this range, Jing Shu could summon countless rotten mermaids anytime she desired, provided, of course, that there were any within that range. Perhaps it wasn’t limited to rotten mermaids; it could also apply to other Dark Creatures.
Just like now, the Mud Sea was teeming with countless rotten mermaids, and Jing Shu casually summoned a giant one. After feeding it diluted White Emulsion, it spawned like a cannonball.
From now on, I will have an endless supply of rotten mermaids!
Jing Shu clenched her fist, the overwhelming sense of doom that had plagued her since being stranded on the isolated island finally dissipating. In this apocalypse, Jing Shu had gained another ace up her sleeve—her lifesaver. It could be said that as long as no nuclear bombs were targeting her, little else could trouble her. At worst, she could covertly summon an endless stream of rotten mermaids. Moreover, these large rotten mermaids, unafraid of bullets and physical attacks, were perfect as meat shields.
Of course, I must consider carefully how to use this ace covertly, and I need to reassess my position.
Jing Shu continued to ponder.
The year of the Mudstone Flow will soon be over, and the Mudstone Flow Sea isn’t a place to stay year-round. To cultivate this secret trump card, I must keep the rotten mermaids somewhere nearby so they can be summoned at any time. All the White Energy underground must be collected. Although the rotten mermaids can survive on anything, they still need a regular supplement of White Energy, especially for reproduction. The advanced form of White Energy is the White Emulsion. However, the White Emulsion in my space is too precious. So, before leaving, it would be best to collect all the White Energy into the space; otherwise, with so many rotten mermaids, losing one means one less. Therefore, it’s imperative I stay in the Mud Sea for a few more days to seize the opportunity and collect all the White Energy.
Jing Shu’s expression turned peculiar again. Previously, the high-rise had been swirling like a vortex for over two months, endlessly circling until it finally reached this central point.
According to my mysterious intuition, everything was the doing of the white insect in my neck. Drawn by energy, it ventured into the Energy Storm. The Magic Cube Space’s ability to directly absorb White Energy and summon rotten mermaids might have all been due to the white insect’s powers. Now that the white insect is gone, the building has come to a standstill. But, to my surprise, all of this has now worked out in my favor.
Touching a small mark on her neck, Jing Shu was deep in thought when Jun Jia arrived in a flurry, bringing a group of people with him. He had managed to work up a sweat running over in this bitterly cold weather, which was no small feat.
"Jackie Chan told me you found something edible? What is it? Please don’t let it be crap. In this empty building, there’s nothing but crap. What else could there be? Are we supposed to eat dirt? But even dirt won’t do; it’s killed quite a few people before..." Jun Jia chattered nonstop as soon as he arrived.
Jing Shu led them to the room where Bone Powder was being made and said, "Try eating Bone Powder. Adding it to the other supplies and boiling it into a mush should help us last another seven or eight days."
Upon seeing a room full of bone racks, Jun Jia found it hard to put his feelings into words. "Can we eat this? It seems harder to digest than dirt, doesn’t it?"
He’d heard that this stuff, when applied to a bite wound, caused instant petrification.
Jing Shu, who hadn’t publicized her initial small experiment, said, "You can eat it, and it’s actually quite fragrant. I originally planned to bring it back as a rare seasoning for the apocalypse, but now we’ve really hit rock bottom." She then explained her small experiment.
The Bone Powder produces a special fragrance in food,
Jing Shu thought.
By making more Bone Powder, not only can it serve as an adhesive, but it can also become a valuable seasoning in the apocalypse. I plan to add it to Insect Cakes later and sell them. At the very least, I could even distribute it nationwide. Sprinkling Bone Powder on rotten corpse insects would make them somewhat more palatable, preventing starvation and possibly saving some lives. That would be doing what’s within my power.
Jun Jia’s eyes lit up. Being trapped here, surviving an extra day meant a greater sliver of hope. Since it was edible and tasted good, he waved his hand magnanimously and said joyfully, "Then let’s add it! Jing Shu, you’ve truly made another great contribution."
Starvation might drive people to cannibalism, let alone eating bones, but who could have imagined grinding bones into powder to consume them? No wonder Jing Shu thrives in the apocalypse. This woman, truly, will try anything to see if it’s edible. She must have suffered from severe hunger before. The fact that she always carries food in her inseparable box, taking it everywhere, shows her deep-seated insecurity. And yet, her fastidiousness in this post-apocalyptic world is baffling.
Perfect! This is also an opportunity to promote Bone Powder and open up the market widely. I can even conduct a large-scale experiment to confirm that Bone Powder is safe for human consumption.
The more Jing Shu thought about it, the happier she became.
Having resolved a major worry, Jing Shu’s mind settled. She continued to feverishly collect the dense White Energy from below while pondering how to get back.
Suddenly, the countless rotten mermaids beneath gave Jing Shu an idea.
Why not use this free labor force to transport the building back? Sleds need reindeer to pull them, and ships at sea can use fish. The building might be rather large, but with countless rotten mermaids in the Mudstone Flow Sea, couldn’t they carry it underwater? This is also fortunate because I want to collect White Energy from different places. If I miss this opportunity, I might miss out completely. I can also capture all the wild rotten mermaids while I’m at it!
In places invisible to others, myriads of densely packed rotten mermaids swam to the base of the building. They burrowed underneath it and slowly began to move in one direction.
Their pace was slow, but the building indeed began to move.

chapters.title: Chapter 671: Hearing of Jing Shu’s Death
chapters.content:
Chapter 671: Hearing of Jing Shu’s Death
This indicates that Jing Shu’s method is effective! As long as she can move, she can return to Wu City!
The only downside is that Jing Shu can’t fully control the rotten mermaids underground like those cultivated in the Magic Cube Space, so she can’t have the rotten mermaids disperse to map the area and find a route.
In other words, Jing Shu’s current knowledge of her location and the basic route to take is practically a shot in the dark.
However, the rotten mermaids cultivated in the milky Magic Cube Space are different. Even if they exceed the distance limit, they can still carry out tasks. So Jing Shu plans to use the underground ones for hard labor, while those from the space are sent out to scout.
At the very least, I should see if there are other treasures in this expanse of the Mud Sea,
she thought.
Unlike others who were feeling oppressed, Jing Shu was in quite a good mood. She was able to collect the milky liquid rich in White Energy from the space and gather the scattered rotten mermaids around her. Most importantly, she could finally return to Wu City.
Therefore, when Liu brought her a bowl of stewed rice for lunch, it didn’t affect Jing Shu’s mood at all. "Give it to the sow," she said. "Let her nourish herself. It’s rare for her to be pregnant in such a situation."
"Ah, look at that! The sow will give birth soon, that’s really great."
Liu was also happy. He knew that the boss didn’t eat the common meals, so he conveniently fed the Jinhua Sow.
Circumstances are so difficult, and the boss is still so picky, but I don’t mind at all,
Liu thought.
She’s so powerful and capable, so what’s wrong with her being choosy? Isn’t it right to nourish the sow? And seeing her so happy, she must have a solution!
Gold Dominator also wanted to give his bowl of rice to the sow, but after thinking it over, he decided against it.
I’m not the same Gold Dominator I was two months ago,
he realized.
I understand the situation now: resources are limited, there isn’t enough food for everyone, and who knows how long the current supply will last?
The building bustled with activity all day before two floors were basically cleared, but at least it was fit to house people now. As for the evening accommodation arrangements, Jun Jia gathered everyone on the seventh floor, shouting at the top of his voice since all the loudspeakers and electricity were gone.
It was like truly returning to a time before liberation.
He first reported the casualty situation: the current number of survivors was over 1,600. In the battle at dawn, 600 people died, and the deceased didn’t even leave corpses behind. Among them, 300 were from the Township Government, as they were on the frontlines. The rest included workers, auction staff, and even Boss Lu along with his people.
Speaking of Jing Shu’s college classmates, more than a dozen were gone. Just from this one battle, everyone became much more silent. Witnessing friends they knew being devoured... That feeling was horrifying.
The dead were gone, but the living had to think about how to survive.
Jun Jia reassured everyone, promising that they would definitely survive and return to Wu City. After a dose of encouragement and assigning tasks for the coming days, he dispersed people to stay on the 5th, 6th, and 7th floors.
Who got to stay on the intact seventh floor?
This time, it was based on contribution. Jing Shu, having fought the monsters and protected Boss Lu’s private stock, made the largest contribution. So, she was arranged to stay in an independent hotpot restaurant and look after a room full of Bone Powder.
A big room for one person, along with a whole room smelling of fragrant Bone Powder—countless people drooled with envy.
Yes, only after today did everyone realize that monster Bone Powder was edible, and it was actually quite tasty—even if it felt gritty like sand between the teeth. If only it could be ground a bit finer... but it really was very fragrant indeed.
"No wonder Jing Shu took so much Bone Powder before. I never expected it to have so many uses."
"All that Bone Powder in one room, to eat as much as you want, how envious."
"What’s there to envy? That’s what she deserves for slaying monsters."
The hotpot restaurant was connected to Boss Lu’s scrap metal shop, where a large hole had been gnawed out by the rotten mermaids.
The storeroom was cleaned out completely; not even a single grain of rice was left, nor a trace of flour.
Jing Shu knew that there had originally been some scattered flour. But, fearing waste, the people cleaning had repeatedly washed and scraped it with water, putting it back into the pot, and only withdrew after not a single bit of food was left.
Therefore, she hadn’t eaten today’s meal, nor did she plan to eat the next one.
With such a large stockpile of military rations from different countries and the food in the Magic Cube Space, I have no intention of mistreating myself,
Jing Shu thought.
Having been reborn, the one thing I can’t stand is being aggrieved.
Furthermore, the Magic Cube Space had upgraded, gaining a lifesaving trump card. Her mood had accordingly lifted.
I’ve always envied the insect woman Xiao Wei’s large tribe, which could reproduce quickly, had combat capability, could dig holes, and followed commands...
Unexpectedly, today I’ve obtained such an ability. Though the process was unpleasant, as long as the outcome is good, that’s all that matters.
With insects and snakes keeping watch outside, Jing Shu happily soaked in a bath and laid out a thick tent to sleep on. Before sleeping, she indulged in a full late-night snack. Feeling content and blissful, she drifted off to sleep, as if she would wake up laughing from her dreams.
It is said that life has its ups and downs. Just as Jing Shu was excitedly dreaming and almost waking up laughing on the isolated island, a major incident occurred in Wu City.
Major incidents happened every day. Ever since the building was swept away, Wu City had truly been thrown into chaos, with various distressing events happening daily.
But for an event to count as major, it had to involve Jing Shu; only then could it be called a major incident.
While Jing Shu was laughing in her sleep, Mrs. Jing was crying nonstop, along with her sister-in-law and Jing Shu’s aunt, whose crying was heartfelt and sincere. Uncle was also heaving sighs of despair.
The site of their crying was naturally not the villa, as they didn’t want to worry the elderly.
In fact, during the several months that Jing Shu had disappeared, nothing much had happened at home. The Jing family had almost gotten used to her disappearing for months at a time.
To stabilize everyone’s emotions, the person in charge, Jin Tianci, had told everyone below him that contact had been made, a rescue was in progress, Jing Shu was fine, and they were figuring out how to bring her back.
Therefore, the Jing family had always thought:
Things are as before. Although the building is gone, there are ample supplies. With Jin Tianci’s own son up there, there probably won’t be any major problems; the helicopter will find them and prioritize their rescue.
The family was worried:
What if someone provokes Jing Shu, and she does something drastic? Her strength is known to the whole family...
But it wasn’t just those two women crying; Jin Tianci’s wife was also sobbing. At that moment, in Jin Tianci’s room, Mr. Jing clenched his fists and, lifting his head with difficulty, asked, "I just want to know now, the inspection team said the building is gone, that everyone in the building died. Jing Shu, she... is it true?"
Jin Tianci hung his head, his hands trembling slightly. He had only one son. Sadly, Jin Tianci himself was not well; he lay in bed.
Jun Bao got up to comfort him, "Uncle, the people from the inspection team only want to take over the Red Worm Cake Factory."

chapters.title: Chapter 672: Sold the Insect Cake Factory?
chapters.content:
Chapter 672: Sold the Insect Cake Factory?
"As for the people in the building..." Jun Bao began, his voice dripping with disdain. They hadn’t even found a trace with round-the-clock flights, various search methods, and even satellites. The inspection team, who were merely observers, stood even less of a chance.
But he couldn’t say that. If he did, Wu City would probably be drowned in tears.
"The inspection team doesn’t know what they’re talking about. They’re just making things up. Think about it, who could possibly know more about the building’s whereabouts and rescue efforts than us?" Jun Bao said confidently. Only after seeing that his aunt behind him had stopped crying did he slowly exhale and purse his lips lightly.
At the same time, Jun Bao turned his gaze to his uncle.
It seemed that the mess of Wu City would have to be cleaned up by him.
It was just happening sooner than expected; his appointment had not yet arrived.
In an instant, numerous plans flashed through Jun Bao’s mind.
The usually calm and reserved young man exuded a chilling intensity at that moment, which was truly fearsome.
It was then that Mrs. Jing and Mr. Jing finally took a deep breath of relief. "So, they’re talking nonsense. That’s good, that’s really good..."
Aunt Wang Fang also let out a sigh, then asked worriedly, "What about the Red Worm Factory? It has already been closed for quite a few days, and so many people in the factory are depending on it for their livelihood.
"But the biggest issue is that the inspection team said that the people have been missing for three months and should be reported as deceased. The Insect Factory shares are now divided into three parts: the largest shareholder is Jing Shu, followed by Wucheng Town Government, and finally the scattered shares Jing Shu allocated to encourage everyone.
"The inspection team wants to buy Jing Shu’s shares..."
Her uncle’s family also owned a small share of the company. Even that small share ensured that their family had nothing to worry about in the apocalypse. However, before they could enjoy it for long, the Red Worm Factory was sealed. According to the inspection team, the factory was to be handed over to higher authorities.
But with so many institutions above, who knows which one it will be? Are they truly concerned with the people’s welfare, or just lining their own pockets, or is it something else?
Jin Tianci coughed a few times and said, "The Red Worm Factory situation is indeed a tough one... If Jing Shu were here, we could find other solutions. We can’t just rob them outright.
"But with the major shareholder missing for three months, once reported dead according to the new laws of the apocalypse, half goes to the next of kin and half to the state. Even if you two still hold a small portion of the shares, you must have received a notice to sell your shares, right?"
Mrs. Jing wiped away her tears, her face flushing with anger. "They actually think they can buy the remaining shares with just 8 million...
To expect to snap up such a huge Insect Cake Factory for 8 million Virtual Coins? What can you even buy with Virtual Coins now?
" If not for the presence of Wu City’s leaders, Mrs. Jing would have cursed them out long ago.
Even so, Jin Tianci felt very awkward. Virtual Coins used to be valuable, but now they were becoming increasingly worthless; this was inevitable.
Mrs. Jing continued to feel indignant.
These shameless people, trying to fool her with a bunch of virtual numbers? But it must be said, if Jing Shu were indeed declared dead, it was uncertain whether they could hold onto the Insect Factory.
At this moment, Mr. Jing said, "As long as Jing Shu comes back alive and well, we ask for nothing else. If those above want to buy the Red Worm Factory, let them. Who can argue with them when they wield the ’Imperial Sword’?"
Mrs. Jing tugged at Mr. Jing. The Insect Cake Factory was their daughter’s labor of love...
Even though she didn’t usually manage its affairs, work there, or concern herself much with it, she would at least visit once every month or two.
Jun Bao squinted. Standing up and gazing at the increasingly frozen earth outside, he spoke softly, "I think this deal can be made, but we’ll need to plan it carefully for the long term."
Although Jing Shu wasn’t present, Jun Bao felt that Wu City, as her support, shouldn’t have its assets seized so easily.
This would be disheartening, especially for someone who had made significant contributions to Wu City.
Of course, his willingness to intervene was also because the inspection team had harmed the interests of the Wu City people. On his own turf, for someone to dare target his logistics... The Insect Cake Factory provided one-tenth or two-tenths of Wu City’s annual food supply.
Such a large prize, a hen that lays golden eggs! His uncle had nurtured it well, providing machinery, manpower, and funds whenever needed. He practically worshipped it...
Jun Bao clenched his fists, a surge of anger rising within him.The next day, Jun Bao hosted the inspection team with Wu City specialties: Spicy Chicken, smoked sausage, and Honey Wine.
The guests and hosts thoroughly enjoyed themselves. The members of the inspection team found Jun Bao from the Imperial Capital to be very astute. He certainly lived up to his origins, with many tricks up his sleeve, and the feast he suggested was exactly to their liking.
"Jin Tianci’s nephew is quite agreeable," they said.
On the other hand, Jing Shu was oblivious to the fact that her Insect Cake Factory was about to be sold. She hummed a tune in high spirits, enjoying the delicacies in her space, which had grown again, adding six more fields.
As the migration drew near, Jing Shu definitely wanted to plant more and prepare semi-finished products.
Anyway, Jing Shu already felt insecure when her phone battery was at 95%, let alone when her space was empty. She also figured that the food supply at home would certainly have dwindled by the time she returned, so she needed to replenish it discreetly.
It’s worth mentioning that at first, the underground army wasn’t very impressive. But as the mansion moved, more and more wild rotten mermaids were attracted to the surroundings, becoming Jing Shu’s labor force.
In the beginning, Jing Shu had no specific destination; she just headed in the general direction. But later, when the homebred rotten mermaids in Jingshu’s space hatched, she dispatched them to scout ahead and draw maps.
Since the space was small, she released them in batches. Day by day, as her mapping efforts progressed, Jing Shu lost count of how many she had sent out, but the map in her mind grew increasingly clear.
With a target and direction, the rest became simpler.
The mansion was moving. Based on the weather, darkness, and other factors, the people on board quickly analyzed their situation. But where were they heading this time? Some with great insight soon deduced from various factors: "It’s very likely we’re drifting back!"
Upon hearing this news, everyone in the mansion was ecstatic. They saw hope!
"Moreover, we’re traveling in a straight line, unlike the circles we took coming here! We’ll be faster this way. It might not be many days before we float back to Wu City."
"If that’s the case, we just need to hold on for a few days, and our rations will be enough!"
Everyone was thrilled. Who wouldn’t be delighted by the prospect of surviving and returning to Wu City alive?
It was an unprovoked disaster, and no one could explain why.
Jing Shu felt that, within the entire mansion, only she truly understood what was happening; only she had reaped these benefits. Others had perhaps just drifted along and suffered considerably, but she had gained this life-saving trump card. Therefore, she felt she had to protect these people going forward.
At the very least, she had to ensure they had food to eat.

chapters.title: Chapter 673: Back to Wu City
chapters.content:
Chapter 673: Back to Wu City
Boss Lu left behind many things, but there were even more people in the building. Even with rationing and adding Bone Powder, their supplies still hit rock bottom in a matter of days.
When old rotten mermaids died, their corpses sank into the ground and swiftly transformed into White Energy. Consuming this White Energy, in turn, would hatch new rotten mermaids. It was an endless cycle of life and death.
This land, it truly was a treasure!
Based on her recent mapping, Jing Shu had a general understanding of this Mudstone Flow Sea area. Huaxia had never possessed such terrain before, so it must have emerged after tectonic shifts. However, whether it originated from a specific location or appeared out of thin air was impossible to determine.
And so, Jing Shu devised a plan to have people salvage the bones from underground as well.
She couldn’t make promises about other things, but at least the Bone Powder was undeniably filling.
As everyone spoke of their arrow-like eagerness to return home, Jing Shu’s longing to quickly reach Wu City intensified. Knowing their approximate location, their progress sped up considerably.
During the general meeting, everyone was excited. After Jun Jia implemented several measures, joy filled every face.
Jing Shu casually asked, "Now that it looks like we might return to Wu City soon, will the auction that’s been delayed for three months still proceed?"
Upon hearing this, Jun Jia shook his head like a rattle drum. "No, no. The necessary handovers were completed at the time. Subsequent damage assessments and subsidies will be handled accordingly. Let’s leave any further matters to... Jun Bao." He clearly no longer wanted to be in charge.
"Oh? Then..." Jing Shu touched her chin, asking nonchalantly, "Does that mean the building isn’t getting auctioned after all?"
Jun Jia gave a wry smile. "The building is in such a state, and we don’t even know where it might drift. If it ends up outside Wu City, it’ll be completely worthless. If, by some miracle, it drifts into Wu City’s residential area, it could only be sold at a steep discount. Perhaps we should ask Qian Duoduo if they need it..." His words may have been casual, but Jing Shu took careful note.
Even though the building was now just an empty shell, filthy with excrement, it was still an edifice capable of sheltering thousands from the wind and rain of the apocalypse. With a thorough cleaning, it could become a decent shelter.
Is it just a matter of waiting to see where the building drifts?
Jing Shu fell silent, a plan already forming in her mind. That day, she didn’t hesitate to use a significant amount of the milky Spiritual Spring to accelerate the breeding of more rotten mermaids.
It’s a pity I’m still short of some Virtual Coins.
Jing Shu was also reluctant to trade all her red worm cakes for the building. After all, with the migration imminent, food supplies like Insect Cakes were of paramount importance.
「After another three days.」
Everyone’s diet had transitioned to solely Bone Powder mush, which was, at least, still filling.
For those who were extremely hungry, the fragrant Bone Powder mush might have chewed like sand, but they could just swallow it down directly.
The only downside was that eating too much of it caused internal heat; bowel movements became like small, dry pellets, uncomfortably irritating one’s rear. These were truly harsh times—either you starved, or if you ate your fill, your backside ached.
Just as Jing Shu was still pondering her dilemma, a series of RUMBLES suddenly echoed from the sky, accompanied by the familiar BLARE of a horn.
"The rescue team is here!"
"They’ve finally found us!"
"We’re saved!"
The people inside the building erupted in cheers. At that moment, they cared little about the potential danger of monsters swarming outside; everyone rushed out to see the helicopter.
The helicopter landed steadily on the building’s periphery. Three people disembarked, their excitement palpable. Their three-month search had nearly driven them to despair, but the one in charge had provided a substantial amount of oil from their private reserves. An untold amount of this fuel had been burned daily, dispatching all of Wu City’s aircraft in an exhaustive carpet search.
It had to be said, while they hadn’t accomplished much else these past few months, they had managed to redraw the map of Wu City and, in doing so, made many other chilling discoveries.
Ultimately, they had found everything *except* for the massive building itself.
Jun Jia had everyone make way and welcomed the newcomers into the conference room. There, he gave the crowd a pep talk, a dose of Chicken Blood, and sternly warned that anyone causing trouble now would be left behind. This managed to calm the boisterous, excited people.
In the conference room, after the rescue team briefly inquired about the situation, they began discussing the evacuation plan. Jing Shu, however, frowned in confusion.
She wasn’t sure if it was a coincidence, but right after she had guided the building out of the Mud Sea, it suddenly felt as if she had crossed some invisible ’boundary,’ and everything had surfaced.
Team leader Liu Ge said, "I’ve already sent the coordinates. They’ll rush here immediately once they get the news. We’re only about eighty kilometers from Wu City... What are your orders for our next steps?"
Jun Jia frowned. "There are 1,600 people in this building. A large plane is too big to land, and the helicopter is too small—it can only carry a few people at a time. Take Gold Dominator back first. Then, dispatch a transport team to bring some food. Finally, depending on where the building comes to a stop, we’ll organize the main rescue operation."
"It’s strange, speaking of which," Liu Ge added. "We thoroughly searched the direction you came from, yet we never once encountered you."
"Let’s not dwell on that now. We need to act quickly," Jun Jia urged. Having faced life and death, he was more eager than ever to go home and enjoy a milk tea, not wanting to stay here a moment longer.
Gold Dominator, holding onto a sow, looked at Jing Shu. "You come with me." Although he couldn’t stand her, this woman had an undeniable knack for raising pigs. The sow had piglets, a matter not to be taken lightly. Crucially, for some unknown reason, the sow was especially attached to Jing Shu; with her around, it remained calm and quiet.
Jing Shu, unaware that Gold Dominator saw her as some kind of pig midwife, was somewhat touched. "You all go first. The principal from our school is still here; it wouldn’t look good if I left before them."
